institution: Kunstuniversität Linz (University of Art and Design Linz), in cooperation with Anton Bruckner Privatuniversit…
programme: Master Programme Postdigital Lutherie
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's; portfolio required, so build it
verdictWhy: This is the single best structural fit in this slice: an English-taught MA that only asks for 'a valid bachelor (or equivalent) degree', has no live audition, no German, and is explicitly aimed at people building instruments at the Design/Technology–Composition boundary — which is what a software engineer with a synth habit actually is. Cost is ~EUR 1,500/yr, not free, but that is affordable. The one thing he must do is build the portfolio, since the university publishes no spec and will judge him purely on the works he shows.
correction: INPUT SAID 'Free' — WRONG for a Tunisian. Austrian public universities charge third-country nationals EUR 726.72 per semester; the programme's own admission page states this figure. Real cost ≈ EUR 1,505/year including ÖH.
qualification: Master — four-semester international master programme (exact degree abbreviation not stated on the official pages; UNVERIFIED)
tuition: CONFIRMED, verbatim: "For EU-citizens the programme is generally free of charge, non-EU-citizens currently have to pay a fee of 726,72 € per semester." (Plus the standard ÖH fee, which the page does not itemise.)
scholarshipDetail: CONFIRMED that "Students can apply to university fee reduction funds" (Studienbeitragsermäßigung). No amounts, eligibility criteria or named external scholarship are published — UNVERIFIED. No stipend of any kind is mentioned.
entry: CONFIRMED, verbatim: "To study at Postdigital Lutherie you need a valid bachelor (or equivalent) degree to qualify for the admission to this master programme." No field restriction, no German requirement. For online registration you must provide a copy of your degree, a motivation letter, your CV and a portfolio of your works.
acceptsNonMusic: Yes — best-in-batch on this point, confirmed verbatim in both language versions: only "a valid bachelor (or equivalent) degree" is required. No music degree, no conservatory training, no German. The subject matter (building instruments, code, interfaces, interaction design) directly rewards a software-engineering background.
portfolio: "a portfolio of your works" — that is the entire published specification. No number of works, no duration, no file format, no size limit is stated on either the English or German admission page. UNVERIFIED at that level of detail; contact Univ.-Prof. Dr. Martin Kaltenbrunner (martin.kaltenbrunner@kunstuni-linz.at), who runs the registration procedure.
audition: An entrance examination in the form of an interview ("Vorstellungsgespräch") built around the submitted portfolio, plus "Materials needed for the interview". Whether attendance in Linz is required is NOT stated (UNVERIFIED); the exam being scheduled for a single fixed day (29 June 2026 for the 26/27 intake) implies on-site attendance. No musical performance audition is mentioned.
deadline: Published on the official page for the 26/27 intake: "The application window for the next academic year 26/27 is now open until June 19, 2026. The entrance exams will take place on June 29, 2026." PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Note this is a JUNE deadline, far later than the usual Oct–Feb window, so the 2027/28 dates will likely not appear until spring 2027.
opens: UNVERIFIED for the 2027/28 cycle — the page only ever shows the currently open window.
duration: CONFIRMED 4 semesters (2 years). ECTS NOT PUBLISHED on either the English or German official page — UNVERIFIED (Austrian masters are normally 120).
study: "Postdigital Musical Instruments on the intersections between Design & Technology, Composition & Performance as well as Art- & Media-Theories." Students reconnect acoustic, electronic and digital approaches to instrument design in tangible sonic artefacts for musical expression — building controllers, interfaces and instruments and then composing/performing with them. Hosted by the Tangible Interaction Design department (tamlab); Anton Bruckner Privatuniversität is the cooperation partner and its composition students may take Lutherie courses as electives.
recommendation: The most realistically enterable, genuinely hands-on, English-taught, near-free option in this batch for a CS/SE graduate with no conservatory record: any bachelor qualifies, no German, €726.72 a semester, and the work itself is building instruments and performing with them. Two caveats: the portfolio specification is not published at all, so he must email Kaltenbrunner early to find out what is actually expected; and it is instrument-design and performance research, not a DJ/producer or mixing-and-mastering course. He must also watch the unusual June deadline rather than assuming an Oct–Feb window.

institution: České vysoké učení technické v Praze (ČVUT) / Czech Technical University in Prague, Fakulta elektrotechnická …

whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's; portfolio required, so build it
qualification: Ing. (inženýr) — real, state-recognised second-cycle engineering degree. CONFIRMED.
accreditation: Nationally accredited public university programme (NAÚ). Supports a Czech long-term residence permit for study. CONFIRMED.
tuition: CZECH-TAUGHT TRACK: 0 CZK for a Tunisian national — tuition-free status attaches to the language of instruction, not citizenship. ENGLISH-TAUGHT TRACK: CORRECTED FROM 'UNPUBLISHED / TREAT AS UNCONFIRMED' TO CONFIRMED. FEL's official tuition-fees page states master's programmes cost 132 000 CZK per academic year (66 000 CZK per semester), ~5,280 EUR/year, ~10,560 EUR over the two-year degree. The faculty reserves the right to adjust each semester, so re-check for 2027/2028, but the figure is now on the record from the primary source rather than a secondary summary.
otherFees: Application fee 950 CZK per programme AND per specialization — two specializations cost 1,900 CZK. Payment must be made the same day the application is filed; the application enters the procedure only once the fee is paid. Prague living costs ~20,000-28,000 CZK/month, the highest of the six.
totalCost: Czech track: ~500,000-670,000 CZK (~20,000-27,000 EUR) over two years, all living costs. English track: add 264,000 CZK tuition (~10,560 EUR), so ~30,000-37,500 EUR total.
scholarshipDetail: The faculty states high-performing international students may be eligible for scholarships, with no amounts or eligibility rules published. UNVERIFIED — ask the FEL international office whether any entry scholarship is open to a first-year non-EU master's student.
entry: A completed bachelor's degree, evidenced before enrolment. For the English track the entrance examination is an ONLINE INTERVIEW plus an optional committee-set test. Required documents: transcript of results, English certificate (if not a native speaker), and a MOTIVATION LETTER; documents not in Czech, Slovak or English need certified translation. Nostrification of the foreign qualification must be completed by end of October of the first semester — i.e. AFTER arrival, which materially lowers the barrier at application time. Programme guarantor for the specialization: prof. Petr Páta (pata@fel.cvut.cz); programme responsible: prof. Stanislav Zvánovec.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — EMPHATICALLY, and confirmed. This is an electrical-engineering faculty programme that actively prefers applicants from electronics, informatics, mathematics or physics. A BSc in Software Engineering is the expected feeder profile. Of the six programmes reviewed, this is the only one where his existing degree is an asset rather than a liability.
portfolio: NONE. No portfolio, no creative dossier, no artistic assessment. Applicants are merely 'recommended' to submit evidence of significant achievements in electrical engineering, informatics, mathematics or physics — which a software-engineering graduate supplies directly from his degree and projects. CONFIRMED.
audition: None. No audition, no musical assessment of any kind. CONFIRMED.
deadline: CORRECTED. The previous record gave 31 March as the English-track deadline. FEL's official admission-procedure page states that for the 2026/2027 academic year the deadline for submitting applications is 13 AUGUST 2026. The 31 March date appears to relate to the Czech-taught round (with entrance examination 5 June 2026). PRIOR CYCLE — for a SEPTEMBER 2027 start, diarise a Czech-track deadline around 31 March 2027 and an English-track deadline around mid-August 2027, and confirm both against the dean's decree when it is issued in November 2026.
opens: Autumn preceding the academic year; the dean's decree for the 2026/2027 cycle was issued 19 November 2025.
duration: 120 ECTS minimum; standard 2 years / 4 semesters, full-time. Study plan 'Elektronika a komunikace — Audiovizuální technika a zpracování signálů'. CONFIRMED.
languageReq: CORRECTED — THERE IS A PUBLISHED BAND, contrary to the previous record's claim that 'no named IELTS/TOEFL band is set, the committee judges it'. FEL's official admission-procedure page names acceptable proof of English proficiency as TOEFL iBT 70 / IELTS 6 / TOEIC 800. He should plan for IELTS Academic 6.0 as a firm target, not treat the requirement as discretionary. For the Czech track: Czech, with the entrance examination in Czech.
englishTest: CORRECTED. TOEFL iBT 70 / IELTS 6 / TOEIC 800, named on FEL's official admission-procedure page. The previous record's 'no fixed band' framing was wrong and would have led him to under-prepare. IELTS 6.0 is well within reach for someone at working-English level, so this is a soft gate, but it is a real one.
study: Sensing, processing and reproduction of audiovisual signals; practical acoustic design and measurement; image and sound technology; modern methods of processing, compression and reconstruction of image, sound and other signals; explicit orientation toward 'člověk jako příjemce audiovizuální informace' (the human as recipient of audiovisual information). Graduates go into television and radio operations, AV and acoustics design, automotive, and biomedical applications. English-language description: 'Get theoretical background and practical skills in acquisition, processing and reproduction of audiovisual signals. Audio, image, video…'
recommendation: TOP PICK, AND THE RE-CHECK STRENGTHENED IT. Three of the four open questions in the previous record are now closed from primary sources: (1) the English-taught track definitively carries the Audiovisual Technology and Signal Processing specialization — it is one of seven listed on the official English programme site, and Electronics and Communications appears by name on FEL's list of programmes conducted in English; (2) the English-track fee is 132 000 CZK per year / 66 000 CZK per semester, published on the faculty's own tuition page, roughly 10,560 EUR for the whole degree; (3) the English requirement is TOEFL iBT 70 / IELTS 6 / TOEIC 800, not an unbounded committee judgement — so he must actually sit a test, but a 6.0 is comfortably reachable. One correction against him: the English-track deadline is mid-August, not 31 March, which is a different diary entry than previously recorded. Everything that made this the best fit still holds: no portfolio, no audition, no music degree, no conservatory training, an online interview plus a motivation letter, and his BSc Software Engineering as the preferred feeder. It is not a DJ or music-production degree — it is audiovisual signal engineering — but it is credible, affordable, visa-supporting, and puts him inside a Prague audio ecosystem where the production career can be built alongside. Three actions: (1) sit IELTS Academic targeting 6.5 for headroom; (2) e-mail pata@fel.cvut.cz to confirm the specialization runs in English for 2027/2028 and ask about entry scholarships; (3) start Czech from zero anyway, because the Czech track costs nothing.

institution: Taideyliopiston Sibelius-Akatemia / Sibelius Academy, University of the Arts Helsinki (Uniarts Helsinki)
programme: Music Technology, master (Musiikkiteknologia) — specialisation path RECORDING ARTS
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's; portfolio required, so build it
qualification: Master of Music (MMus), musiikin maisteri
accreditation: State university (Taideyliopisto / University of the Arts Helsinki), Sibelius Academy is its music faculty
tuition: EUR 0 IF STUDYING IN FINNISH OR SWEDISH. EUR 28,000 per academic year if studying in English, for students starting 1 August 2026 or later. THIS IS THE FINNISH-LANGUAGE LOOPHOLE THE BRIEF ASKED ABOUT AND IT IS REAL. Uniarts states VERBATIM: "Tuition fees at Uniarts Helsinki are applicable to bachelor and master students who study in English and who are not citizens of EU, EEA, or Switzerland" and "If a student’s language of studies changes to Finnish or Swedish, they will no longer have to pay annual tuition fees." Finnish national law only permits fees for vieraskielinen (foreign-language) degree education; Finnish- and Swedish-taught degrees are free of charge regardless of nationality. Music Technology is one of the very few Sibelius Academy programmes that formally offers Finnish, Swedish AND English as tuition languages, so the exemption is genuinely reachable here rather than theoretical.
otherFees: EUR 100 application fee for applicants from outside the EU/EEA/Switzerland. Language test must be completed by the stated date if proficiency is not evidenced by prior studies.
totalCost: If admitted in Finnish/Swedish: EUR 0 tuition + EUR 100 application + Helsinki living costs (Finnish residence-permit maintenance requirement approx. EUR 800/month, UNVERIFIED 2027 figure) — roughly EUR 24,000 over 2.5 years, all living costs. If admitted in English: add EUR 70,000 tuition over 2.5 years with NO scholarship available.
scholarshipDetail: VERBATIM: "The university does not grant any scholarships to cover the tuition fee for students starting in August 2026 or later" and "Uniarts Helsinki does not grant scholarships for living expenses." The ONLY way to make this affordable is the Finnish/Swedish language exemption.
entry: VERBATIM: applicants need "at least one of the following: A lower university degree in music (Bachelor), a university of applied sciences degree in music, a foreign degree or qualification in music", or a non-music degree with supplementary music studies. Programme-specific clause VERBATIM: "a higher education degree in the field of technology or media is also applicable if you also have a sufficient amount of music studies."
acceptsNonMusic: YES — CONDITIONALLY, AND THIS IS THE BEST NON-MUSIC CLAUSE FOUND IN THE WHOLE REGION. QUOTE: "a higher education degree in the field of technology or media is also applicable if you also have a sufficient amount of music studies." A BSc Software Engineering is a higher education degree in the field of technology. The binding condition is "a sufficient amount of music studies", which is not quantified on the page (UNVERIFIED how many ECTS of music study count). This clause exists specifically because Music Technology expects engineers — it is a designed door for exactly this candidate profile, provided he accumulates formal music studies before applying.
portfolio: EXACT advance assignments: (1) Portfolio of MAXIMUM 3 WORKS, total length 10 MINUTES OR LESS, audio in MP3 or video in MP4 format. (2) Video self-presentation, 3 minutes or less. (3) Project description forms (PDF). (4) Motivation letter, max 2 A4 pages. (5) CV (PDF). (6) Final project plan, max 2 A4 pages. (7) Preliminary study plan (max 150 ECTS credits). Advance assignments are weighted 100%.
audition: THERE IS A PERFORMANCE AUDITION — this is the decisive distinction for this candidate and it counts AGAINST him. The remote examination has two parts: (1) "Instrument or voice audition (7-10 minutes) - any tradition welcome" weighted 40%; (2) "Interview (up to 25 minutes)" discussing portfolio, audition, background and plans, weighted 60%. So a live instrumental or vocal performance of 7-10 minutes IS required, although any musical tradition is accepted. NO ear-training or music-theory test is mentioned in the documentation. GOOD NEWS: the examination is REMOTE — no travel to Helsinki needed.
deadline: *** NO INTAKE IN 2027 *** VERBATIM from the programme page: "No admission in 2027. Next possible time to apply will be announced later." The programme admits every other year. The 2026 cycle (PRIOR CYCLE) ran: applications 7-21 January 2026 (by 15:00 EET); supporting documents and advance assignments 28 January 2026 (15:00 EET); language test completed by 2 March 2026; entrance exams 31 March - 1 April 2026 (REMOTE); results 10 April 2026; study place acceptance by 9 July 2026. Next master-only intake most likely 2028 — UNVERIFIED.
opens: 7 January 2026 for the 2026 cycle — PRIOR CYCLE. No 2027 cycle.
duration: 2.5 years (150 ECTS equivalent). Admits new students on ALTERNATING years — either a 5.5-year bachelor+master cohort or a 2.5-year master-only cohort.
languageReq: Must demonstrate proficiency in Finnish, Swedish OR English by the application deadline, through prior studies or a standardised test. To get the fee exemption the language of studies must be Finnish or Swedish — which means real Finnish (or Swedish) proficiency, realistically B2/C1, achieved before applying. UNVERIFIED exact required level.
englishTest: Accepted as one of the three qualifying languages; exact test/score UNVERIFIED. Note: choosing English triggers the EUR 28,000/yr fee.
study: Three specialisation paths. (1) RECORDING ARTS — the in-scope one: students develop expertise in "music producer and sound engineer" roles, covering recording, editing and mixing techniques for both popular AND classical music, plus live sound reinforcement and audio technology. (2) Film and Game Music — music production for film, game and visual media, music design, sound design, composing and arranging for virtual instruments. (3) Creative Electronic Music Practices — electroacoustic, live electronics, sonic arts, sound installation, generative music (OUT OF SCOPE per brief). Students participate in recording Sibelius Academy concerts and in contemporary-music, multimedia and electroacoustic concert production.

institution: Consortium coordinated by Université Jean Monnet Saint-Étienne (France), with Universidade Católica Portugues…

whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's; portfolio required, so build it
verdictWhy: This is the highest-value target in the slice and the calendar lines up exactly: the 2027-2029 cohort call opens November 2026 for a September 2027 start, tuition is zero for everyone, and the EUR 1,400/month × 24 months Erasmus Mundus scholarship needs no separate application. He must do two things before November 2026: sit IELTS (6.0 minimum, aim higher since C1 is 'recommended' and this is a competitive EMJM) and produce 3-5 finished sound works.
correction: No cost correction needed — 'Free' is confirmed verbatim. CORRECTION TO THE CYCLE: the next intake is the 2027-2029 cohort with the call opening November 2026, not a rolling/spring deadline; the February deadline in circulation belongs to the closed 2026-2028 cycle.
qualification: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (EMJM) — multiple degrees from the three consortium universities
tuition: ZERO. Confirmed verbatim on the official financial-aid page: 'Students (scholarship holders and non-scholarship holders) are not charged any tuition fees.' Selected self-funded applicants must supply a 'Guarantee of full financial support' with a budget simulation before enrolment, and document income for the visa.
scholarshipDetail: CONFIRMED: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (EMJM) scholarship — €1,400 per month for a total duration of 24 months, maximum €33,600 per student, covering travel, visa, installation and subsistence, paid to the student. A limited number are awarded per cohort. The scholarship application is included within the programme application itself, so there is no separate form. Non-scholarship holders may add Erasmus+ KA131/KA171 mobility funds. Additional support exists for students with long-term physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairments. Tunisian nationality is no barrier — EMJM scholarships are explicitly open to non-EU applicants.
entry: CONFIRMED: 'A Bachelor's degree of at least 180 ECTS is the minimum requirement to enrol', with NO field restriction stated anywhere on the official pages. Candidates holding at least 150 ECTS at application may apply with a sworn statement that 180 ECTS will be completed before the programme starts. Documents: Europass CV in English; ID/passport; certified copies (with certified English translations) of higher-education and high-school diplomas and complete transcripts showing courses, grades, ECTS and final marks; at least two letters of recommendation in English on official letterhead with referee contacts; a 'Science qualification and experience in New Technology' self-assessment form covering level in mathematics, digital signal processing and computer science, and skills in JavaScript, Python or C, HTML, real-time graphics programming, geometry, trigonometry and algebra; certified English test at B2 minimum (C1 recommended); signed application notice. Applications go through the UJM eCandidat portal, explicitly NOT through Études en France.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — the strongest and clearest case among all six programmes. The only academic requirement published is 'A Bachelor's degree of at least 180 ECTS', with no field restriction. The application actively rewards a software background: a compulsory form asks candidates to self-assess their level in mathematics, digital signal processing and computer science, and specifically in JavaScript, Python or C, HTML, real-time graphics programming, geometry, trigonometric functions and algebra. A software-engineering graduate with a music portfolio is close to the ideal applicant profile.
portfolio: CONFIRMED and exact: an Artistic or Professional Portfolio presenting productions related to the chosen specialization path. 'All projects included in the portfolio must not be more than 5 years old.' Submit EXACTLY 3 to 5 works or projects (video/audio/images) with metadata — title, short description, public link, and the applicant's role — numbered 1 to 5. For Sound-Music applicants this may be a composition project (orchestral or electronic), a sound design project, a sound concept project, a music piece cycle, a demo, etc. The PDF is capped at 5 MB, so media is supplied via online links. ALSO required in place of a cover letter: a VIDEO PRESENTATION of maximum 2 minutes covering, in order, current situation, motivation for applying, understanding of the programme, why the candidate can succeed, and ideas for applied research and professional development; the link is supplied in a PDF in the 'Motivation letter' field and must stay accessible to the selection board through mid-April.
audition: No live audition and no on-site test. Stage I is document review only. Stage II, for shortlisted applicants only, is an ONLINE 15-minute interview (2026 cycle: 24-30 March 2026) assessing personality characteristics, way of thinking, personal life experience and character attributes. Candidates may additionally be asked to join a videoconference to verify English level. No travel is required at any point in the selection.
deadline: 2027-2029 deadline NOT YET PUBLISHED — expected around mid-February 2027, to be confirmed from November 2026. PRIOR CYCLE reference (confirmed on the official page): the 2026-2028 call opened 14 November 2025 and closed 16 February 2026, with Stage II online interviews 24-30 March 2026.
opens: 2027 CYCLE, CONFIRMED ON THE OFFICIAL PAGE: 'The call for applications for the next DIGICREA cohort 2027-2029 is expected to open in November 2026. Further information regarding this procedure will be available in the autumn. Please note that some requirements will differ from those of the 2026 selection process.'
duration: 2 years / 4 semesters, ending with an internship. Total ECTS not stated on the official pages read (EMJM standard is 120) — CONFIRMED duration, ECTS figure UNVERIFIED.
study: Audiovisual new media, emerging technologies in the film industry, music, graphic design, artificial intelligence, virtual/extended reality and their applications. Two specialization paths (SOUND-MUSIC and IMAGE); the Selection Board assesses 'predispositions for professions related to the production of audio-visual and musical forms, including the production of Extended Reality films'. Mobility Saint-Étienne to Porto to Katowice, then an internship with public and private partners. The Saint-Étienne semester shares teaching with the UJM CCNT/RIM programme, which provides a music studio, video studio and multimedia prototyping studio. Detailed module-by-module list is not published — UNVERIFIED.
recommendation: The standout recommendation and the only programme here that clears every one of his constraints at once: zero tuition, €1,400/month for two years, taught in English (so IELTS/TOEFL rather than a French DALF C1), a bachelor in ANY field accepted, a Sound-Music specialization, an application form that explicitly credits his programming skills, and a fully remote selection (one 15-minute online interview). The 2027-2029 call is expected to open November 2026 — precisely his window. Two concrete tasks now: build a portfolio of exactly 3-5 numbered works with public links and metadata (a composition, a sound-design project, a demo, a music cycle), and book an English test at B2 minimum, C1 preferred. Caveats: the curriculum is broad digital creativity — AI, XR, graphic design — rather than a dedicated club-music production course, and EMJM scholarships are highly competitive with only a limited number per cohort.

recommendation: The attractive parts are real: tuition-free, portfolio-only admission, no audition, no compulsory interview, and a genuine cluster of six sound professorships. He needs IELTS 7.0 (a full band above the IELTS 6.0 most programmes ask, and he has not sat the test); his 180-ECTS BSc falls short of the 240-ECTS assumption and would trigger bridge semesters; "professionally relevant" is a discretionary judgement his CS degree may not survive without a substantial media-art portfolio he does not yet have; and the two official pages disagree on whether he also needs German C1. On top of that the output is sound art and experimental radio, not production or DJing. Worth a written enquiry to the faculty about the German level and the ECTS gap before spending any effort.

Verbatim: 'Third Country Nationals: A cost contribution of 727 euros per semester applies, which must be prepaid to FH JOANNEUM for the first two semesters (1,454 euros total) before the study place confirmation.' Compare the EU rate on the programme page: '€ 363,36 per semester' — so a third-country national pays exactly DOUBLE the EU rate. NOTE THE CASH-FLOW TRAP: €1,454 is due up front, before your place is confirmed.
otherFees: ÖH student-union contribution, currently €20.70 per semester. Cost of the English certificate (TOEFL/IELTS/telc/Cambridge/PTE). Austrian residence-permit fees and proof-of-funds requirement.
totalCost: Tuition €1,454/yr + ÖH ~€41/yr = ~€1,495/yr. Graz living costs are the lowest of any city in this search — budget roughly €10,000–12,000/yr (UNVERIFIED). Two-year total including living: roughly €23,000–27,000. THIS IS THE CHEAPEST VIABLE OPTION IN THE WHOLE TERRITORY.
scholarshipDetail: Not published on the admissions pages. Austrian options a Tunisian could pursue separately include the OeAD Ernst Mach Grant and the Austrian Development Cooperation scholarships, neither of which was verified for this programme. UNVERIFIED.
entry: Verbatim: 'If you want to apply for this Master's degree programme you need to have a relevant Bachelor's degree or equivalent qualification.' Then, verbatim and in detail: 'Graduates of technical, artistic, humanities, social sciences, economics, natural sciences and interdisciplinary programmes at universities, technical universities or art universities with a Bachelor's, Master's or Diplom degree will be admitted if: 80 ECTS credits from their previous studies largely correspond to the core subject areas of the Bachelor's programme in Information Design at FH JOANNEUM or a comparable relevant degree programme, AND at least one of the following eligibility criteria is met: Relevant professional experience spanning a period of at least two years; Assessment of professional aptitude based on the submitted portfolio; Relevant further training or study modules with a workload equivalent of at least 30 ECTS. The degree must be from a recognised institution of postsecondary education in Austria or abroad. In ambiguous cases, the head of degree programme will decide whether the candidate meets the admission requirements.' Documents: signed letter of application (in English), signed CV (in English), degree certificate, transcript of records, university-entrance qualification, English proof, passport copy, and the portfolio PDF.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — TECHNICAL GRADUATES ARE NAMED FIRST. Quoted verbatim: 'Graduates of TECHNICAL, artistic, humanities, social sciences, economics, natural sciences and interdisciplinary programmes ... will be admitted if ...'. And separately: 'Students from relatively distant (non-design-related) study programs may be given the opportunity to participate in the admissions examination if they demonstrate appropriate talent and prior performance. The study program management of FH JOANNEUM decides on equivalence after a complete application is submitted and may require additional workshops, exercises, and courses.' TWO REAL HURDLES FOR HIM: (1) the 80-ECTS correspondence with the Information Design bachelor's core areas — a software-engineering BSc will match on the technical/media-technology side but not on the design side, and the programme head decides; (2) of the three supplementary criteria he currently meets NONE cleanly — he has no two years of relevant professional experience and no 30 ECTS of further training, so he must rely on 'Assessment of professional aptitude based on the submitted portfolio'. THE PORTFOLIO IS THEREFORE HIS ONLY QUALIFYING LIMB, and it must carry the whole argument.
portfolio: EXACT AND DEMANDING. Verbatim guidelines: 'Only online portfolios are accepted. The portfolio should comprise approximately 10 TO 20 REPRESENTATIVE WORK PIECES. The selection and form of the work samples is totally up to the applicant, but should correspond to the applicant's range of interests and competencies. All media formats are allowed – e.g. graphics, illustrations, photos, texts, videos, animations, apps, AUDIO PRODUCTIONS, web sites, media installations, project documentations, and the like. All descriptive texts must be written in German or English. THE ONLINE PORTFOLIO HAS TO BE ACCESSIBLE IN THE PERIOD FROM THE APPLICATION DEADLINE UNTIL THE END OF OCTOBER.' Submitted as a web link, plus 'a PDF including the web-link to your online portfolio in the first line of the first page; a list of all the work pieces with correct attribution of the authorship. In case of teamwork the applicant's responsibilities have to be clearly outlined; screenshots of all pages of the online portfolio (also screenshots of videos, animations or interactive applications).' 10–20 pieces is a LOT for someone with no portfolio today — but note apps and project documentation count, so his software work is admissible material alongside audio.
audition: NO AUDITION, NO EAR-TRAINING EXAM — A PORTFOLIO REVIEW PLUS AN ONLINE INTERVIEW. Verbatim: 'The admissions process consists of: a complete application, an assessment of the online portfolio by the admissions committee, an online interview with the admissions committee and an assessment of previous qualifications and practical professional experience. The form of the application will also be taken into consideration.' On the interview, verbatim: 'All candidates are invited to an interview. You are given the opportunity to demonstrate both your knowledge in the field of sound design and your motivation, suitability and talent for the chosen course of study and a subsequent career in this field. The admissions interview will either be held via video call. At the beginning of the online interview the applicant must confirm that no unauthorised aids are used and no one else is present to help. The applicant must also present official photo identification. The interview will be conducted by key staff from the Institute of Design & Communication. It will last around 20 minutes.' No performance, no aural test, no set production task — and it is CONDUCTED BY VIDEO CALL, so no Schengen visa is needed to be selected.
deadline: MULTIPLE ROUNDS PER YEAR — the most forgiving calendar found anywhere. PRIOR CYCLE OBSERVED (for the 28.09.2026 start): application until 01.02.2026 with interviews 23–27.02.2026; until 24.03.2026 with interviews 20–24.04.2026; until 27.04.2026 with interviews 11–15.05.2026; until 26.05.2026 with interviews 29.06–03.07.2026; until 29.06.2026 with interview 16.07.2026. Five separate windows. For a September 2027 start expect the same rolling pattern from about February 2027 to late June 2027; FH JOANNEUM notes 'The dates on this page will be updated on an ongoing basis.' International applicants are directed to a separate deadline page — those specific international deadlines are UNVERIFIED and may be earlier, so apply in the FIRST round.
opens: Rolling; the first round closed 1 February in the 2026 cycle. Note the portfolio must stay online from the application deadline until the end of October.
duration: 4 semesters, 120 ECTS, 'Work-friendly' mode (berufsbegleitend). Attendance is light: 'One day per week is lesson-free. The average attendance during the first three semesters is 19 hours per week. During the fourth semester, students write a master's thesis, which means that during this time the average attendance is three hours per week.' CAUTION FOR A STUDENT VISA: a part-time/work-friendly programme can complicate an Austrian student residence permit, which normally expects full-time study — verify with the Austrian embassy.
languageReq: English only, B2 CEFR. No German requirement whatsoever for admission or study. (German would still be needed for daily life and for any part-time work in Graz.)
englishTest: SPECIFIC SCORES PUBLISHED, verbatim: 'Proof of proficiency in English must be provided in the form of a TOEFL Certificate (min. 87 points), a TELC Certificate (B2), a Cambridge Certificate (First Certificate in English, FCE), an IELTS Certificate (5.0), a PTE Academic Certificate (Pearson Test of English; min. 59 points), an Austrian secondary school leaving certificate or another equivalent school certificate.' IELTS 5.0 IS AN UNUSUALLY LOW BAR — his working English clears it comfortably.
study: Verbatim: 'Storytelling with sound forms the core of this inter-university programme ... Students of the Sound Design study track ... develop knowledge of sound design, media preparation and technical processing. The master's programme covers topics relevant to musicians, sound designers, digital artists and the creative industry, including sound design, immersive audio, product sound design, sonification and sonic interaction design. Students design sounds for films, computer games, audio logos and podcasts, bring data to life through sound, optimise the sound of products and explore immersive sound.' FIT CAVEAT: this is Audiodesign in the media sense — film, games, podcasts, audio logos, product sound, sonification. It is NOT record production, and it will not teach him to mix and master songs. It IS in the brief's field list (Audiodesign) and it is by far the most accessible door; but it is a different career from making records. Projects run 'under real world conditions' with media-industry and festival partners, and 'virtually all project results are published'.

acceptsNonMusic: YES in spirit — the accepted list is design/acoustics/audio-engineering/architecture-led rather than music-led, and "related fields" plus the explicit bridging mechanism ("Candidates from non-design backgrounds may receive mandatory supplementary coursework requirements during semesters one and two") make a software-engineering BSc a credible application. Not named verbatim, so: Check.

study: Four specialisation areas: product sound design, acoustic data display (sonification), sound for moving images, and sound with interfaces. Technical-scientific and sound-design content are treated as equally core, integrated with seminars in communication, media and interaction design. Candidates from non-design backgrounds may be given mandatory supplementary coursework in semesters 1-2.
recommendation: Notable because it is the one programme in this slice whose 2027 application rounds are already published in outline, and because its accepted-bachelor list is engineering/design-led rather than music-led — so a software-engineering BSc has a real path here. But be clear about content: this is product/interface/sonification sound design, not music production and not DJing. Recommend only if his interest genuinely extends to sound design for objects, screens and interfaces.

institution: Fachhochschule Salzburg (FH Salzburg / Salzburg University of Applied Sciences)

whyChance: Names engineering or computing as a welcome background; portfolio required, so build it
verdictWhy: Cheap (about EUR 780/yr), English-taught, no audition, and the deadline structure fits a September 2027 start — but admission is not on portfolio alone: they demand 'proof of ECTS credits in the core subject areas required for the Master's programme', and a software-engineering transcript has none of them. He must email study@fh-salzburg.ac.at with his transcript BEFORE investing in the application and get a written answer on whether his credits count. If they say no, this is dead.
correction: Cost band 'Under EUR 1.5k/yr' is CONFIRMED and is actually generous — the real figure is ~EUR 778/yr. But the input's gate description is incomplete: the binding hurdle is not the portfolio or interview, it is the requirement for prior ECTS in the programme's core subject areas. Also a refundable tuition deposit is demanded from third-country applicants at application time.
qualification: Master of Arts in Arts and Design (MA)
tuition: €363.36 per semester tuition plus €26.20 ÖH fee, with no separate higher non-EU rate published. CONFIRMED additionally: "Salzburg University of Applied Sciences (FH Salzburg) requires a tuition fee deposit from applicants who do not hold a citizenship or do not have an entrance qualification or a university degree from one of these states: European Union member states, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland." The deposit is credited against the first semester's tuition and ÖH fee, or refunded if you do not enrol. The DEPOSIT AMOUNT is set in a separate guideline and remains UNVERIFIED.
scholarshipDetail: None found on the pages read.
entry: CONFIRMED from the official Master-Admission info sheet (WS 2026/27 edition), three conditions: (1) a university degree or equivalent from a recognised post-secondary institution in Austria or abroad; (2) proof of a minimum number of ECTS in three core subject areas — 35 ECTS Creative-artistic design practice (graphic design, media design, film, TV, audio, music, game design), 10 ECTS Basic sciences (media theory, cultural theory, art theory, media informatics, media technology, media sociology, media history, communication and media studies, media psychology, aesthetics), 5 ECTS Economics and working methods in the field of media (project management, media economics, entrepreneurship, business administration, marketing, media law); (3) mastery of English at least level B2. Non-Austrian documents must be notarised/legalised where no international agreement applies, and certified translations of the degree certificate and transcripts must be uploaded.
acceptsNonMusic: Check — the degree field is flexible but the ECTS gate is the real obstacle, and this is now confirmed precisely. The official "List of relevant disciplines" includes a category "Media Technology and Media Informatics — Internet Technology, Internet Technologies, Information Management, Media Technology and Design, Digital Media, etc.", and the list is explicitly "not exhaustive" — so a software-engineering BSc can plausibly count as a relevant degree. BUT he must separately document 35 ECTS of creative-artistic design practice, 10 ECTS of basic sciences and 5 ECTS of media economics from his transcript. CONFIRMED that the waiver of full ECTS proof applies ONLY to the Producing department: "Applications for the Department of Producing are possible even if proof of ECTS credits in the required core subject areas cannot be provided in full." Audio gets no such exemption.
portfolio: CONFIRMED verbatim from the official Master info sheet: "Portfolio: If you want to apply for Audio, Film or Communication Design, upload your portfolio in the application portal under 'Upload application project' as a ZIP file (which should contain a PDF). Present at least three of your best creative works from the last few years. Describe in your portfolio the role you played in the projects shown." Only the Producing department substitutes a letter of motivation. Also required: bachelor's degree certificate (may be submitted by 31 October at the latest), proof of English B2, passport copy, CV in English, the choice-of-department form (p.11 of the info sheet), the proof-of-academic-level form (p.9) and transcripts incl. ECTS key. All third-party material and any soundtrack used must be credited; undeclared external material or copied ideas cause exclusion from the admission procedure. NOTE: a separate FH Salzburg PDF titled "MultiMediaArt PORTFOLIO REQUIREMENTS" describes an Audio portfolio as a link to soundcloud/bandcamp/youtube plus CV, credit list and software/hardware list — that document uses the BACHELOR major names (computeranimation, audio, communicationdesign, film) and should not be relied on for the master. The master info sheet is the governing document.
audition: CONFIRMED: no performance audition. The procedure has exactly two mandatory phases — online application with document upload, then "Personal interview or, if travel to Salzburg is not possible, via video conference via MS Teams". The interview lasts about 15 minutes, is conducted by the department head and departmental lecturers, and covers motivation, previous projects and professional experience, plus any master-project ideas; you may show further creative work (audio snippets, music streaming, screenshots). Invitations go out about two weeks after the application deadline, interviews about one week later. Failure to attend the interview means exclusion.
deadline: CONFIRMED for the prior cycle on the official Dates & Deadlines page: applications opened 30 October 2025; the standard deadline has passed and a limited number of places remained open until 15 August 2026; and — the one that actually binds him — the FINAL deadline of 1 APRIL 2026 for applicants holding neither EU/EEA/Swiss citizenship nor an entrance qualification or degree from those countries. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date; expect roughly a late-October 2026 opening with an ~1 April 2027 non-EU cut-off. He must plan around the April cut-off, not the summer one.
opens: 30 October 2025 for the WS 2026/27 intake — PRIOR CYCLE
duration: CONFIRMED 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS, full-time
study: You choose ONE of four departments — Audio, Film, Communication Design or Producing — and build advanced skills in conceiving, designing, implementing and managing cross-media creative projects. The Audio department covers music production and recording, composition, sound synthesis and sound design, mix and mastering, interactive audio, soundtracks and audio post-production, and sound and performance, with cross-department collaboration on film soundtracks, game audio and multimedia installations.
recommendation: The strongest English-taught, low-fee, studio-equipped music-production and sound-design master in this batch, and the admission mechanics are humane: three works in a PDF inside a ZIP, plus a 15-minute interview that FH Salzburg explicitly allows over MS Teams if travel to Salzburg is impossible. The obstacle is arithmetic, not artistic — the 35 ECTS of creative-artistic design practice, which a pure software-engineering curriculum will not contain. Concrete action: email office.ct@fh-salzburg.ac.at (department office, +43 50-2211-6030) or studienberatung@fh-salzburg.ac.at with his transcript now, and if short, spend 2026/27 accumulating creditable audio/media coursework. Producing is the documented fallback because it is the only department exempt from full ECTS proof — but it is management, not craft, so it does not serve his goal. Rated B rather than A purely because of the ECTS gate plus the early 1 April non-EU deadline.

tuition: €726.72 per semester tuition for third-country nationals (Tunisia = third country), i.e. roughly €1,453 per academic year, plus the Austrian Students' Union (ÖH) fee. Waivers exist for third-country nationals legally equated to EU/EEA nationals, and KUG operates a separate tuition-rebate decree under its Eastern/South-Eastern Europe focus — Tunisia is NOT in that scheme.
scholarshipDetail: None found specific to this programme. OeAD / Austrian government scholarship schemes exist nationally but eligibility for a Tunisian applicant to this programme is UNVERIFIED.
entry: A completed Bachelor's degree. Credentials must be submitted for equivalency review: "Only after the Dean of Studies has confirmed the equivalency of your preliminary studies you will be notified for the entrance exam." Artistic work samples are a hard precondition — "if you do not submit examples of your artistic work, you will not be invited to the examination interview." No published IELTS/TOEFL threshold found on the programme page (UNVERIFIED).
acceptsNonMusic: CHECK — the page does not exclude non-music bachelors and imposes no music-degree requirement; entry hinges on the Dean of Studies' equivalency decision plus the artistic portfolio. But nothing on the page positively states a non-music degree is accepted, so this must be confirmed in writing with the IEM office before investing in an application. Practically, the two 5-minute works carry the weight, not the diploma subject.
portfolio: "Two examples of your artistic work, each with a duration of approximately 5 minutes", uploaded before the deadline at go.iem.at/cmkk as a single document or zip named surname_firstname. All multichannel work must be reduced to stereo. Audio/video compressed (mp3, h264 or similar). Total size no more than approximately 150 MB.
audition: No on-site audition. One oral examination interview via Zoom (German or English) based on the submitted work samples, held in June. Invitation is conditional on (a) portfolio submitted and (b) Dean of Studies confirming degree equivalency.
deadline: Registration 1 March – 1 May; examination interview in June. The page displays the June date as "June xx, 2027" — treat the 1 March – 1 May window as the published pattern and PRIOR CYCLE / PROVISIONAL - confirm the exact 2027 dates when KUG publishes them (expect late 2026).
duration: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS
study: Four named focus areas: computer music composition; performance and interpretation of electronic works; development of new electronic instruments; music informatics. Master level adds "methods of artistic-scientific research" on top of those skills. IEM is the Austrian centre for Ambisonics and spatial audio research (the CUBE multichannel hall and Ambisonics loudspeaker arrays are IEM's signature facilities — detailed studio/software inventory UNVERIFIED on the official programme page).
recommendation: One of the cheapest serious European routes into computer music: ~€1.45k/year all-in tuition and no on-site audition. The catch is that the entry gate is two finished ~5-minute artistic works plus a Dean-of-Studies equivalency ruling on a software-engineering BSc — so he needs roughly a year of deliberate portfolio-building before the March 2027 window. Aesthetically it is art-music / spatial-audio / instrument-building, not club or dance production; it would give him extraordinary sound-design and Max/DSP depth but will not by itself teach him to finish a release-ready track.

institution: Universität für künstlerische und industrielle Gestaltung Linz (Kunstuniversität Linz / University of Arts Li…
programme: Interface Cultures — Master Programme (MA)
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's; portfolio required, so build it
qualification: Master of Arts (MA), 4 semesters. A genuine second-cycle degree, not a Lehrgang or certificate.
accreditation: CONFIRMED. Real, state-recognised second-cycle degree. Ordentliches Masterstudium under UG 2002 at a federal public university, awarding a Master of Arts. The university's own 'Information for international applicants' PDF describes the exact §64 NAG route: visa to attend the admission exam, return home, then apply for the Aufenthaltsbewilligung – Studierende on the strength of a confirmation of passing the exam issued by studien.office@kunstuni-linz.at.
tuition: EUR 726.72 PER SEMESTER — CONFIRMED on the university's own tuition-fee page ('Euro 726.72 per semester' for international students) and repeated verbatim on the sibling Postdigital Lutherie admission page ('non-EU-citizens currently have to pay a fee of 726,72 € per semester'). This is the rate he pays as a Tunisian national. EUR 1,453.44 per year; EUR 2,906.88 for the whole 4-semester degree. Among the cheapest real master's degrees in Western Europe. Payment must be complete within the admission period — partial payment is not accepted and non-payment means no admission or de-matriculation.
otherFees: CORRECTION — ÖH student union fee (incl. liability insurance) is EUR 26.20 PER SEMESTER for winter semester 2026/27, not the EUR 24.70 previously recorded. The figure is indexed annually; confirm at enrolment. ADDITION the previous record missed entirely: Austrian student self-insurance (health) runs about EUR 65 per month for students not covered by a parent's policy — roughly EUR 780/year, EUR 1,560 over the degree. This is a bigger line than tuition and it is compulsory in practice for a residence permit.
totalCost: Institutional cost over 2 years: tuition EUR 2,906.88 + ÖH EUR 104.80 = EUR 3,011.68. Add health insurance ~EUR 1,560. Realistic institutional + insurance total ~EUR 4,570 for the whole degree. Living costs in Linz are the dominant expense and are not published by the university. For the residence permit he must additionally prove sufficient means to the Magistrat der Stadt Linz or BH Linz-Land (annual ASVG-linked figure — confirm with the Austrian embassy in Tunis / OeAD).
scholarshipDetail: CORRECTION — the previous record said 'none'. There is one real, winnable instrument: the ÖH Kunstuniversität Linz TUITION FEE GRANT (Zuschuss zum Studienbeitrag), administered by the student union's University Representation. It is a pot of just under EUR 15,000 per semester distributed by a jury (chair of the University Representation, economic advisor, social department advisor) as a REFUND of tuition already paid. It is explicitly open to 'regular degree students (Austrian or foreign nationals)' — so a Tunisian master's student qualifies. Announced each semester via calls.kunstuni-linz.at (e.g. 'Tuition Fee Grant SS24'); contact oeh.sozial@kunstuni-linz.at. It will not fund living costs, but it can plausibly zero out the EUR 726.72. SEPARATELY: the university's own 'scholarships' page is entirely OUTGOING mobility funding for Austrians going abroad — nothing there applies to an incoming Tunisian, and the tuition-fee page states the university 'generally does not offer any scholarships'. External route remains OeAD/grants.at; the Ernst Mach Grant is oriented to short research stays, not full masters — still UNVERIFIED as a full-degree route.
entry: 'To study at Interface Cultures you need a valid bachelor (or equivalent) degree.' The official dates PDF states the enrolment prerequisite for all master's programmes as: 'Master's Degree: a Bachelor's degree or another equivalent certificate' — no subject restriction whatsoever. Plus the departmental entrance exam (portfolio submission + interview). Foreign degrees may need legalisation (see the university's 'Legalization of Foreign Documents in Higher Education' PDF) — a Tunisian BSc will need this, and it takes weeks, so start early. No music degree, no conservatory training, no art degree required.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — explicitly and without qualification. The official requirement is 'a valid bachelor (or equivalent) degree' / 'a Bachelor's degree or another equivalent certificate'. No subject restriction, no music degree, no art degree, no conservatory training, no audition. A BSc Software Engineering with a strong interactive/sound portfolio is a coherent and even attractive application here.
portfolio: Digital portfolio of own works + letter of motivation + CV + copy of degree, uploaded during online registration at calls.kunstuni-linz.at. The official dates PDF: 'The portfolio must be submitted in digital form. You can find further information on work samples, written examinations and interviews listed by study programme on our homepage and when you are signing up for the exam.' Exact file/format limits are published only inside the live call — UNVERIFIED until a call opens; ask interfacecultures@kunstuni-linz.at.
audition: No musical audition. A departmental entrance exam consisting of portfolio review and an admission interview (English), held in the department. The sibling programmes run ~30-minute interviews including a 10-minute presentation of selected work samples; international applicants may request Webex participation instead of travelling. CONFIRM Webex availability for Interface Cultures in writing — it removes the visa-to-attend-the-exam problem entirely and is worth more to him than any other single concession.
deadline: MAJOR CORRECTION — the previous record said 'spring deadline only, UNVERIFIED'. Both rounds are now verified from the official PDF. SUMMER ROUND: online registration + portfolio 18 March – 09 June 2026, entrance exam 30 June – 01 July 2026. AUTUMN ROUND: online registration + portfolio 01 – 25 August 2026, entrance exam 15 September 2026. Both feed academic year 2026/27. PLANNING CONSEQUENCE FOR HIM: for a September 2027 start his two shots are approximately 18 March – 09 June 2027 (exam late June/early July) and 01 – 25 August 2027 (exam mid-September). Neither falls in the October–February window he has assumed — but the August round is a genuine second chance in the same cycle, which almost no directory records. Also worth stating plainly: the autumn 2026 round (registration 01–25 August 2026, exam 15 September 2026) is OPEN AS OF TODAY, 7 August 2026. He has no portfolio, so this is not actionable — but it proves the pattern and he should watch that same page in August 2027.
opens: MAJOR CORRECTION — there are TWO opening dates per year, not one. Per the official 'Dates entrance examination 2026' PDF (document dated 15.07.2026): summer round opens 18 March; autumn round opens 01 August. For a September 2027 start expect roughly 18 March 2027 and 01 August 2027.
duration: 4 semesters. Exact ECTS still not published on any Interface Cultures page — UNVERIFIED (Austrian norm for a 4-semester master is 120). Ask interfacecultures@kunstuni-linz.at.
languageReq: MAJOR CORRECTION — NO IELTS/TOEFL IS REQUIRED, AT ANY STAGE. Two official statements settle this. (1) The 'Dates entrance examination 2026' PDF: 'Language certificates for international applicants are not required for the entrance exam.' (2) The 'Proof of Language Skills' PDF: for Interface Cultures (and Postdigital Lutherie) 'the admission boards confirm the required language skills (English) as part of the entrance exam' — i.e. the panel judges his English in the interview and no certificate is filed. Contrast this with every other Kunstuni Linz master, all of which are listed in that PDF as needing a German B1 or English B2 CERTIFICATE. Interface Cultures is a named exception. The previous record marked this UNVERIFIED; it is now verified and it is the single strongest thing about this programme for him, because he has not sat IELTS or TOEFL.
study: Teaching on interactive art and interface technologies; research on cultural aspects of interface and interaction design; focus on critical data and sustainable IT; support in conceptual and practical prototype development. Qualification profile: methodological, conceptual and technological competencies plus supported development of independent artistic projects between physical and virtual worlds (object, performance, immersive setting). Strong Ars Electronica link — the 2026 festival runs 9–13 September in Linz.
recommendation: THE BEST-FITTING AND MOST ATTAINABLE PROGRAMME IN THIS SET — and it is stronger than the previous record concluded, because the language question is now settled in his favour. Confirmed advantages: English-taught with the language judged at interview and NO certificate ever required (he never has to sit IELTS or TOEFL for this one); EUR 726.72/semester with a real ÖH fee-refund fund on top; any bachelor accepted; no audition; a portfolio gate a software engineer can genuinely build in a year; sound art named by the department itself; the Ars Electronica connection. Confirmed limits: it is media art, not music production — it will not train him as a DJ or a record producer, and there is no published pro studio or spatial-audio rig. THREE CORRECTIONS TO HIS PLANNING. (1) There are TWO application rounds a year (≈18 Mar–09 Jun and 01–25 Aug), not one, and neither is in his assumed Oct–Feb window. (2) No English certificate is needed — he can stop worrying about IELTS for this application. (3) Start the Tunisian degree legalisation now; it is slower than the portfolio. ACTIONS: email interfacecultures@kunstuni-linz.at and ask (a) for the exact portfolio spec, (b) whether the admission interview can be held via Webex — this would save him an entire embassy visa run for the exam, and (c) the ECTS figure. ALSO FLAG, because it may be the better programme: the same university runs POSTDIGITAL LUTHERIE (MA) in the Tangible Interaction Design department (Prof. Martin Kaltenbrunner, tamlab). Its official admission page states: 'you need a valid bachelor (or equivalent) degree'; 'German skills are not required to join the programme. Our faculty can support German, English and Spanish speaking students'; same EUR 726.72/semester; same two rounds (18 Mar–19 Jun and 01 Aug–01 Sep in 2026). Postdigital lutherie is the design and building of new digital musical instruments — measurably closer to his stated goal than media art is. He should apply to BOTH in the same cycle; the marginal cost is one extra portfolio submission.

institution: Universität für künstlerische und industrielle Gestaltung Linz (Kunstuniversität Linz / University of Arts Li…
programme: Zeitbasierte Medien / Timebased Media — Master Programme (MA)
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's; portfolio required, so build it
qualification: Master of Arts (MA), 4 semesters. A genuine second-cycle degree.
accreditation: CONFIRMED. Ordentliches Masterstudium under UG 2002 awarding a Master of Arts. Supports the §64 NAG student residence permit via the procedure published in the university's 'Information for international applicants' PDF.
tuition: EUR 726.72 PER SEMESTER — CONFIRMED on the university's tuition-fee page. EUR 1,453.44/year; EUR 2,906.88 for the full degree. Payment in full within the admission period; partial payment not accepted.
otherFees: CORRECTION — ÖH fee incl. insurance is EUR 26.20 per semester for WS 2026/27, not EUR 24.70. Indexed annually. ADDITION: Austrian student health self-insurance ~EUR 65/month (~EUR 1,560 over the degree) for students not covered by a parent's policy.
totalCost: Institutional: EUR 2,906.88 tuition + EUR 104.80 ÖH = EUR 3,011.68 over 2 years. Plus ~EUR 1,560 health insurance. Plus IELTS/TOEFL exam cost (needed here, unlike Interface Cultures). Plus living costs in Linz and the means-of-subsistence proof for the residence permit.
scholarshipDetail: CORRECTION — same as Interface Cultures: the ÖH Kunstuniversität Linz tuition-fee grant fund (~EUR 15,000/semester pot, refunds tuition already paid, explicitly open to foreign nationals) is a real partial route. Apply via calls.kunstuni-linz.at each semester; contact oeh.sozial@kunstuni-linz.at. No programme-level scholarship; the university's published 'scholarships' page is outgoing-mobility funding for Austrians only and is irrelevant to him. External: OeAD/grants.at, UNVERIFIED for a full master's.
entry: 'A completed bachelor degree programme in a study area with interdisciplinary focuses' — the page names time-based/interactive media, media design, film, video, sound, or comparable credentials from accredited institutions. Plus the departmental entrance exam. RISK UNCHANGED AND CONFIRMED: unlike Interface Cultures this programme names related disciplines rather than accepting any bachelor. A Software Engineering BSc rides on the 'comparable' clause and on the portfolio. Get it confirmed in writing before investing. Note also that the central dates PDF states the generic master's prerequisite as simply 'a Bachelor's degree or another equivalent certificate' — so the departmental wording is the binding constraint, not the university's.
acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY — CONFIRMED UNCHANGED. No music degree is needed anywhere, but the named prior fields are media/film/video/sound rather than 'any bachelor'. A CS/software background must be carried by the 'comparable' clause plus the portfolio. Ask the department in writing before applying.
portfolio: Four-step procedure, all published officially: (1) online registration through the university portal; (2) upload of portfolio AND a short letter of motivation explaining personal goals and fit; (3) admission interview with the Selection Committee, approx. 30 minutes, requiring a ten-minute presentation of selected work samples; (4) result by email and PIN. The committee assesses aptitude and how the work aligns with the programme's academic profile. Exact format/size limits not published — UNVERIFIED.
audition: No musical audition. A 30-minute selection interview with a 10-minute presentation of work samples. IMPORTANT AND CONFIRMED: 'Interviews occur in-person but international applicants may request Webex participation by notifying gerlinde.schmierer@kunstuni-linz.at.' This removes the need for a separate Austrian visa merely to attend the exam — a concrete, decisive advantage over every Swiss option in this set. Request it in writing at registration.
deadline: MAJOR CORRECTION — the previous record recorded only the spring round and concluded the deadline falls outside his planning window. That is wrong. The official 'Dates entrance examination 2026' PDF (dated 15.07.2026) lists TWO rounds for Timebased Media (MA): WINTER ROUND — online registration and portfolio 15 December 2025 – 18 January 2026, exam 04 February 2026. SUMMER ROUND — online registration and portfolio 18 March – 07 June 2026, exam 30 June – 01 July 2026. There is NO autumn round for this programme (unlike Interface Cultures). PLANNING CONSEQUENCE: the winter round — roughly mid-December 2026 to mid-January 2027, exam early February 2027 — falls squarely INSIDE his October 2026–February 2027 window. This is one of only two programmes in this set that does. He can apply in the winter round and, if unsuccessful, apply again in the summer round of the same cycle.
opens: CORRECTED — two openings per year: mid-December and mid-March. For 2026/27 the official dates PDF gives 15 December 2025 (winter round) and 18 March 2026 (summer round). Expect roughly mid-December 2026 and mid-March 2027 for a September 2027 start.
duration: 4 semesters. ECTS not published — UNVERIFIED (Austrian norm 120). Ask gerlinde.schmierer@kunstuni-linz.at.
languageReq: CORRECTED AND NOW PRECISE — and it is materially worse for him than for Interface Cultures. The official 'Proof of Language Skills' PDF places Timebased Media (MA) in the group requiring 'a German language certificate at level B1 OR an English language certificate at level B2'. Critically: 'The ENGLISH language certificate needs to be submitted AT THE TIME OF ENROLMENT. Otherwise, students need to provide a German language certificate before they can receive the enrolment confirmation for their third semester.' So: no certificate is needed for the entrance exam itself (the dates PDF confirms 'language certificates for international applicants are not required for the entrance exam'), but he MUST hand over an English B2 certificate — i.e. an IELTS/TOEFL or equivalent — when he enrols, or else reach certified German B1 within a year. He has taken neither test. Unlike Interface Cultures, this programme gives him no exemption. Budget for IELTS.
study: Interdisciplinary work across time-based media — audiovisual culture, moving image, sound, installation, interactive systems and creative coding; professional handling of works and products of audiovisual culture.
recommendation: APPLY TO IT ALONGSIDE INTERFACE CULTURES — and the case is now stronger than the previous record allowed, for one reason it got wrong. There is a WINTER round (registration ≈15 December – 18 January, exam early February) as well as the spring round, so this is one of only two programmes in this set whose deadline lands inside his October–February planning window. Advantages: sound is an explicitly named subject; German is never required at entry; the fee is the same EUR 726.72/semester; no audition; the interview can be taken by Webex from Tunis. Disadvantages against Interface Cultures: the bachelor-field requirement is narrower and he must argue 'comparable'; teaching is bilingual rather than English-only; and he WOULD need an English B2 certificate (IELTS/TOEFL) at enrolment, which Interface Cultures waives entirely. No facilities inventory is published — a serious unknown for someone whose goal is production. ACTIONS, all free and all decision-changing: write to gerlinde.schmierer@kunstuni-linz.at asking (a) does a BSc Software Engineering count as 'comparable' for admission, (b) what audio facilities does the department actually have, (c) confirm Webex interview availability, and (d) which English certificates satisfy the B2 requirement. Then sit IELTS in good time — for this programme, unlike Interface Cultures, he cannot avoid it.

whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's; portfolio required, so build it
scholarship: OeAD Ernst Mach Grant; Kunstuniversität Linz Leistungsstipendium
verdictWhy: Fully English-taught with declared French-speaking faculty support, no German, no audition, a bachelor in any subject accepted, and a Tunisian pays €726.72/semester — genuinely at the edge of 'can pay a little'. The whole gate is a portfolio plus an interview, which is exactly what he can build in the fourteen months he has. Confirm whether the interview can be held online before booking travel.

Input cost 'Under EUR 1.5k/yr' is right but only just — €1,453.44/yr plus ÖH fees.
qualification: Master of Arts (MA) — Masterstudium

institution: ARTS² – École supérieure des Arts / Conservatoire royal de Mons
programme: Master en Musique – Composition acousmatique (section de musique électroacoustique)
whyChance: Names engineering or computing as a welcome background
verdictWhy: This is the best-funded French-language option he has — WBI 'MASTER IN' pays up to EUR 10,020/yr including tuition, travel and health insurance, and his French is fluent — but it is a royal conservatoire with a compulsory entrance examination whose content ARTS² only publishes in PDFs I could not open, in a section whose core courses are solfège de l'objet sonore and perceptual analysis. Before he spends a day on this he must email admission@artsaucarre.be for the 'CONTENUS DES ÉPREUVES D'ADMISSION' for composition acousmatique. If that document contains aural or solfège testing, this becomes an AVOID; if it is a works-presentation and interview, it becomes his strongest francophone target.
correction: TWO CORRECTIONS. (1) COST: 'Under EUR 1.5k/yr' is WRONG. A Tunisian pays the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles additional contribution of EUR 4,175 per year plus the ordinary minerval — roughly EUR 4,400-4,500/yr unless he wins the WBI grant, which waives it. (2) GATE: the input says 'None found in the text'. There IS a compulsory épreuve d'admission — ARTS² states unfunded candidates 'must register for and take the entrance examinations', and musicians must submit 15-20 minutes of video recordings.
qualification: Master en Musique (2nd cycle); the music domain also offers a Master à finalité spécialisée and a Master en Enseignement
tuition: €1,194 + €4,175 non-EU supplementary contribution = c. €5,369/year for 2026-2027 (indicative, pending parliamentary adoption). The supplement is waived only for UN LDC nationals, Wallonia-Brussels Federation secondary-diploma holders, or WBI scholarship holders; Tunisia does not qualify as an LDC, so the WBI route is the only waiver available to him.
scholarshipDetail: MASTER IN – WBI Grant. Now confirmed as applicable: ARTS² is an official host institution and 'All programmes available at ARTS²' are eligible, which covers this section; Tunisia is an explicit priority country. Holding it also waives the €4,175 supplement.
entry: Admission exam required: 'il est nécessaire de passer l'examen d'admission.' Plus the standard ARTS² non-first-year dossier via artsaucarre.horizon.wbe.be — passport, photo, secondary diploma, evidence of prior artistic training, records of previous non-artistic higher education with justification, five-year activity documentation, and a debt-clearance letter if previously enrolled in Wallonia-Brussels. Language: French.
acceptsNonMusic: UNVERIFIED — no published statement. Decided by the admission jury. As with the sister section, the dossier form's explicit request for records of previous non-artistic higher education shows such candidates are contemplated. For the WBI grant, ARTS² requires the bachelor to be 'relevant and directly related to the Master's programme applied for', which is a harder argument to make for acousmatic composition than for interactive music.
portfolio: UNVERIFIED — section-specific exam requirements are not published; request from info@artsaucarre.be. For an acousmatic composition section, submitted fixed-media works would normally be central, but no number, duration or format is published anywhere reachable.
audition: LIVE admission exam in Mons. ARTS² institution-wide schedule confirmed: 'Des épreuves d'admission sont organisées chaque année en mai et en septembre.' Content for the acousmatic section specifically: UNVERIFIED.
deadline: Admission-exam sessions recur every May and September, so the May/September 2027 sessions apply for a September 2027 start. Tuition payment milestones for 2026-27: €50 deposit by 15 September 2026, balance plus non-EU supplement by 15 January 2027 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm equivalent 2027-28 dates. MASTER IN – WBI grant deadline was 31 March 2026 for the 2026-2027 intake — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date, expect c. 31 March 2027.
opens: Online registration at artsaucarre.horizon.wbe.be before the admission exam. MASTER IN – WBI grant applications go separately to service.erasmus@artsaucarre.be on a much earlier timetable.
duration: Confirmed as 'une formation de composition acousmatique entièrement spécifique, en cinq ans (bachelier + master)' — five years bachelor plus master. Master ECTS: UNVERIFIED; grids are published only as PDFs on the music domain presentation page.
study: Now substantially better documented than before. Courses cover 'tant les aspects esthétiques et culturels des musiques électroacoustiques que les questions techniques'. Artistic courses, quoted: 'techniques d'écriture, composition sur support, solfège de l'objet sonore, spatialisation, analyse perceptive'. These run alongside a set of technical courses, quoted: 'techniques de prise de son, techniques de synthèse, informatique musicale' — i.e. recording technique, synthesis technique and music computing, all directly transferable to production work. The section is 'la seule école supérieure de Belgique où est organisé un tel enseignement' and holds an international reputation, having taken students from the USA, Japan and across Europe. Studio and loudspeaker-orchestra inventory: still UNVERIFIED (electroacoustique.be returned HTTP 500 again on re-check).
recommendation: Better documented than before, and cheaper to fund than previously thought, but the strategic verdict is unchanged. The technical course spine — techniques de prise de son, techniques de synthèse, informatique musicale, spatialisation — is genuinely transferable craft, and his software background would be an asset in informatique musicale. Cost is c. €5,369/yr, or c. €1,194 plus a €10,020 living grant if the WBI grant lands, and there is no English-test barrier. But acousmatic music on fixed media is art music for concert diffusion, not club music: this would give him a serious sonic-craft education while pointing away from DJing and commercial production. Also, the WBI requirement that the bachelor be 'directly related' to the master is harder to argue here than for the interactive-music section. Choose the Mons Musiques appliquées section over this one unless he genuinely wants to compose art music.

entry: Admission is subject to an épreuve d'admission. First complete the online registration form at artsaucarre.horizon.wbe.be, supplying diplomas, CV, experience, artistic background and transcripts of prior higher education; each domain then reviews submissions and schedules candidates for exams. Full enrolment requires submitting administrative documents, paying tuition and signing the PAE (annual study plan).

Ask the section at info@artsaucarre.be.
portfolio: UNVERIFIED — each domain and option sets its own exam requirements and the Musiques appliquées page publishes none. Must be requested from the section (info@artsaucarre.be). Registration for the exam is via the online form; candidates are then scheduled by the domain. Exam content for this section: UNVERIFIED. Belgian French-Community music masters are normally 60 or 120 ECTS.
study: Confirmed and sharpened. Quoted: 'Le programme de Bachelier et de Master s'adresse aux musicien·ne·s désireux de développer une approche créative' — so a Master exists. The curriculum 'combine l'apprentissage des fondamentaux (écriture, orchestration, production sonore) et la réalisation de projets concrets', i.e. writing, orchestration and SOUND PRODUCTION alongside concrete project work, with collaborations, masterclasses, festival visits and individualised guidance on a final artistic project. ARTS² presents the section as unique in Belgium, focused on composition for image, performing arts and new technologies. Graduates work as composers for cinema, theatre, video games, advertising and interactive media, in sound design and sound creation, or in music education. Detailed course list and studio inventory: still UNVERIFIED (PDF grids not parsed).
recommendation: Upgraded to the top tier on verification, alongside KASK, and for a different reason: the money. Three things now line up. It is taught in FRENCH, which he speaks fluently, so no IELTS/TOEFL is on the critical path at all — a cleaner advantage than KASK's, where Master Mind reintroduces an English test. Base cost is c. €5,369/yr, half the Dutch conservatoires. And ARTS² is a confirmed host for the MASTER IN – WBI grant, for which Tunisia is an explicit priority country, worth €10,020/yr plus insurance plus a waiver of the €4,175 supplement — a near-full package. The content is genuinely applied: écriture, orchestration and production sonore, composing and sound design for film, games, theatre, advertising and interactive media. Two caveats remain honest. Everything about the admission exam and portfolio is unpublished and must be extracted by email. And the WBI condition that the bachelor be 'relevant and directly related' to the master is a real risk for a software-engineering graduate — he should build the argument that software engineering is directly relevant to INTERACTIVE music and game audio, which for this specific section is a defensible case. Act early: the WBI deadline (c. 31 March) falls before the May admission exam.
