entry: Confirmed verbatim, and it is the most degree-agnostic wording in this whole slice: 'La plupart des masters 60 ou 120 organisés à l'IAD sont ouverts aux étudiants titulaires d'un bachelier' — most 60- or 120-credit masters at IAD are open to holders of a bachelor's degree. The only stated exception is the teaching master (Section 5), which requires an existing master. Application is by email to admissions-masters@iad-arts.be with: identity photo, CV, motivation letter, secondary-education diploma, the relevant degree, ID copy, birth certificate, prior academic records, and the portfolio. Candidates selected on file and works are then auditioned by a jury.
acceptsNonMusic: Yes on paper — the strongest published position in this slice. IAD's wording is degree-agnostic ('La plupart des masters 60 ou 120 organisés à l'IAD sont ouverts aux étudiants titulaires d'un bachelier') and imposes no requirement for a music, sound or arts bachelor. The real gate is the portfolio, which must prove technical and artistic ability in the chosen orientation, and the assumed technical baseline is that of IAD's own 180-ECTS sound bachelor.
portfolio: Confirmed verbatim: 'un book de travaux aboutis qui prouvent vos aptitudes techniques et artistiques' — a portfolio of COMPLETED works proving technical and artistic aptitude, specific to the chosen orientation. Submitted alongside identity photo, CV, motivation letter, diplomas, ID and birth certificate. Number of works, durations and formats: UNVERIFIED — not published.
audition: Two-stage with a mandatory IN-PERSON jury at Louvain-la-Neuve. Candidates are first selected on the basis of their file and works; those shortlisted are then auditioned by a jury. For the 2026-2027 intake the admission commissions ran in person from 24 August to 11 September 2026, with dates communicated individually by email. Requires travel to Belgium at the very end of the summer.
deadline: Applications 4 May – 14 August 2026; in-person admission juries 24 August – 11 September 2026 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. For a September 2027 start expect roughly 4 May – 14 August 2027 with juries late August to mid-September 2027. Non-EU supplementary contribution must be paid by 31 January.
opens: 4 May for the 2026-2027 intake (applications by email to admissions-masters@iad-arts.be). Application deposit for first-year masters is free.
duration: 60 crédits each — confirmed verbatim on the IAD sound faculty page — following a 180-ECTS professional bachelor in sound. A 3+1 structure.
study: IAD's sound training covers the full sound-engineer profession: studio and live recording, mixing, editing, mastering, event sound reinforcement (sonorisation) and sound design, training 'sound engineers who master sound recording tools and techniques in radio, television and multimedia, as well as editors and sound mixers who master editing and sound mixing tools'. The master combines artistic and technical coursework with workshops, an in-depth internship more advanced than at bachelor level, a final work evaluated by a jury of industry professionals, and a written thesis. Students collaborate with IAD's multimedia, theatre and directing programmes on real productions. The three orientations split the field: Son Studio is closest to music recording and mixing, Son Sono covers live sound, Cinéma Son covers film sound.
recommendation: Confirmed as a serious, very practical French-language route into professional audio, with the most welcoming admission wording anywhere in this slice — most IAD masters are open to any bachelor's holder, so his software-engineering BSc is not automatically disqualifying, and Son Studio is the orientation closest to music recording and mixing. Cost is now confirmed at a modest c. €5,369/yr and there is no English-test barrier. But verification made the funding picture worse rather than better: IAD is absent from the MASTER IN – WBI host-institution list, so the €10,020 grant that makes ARTS² so attractive simply cannot be used here, and no IAD-internal scholarship exists. That makes IAD a self-pay option. Add the in-person jury in Louvain-la-Neuve in late August/early September and a 60-credit master built on top of IAD's own three-year sound bachelor — meaning the assumed technical baseline is high and his portfolio must genuinely prove it — and this ranks below both ARTS² Musiques appliquées and KASK for him. Strong programme, weak funding fit.

The English-language track and the absence of an IELTS requirement are the only attractive parts, and they do not outweigh a six-figure-adjacent cost gap and an extra year of study he has not budgeted for.
correction: TWO MAJOR CORRECTIONS. (1) COST: 'Under EUR 1.5k/yr' is WRONG BY A FACTOR OF SIX. A non-EEA student pays EUR 8,800.20 for a 60-credit year (EUR 916.20 fixed + EUR 131.40 per credit), plus study-cost contributions. The EUR 1,181.40 figure circulating is the EEA rate. qualification: Master of Music (2nd cycle, Master in de muziek)
tuition: VERIFIED on the KASK financial page for 2026-2027: non-EEA increased tuition = fixed administrative amount €916.20 + €131.40 per credit, giving €8,800.20 for a standard 60-credit year. Advanced master and postgraduate programmes cost more; the master in music production is charged at the standard rate above.
scholarshipDetail: (1) KASK & Conservatorium's own non-EEA scholarship system for drama, visual arts, audiovisual arts and music — the institution 'will implement a scholarship system for non-EEA students' with awards that 'equal the amount of the increased tuition for non EEA-students', and 'Scholarships can be awarded to students in a bridging program, preparation program and master program'. (2) Government of Flanders Master Mind Scholarship — HOGENT is a participating institution, and 'All nationalities, except for Russian, can apply', so Tunisia is eligible.
entry: Degree route, quoted: 'a bachelor in performing music (for the master in classical music or jazz/pop), or a bachelor in composing music (for the master in music production, composition or music theory).' Language, quoted: 'You can study all our master's programs in Dutch or English. There are no formal level requirements for English in the master programs, but the Vantage B2 level is strongly recommended' — NO IELTS/TOEFL required for admission. IMPORTANT CAVEAT DISCOVERED ON VERIFICATION: this only removes the test from the ADMISSION path. The Master Mind scholarship separately requires, for Schools of Arts, IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL 90 / B2 certification AND a GPA of 3.5 out of 4.0 — so if he wants Master Mind money he must test after all.
acceptsNonMusic: Check — bridging is the realistic route. Two published statements apply. On other artistic disciplines: holders of 'an academic bachelor's degree in another artistic discipline may have to take a preparatory program before they are admitted to the master's programs.' On mismatched degrees generally: 'If you wish to begin a master's program, but do not have the appropriate underlying bachelor's degree, you may, in some cases, follow a bridging program. In such cases, it is best to contact your study program supervisor.' Software engineering is neither performing nor composing music nor an artistic discipline, so a bridging (schakel) programme is the probable path, not direct master entry. Critically, funding is NOT lost by bridging: 'Scholarships can be awarded to students in a bridging program, preparation program and master program.'
portfolio: CORRECTED. The widely-quoted 'four songs' specification is the BACHELOR admission-test spec, not the master's. The bachelor test asks for four songs or compositions (three to five submitted initially plus one theme test piece), each 'composed (individually or in collaboration) and/or recorded, mixed, produced, and/or performed as a musician and/or arranged by the candidate', with 'a maximum of one non-original work, such as a cover, adaptation, or remix'. For the MASTER, what is actually published is: a digital portfolio plus a master proposal, judged by the orientation committee; 'You must upload links to an online portfolio or upload a PDF portfolio. We do not accept portfolios in physical format (usb, dvd, paper...)'; plus a motivation letter of max 1 page. Number of works for the master: UNVERIFIED — confirm with paul.lamont@hogent.be. Assessment criteria are published: creations 'in which you yourself have played an important, supporting, creative role', above-average musical talent, diversity in productions and collaborations, and originality and authenticity.
audition: Two-stage, dossier-first — the gentlest admission format in this slice. Orientation test (oriënteringsproef) organised several times per academic year; 'Based on your portfolio and master proposal, the orientation committee will decide whether or not to invite you for an intake interview or audition.' Applicants are notified of the committee's decision by email. So stage 1 requires no travel; an on-site intake interview or audition follows only if shortlisted.
deadline: Published session for music production: orientation test, August session, 24.08.26 — this is the CURRENT cycle, for September 2026 entry. For a SEPTEMBER 2027 start: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Expect sessions spread across the 2026-27 academic year plus a late-August 2027 session. Registration deadlines per session are not published on the master pages. Master Mind 2027-2028 call: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date (the 2026-2027 call launched January 2026 with institution deadlines between 1 February and 1 April 2026).
opens: Registration for each orientation-test session via HOGENT web registration, ahead of the session date.
duration: 2 years / 120 ECTS (60 per year), on top of a 3-year bachelor — 3+2 path. Confirmed on the programme page.
study: Module list confirmed exactly. Year 1 (60 ECTS): Producing & artistic research 31 ECTS; Projects master 1, 3 ECTS; Masterseminaries 8 ECTS; Thesis 1, 3 ECTS; Professional skills 3 ECTS; Minor/Specialisation/Electives 12 ECTS. Year 2 (60 ECTS): Master project Producing 33 ECTS; Projects master 2, 3 ECTS; Thesis 2, 6 ECTS; Arts in Practice 6 ECTS; Minor/Specialisation/Electives 12 ECTS. So 64 of 120 credits sit in producing and the producing capstone. Departmental philosophy: 'creativity, musicality (both performance and songwriting/composition) and technique', working in professionally equipped studios. Industry bridge via external mentors, internships and 'Arts in Practice'.
recommendation: Still the strongest overall bet in this slice, and verification strengthened rather than weakened it: 64 of 120 credits are literally producing and a producing capstone; stage-one admission is dossier-only so his portfolio does the work before any travel; the non-EEA fee of €8,800.20 is confirmed and the school's own scholarship is confirmed to be sized to erase it, including for bridging students. Two honest caveats sharpened by this check. First, the master formally expects a bachelor in composing music, so September 2027 should be planned as entry into a bridging or preparatory year, not the master itself. Second, the much-cited 'no English test' advantage is real for admission but does NOT extend to Master Mind funding, which demands IELTS 6.5 and a 3.5/4.0 GPA — so if Master Mind is the funding plan, he must sit IELTS anyway. The KASK internal scholarship, which has no published language test, is therefore the more realistic money.

However the call addresses itself to "composers", selection is by jury against an international field, and the partner routes are through conservatoire master's programmes in composition. A software-engineering graduate with no compositional track record would be a very long shot in year one, though his programming ability is exactly what the Max/OpenMusic/Modalys curriculum assumes.

duration: 1 year, 850 hours. For 2026-2027: 12 October 2026 to 30 September 2027, Monday to Friday 10:00–13:00 and 14:30–17:30, with two weeks off in December. No ECTS award — UNVERIFIED whether any credit transfer is possible for non-partner students.
study: Training aimed at "in-depth technical independence and mastery" of IRCAM-developed software used in composition: MAX, OpenMusic, Modalys, ASAP, Partiel and SPAT (spatialisation). The 850 hours comprise theory and technique classes, hands-on workshops, composition sessions, lectures by guest artists and scientists, individual follow-up meetings, rehearsals, and a FINAL CONCERT. The programme is "open to all forms of artistic practice, integrating technology into a wide range of aesthetic approaches and forms." The 2026-2027 edition, under Associate Composer Eva Reiter, emphasises technology serving musical thought, artificial-intelligence integration, and musicology.
recommendation: Include for completeness and as a MEDIUM-TERM AMBITION rather than a 2027 application. The upsides are real: taught in ENGLISH, only €2,000 for 850 hours, no formal degree requirement published, and a curriculum (Max, OpenMusic, SPAT, Modalys) that rewards a programmer more than almost any other option here. The problems are that it is NOT A DEGREE — which matters for a student visa, for recognition, and for the task's own master's-level scope — and that the jury selects from international composers with substantial portfolios. Realistic path: do a master's elsewhere first (Sonology, ZHdK, KMH), then apply to Cursus. If he does want to try for 2027-28, the deadline is around December 2026, so the portfolio decision is immediate.

Teaching is shared between the Arts plastiques and Musicologie departments — described by the university as unique in France — with contributions from many internationally recognised professionals. Max/MSP appears in module descriptions. Dedicated equipment and production spaces are provided across both years: computers, sensors, interfaces, image-capture, sound-capture and diffusion tools, plus a 'studio musical', a 'studio de prise de vue' and a 'studio de maquettage de dispositifs multimédia'. Connaissances souhaitées: 'Mathématiques, Physique : niveau minimum requis BAC + 1 scientifique' — published syllabus covers integral calculus, linear ODEs of 1st and 2nd order, complex numbers and De Moivre, log/exp/power functions, Taylor expansions, derivatives, binary arithmetic and 'Notion de programmation algorithmique'; physics covers electricity and electromagnetism (Ohm, Kirchhoff, superposition, Thévenin/Norton, capacitors, Laplace, Faraday, Lenz, impedance/admittance), mechanics, damped and forced oscillators, resonance, bandwidth, Q factor, and travelling/standing waves with interference. Also: writing ability; broad general, literary, contemporary-art (photo, plastic arts, cinema, music) and theatre culture; ability to work collectively; 'Toute expérience vécue en milieu professionnel, au sens large, est souhaitée'. Three recommended books: Daniel Deshays 'Pour une écriture du son'; Larrue & Mervant-Roux 'Le son du théâtre XIXe-XXIe siècle'; Yann Paranthoën 'Propos d'un tailleur de sons'. A candidature-review commission decides who is authorised to compete at all.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — CONFIRMED and unusually favourable. No music, audio or artistic diploma is required: only the baccalauréat plus 2 years of higher education totalling 120 ECTS in a State-recognised formation. The desired knowledge is explicitly scientific at Bac+1 level in maths and physics, and the published maths syllabus even lists 'Arithmétique binaire. Notion de programmation algorithmique.' A software-engineering BSc over-satisfies both the credit requirement and the maths/physics expectation. The genuine filters are the self-recorded 3-minute sound portrait, the theatre/contemporary-art culture expected, the DALF C1, and 6 places.

institution: Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam (ARI Education NL — franchise of Abbey Road Studios, London / Universal Music)

whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's; portfolio required, so build it
qualification: Advanced Diploma — the institute's OWN qualification. NOT a master, NOT a bachelor, NOT a degree of any kind, NOT NVAO-accredited, NOT awarded or validated by any university. The institute states plainly that 'the Advanced Diploma is not a 3 year degree programme'.
accreditation: NOT OFFICIAL — NOT NVAO-ACCREDITED. Verified on the official fees page: the programme 'is registered as short vocational education in the Netherlands' (CRKBO). CRKBO is a VAT-exemption and quality register for short vocational training — it is NOT higher-education accreditation, is NOT NVAO, and gives the diploma no legal status as a Dutch degree and no ECTS. The institution is 'niet-bekostigd' (private/unfunded) and explicitly 'not eligible for NL undergraduate student loans'. No accreditation statement of any kind appears on the course, fees or FAQ pages. In EHEA terms this diploma is unrecognised: it will not admit him to a PhD, will not transfer credit anywhere, and cannot be used for professional recognition.
tuition: NOW VERIFIED (prior record said unpublished). Full-time, one year, three payment plans: Plan A — €200 application fee + €20,160 in 12 monthly instalments of €1,680; Plan B — €200 + €19,380 in 3 term instalments of €6,460; Plan C — €200 + €18,860 paid upfront. No separate international rate is published (there is no international cohort to price, since non-EU residents cannot get a visa). The Dutch tuition tax deduction that softens the cost is only useful to someone with Dutch taxable income — not to him.
otherFees: €200 application fee — refundable if the applicant does not complete the admission process successfully. Paid by wire transfer to ARI Education NL. NO enrolment, matriculation, materials, exam, insurance or services fee is published; whether any exist is UNVERIFIED — ask for a complete schedule of charges in writing.
totalCost: €19,060–€20,360 for the year (tuition + €200 application fee), plus Amsterdam living costs of roughly €14,000–€18,000, plus flights and insurance. REALISTIC FIRST-YEAR OUTLAY IF ATTENDANCE WERE POSSIBLE: €33,000–€39,000 — for a diploma with no accreditation, no ECTS and no degree status.

Required: a music portfolio of 4–8 productions; 'Any academic qualifications to give us an idea about your academic background'; music qualifications OR a statement of 'your level of music knowledge and experience in your motivation letter' if formal credentials are lacking; a motivation letter; a CV/résumé; demonstrated competence in English; a copy of a photographic passport; and a €200 application fee. REGARDLESS OF WHETHER HE APPLIES HERE, THIS IS THE PORTFOLIO SPEC HE SHOULD BUILD TO: 4–8 finished tracks, each documenting a distinct role, satisfies or exceeds what almost every accredited European master will ask of him. Start now — it is roughly a 12-month build from zero.

duration: 12 months full-time, 48 weeks of tuition. NO ECTS — not credit-bearing. Verified timetable: scheduled classes Mon–Thu 10:00–14:00; workshops Fridays; flexible practical studio access Mon–Sat; total expected workload 40 hrs/week including 20 hrs self-study.
englishTest: 'Demonstrated competence in English (for non-English speaking countries)'. NO IELTS band and no formal test score is published, and no test is named. It is plausible that a motivation letter plus an interview satisfies this — which would save him the IELTS fee and several weeks. UNVERIFIED; worth asking directly, and the answer is useful intelligence regardless of whether he applies here.
study: Verified at topic level: production, engineering, mixing, mastering and music business fundamentals, using 'industry-standard tools for creating, performing, recording, editing, mixing and mastering music', drawing on 'over 85 years of experience at Abbey Road Studios'. Guest lectures from award-winning industry professionals. A named, week-by-week module list is NOT published — UNVERIFIED; demand the full syllabus in writing before committing.
recommendation: OUTSTANDING SCHOOL, WRONG COUNTRY, AND NOT A MASTER — DO NOT APPLY. On pure craft this is the best hands-on music production and sound engineering training in this entire Dutch slice: real studios six days a week, Abbey Road pedigree, industry teaching, a serious portfolio-selected cohort. Three things kill it for him, and the first is fatal on its own. (1) IT CANNOT GET HIM A DUTCH RESIDENCE PERMIT — stated in writing by the institute, and the workarounds it suggests are open to Working Holiday and US DAFT nationals, not Tunisians. (2) It is NOT a master or any accredited degree — no NVAO, no ECTS, no PhD route, no credit transfer. (3) At €18,860–€20,160 tuition plus roughly €16,000 living costs it is among the most expensive options here for the least formal recognition — €33,000–€39,000 for an unaccredited diploma. He also does not currently hold the mandatory 4–8 track portfolio. MY ADVICE: rule Amsterdam out now and spend no application fee on it. If the Abbey Road brand genuinely appeals, look at Abbey Road Institute campuses in countries where a private school CAN sponsor a student visa — but go in understanding he would be buying training, not a qualification, and check that campus's accreditation separately, since it does not transfer across the franchise. THE ONE THING TO TAKE FROM THIS ENTRY REGARDLESS: adopt its portfolio spec — 4–8 finished tracks, each demonstrating a different role (performer, producer, engineer, writer), with his role documented per track — as his personal build target for September 2027 applications anywhere.

institution: Universitatea Babeș-Bolyai din Cluj-Napoca (UBB), Facultatea de Teatru și Film — Departamentul de Cinematogra…
programme: Digital Interactive Arts (Arte digitale interactive), MA
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's; portfolio required, so build it
qualification: Diplomă de master — genuine state-recognised second-cycle degree (ciclul II), accredited under the Bologna Process per the official programme page. Supports a non-EU student residence permit via the Ministry of Education Letter of Acceptance.
accreditation: ARACIS-accredited state university; the programme page states accreditation by the Romanian Ministry of Education under the Bologna Process. Listed among the English-taught master's programmes of the Cinematography and Media department.
tuition: €950 PER MONTH — CONFIRMED VERBATIM. I extracted the full text of the UBB Senate fee regulation and located Anexa nr. 4 ('Taxe de şcolarizare în valută ale cetăţenilor care studiază pe cont propriu în România, proveniți din state care nu sunt membre ale Uniunii Europene...'). Row 11 lists the Faculty of Theatre and Film split across two domains: 'domeniul teatru și artele spectacolului' at €750/month and 'domeniul cinematografie şi media' at €950/month, for masterat, învățământ cu frecvență. Digital Interactive Arts sits in the Department of Cinematography and Media, so €950/month is the rate he pays. Art. 15.2(a) confirms fees are payable over 9 months where the curriculum has no distinct practice period, or 10 months where it does. At 9 months that is €8,550/year and €17,100 over two years; at 10 months, €9,500/year and €19,000. The previous entry's figures were correct — but he should confirm in writing whether this curriculum triggers the 10-month rule, a €950/year difference, and separately confirm the domain classification, worth €1,800/year.
otherFees: €50 non-refundable admission dossier processing fee for non-EU applicants — CONFIRMED VERBATIM at art. 15.1 of the Senate regulation: 'Pentru procesarea dosarului de admitere se va achita o taxă de 50 Euro, indiferent de nivelul de studiu sau forma de învățământ'. Art. 15.2(c) confirms tuition EXCLUDES accommodation and meals, and art. 15.4 confirms any other personal costs including housing, food and transport are the student's own. A separate dissertation defence fee applies per Anexa nr. 6 (amount UNVERIFIED). Add document legalisation, translation, Letter of Acceptance costs and Cluj-Napoca living costs.
totalCost: About €17,100 in tuition over two years (€950 × 9 months × 2), or about €19,000 if the 10-month practice rule applies, plus the €50 application fee, plus a dissertation defence fee, plus Cluj-Napoca living costs (UNVERIFIED, no official figure), plus IELTS/TOEFL costs. No preparatory language year needed, saving a full year of time and money relative to every Romanian-taught option.
scholarshipDetail: The Romanian Government/MFA route (scholarships.studyinromania.gov.ro) is established under Government Decision no. 288/1993 for non-EU citizens and requires a minimum study-years average of 7/10 or 'Good' — CONFIRMED. But the critical catch stands and I could NOT resolve it: the MFA scheme's published rule is that bachelor's and master's beneficiaries study only in Romanian, with only doctoral holders permitted a foreign language, which would exclude an English-taught master's from MFA funding. The scholarship portal's public pages do not state the language rule explicitly, so this must be settled by direct enquiry. This single question decides whether the programme is a €17,100 self-pay or a funded option. ARICE may operate differently — verify separately. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY: the very feature that makes this programme accessible to him (English) may be what disqualifies it from the main Romanian scholarship, whereas UNATC's Romanian-taught programmes are scholarship-eligible but linguistically closed to him.
entry: CORRECTED AND IMPROVED — the previous entry said 'no field restriction published', which understated the case. The official page states the programme 'addresses graduate students in visual arts, architecture, music, theater, and film AND GRADUATES FROM OTHER FIELDS interested in a theoretical and practical interdisciplinary approach to new digital technologies in visual, performing, and cinematic arts.' So non-arts graduates are EXPLICITLY invited by name, not merely un-excluded. His BSc Software Engineering is squarely within the published eligibility. Non-EU applicants apply through UBB's Centrul de Cooperări Internaționale with a Ministry of Education Letter of Acceptance.
acceptsNonMusic: YES, EXPLICITLY AND BY NAME — this is stronger than the previous entry claimed. The official page names 'graduates from other fields' as an intended audience alongside arts graduates. No music degree, no conservatoire training and no instrumental audition are required. Selection turns on an interactive-technology artistic project, which a software engineering graduate is unusually well placed to produce. Caveat: the interview also assesses general cinema and media studies knowledge, which he must read up on.
portfolio: MANDATORY, TWO PARTS — CONFIRMED: (1) an individual artistic project, submitted in writing, demonstrating interest in interactive technologies, and (2) a portfolio of artistic works, either previous work or work related to the proposed project. The application is complete only on confirmed receipt of both. The project may be PROPOSED rather than completed — the interview tests whether he can argue its relevance. For a software engineer this remains among the most reachable portfolio requirements available: a generative music system, a reactive audio-visual installation, an audio plugin or a game-audio prototype all qualify and all build on skills he already has.
audition: CONFIRMED AND EXPANDED. An ONLINE interview conducted in English — note 'online', which means no travel cost for the entrance exam, a real advantage over UNATC's Romanian-taught programmes. Assessment covers: ability to articulate the concept and relevance of the proposed project; domain knowledge; command of terminology; and general knowledge of cinema and media studies. That last criterion is new and worth flagging — he will be assessed on general cinema and media studies knowledge, an area where a software engineering graduate has no formal grounding and should read deliberately during his portfolio year.
deadline: 17 July 2026 for the 2026-27 cycle — CONFIRMED. For a September 2027 start expect a mid-July 2027 window, with the Ministry Letter of Acceptance process beginning several months earlier. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates.
opens: Application 13-17 July 2026; exam 24 July 2026; final results 30 July 2026 (2026-27 cycle) — CONFIRMED. PRIOR CYCLE. Non-EU applicants must start months earlier for the Letter of Acceptance.
duration: 4 semesters (2 years), full-time. Total ECTS still NOT stated on the official programme page — UNVERIFIED. A Romanian two-year master's is normally 120 ECTS and UBB's fee regulation treats it as a standard masterat, but get this in writing from the faculty.
languageReq: English. The specific certificate and band remain UNVERIFIED — no English test requirement is stated anywhere on the programme page or in the admission criteria, and UBB's central non-EU degree-student page was unreachable (HTTP 404) at the time of checking. Because he has not taken IELTS or TOEFL, this is his single most urgent question. CORRECTED CONTACT: the programme page names Assistant Professor Cristina Pop-Tiron (cristina.pop-tiron@ubbcluj.ro) as the contact — the previous entry gave constantin.parvulescu@ubbcluj.ro and Prof. Rodica Mocan, which are not the contacts published on the current page. Faculty secretariat: +40 264 590 066 / +40 264 405 357. Confirmed advantage: no Romanian requirement and no preparatory Romanian year, since Romanian rules exempt students on foreign-language programmes.
study: CONFIRMED AND EXPANDED with the full four-semester curriculum. Semester I: Interactive Digital Performance, Production Management, Creative Performing Arts Project, plus electives in Visual Culture, Performance Theory or Practice as Research. Semester II: Creative Industries, Curatorial Models in Digital Media, Creative Visual Arts Project, plus electives in Augmented Reality or Visual Programming. Semester III: New Media Documentary, Creative Transmedia Project, Management and Marketing for Independent Artists, plus electives in Spectatorship Studies or Visual Storytelling. Semester IV: Academic Ethics, Directed Reading and Dissertation Writing, Digital Technologies in Art, plus electives in Sound Design or Interactive Media. CRITICAL: 'Sound Design for Digital Media' is an elective in SEMESTER IV ONLY — the final semester — and it competes with 'Interactive Media' for the same elective slot. So across a two-year degree he would take at most ONE sound course, in his last six months. The previous entry called sound 'one elective'; that is right, but it understated how late and how marginal it is. Note also 'Visual Programming' (Sem II elective) and 'Augmented Reality' — those play to his coding background more than the sound course does.
recommendation: CONFIRMED ACCURATE ON FEES AND ELIGIBILITY, BUT ITS HEADLINE CLAIM IS FALSE AND ITS RANKING MUST CHANGE. Everything financial checks out verbatim: €950/month for the cinematografie și media domain, 9-10 months a year, €50 dossier fee, all confirmed in Anexa nr. 4 and art. 15 of the UBB Senate regulation. Eligibility is better than previously described — the page explicitly invites 'graduates from other fields', so his BSc is named-in rather than merely not excluded. CORRECTION 1, and it is the important one: the previous entry asserted this is 'the ONLY English-taught programme with meaningful sound content found anywhere in Hungary, Romania or Bulgaria'. That is wrong. UNATC Bucharest runs at least five English-taught master's programmes — Design for New Media, Visual Effects, Audiovisual Preservation and Programming, Interactive Technologies for Performing and Media Arts, and Art of Game Design — all listed in its Senate fee decision at 13,750 lei per year, roughly €2,750, with budget places available. ITPMA in particular is a 120-ECTS English-taught MA that trains students in 'digitally controlling sound, light, image and code for the arts', explicitly welcomes science and engineering graduates, and accepts a 1500-2000 word essay in place of a portfolio. It costs roughly one third of this programme and has MORE sound content, not less. CORRECTION 2: the contact is Cristina Pop-Tiron, not the names previously given. CORRECTION 3: the Sound Design elective falls in semester IV and competes with Interactive Media for the same slot, so he may take at most one sound course, at the very end. Rating B rather than A: it is a legitimate, well-matched, visa-supporting degree with an online English entrance interview and no language-year penalty, but at €17,100 it is expensive for a programme where sound is a single final-semester elective, and its scholarship eligibility is unresolved. Actions in order: (1) apply to UNATC ITPMA as the primary Romanian target and treat this as the parallel application; (2) ask studyinromania.gov.ro in writing whether an English-taught master's can be MFA-funded; (3) ask Cristina Pop-Tiron what English certificate is required, whether the fee domain is cinematografie și media (€950) or teatru (€750), and whether the curriculum triggers 9 or 10 months of fees; (4) spend the portfolio year building ONE strong interactive audio project with proper documentation, which serves both applications.

Level 2 is 'designed for those of you who have already mastered the basics (or who have graduated from the Ibiza DJ/Producer Course - Level 1 or similar)' and covers beat matching, looping, harmonic mixing, effects, plus sound design, sidechaining, synthesis, warping, slicing, mixing and mastering. 26 hours of tuition per week, comprising classroom time plus the DJ experiences playing out at venues. CONDITIONAL strictly on that framing — if he is tempted to substitute it for an accredited programme, the answer is AVOID.

entry: VERIFIED on UPF's official admission-requirements page under this exact master: official bachelor's or master's degree from the EHEA or an equivalent foreign degree giving access to postgraduate study in the issuing country — and, verbatim, "S'accepten titulacions de qualsevol àmbit acadèmic" (degrees from ANY academic field are accepted); academic transcript with grade average; CV in English; motivation letter in English of 400–600 words; at least ONE academic recommendation letter (requested through the online application, institutional email addresses only — no gmail/yahoo/hotmail); accredited English at B2 level; passport/ID. "Complementàriament ... la comissió de selecció pot concertar una entrevista amb el candidat" — the committee may additionally arrange an interview. The SMC FAQ adds that the most important criterion is "excellence in the academic CV as related to the topics of the master", then the motivation letter, and that "if you do not have a Computer Science degree, you should be able to demonstrate an equivalent background" in maths, programming, signal processing and/or machine learning. His BSc Software Engineering is literally the preferred profile. No music degree is required at any point.
portfolio: CONFIRMED: no portfolio required. Admission is CV + transcript + 400–600-word motivation letter + one academic reference + English B2 + passport, with a possible interview. The FAQ notes that if he has no formal music education, "the motivation letter is a good place to explain your non-formal musical training" — so his music case is made in prose, not in a submitted body of work.

duration: VERIFIED: 60 ECTS — 40 credits of compulsory and optional subjects plus a 20-credit master's thesis (the official Catalan register breaks this into 25 mandatory + 15 optional + 20 thesis). Face-to-face, full-time, one year by default; an official PART-TIME route spreads the 60 ECTS over two years. Depending on prior education you may be required to take up to 15 (full-time) or up to 50 (part-time) complementary undergraduate credits, extending the master to two years. Three trimesters: Sept–Dec, Jan–Mar, Apr–Jun; classes start around 21 September; thesis defended orally in the first week of July, final document due end of August. 25 places.
study: VERIFIED: the whole sound-communication chain — creation and generation of sound, transmission, perception. Grounding in "the most advanced technologies for the analysis, synthesis, transformation, and production of sound and music" plus the technologies and processes supporting sound and musical creation. Draws on music (composition, performance, musicology), physics/acoustics, engineering (signal processing, AI, human-computer interaction, electronics) and psychology (psychoacoustics). The programme explicitly "focuses on the more technical aspects of this field". Research focus mirrors the MTG: audio signal processing, music information retrieval, musical interfaces, computational musicology. Coordinator: Xavier Serra. Workload is openly stated as roughly 50 hours/week; mornings are deliberately kept free for study and NOT to make the master compatible with parallel work.
recommendation: The best academic fit in this batch for his existing skill set and the easiest to get into on paper: any-field degrees accepted, CS explicitly the ideal profile, English, no portfolio, no audition, Barcelona. It is also the worst fit for the stated goal — its own FAQ says graduates go to R&D jobs or PhDs. Two points in his favour: the B2 English requirement can be met without IELTS/TOEFL by taking UPF's own non-accrediting level test and attaching the receipt, and a part-time route exists. Two against: €5,749.80 with no non-EU funding, and a self-declared ~50 hour/week load UPF says is incompatible with parallel work. Take it only if he enters the industry through the technology door.

whyChance: Names engineering or computing as a welcome background; portfolio required, so build it
scholarship: FHNW / HSM Basel Stipendien (page exists under Quicklinks: 'Studiengebühren & Finanzierung', 'Stipendien'); Swiss Gover…
qualification: Master of Arts FHNW in Musikalischer Performance, Studienrichtung Producing/Performance Jazz — full second-cycle degree, 120 ECTS
accreditation: Public Fachhochschule (FHNW). Governed by the 'Rahmenordnung für die Studiengänge der FHNW' of 2 Feb 2015 (as at 21 June 2021) and the 'Studien- und Prüfungsordnung der Hochschule für Musik Basel FHNW' of 1 December 2024, plus the binding 'Studienrichtungsreglement MA Musikalische Performance, Studienrichtung Jazz Producing/Performance'.
tuition: CHF 1,250 PER SEMESTER = CHF 2,500 PER YEAR for a Tunisian. FHNW publishes an explicit three-tier rate, quoted verbatim from the Steckbrief: 'Semestergebühr 750 CHF (CH) | 1000 CHF (EU/EFTA-Länder) | 1250 CHF (Nicht-EU/Nicht-EFTA)'. This is the clearest example of a Swiss school charging third-country nationals a higher rate — a Tunisian pays CHF 250/semester more than an EU student and CHF 500/semester more than a Swiss. Still only about CHF 2,500/year in absolute terms.
otherFees: Anmeldegebühr CHF 200 (application fee, stated on the Steckbrief). Compulsory Swiss health insurance. Instrument/equipment costs at own expense.
totalCost: Tuition CHF 2,500/yr + CHF 200 one-off application fee. Basel living costs approx CHF 20,000–24,000/yr (UNVERIFIED — not read from an FHNW page). Two-year total including living: roughly CHF 45,000–53,000.
scholarshipDetail: The programme page carries Quicklinks to 'Studiengebühren & Finanzierung' and 'Stipendien' but the substance of those pages was NOT read here — the amounts, eligibility for third-country nationals and deadlines are UNVERIFIED. Swiss cantonal scholarships are generally closed to students who move to Switzerland purely to study, so the realistic funding route is the Swiss Government Excellence Scholarship or Tunisian sources. FUNDING FOR THIS PROGRAMME: UNVERIFIED.
entry: Verbatim from the programme page: 'Zum Masterstudium in Musikalischer Performance Jazz (Producing/Performance) zugelassen wird, wer über ein abgeschlossenes Bachelorstudium in Musik (Profil Jazz) oder eine äquivalente Vorbildung verfügt, die Aufnahmeprüfung bestanden und einen Studienplatz erhalten hat (Anzahl beschränkt).' Documents required with the application per Studienrichtungsreglement §4(4): 'a. Lebenslauf, b. Motivationsschreiben, c. Maturzeugnis, d. Passfoto (für Studierendenausweis)' — note it asks for the school-leaving certificate, plus the subject dossiers described below. Places are capped and awarded by rank: §5(1) 'werden die vorhandenen Studienplätze ... in einem rangorientierten Verfahren entsprechend ihrer Gesamtbewertung der Eignungsabklärung ... vergeben.' §4(5): 'Bei Nichtbestehen der Prüfung im Hauptfach ist die Eignungsabklärung insgesamt nicht bestanden.' The aptitude assessment may be repeated once.
acceptsNonMusic: THE MOST OPEN WORDING FOUND IN SWITZERLAND. Quoted verbatim from the programme page's target-group paragraph: 'Diese Studienrichtung richtet sich an fortgeschrittene Instrumentalist:innen, Sänger:innen, Komponist:innen oder Produzent:innen mit einem Bachelorabschluss in Musik, einem gleichwertigen Studienabschluss oder gleichwertiger Berufserfahrung.' Two things matter here: (a) 'Produzent:innen' are named as a target group in their own right, and (b) the qualifying route is a music bachelor OR an equivalent degree OR EQUIVALENT PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE — the regulation's own phrasing is 'oder eine äquivalente Vorbildung'. A BSc Software Engineering is not by itself an äquivalente Vorbildung for a jazz master, so the realistic route is the professional-experience limb. HE HAS NONE TODAY. This is the single thing that would most change his odds: between now and February 2027 he needs credited production/mix work he can name. There is no ear-training exam and no compulsory instrument audition on the Realisation track.
portfolio: Schwerpunkt Realisation, first round, verbatim: 'Produktions-Dossier — Es ist ein Soundfile einer selbständig produzierten Aufnahme/Mischung (Studioproduktion) und/oder einer Film-/Video-Vertonung oder eines Remixes/Sounddesigns mit einer kurzen Erläuterung der Produktionsweise (PDF) einzureichen.' So: ONE sound file of an independently produced recording/mix (studio production) and/or film-video scoring and/or a remix/sound design, PLUS a short PDF explaining how it was produced. No track count beyond one, no stated length limit, no stated file format beyond 'Soundfile' — UNVERIFIED whether wav or mp3 is preferred. Also required in round one: a Motivationsschreiben ('Im Motivationsschreiben soll die bisherige musikalische und anderweitige Vorbildung tabellarisch beschrieben werden. Daneben soll die Motivation für sowie die Erwartungen an ein Masterstudium ... dargelegt werden') and a MASTER PROJECT PLAN sketching artistic-research interests. YOU MUST ALSO SUBMIT A KOMBINATIONSFACH DOSSIER: verbatim, 'Mit dem Schwerpunktfach Realisation (Produktion) ist Performance (Instrument/Stimme) oder Komposition als Kombinationsfach wählbar.' If Komposition is chosen: 'Es sind drei Kompositionen aus dem aktuellen kompositorischen Schaffen ... einzureichen.' If Performance is chosen: an audiovisual recording of 'mindestens drei Stücken' solo and/or with ensemble. CHOOSING KOMPOSITION AS THE COMBINATION SUBJECT AVOIDS HAVING TO PLAY AN INSTRUMENT ON CAMERA. Deadline for uploads: 'laden Sie die geforderten Unterlagen sowohl für das Schwerpunkt- als auch für das Kombinationsfach bis zum 15. Februar hoch.'
audition: TWO ROUNDS, AND THE DECISIVE PART IS A PORTFOLIO HEARING, NOT AN AUDITION. Round 1 is pure dossier: 'Vorselektion — Anhand des eingereichten Dossiers inkl. Motivationsschreiben und Master Project Plan entscheidet eine Kommission über die Zulassung zur zweiten Runde.' Round 2 for Schwerpunkt Realisation consists of: (a) 'Hearing Realisation (Dauer: 20 Minuten)' — a 20-minute hearing of your productions; the school publishes the duration but no further content detail, so the internal format is UNVERIFIED; (b) the Kombinationsfach element, and this is only conditional — verbatim: 'Auf Verlangen der Prüfungskommission Vorspiel (bei Kombinationsfach Performance; es sind zwei bis drei Stücke vorzubereiten) oder Präsentation (bei Kombinationsfach Komposition; kurze Präsentation/Vorspiel von ein bis zwei eigenen Kompositionsarbeiten)' — i.e. ONLY IF THE COMMISSION ASKS; (c) 'Gespräch mit der Kommission zum Master Project Plan (Dauer: 10 Minuten). In den präsentierten Produktionen soll ein Bezug zum im Master Project Plan dargelegten künstlerischen Interesse gemacht werden.' NO EAR-TRAINING EXAM ANYWHERE. NO COMPULSORY PERFORMANCE AUDITION on the Realisation track. AND ROUND 2 CAN BE DONE ONLINE: verbatim, 'Die zweite Runde (Präsentation/Audition) ... findet in der Regel in Präsenz (vor Ort) statt. Auf Antrag kann die Audition online absolviert werden. Die Zuteilung ins Online-Verfahren erfolgt nach Genehmigung des Antrags, der mit Einreichen des Dossiers verbindlich gestellt werden muss.' A Tunisian can therefore complete the whole selection without a Schengen visa. Reglement §4(2)-(3): 'Der praktische Prüfungsteil besteht aus einer ersten Runde «per Video» und einer zweiten Runde in Form eines Live-Vorspiels ... Das Vorspiel vor Ort findet in April statt.' §4(6): 'Die Ergebnisse werden im Mai per E-Mail bekannt gegeben.'
deadline: 15 FEBRUARY. Verbatim: 'Das Anmeldewindow ist vom 15. Dezember bis zum 15. Februar geöffnet' (page: 'Das Anmeldefenster ist vom 15. Dezember bis zum 15. Februar geöffnet'). NOT a prior cycle — the page already advertises the start date 13.9.2027, so for the September 2027 intake the window is 15 December 2026 – 15 February 2027, live round in April 2027, results by e-mail in May 2027.
opens: 15 December (i.e. 15 December 2026 for the September 2027 intake).
duration: 4 semesters, full-time, on-campus (Präsenz), 120 ECTS. NEXT START PUBLISHED AS 13 SEPTEMBER 2027 — exactly his target intake.
languageReq: 'Gute Grundkenntnisse in Englisch' — good basic English, evaluated during the admission procedure. NO GERMAN REQUIREMENT PUBLISHED. Conditional admission possible if language is short but the artistic assessment convinces.
englishTest: No test score named. Verbatim: 'Diese werden im Verlauf des Zulassungsverfahrens evaluiert' — English is assessed in-process, not by certificate. UNVERIFIED whether an IELTS/TOEFL is ever accepted or required.
study: The Hauptfach is a combination of three areas — Instrument/Gesang (Performance), Komposition and REALISATION (Produktion). Verbatim: 'Im Profil «allrounder» wird einer dieser drei Bereiche zum Schwerpunkt gewählt, die beiden übrigen ergänzen diesen als Kombinationsfächer I+II.' Choosing Realisation as the Schwerpunkt makes this a production degree. Programme aims verbatim: 'Fundierte musikalische, technische und kulturelle Kenntnisse ermöglichen ein rasches Erfassen von Aufbau und Ablauf einer kompletten Produktion im Studio und bei Live-Projekten sowie die überzeugende Umsetzung eigener Ideen auf dem Instrument und in einem technologisch komplexen Umfeld.' Highlights listed: 'flexibler und projektorientierter Aufbau des Studiums mit individuellen Schwerpunkten in Performance, Komposition und Produktion'; 'Arbeit in hervorragend ausgestatteten Studios'; 'Coaching durch erfahrene, renommierte Dozierende'. Artistic Research module. Final assessment verbatim: 'Beim Abschluss präsentieren die Studierenden ein Portfolio aus Kompositionen und/oder professionellen Produktionen und/oder eine Live-Performance.' Named teaching staff for Realisation: Daniel Dettwiler (Basel recording/mixing/mastering engineer) and Prof. Patrik Zosso (programme director). Idiom is jazz and 'verwandte Musikrichtungen' — not pop/hip-hop record production, which is a genuine fit caveat.

entry: First master's only (must not hold a master's at scholarship start); bachelor completed by 31 July 2027; born after 31 December 1991; admission confirmation from a Swiss arts institution; art scholarships open to a LIMITED country list only
portfolio: Y - for music: recordings/links demonstrating three different styles; plus admission confirmation/proof of application to a Swiss arts/music institution
deadline: Country-specific embassy deadlines published 20 Aug 2026 for the 2027-28 award (typically Oct-Dec 2026); decisions announced by end of May 2027
opens: 20 August 2026 (official, for 2027-28 cycle, via online portal)
recommendation: The single most important funding lever for the whole Swiss arts-track list: if Tunisia is on the 2027-28 art-scholarship list, it can fund living costs for a ZHdK/HKB/HEM/Basel sound master - timeline (apply Oct-Dec 2026) exactly matches the Sept 2027 intake. Candidate meets the age cutoff (born after 31 Dec 1991) only if born 1992 or later - verify.

tuition: CHF 580/semester + admin fees for regular non-Swiss students; GRANT HOLDERS are exempt from course fees and pay only CHF 80/semester (confirmed on official grant page - even better than previously stated)

entry: Foreign university bachelor equivalent to a Swiss bachelor (180 ECTS) with outstanding academic results; C1 in teaching language (candidate must take an English test); grant application separate from program admission. CAVEAT for this candidate: HEC MiM admission expects a management/economics-related bachelor - applicants from foreign universities with other degrees may be required to complete a bridging programme (per HEC admission info); a software-engineering degree is an admission risk for this specific programme (Check with HECmasterAdmission@unil.ch)
portfolio: N
deadline: 1 November 2026 for September 2027 start (2027/2028 intake) - confirmed on official page; selection Dec-Mar, notification early April 2027
opens: September 2026 (confirmed on official grant page for the 2027/28 intake)
recommendation: Best funded business route in the slice: CHF 1,600/month + fee exemption (CHF 80/sem) with a confirmed 1 Nov 2026 deadline exactly matching the Sept 2027 plan; business generalist rather than music-specific, and the CS-to-management admission gap (possible bridging requirement) is the main risk - consider also pairing the grant with a more CS-compatible UNIL master.

institution: Zürcher Hochschule der Künste (ZHdK) — Departement Musik, with the Institute for Computer Music and Sound Tec…
programme: Master of Arts in Music, Major Komposition und Theorie — Vertiefung Elektroakustische Komposition
whyChance: Names engineering or computing as a welcome background; portfolio required, so build it
scholarship: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships for Foreign Scholars and Artists — Tunisia's inclusion in the arts scholarship…
qualification: Master of Arts ZFH in Music (Komposition und Theorie)
accreditation: Swiss university of the arts, institutionally accredited; MA is a recognised Swiss master's degree
tuition: CHF 1,220 per semester for non-Swiss students (CHF 720 for Swiss) — i.e. approx. CHF 2,440 per year for a Tunisian national
otherFees: QUOTE: 'Die Einschreibegebühr zum Aufnahmeverfahren beträgt CHF 100' (CHF 100 registration fee for the admission procedure) plus CHF 200 examination fee for those invited to the aptitude examination
totalCost: approx. CHF 2,440/year tuition + CHF 300 admission fees + Zurich living costs (very high; UNVERIFIED)
scholarshipDetail: UNVERIFIED — no programme-specific scholarship published
entry: QUOTE: 'Die Voraussetzungen für die Zulassung zum Studium und Immatrikulation sind der Rahmenordnung der ZHdK (RO § 19 bis 24) zu entnehmen.' — the baseline is a Bachelor's degree or equivalent from a recognised, accredited higher-education institution. Plus the exception clause, QUOTE: 'In Ausnahmefällen kann die ZHdK Personen ohne Bachelorabschluss oder gleichwertigen Abschluss einer anerkannten und akkreditierten Hochschule zulassen' (admission 'sur dossier' in exceptional cases even without a bachelor's degree). Selection is by dossier plus a two-stage aptitude assessment.
acceptsNonMusic: QUOTE: the admission page requires a 'Bachelorabschluss oder gleichwertige[r] Abschluss einer anerkannten und akkreditierten Hochschule' — a bachelor's degree or equivalent from a recognised and accredited higher-education institution — and names NO subject or field anywhere; it further states 'In Ausnahmefällen kann die ZHdK Personen ohne Bachelorabschluss ... zulassen'. Verdict: YES on the degree subject (no music degree is demanded; a software-engineering BSc satisfies the stated condition), but CASE-BY-CASE overall because the decisive gate is the dossier of 3–4 of the applicant's OWN WORKS and the aptitude examination. This is a realistic target ONLY once a portfolio exists.
portfolio: EXACT: '3 bis 4 eigenen Arbeiten (max. 1.95 GB)' — submit 3 to 4 of your own works or work extracts totalling approximately 10 minutes, each with a written commentary (concept, significance, process) of maximum 2 A4 pages; files delivered as a ZIP, filenames must contain no special characters or umlauts.
audition: Yes — Eignungsabklärung in person: presentation of the submitted portfolio works; an analytical task with 60 minutes' preparation; if required an additional technical/musical aptitude test of 30 minutes; and a discussion of professional goals and study motivation, with jury feedback after deliberation.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE: '6. Januar – 2. März 2026' (registration window for autumn 2026 entry). For a September 2027 start expect roughly 6 January – 2 March 2027.
duration: 4 semesters (Regelstudienzeit); 90 credits for the Major / 120 credits for the full MA; starts in the autumn semester
languageReq: German or English; applicants must demonstrate sufficient competence via native-speaker status, a passing subject grade (≥4), a recognised certificate (normally not older than 5 years), or a degree completed in that language.
englishTest: Accepted as proof of the language of instruction if teaching is in English; specific score UNVERIFIED
study: Electroacoustic composition with access to the ICST — spatial sound projection (Ambisonics), augmented instruments, auditory perception, generative art, electroacoustic music pedagogy; ICST also runs artist residencies and the EARS pre-PhD training.

institution: Zürcher Hochschule der Künste (Zurich University of the Arts, ZHdK) — Institute for Computer Music and Sound …
programme: MA Composition and Theory, Major Sound Design
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's; portfolio required, so build it
verdictWhy: The thirty-minute oral music-theory examination is disqualifying for someone with no conservatoire training, and it sits alongside a 90-minute timed practical sound-design task and a film/game analysis oral, all sat in person in Zurich at his own expense plus a CHF 200 exam fee. The programme is also aimed at sound design for film and games, not at electronic music authorship. Cost is roughly double what his list claimed, in the most expensive city on it.
correction: TWO CORRECTIONS. (1) COST: 'Under EUR 1.5k/yr' is WRONG — a non-resident international pays CHF 720 + CHF 500 per semester = CHF 2,440/yr, plus ASVZ and union fees and a CHF 200 examination fee, so about CHF 2,510/yr recurring (~EUR 2,700). (2) GATE: 'Portfolio + exam/interview' badly understates it. The Eignungsprüfung is an ON-SITE three-part examination that includes a 30-minute ORAL MUSIC-THEORY TEST plus a 90-minute practical sound-design task under exam conditions.
qualification: MA (Master of Arts in Music)
tuition: CHF 720 tuition per semester + CHF 500 per semester international surcharge (for international students taking up residence in Switzerland) + CHF 35 ASVZ sports + CHF 32 optional student union = roughly CHF 1,255/semester, i.e. about CHF 2,510 per year. Plus CHF 100 registration and CHF 200 aptitude-test fee.
scholarshipDetail: None found specific to this programme for a Tunisian applicant. Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships exist nationally but eligibility for ZHdK arts masters and for Tunisia is UNVERIFIED.
entry: A bachelor's degree from an accredited university. "In exceptional cases, ZHdK may admit individuals without a bachelor's degree or equivalent qualification from a recognized and accredited university." Full document set: letter of motivation (max 2 A4, German or English, covering school and musical education, musical activities, knowledge of music software, and why you want to study Sound Design at ZHdK); application video 3–5 min (.mp4, max 1 GB); portfolio; audiogram not older than 2 months; CV; language proof; transcripts/diplomas; passport copy; passport photo. AI use is permitted but must be declared at registration.
acceptsNonMusic: YES, with an explicit extra hurdle — the application document list contains an item required specifically for "non-music bachelor holders": a video of an artistic-musical performance. So the school formally anticipates and admits non-music bachelors. The binding constraint is not the diploma but the on-site musical aptitude test (intervals, chords, rhythm/melody reproduction), which is real ear-training work he does not yet have.
portfolio: "3 or 4 own works", total approximately 10 minutes in length, files labelled with your name, no special characters, compressed into a single ZIP (max 1.95 GB), accompanied by written comments on each work (max 2 A4 pages combined). Separately: an application video of 3–5 minutes (max 1 GB, .mp4). Applicants who hold a NON-MUSIC bachelor must additionally submit a video of an artistic-musical performance.
audition: On-site aptitude test in Zurich, two days (13–14 April in the 2026 cycle): (1) practical exam — 90 min preparation, 20 min presentation on sound-design tasks; (2) oral exam analysing media — 60 min preparation, 10 min presentation; (3) 10 min presentation on the submitted works; (4) a "musical aptitude test" covering memory exercise, presentation of rhythms and melodies, and recognising, naming and writing intervals and chords. Fees: CHF 100 registration + CHF 200 aptitude-test fee if invited to the second phase.
deadline: Application 6 January – 2 March; minor selection 10–30 March; aptitude test 13–14 April; studies begin 14 September. Information day 20 November of the preceding year. ALL PRIOR CYCLE (2026 intake) - confirm new dates; expect an equivalent Jan–Mar 2027 window for September 2027.
duration: 2 years (studies begin 14 September 2026 for the 2026 cycle). ECTS total UNVERIFIED on the pages read.
study: "The creative use of sound and the content-related examination of the interaction between images and sound in connection with linear and interactive media." Technical and artistic skills in "sound production and manipulation as well as linear and interactive sound dramaturgy." Delivered via mentoring, one-to-one meetings and specialist classes including sound-engineering principles, plus courses in electroacoustic composition and theory. Access to the Immersive Arts Space (IAS) and the Institute for Computer Music and Sound Technology (ICST). Final assessment = a performative (optionally installation-based) Master's project + research-led written paper + colloquium + dossier.
recommendation: Arguably the best value-for-craft in the slice: about CHF 2.5k/year tuition at a top-tier institute, and the school explicitly has a route for non-music bachelors. The decisive obstacle is the two-day ON-SITE aptitude test with a classical musical-aptitude component (naming and writing intervals and chords) — that is 9–12 months of deliberate ear-training and theory work he must start now, plus a travel/visa trip to Zurich in spring 2027. German or English both work, so his language profile is fine.

institution: Istanbul Technical University (İTÜ) — Dr. Erol Üçer Center for Advanced Studies in Music (MIAM)
programme: Music (M.A.) — Sonic Arts concentration area (1st Education, thesis master)
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's; portfolio required, so build it
verdictWhy: Admissions rules that could have been written for him: no subject requirement, no GRE/ALES, no IELTS, fully English-taught, portfolio plus interview, and an April-to-June window that fits a September 2027 start. The unresolved thing is money — the 'Full funding' on his list is unsupported by any ITU page, and the international tuition figure is unpublished, so the only credible full ride is Türkiye Bursları, a separate national competition with an earlier deadline he would have to plan for independently.
correction: DUPLICATE of index 7 and 23 — three rows for one application. CORRECTIONS: (1) 'Funding: Full' is unsubstantiated by any ITU/MIAM page; the only credible full-funding route is Türkiye Bursları, a separate earlier national competition. (2) 'Under EUR 1.5k/yr' is UNVERIFIED — ITU does not publish the international graduate tuition figure on the pages reached. (3) The process includes an interview stage (1-3 July in the prior cycle), not portfolio alone.
qualification: M.A. in Music, thesis track (1st Education). A non-thesis '2nd Education' variant exists and awards a Term Project instead of a thesis.
tuition: NOW VERIFIED and far cheaper than previously estimated. İTÜ Registrar's published fee schedule: international graduate ('Institute') students who entered in 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 pay 33,300 TL for the academic year (those from 2023-2024 and earlier pay 23,500 TL). Turkish citizens at graduate level pay 1,115 TL/year. Paid in two equal instalments, first at registration, second at the start of the second semester. The earlier third-party estimate of USD 2,000-5,000/year was WRONG — 33,300 TL is roughly USD 800-1,000. The 2026-2027 figure will be set annually by the Council of Higher Education; expect an inflation-linked rise.
scholarshipDetail: Türkiye Bursları (Türkiye Scholarships, YTB). CONFIRMED on turkiyeburslari.gov.tr: a government scholarship open to non-Turkish nationals, covering Associate, Bachelor's, Master's, PhD and Research levels, with 'Music and Musicology', 'Fine Arts (Painting, Sculpture, Lithography)', 'Design', 'Photography' and 'Cinematography' among the listed eligible fields, and 2026 applications announced as open. NOT CONFIRMED in this pass: the specific 'Arts Scholarship Programme' sub-track, the claim that İTÜ is one of only three participating universities, and the claim that music technology is explicitly listed at master's level — the YTB site is JavaScript-driven and those detail pages did not render. Treat the Arts sub-programme as plausible but unverified; check tbbs.turkiyeburslari.gov.tr directly. Structural caveat: YTB places the scholar at a university rather than the scholar choosing freely, and a YTB award would still not exempt him from the MIAM entrance exam.
entry: CONFIRMED verbatim on the 1st Education Masters page: 'GPA: Not required.' 'ALES/GMAT/GRE: Talep edilmemektedir' (not requested). 'Concentration area requirements: There are no department / concentration area requirements.' Additional documents: 'Two letters of recommendations must be submitted by the candidate to verify their motivation and determination' and 'Candidates must prepare a portfolio relevant to their application area.' Online pre-registration at www.sis.itu.edu.tr, selecting the 'Müzik/Music' programme (NOT 'Müzik Teorisi ve Kompozisyon', which belongs to the Turkish Music State Conservatory). IMPORTANT CORRECTION ON ENGLISH: İTÜ does NOT accept IELTS. Accepted tests and minimum scores for master's entry are İTÜ Proficiency 65/100, TOEFL iBT 78/120, PTE Academic 62/90 (rising to 67/90 from 2026-2027 fall), YDS/e-YDS/YÖKDİL 65/100, OTE Advanced 111/140, e-Tep 50. Scores valid 2 years (YDS variants 5 years). Further constraint: 'TOEFL iBT and PTE Academic exam results must be taken from the exam centers in state universities.' He must plan for TOEFL iBT (at a qualifying centre) or the İTÜ Proficiency exam — booking IELTS would be wasted money.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — now confirmed, not merely 'leaning favourable'. The 1st Education Masters page states in the Application Conditions section: 'Concentration area requirements: There are no department / concentration area requirements.' Combined with 'GPA: Not required' and no ALES/GRE, entry is decided on portfolio + exams + interview + two references. The 0-credit preparatory semester (Introduction to Music Theory, Ear Training and Sight Singing, Preparatory Studies in Sonic Arts, Studio Practices) is the institution's published mechanism for entrants without prior music training. The 2026-2027 Sonic Arts portfolio spec explicitly invites 'examples of creative audio coding / programming', which directly rewards a software-engineering background. The one thing NOT waived for non-music applicants is the written General Music Knowledge and Music Theory exam.
portfolio: CORRECTED — the prior-cycle text on file is obsolete. Current spec is the İTÜ MİAM 2026-2027 Fall Term Entrance Exam Handbook (published 13 May 2026), Sonic Arts section, verbatim: 'Applicants should submit a representative portfolio of creative work. The portfolio can include any of the following: electroacoustic or acousmatic compositions; sound installations; sound design; live performance(s); any other sound-based works using physical, digital, or electronic media; examples of creative audio coding / programming. You can include non-sonic elements if these are an important part of your creative practice (e.g. video, architectural drawings, text), but overall the portfolio must demonstrate a clear interest in sound/music. Please provide audio or audiovisual documentation as appropriate. You may also share examples of writing related to sound or music that you have produced (journal articles, reviews, curatorial statements etc.), though this is not required.' NO minimum number of works, NO duration, NO format prescribed. Delivery method has ALSO changed: no longer e-mail. Now: compress everything into a single .zip or .rar, upload to Google Drive / Dropbox / OneDrive only ('Please do not use any other service, such as Wetransfer or Rapidshare, since such services delete the files'), create an open sharing link, and submit it through the web form at http://tiny.cc/MiamApplication26-27Fall. Files must be named so 'the exam jury members will be able to understand its contents from the file name'. Portfolio contacts: Dr. Reuben de Lautour (lautour@itu.edu.tr) or Dr. Sair Sinan Kestelli (kestelli@itu.edu.tr). Portfolio submission does NOT replace registration at sis.itu.edu.tr — candidates who skip SIS registration 'will not be permitted to participate in the İTÜ MİAM Entrance Exams, even if a portfolio has been submitted by them.'

The 2026-2027 portfolio wording is close to written for his profile: his own electronic tracks plus any Max/SuperCollider/Pure Data patches count as 'examples of creative audio coding / programming'. No certificate level is published, but this is a hard practical block for someone starting from zero Czech. ENGLISH TRACK (IFS): English at B2, and critically NO IELTS OR TOEFL — proficiency is verified through an online conversation with a native speaker. The FAMO studium page lists eight ateliérs applying to both the bachelor and the follow-up master's, including Ateliér zvuku, and the IFS master's page independently names 'Sound design' among the MA specializations alongside Screenwriting and Directing, Cinematography, Production and Animation. The remaining mismatch is one of content, not existence: this is screen-and-stage sound engineering, whereas the candidate's stated goal is international DJ and music producer. Nothing in either track's published specialization list covers music production, electronic music composition, or club/dance music.
recommendation: The previous record treated this as a cheap Plan C fallback at ~3,200 EUR/year. That framing collapses once the English track is priced correctly. The route he can actually walk — English-taught, no IELTS, non-music bachelor accepted — costs 7,500 EUR per semester, 30,000 EUR for the degree, roughly 42,000-45,500 EUR all-in. The route that costs 3,200 EUR/year requires Czech language proficiency as a precondition of commencing study, which he cannot reach from zero by September 2027 while also building a portfolio. So the cheap option and the accessible option are not the same option, and the earlier entry conflated them. On top of the price, three things push this to AVOID for HIM specifically. First, fit: Ateliér zvuku and the IFS Sound design line train sound engineers for film, television, radio and theatre — screen and stage post-production. His goal is international DJ and music producer. Neither track's published specialization list contains music production, electronic music, or composition. He would pay 30,000 EUR to learn a genuinely skilled trade that is adjacent to, not aimed at, what he wants. Second, accreditation asymmetry: the Czech programme's national accreditation is well corroborated, but neither the IFS homepage nor its about-page makes any accreditation statement whatsoever, and the English MA's register status and degree title (MgA. or an in-house 'Master of Arts') are unconfirmed. Paying master-level money for a private award whose state recognition is unverified is exactly the trap to refuse. Third, money at risk before certainty: a 50% first-semester deposit, about 3,750 EUR, is demanded before formal acceptance and therefore long before a visa decision. That said, record the genuine positives honestly, because they are unusual and may matter if better options fail: no IELTS or TOEFL at all, a conversational rather than performance-based entrance, explicit willingness to assess non-traditional candidates individually, a confirmed master-level sound specialization, a portfolio requirement he has a full year to satisfy, and an April deadline that fits his timeline comfortably. If he ever reconsiders, he must first get in writing (1) the English MA's entry in the MŠMT register and the exact degree title, (2) confirmation the deposit is refundable on visa refusal, and (3) a syllabus showing how much music-production content, if any, the sound line contains. Until then this is a 30,000 EUR answer to a question he has not asked.

ALSO CORRECTED: the previous entry said 'no institutional exemption'. That overstates it — the annex records that three EPN (ESGT, INSEAC, EPN5) volunteered exemptions and ENJMIN was not among them, BUT the same document then asks the governing board to approve a scheme covering up to 10% of FI enrolments per programme, on the basis of national fees for students under a partnership convention and 50% of the differentiated fee for candidature libre non-EU students, with 'chaque EPN concernée' running its own academic/social selection. ENJMIN is one of the concerned EPN. So a 50% reduction (~1 970 €) may exist — he must ask enjmin@lecnam.fr directly. Confirm the 2027-2028 figure.
otherFees: CONFIRMED — CVEC 105 € per year, stated explicitly on Enjmin's own tariff sheet, payable in addition by both EU and non-EU students.
totalCost: 3 941 € + 105 € CVEC = 4 046 €/year at full rate, or roughly 2 075 €/year if he wins the 50% EPN exemption. Plus ENIC-NARIC comparability fee, plus Angoulême living costs (a genuinely cheap French town — materially cheaper than Lyon, Paris or Strasbourg).
scholarshipDetail: None programme-specific. Two real levers: (1) the Cnam/EPN 10% differentiated-fee exemption scheme described above — ask Enjmin; (2) national French routes (Eiffel, Campus France Tunisie, French Embassy Tunis) which must be pursued in parallel from autumn 2026.
entry: CONFIRMED — RNCP level 6 diploma / bac+3 (licence, licence pro, BUT, bachelor); or equivalent 3-year study requiring VES validation; or 3+ years professional/personal experience via VAPP. For a foreign diploma the official page requires an ENIC-NARIC France attestation de comparabilité (roughly 4 months processing, fee-paying) plus a B2 French certificate. Then the internal concours: creative dossier → written exam → oral exam. His BSc Software Engineering clears the academic bar; the concours does not.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — CONFIRMED. The official application page states the programme accepts candidates from diverse educational backgrounds, not limited to game design or music. No music degree, conservatoire training or prior audio employment is required. The practical filter is the creative dossier, not the diploma.
portfolio: Mandatory 'dossier créatif' answering a published brief (Cahier des charges et sujet du concours), released each December on enjmin.cnam.fr. Followed by a written exam and an oral. The 2027 brief was NOT yet published as of August 2026 — expect it mid-December 2026.
audition: No musical audition. Selection is: creative dossier → remote written exam → oral (remote or on site).
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE (2026, CONFIRMED on the official page): dossier deadline Friday 23 January 2026, 12:00 UTC+1; dossier results 5 March 2026; written exam 28 March 2026 (remote); oral-exam eligibility results 5 May 2026; orals 26–29 May 2026; final admissions 3 June 2026; term starts 7 September 2026. languageReq: CONFIRMED — the official Enjmin application page requires international candidates to supply a B2-level French qualification with the concours dossier. study: Sound design and audio production for games and interactive media inside a multidisciplinary game-production master; the six tracks (conception sonore, conception visuelle, ergonomie/UX, game design, management de projet, programmation) build games together. Track chosen at application (maximum 2 track choices allowed — confirmed on the official Cnam page). Detailed module maquette is not published online; request it from the scolarité.
recommendation: Still the single best thematic fit in this batch: game audio sits exactly on the seam between a software-engineering BSc and a career in sound, and the official page genuinely accepts any bac+3 background with no music degree. It is a real accredited state master (RNCP 38202) that fully supports a student residence permit, and the language gate is French B2 — a certificate he can realistically get, unlike IELTS which is not even asked for here. Three corrections to the previous entry: the non-EU fee is 3 941 €, not 3 879 €; the EU rate is 254 €; and CVEC is 105 €, both published on Enjmin's own tariff sheet. Also, an institutional exemption of up to 50% may be reachable through the Cnam's EPN scheme — worth an email, because it would halve the cost. CONDITIONAL rather than WORTH IT for one reason only: the gate is a creative dossier plus written and oral exams at a very small, very competitive national school, and he has no portfolio today. His entire 2026 has to go into producing game-audio work aimed at the cahier des charges that drops in mid-December. Second caution: this trains game sound designers, not DJs or record producers — the club/production ambition has to run alongside it. Practical sequencing: file the ENIC-NARIC attestation de comparabilité by September 2026 (four-month turnaround), sit a DELF/TCF B2 by November 2026, then answer the December brief.

correction: The record treats M1 and M2 as parallel entry points. They are not: M2 entry requires "avoir effectué un master 1 MAAAV", so there is exactly one door and it is M1. The record's gate 'Portfolio + exam/interview' should read CONCOURS with 16 places. And the record's cost band 'EUR 1.5k-5k/yr' is only just right for the wrong reason: Lyon 2 has CONFIRMED that from the 2026/2027 rentrée all extracommunautaire students must pay the droits différenciés — the previous blanket exemption is gone — so he pays the décret n°2026-385 master rate of €3,941/yr plus CVEC, not the ~€250 national rate.

Also CONFIRMED: Lyon 2's own page states its transitional exemption regime 'prend fin dès la rentrée 2026/2027' and that prior automatic exemptions no longer carry over — limited exemptions remain only in 'des cas très spécifiques'. entry: CONFIRMED — M1 entry by competitive selection, 16 places ('une promotion de 16 étudiants compositeurs'), open to holders of a licence in ANY field, or via VAPP with at least 5 years of professional activity in music. Semester 4 (30 ECTS) is the compulsory internship plus report and defence. Core competences: image analysis, orchestration technique, and command of digital audio workstations.
recommendation: All the previous entry's key claims are confirmed, and two things are now firmer: M2 entry is explicitly reserved for students who completed M1 MAAAV, so there is no lateral entry, and the mandatory equipment list is more specific than reported (1 TB+ SSD, Logic Pro X / Reaper / Cubase, audio interface with mic inputs, quality headphones) — a real 2 000–3 000 € cost on top of tuition. The AVOID is about eligibility, not legitimacy: this is a properly accredited public master (RNCP 39199) that supports a residence permit. But the gate closes it for him. Sixteen places a year, decided on three original compositions scored to three short films with PDF scores, and an official page stating the candidate must ALREADY be a composer commanding music notation and orchestration. He cannot write orchestral scores and has one year, not five. The unusual open-discipline rule (a licence in any field) makes it look reachable for a software engineer, and the M2 content — electronic music, synthesis, advanced mixing, composition for image — reads beautifully against his goals, which is exactly why it needs the explicit warning. Report it so he knows it exists; do not queue it for 2027. If film and game scoring genuinely attracts him, this is a 2029-2030 target reachable only after sustained composition study. The Enjmin sound-design route and the two engineering routes are the ones that fit the profile he actually has.

acceptsNonMusic: YES for the M1 entry point, and this remains the most explicitly CS-friendly admissions wording found in France: the accepted bachelor list names 'DE L'INFORMATIQUE' outright, so a Bac+3 in computer science is a named, accepted qualification for the Master 1 Généraliste. UNVERIFIED. He must request the current dossier from ensav@univ-tlse2.fr.

Taught content covers acoustic principles, analogue and digital audio technology, sound recording, editing, mixing and diffusion. CONFIRMED M2 Son exercises specifically: location sound recording (phonography), documentary sound creation, sound post-production, a written audio-technology dissertation, sound design for a visual sequence, collaborative work with the Image and Réalisation M2 students on the 'Filmer le Travail' project, and a final thesis with an accompanying audio or audiovisual product defended before a professional jury.
recommendation: Verification changed the verdict here. The admissions wording is still the most CS-friendly in France — 'de l'informatique' is a named accepted licence — and the route into the M1 Généraliste is genuinely open to him, dossier plus possible interview, no audition. But Son is not an M1 parcours: it is one of seven M2 specialisations, and ENSAV states that M2 Son entrants are expected to have already acquired sound basics during the school's own Licence and M1 years. So the realistic path is two-step and uncertain: get into the generalist M1, absorb the sound fundamentals there, then compete for one of the M2 Son places. Layered on top: it is cinema sound rather than music production, so it trains a boom operator or re-recording mixer, not a DJ or producer; it is French-language throughout (fine for him, though a C1 certificate will still be asked for); the dossier contents are not public so he must write to ENSAV; and the fee is now €3,950/yr rather than near-free. Good school, wrong craft for his stated goal, and a bottleneck between entry and specialisation.
