study: CONFIRMED sound modules: Electroacoustics & Room Acoustics (S7); Microphones and Loudspeakers (S7); Audio Signal Processing (S7); Sonic Perception (S8); Studio recording, mixing and mastering (S8-S9); Spatialized Sound covering stereo, object-based and binaural formats (S9). NEW DETAIL confirmed in verification: students choose between a Sound/Music specialisation and a Cinema specialisation in S8-S9, and the practical project is either a short film / sound fiction OR musical recordings with mixing and mastering — i.e. a genuine music-production route exists inside the degree. Graduates go into audiovisual and cinema (lighting, editing, sound, post-production) and into music careers in recording studios and live events.
recommendation: Technically the closest French public master here to a real sound-engineer training, and verification improved the picture on content: the S8-S9 split confirms an explicit Sound/Music track whose practical project can be musical recordings with mixing and mastering, not just film sound. With 18 students per year, studio time should be genuinely available. Three frictions, one of them new. First, entry: the programme is built as a continuation of its own L3 Image & Son, so a direct M1 entry from a Tunisian CS degree needs a case-by-case ruling — send an eligibility email well before February 2027. Second, money: the blanket partial exemption is gone, so this is now a €3,950/yr proposition rather than the near-free option previously assumed. Third, place: Brest is a long way from any electronic-music scene, which matters for someone whose goal is to become a working DJ. If they accept him, the curriculum-to-goal alignment is among the best in this batch; the risk is that they simply do not.

A new procedural problem also surfaced: Centrale Lyon's official application page says the International Master in Acoustics M1 goes through MonMaster, while also saying non-EU students must use Études en France plus candidature.ec-lyon.fr — the two are inconsistent for a Tunisian applicant, and the complementary late session is restricted to European applicants, so he cannot rely on a spring catch-up. On the merits it remains highly admissible: no portfolio, no audition, no music degree, no French-language gate, and an entry rule written for science graduates, with 'sound perception' and signal processing as a legitimate on-ramp to audio DSP and immersive audio. CONDITIONAL on three things. (1) He must book IELTS or TOEFL — unless he can evidence three years of instruction in English at SMU MedTech, which is the one waiver on the official page that could plausibly apply to him and is worth checking immediately. (2) His curriculum is software, not mechanics or physics; email the programme office with his transcript in autumn 2026 before spending money on the application. (3) It is acoustics engineering, not music production — the DJ/producer ambition runs in parallel, not through this degree. Cost is the full non-EU rate in France's second most expensive student city, so this is also the most expensive of the three viable options.

institution: Filmakademie Baden-Württemberg
programme: Filmton / Sounddesign (Diplomaufbaustudium – postgraduate diploma)
whyChance: Names engineering or computing as a welcome background; portfolio required, so build it
verdictWhy: Three independent blockers, any one of which is fatal: it demands German at B2 and he has none; it ends in a Filmakademie Diplom rather than a recognised master's degree; and admission runs through an in-person multi-day entrance exam including a 72-hour practical task that assumes existing studio and DAW craft. It is also film post-production, not electronic music.
correction: DEGREE TYPE: the input treats this as a master-level option. It is not a master's — it awards a "Diplom der Filmakademie Baden-Württemberg" from a Diplomaufbaustudium, not an accredited second-cycle degree. GATE: 'Exam/interview only' understates it — the exam includes a 72-hour set practical task plus a colloquium, in person. LANGUAGE: German B2 (Goethe B2 / TestDaF 4 / DSH-2) is required and is not flagged in the input.
qualification: Diplom der Filmakademie Baden-Württemberg. IMPORTANT CAVEAT NOW CONFIRMED: this is an institutional diploma, described by the academy as 'vergleichbar berufsbefähigenden Abschlüssen' of state art universities under Baden-Württemberg law — i.e. comparable to a professional qualifying degree. It is NOT an accredited M.A./M.F.A. and the pages do not state an EQF/ECTS master equivalence. If he needs a recognised master's degree (for a visa track, a later PhD, or recognition in Tunisia), verify this in writing first.
tuition: CORRECTED AND MORE EXPENSIVE THAN RECORDED: the €1,500 is PER SEMESTER, not a one-off. The academy's fee schedule is €0/semester for a first degree, €650/semester for a second degree or Projektstudium, and €1,500/semester for non-EU citizens, plus a €131.50 semester contribution for everyone. As a Tunisian national over 5 semesters that is roughly €7,500 in fees plus ~€658 in contributions — about €8,150 total, before living costs. The Diplomaufbaustudiengänge are exempt from the second-degree fee, but NOT from the non-EU fee.
scholarshipDetail: None found at the academy. External only: DAAD Study Scholarships (Film/Fine Art strand), Deutschlandstipendium. DAAD/Tunisia eligibility NOT re-verified in this pass. Note that DAAD art/film scholarships generally target accredited degree programmes, so the non-master status of this Diplom should be checked against DAAD's eligibility rules before counting on it.
entry: General/subject-specific Hochschulreife (with a talent clause, the 'Begabtenpassus' under §10 of the exam regulations, for applicants without Abitur — an extended interview substitutes). For the Diplomaufbaustudiengänge specifically, an 'entsprechende Vorqualifikation, etwa mindestens ein Vordiplom oder Bachelor' is required, submitted as an officially certified copy. Applicants must bring working knowledge of studio audio technology, microphones and DAW operation. B2 German per the academy's general standard.
acceptsNonMusic: CHECK — most likely YES, but with one conflicting signal. The programme-overview table requires only 'entsprechende Vorqualifikation, etwa mindestens ein Vordiplom oder Bachelor' with NO subject restriction, and no music degree is anywhere demanded — a BSc Software Engineering satisfies that on its face. However, the general application page summarises Diplomaufbaustudium entry as requiring a 'completed degree in a related field', which introduces a relatedness test that is not defined for Filmton. A software-engineering degree is plausibly 'related' to audio technology, but he must get this confirmed in writing before applying. The decisive filter in practice is the Pro Tools practical exam, not the bachelor subject.
portfolio: PARTIAL. Own projects/work samples are uploaded via the online portal, and applicants must clearly identify their individual contribution to each. Published technical limits (example spec, varies by department): video up to 1 GB, MP4 container, H.264 codec, data rate 15 MB/s, typically 5–7 minutes maximum. The exact number and duration of AUDIO samples required for Filmton/Sounddesign is not published — UNVERIFIED. Also submit certified copies of the Hochschulreife and of any Vordiplom/Diplom/Bachelor/Master.
audition: YES — pre-selection on the file, then an on-site Aufnahmeprüfung conducted IN PRO TOOLS. Confirmed: 'Die Aufnahmeprüfung für Filmton/Sounddesign wird mit dem Programm Pro Tools durchgeführt. Bewerber*innen sollten daher Grundkenntnisse in den Disziplinen Aufnahme, Sounddesign, Mischung und Bouncing mitbringen.' There is NO instrumental audition and no music-theory paper — the gate is a DAW competence test. This is by far the most learnable audition of the six programmes here.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 15 February, annually and without a year published on the programme page. The 2026 cycle ran with a portal opening on 7 January 2026 and the standard 15 February deadline (other departments had later dates: Motion Design 15 May 2026, Werbefilm Producing lateral entry 7 April 2026). For a 2027 start plan on 15 February 2027 and confirm when posted.
opens: The online portal opened 7 January in the current (2026) cycle. Expect a comparable early-January opening for the 2027 cycle — confirm.
duration: 4 semesters plus 1 diploma semester for the final project = 5 semesters total. ECTS NOT published — UNVERIFIED.
study: CONFIRMED: production of the audio layers of film and television. Year 1 concentrates on original sound recording on set; year 2 on post-production. Content includes location recording, sound design, mixing in a DAW, cinema film mixing and Dolby Atmos, working with Foley artists, film-music recording and mixing, and dialogue editing. Optional specialisations in media design and sound for games. Entirely project-based — students work on the academy's own film productions.
recommendation: The most realistically ENTERABLE film-sound route in Germany for someone without a music degree — the gate is a Pro Tools practical test he can genuinely train for, not a conservatory audition or a theory paper, and no music bachelor is demanded. But verification worsened two things: the fee is €1,500 PER SEMESTER (~€8,150 total, no funding found), and the award is an institutional Diplom rather than an accredited master's. And it makes film and game sound designers, not DJs or producers. Only worth an application if he decides he genuinely wants a screen-audio career alongside producing, and only after confirming both the degree recognition and whether his SE bachelor counts as 'related'.

study: Verified from the official curriculum and regulation. Semester A, both specialisations: Ήχος και Τέχνη / Sound and Art (6 ECTS) and Μουσική Πληροφορική / Music Informatics (6) — the latter teaching code-based representation of musical structures, Music Information Retrieval, SuperCollider, ChucK, Python, TensorFlow and LilyPond, plus hands-on additive, subtractive, FM, non-linear waveshaping, spectral, convolution, physical-modelling, granular and stochastic synthesis. Specialisation A adds Σύνθεση Ηλεκτροακουστικής Μουσικής (6) and Ηχητικός Σχεδιασμός / Sound Design (6); Specialisation B adds Τεχνική και Τεχνολογία της Ηχογράφησης / Recording Technique and Technology (6) and Ακουστική – Ψηφιακός Ήχος (6). Semester B: a compulsory 12-ECTS individual research project producing a complete creative work, plus Ραδιοφωνική Ηχητική Τέχνη, Διαδραστικά Ηχητικά Περιβάλλοντα, Σχεδιασμός Λογισμικού Ηχητικής Επεξεργασίας (audio-software design), ΜΟΥΣΙΚΗ ΠΑΡΑΓΩΓΗ / Music Production (6), Ηχητική Επένδυση and Ακουστικός Σχεδιασμός Χώρων. Semester C: 30-ECTS thesis. Article 7 and the curriculum page both guarantee that applied creative work "αντιστοιχούν κατ' ελάχιστον στο 50% του συνολικού διδακτικού έργου" — at least half of all teaching work is practical creation, not theory. Seminars named include MAX/MSP, PureData and SuperCollider, video-game sound design, radio art, acoustic ecology, new interfaces for musical expression, and rights management.
recommendation: On paper still the best-designed curriculum in the slice for his profile — an Informatics/engineering bachelor is named as eligible, there is no audition, the portfolio is formally optional, the interview can be done online from Tunis, tuition is only €2,700 with a real 30% chance of a full waiver, at least half of all teaching is guaranteed to be applied creative work, and Specialisation B literally contains a Music Production module. But three verified facts push it down. FIRST AND DECISIVE: the language of instruction is stated as Greek, with only some parts in English and no English track — he does not have Greek and cannot realistically reach delivery-level Greek by September 2027. SECOND: foreign degrees require formal DOATAP equivalence recognition, a slow bureaucratic step he must start well over a year out. THIRD, and the one to check before spending any effort: the most recent call on the official site is 2022-23, the site was last updated 31 May 2022, the announcements page is empty, and Article 1 of the regulation states the programme was established to run for eight academic years from its 2018-19 start — which expires with 2025-26. It may well have been renewed, but nothing published confirms it. Email the secretariat (kaiti@ionio.gr) to ask whether the programme is still running for 2027-28 and how much of Specialisation B is deliverable in English before treating this as a live option.

CONFIRMED verbatim: "Applicants must submit a preliminary credit recognition request directly to the Liszt Academy to determine whether the applicant's BA diploma can be accepted to apply for the programme, unless they have finished their BA studies at the Liszt Academy in the same field. Deadline: 31 March." Acceptable BA diplomas are defined in Annex 8 of the Academic Regulations for Students. acceptsNonMusic: Check — no longer a flat 'no', but genuinely uncertain and gated. Nothing formally bars a non-music BA, and the electroacoustic exam does NOT test classical composition craft. The binding gate is the mandatory preliminary credit recognition request, which decides "whether the applicant's BA diploma can be accepted to apply for the programme" against Annex 8 of the Academic Regulations — a software-engineering BSc may simply fail that check, and it is decided before the exam. The exam itself still assumes he can produce two credible electroacoustic works including one with live electronics and an acoustic instrument, write two style etudes, analyse 20th-century scores and graphic notation, and pass an electronic-music theory test. This is buildable in a year of hard work in a way a Bach fugue is not. Submit the credit recognition request early and treat its outcome as the go/no-go.
portfolio: MAJOR CORRECTION — this is far less classical than previously recorded. For the ELECTROACOUSTIC COMPOSITION specialisation, verbatim: "Presentation of a fixed electroacoustic music piece and another piece applying live electronics with an acoustic instrument", and "The pieces submitted together must not exceed 25-30 minutes." Style exercises for electroacoustic are: "1 short etude in the style of any significant 20th-century musique concrète composer" and "1 short etude in the style of significant 20th-century synthesis technique composer". THERE IS NO BACH FUGUE AND NO CLASSICAL SONATA REQUIREMENT for this specialisation — the fugue, the Viennese Classical sonata movement and the 20th-century etude apply ONLY to Classical and Applied Composition. Separately, the Stipendium Hungaricum course record states generically that applicants "are to upload sheet music of three of their own compositions (and recordings if possible)" and are first pre-screened on that portfolio — reconcile this generic wording with the specialisation-specific spec directly with the Academy.
audition: In person in Budapest, per the Academy's Stipendium Hungaricum page, verbatim: "All applicants are required to appear at the entrance examinations in person in Budapest, Hungary. The live entrance examinations cannot be substituted in any way", and on the SH course record: "Live streaming, video streaming, DVDs, CDs, or any other recordings are not accepted as a substitute." Exams take place late June / early July; candidates who clear the portfolio pre-screening are told their date during May. Components FOR ELECTROACOUSTIC specifically: formal analysis, written and oral, of a 20th-century instrumental work and an electroacoustic work; orchestration assessed as "MIDI sequencer orchestrating a chamber music piece for MIDI instruments or sampler" (not symphony-orchestra orchestration, which is the Classical track); score reading replaced by "Analysis of a contemporary graphic music notation"; a mandatory written test on the basics of electronic music (history from Varèse through Stockhausen, Xenakis, Chowning; sound parameters; waveform/spectrum/sonogram; sound types; tunings; sampling rate, Nyquist, bit depth; additive, subtractive, FM and granular synthesis); an oral practical computer task — mounting in ProTools or another DAW, algorithmic music in MAX/MSP or Pd, or sound synthesis in MAX/MSP, CSound, Pd or SuperCollider; and a personal interview on artistic beliefs, goals and general musical literacy. NOTE A CONTRADICTION: the admission-requirements page carries the heading "For applicants for the online entrance examination:", implying an online route exists, while the SH pages insist on in-person only. Resolve with international.office@lisztacademy.hu.

study: CONFIRMED programme description: one-to-one lessons with a composition teacher developing one's own compositions and analysing 20th- and 21st-century pieces; performance of orchestral and vocal final diploma pieces; composition-related special courses freely chosen by interest; master courses from visiting professors and artists; and explicitly "Possibility to deepen studies in the field of electronic music." Applicants admitted to Classical Composition who have not studied electronic music before may have to complete two semesters of 'The basics of electronic composition'. Note: no specialisation named "Elektronikus zenei médiaművészet" or "EZMM" appears on the official MA admission page — the three published tracks are Classical, Electroacoustic and Applied Composition.
recommendation: SUBSTANTIALLY UPGRADED on verification. This is the only fully-funded, English-taught, Tunisia-eligible route in the slice, and the electroacoustic entrance exam turns out to be about electroacoustic craft, not classical conservatory training — no fugue, no sonata, no orchestral score reading, and the orchestration test is MIDI sequencing. The real work he would have to do is genuine and specific: produce a fixed-media piece plus a piece for acoustic instrument with live electronics inside 25–30 minutes, write two style etudes in musique concrète and synthesis idioms, learn 20th-century analysis and graphic notation, and pass an electronic-music theory test. Two hard gates remain: the preliminary credit recognition decision on a software-engineering BSc, and a mandatory in-person exam in Budapest. IELTS 5.0 is a low bar he can clear easily. Also be clear this is art-music composition, not dancefloor production.

entry: TWO different statements exist and the international one is the one that governs his case. Course page: "Diploma accademico triennale di primo livello già conseguito o da conseguirsi entro la sessione di Febbraio (iscrizione con riserva)". Official international-students page: "Accademici di II Livello: possono richiedere l'ammissione Cittadini UE o NON-UE in possesso del Diploma di Triennio universitario o accademico (o equivalente), ottenuto in Italia o nel proprio Paese di provenienza. È inoltre necessario dimostrare di avere un minimo di 15 anni di scolarizzazione." Degree must be submitted as a scanned original plus certified translation plus DOV (Dichiarazione di Valore) from the Italian embassy/consulate, or alternatively a CIMEA Diplome certificate. Attendance minimum 80% of classes; a part-time route exists. Erasmus+ mobility up to 12 months within the biennio. Non-EU applicants must ALSO run the parallel Universitaly pre-enrolment through the Italian diplomatic mission in Tunisia, which normally closes in July with no extensions; Saint Louis advises starting it no later than January/February.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — RESOLVED, and this is the biggest correction to the prior record. The official international-students page states that admission to II livello is open to EU or NON-EU citizens holding a "Diploma di Triennio universitario o accademico (o equivalente)" obtained in Italy or in their home country, with a minimum of 15 years of schooling. A university bachelor is therefore explicitly acceptable — no Italian first-level music diploma is required of an international applicant. What he must supply is the DOV or CIMEA certificate. Residual risk: "Gli studenti la cui preparazione in entrata NON sia RITENUTA IDONEA all'ingresso diretto ai Corsi di livello Accademico, potranno accedere ai Corsi di livello pre-accademico" — if the commission judges his musical preparation inadequate he can be routed to a pre-accademico year instead.
portfolio: CORRECTED — the prior record's "3 pieces in a group of at least a trio" brief does NOT apply to him. That wording belongs to the performer accordions (Jazz, Composizione Jazz, Pop). The accordion that actually covers this course — "SONGWRITING + FILM TV SCORING + MUSICA APPLICATA + LIVE ELECTRONICS + MUSIC PRODUCTION + MIX E MASTERING" — omits the videoclip step entirely. And the official international-students page gives the applicable brief verbatim: "Composizione/Musica Elettronica/Musica Applicata: Prepara un link contenente il Portfolio (video, audio, spartiti) dei tuoi lavori più indicativi e recenti." So: a single link to a portfolio of his most representative and recent works (video, audio, scores). No number of works, no duration, no format prescribed.
audition: NO performance audition. The official Piano di studi publishes the exact test: "PROVA DI AMMISSIONE — 1) colloquio individuale; 2) test a risposte multiple su argomenti di tecnologia musicale: fondamenti di audio digitale, sintesi sonora, protocollo MIDI; 3) clausura di 5 ore in cui gli allievi dovranno produrre un brano in due versioni diverse senza vincoli stilistici, a partire da una traccia vocale che verrà fornita loro." That third element is a supervised FIVE-HOUR production test: build a track in two different versions, any style, from a supplied vocal. CRUCIAL for him: the international-students page states that for international candidates the admission tests "potranno essere sostenute online tra Gennaio e Giugno, in date da concordare individualmente" — online, individually scheduled, January to June; only if he chooses to sit them in person is there a single June session. Numero chiuso: maximum 20 students per academic year, from Saint Louis's own first-level courses or selected by audition among external candidates.
deadline: 30 April (standing annual rule: "dal 3 febbraio al 30 aprile" on the course page; "a partire dal 1° gennaio, entro e non oltre il 30 APRILE" on the international page). Late applications considered only against remaining places. In-person admission tests in June and September; online tests for internationals January–June. opens: 1 January for international applicants ("Le domande di ammissione ai corsi accademici, che devono essere inviate complete dei link per la pre-selezione, vengono accettate ogni anno a partire dal 1° gennaio"). The generic Italian course page instead says 3 February. Both are standing annual rules rather than a dated cycle, but confirm the 2027 edition.
duration: 2 years / 120 CFA — NOW VERIFIED from the official Piano di studi PDF (Year 1 = 60 CFA: Tecnologie e tecniche della ripresa e registrazione 1 (6) + Analisi compositiva (8) + Composizione musicale elettroacustica I (22) + Storia delle tecnologie elettroacustiche (8) + Tecniche compositive pop rock I (10) + Materie elettive (6); Year 2 = 60 CFA: Ripresa e registrazione II (6) + Forme, sistemi e linguaggi musicali (8) + Composizione musicale elettroacustica II (22) + Diritto d'autore e royalties (5) + Tecniche compositive pop rock II (10) + Tesi e prova finale (9)). Teaching is fortnightly, concentrated in two consecutive days, approx. 300 contact hours per year.
englishTest: No IELTS published. Language checked at interview.
study: Verified against BOTH the course page and the official Piano di studi PDF, and they differ in emphasis — read the PDF, not the marketing copy. Marketing prose: managing a music-production project through every phase, from creative idea to arrangement with real and virtual instruments, recording, mixing and mastering. The actual credit-weighted plan is: COMPOSIZIONE MUSICALE ELETTROACUSTICA I and II — 22 CFA each, by far the largest component; TECNOLOGIE E TECNICHE DELLA RIPRESA E DELLA REGISTRAZIONE 1 and II (6 CFA each) — the Music Producer specialisation strand, in which "ciascuno specializzando produrra' sotto la guida del docente due brani", taking two tracks from songwriting and pre-production (key, bpm, groove, feel, style) through arrangement with real and virtual instruments, rehearsals, recording and overdubbing in both a home and a commercial studio, microphone choice and placement, monitoring, executive production, mix and mastering, for himself and for third parties; TECNICHE COMPOSITIVE POP ROCK I and II (10 CFA each); ANALISI COMPOSITIVA (8) and FORME, SISTEMI E LINGUAGGI MUSICALI (8); STORIA DELLE TECNOLOGIE ELETTROACUSTICHE (8); DIRITTO D'AUTORE E ROYALTIES (5) covering copyright, royalties, licence, publishing, production and performance contracts; 6 CFA of free electives usable across any department; 9 CFA thesis and final work. The bienni are "costruiti intorno alle inclinazioni artistiche di ciascuno studente", with original productions and third-party commissioned work running through the degree.
recommendation: AVOID AS FIRST CHOICE — the ensemble-performance audition is a hard gate he cannot clear. Excellent value and a real degree, but the wrong door. If he wants Saint Louis, go through Sound Design or Live Electronics, both of which pre-select on portfolio rather than instrumental performance.

Excellent for a software engineer who wants to become a games researcher or graphics programmer; useless for becoming a producer, DJ or sound designer. Exclude from the audio shortlist.

THE RATIONAL SEQUENCE IS THE INVERSE: use an accredited master's (UCP Porto, Lusófona, or a funded ReSound place) to obtain the D4 visa and residence permit, then, once legally resident, add ProDJ's Master Producer as a €2,955 evening top-up in English while his status is secure. Never the other way round. One practical instruction: before paying anything, make ProDJ confirm in writing the enrolment fee (their own pages say €420 and €520), whether a DAW licence is included, and the exact total.

city: Belgrade (delivered in person at the Be…
institution: Univerzitet Metropolitan
programme: Master akademske studije MUZIČKA PRODUKCIJA (MAS Music Production), Fakultet digitalnih umetnosti
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's; portfolio required, so build it
verdictWhy: Taught entirely in Serbian, which he does not speak, and structurally blocked besides: he needs 240 ECTS and holds 180, so he would first pay for a fourth undergraduate year, then sit differential exams as a non-cognate applicant, then pay €4,500 for a one-year 60-ECTS degree with zero funding available to foreigners. Every part of that is money and time spent to end up with half a master's in a language he cannot study in.
correction: The record's gate 'Portfolio + exam/interview' is WRONG — no audition, no portfolio and no entrance exam are published anywhere; the only hurdle is documentary plus differential exams for non-cognate applicants. The record also fails to flag the two killers: the programme is Serbian-language only with no English variant on the accreditation register, and it requires 240 ECTS, which a 180-ECTS Tunisian licence does not meet.
qualification: Master akademske studije (MAS), 60 ECTS, 1 year, 2 semesters. Professional title: 'Master muzički producent' (Master Music Producer). Field declared as IMT (interdisciplinary/multidisciplinary/dual-field); areas: Dramatic and Audiovisual Arts + Management and Business. This is a genuine second-cycle academic degree, not a private certificate — confirmed by its presence in the national register of accredited programmes.
accreditation: ACCREDITED — CORRECTED and now pinned to a specific decision, replacing the previous record's 'specific accreditation decision number/date NOT published — UNVERIFIED'. The National Body for Accreditation and Quality Assurance in Higher Education (NAT) register of 21 July 2026 lists, under Univerzitet „Metropolitan“, entry 53: 'ИМТ МАС - МУЗИЧКА ПРОДУКЦИЈА, 03.06.2025, БС 20'. So: accredited 3 June 2025, field IMT, approved annual intake 20 students, valid 7 years to June 2032. This is newer than the Novi Sad programme's accreditation and comfortably covers a 2027 entry. Institution accreditation 04.06.2010 / 21.07.2017 / 21.01.2025.
tuition: EUR 4,500 for the degree — CORRECTED, and this is the single most important change to this record. The previous agent reported the non-EU rate as 'NOT PUBLISHED, do not assume it is EUR 4,500, private Serbian universities commonly charge non-regional students more' and built its whole recommendation on that warning. That is wrong. Metropolitan's official master admission page states, under 'Upis stranih državljana': 'Strani državljanin može se upisati na studijski program pod istim uslovima kao i domaći državljani, KAO I POD ISTIM USLOVIMA FINANSIRANJA ŠKOLARINE' — a foreign national enrols under the same conditions as domestic citizens AND under the same tuition-financing conditions. There is no separate foreigner tariff. A Tunisian therefore pays EUR 4,500, the same as a Serbian. The residual caveat is real but minor: the price tables themselves are headed 'ŠKOLARINE ZA NOVE STUDENTE (u EUR) za državljane Srbije i bivših republika SFR Jugoslavije', so the two official statements sit in tension and it is worth one confirming e-mail — but the correct working figure is EUR 4,500, not 'unknown and probably higher'.
otherFees: CORRECTED from 'not published'. Published figures: administrative fee 1,000 RSD payable with the enrolment documents; on enrolment all students must pay a 20% deposit (akontacija) — EUR 900 for this programme — plus a further 20% as the first instalment, no later than 1 October; enrolling after 1 September requires 40% of the tuition up front; the remaining balance runs as 11 monthly instalments of EUR 327.27 with no interest. DISCOUNT: candidates who enrol preliminarily and pay the 20% deposit by 31 March receive a 10% tuition discount, valid for the first year of studies only, and discounts cannot be combined. Nostrification/recognition of his Tunisian diploma is required and is charged separately by the recognising body. Health-insurance cost for foreign students — UNVERIFIED.
totalCost: EUR 4,500 tuition for the one-year 60-ECTS master, or about EUR 4,050 with the 31 March early-payment discount, plus ~1,000 RSD administrative fee and separate diploma-recognition costs, before living costs in Belgrade, visa and health insurance. If his degree is 180 ECTS he must first fund a fourth bachelor year at Metropolitan, which on the published bachelor table runs EUR 2,990–3,990 depending on programme — pushing the realistic total past EUR 7,000–8,500. Against the state Academy of Arts Novi Sad at EUR 1,800 for a comparable one-year MAS, this is roughly 2.5x on tuition alone. It fails his 'self-pay only if genuinely cheap' test.
scholarshipDetail: CONFIRMED: nothing a Tunisian master applicant can win. Re-checked the official Stipendije page. What exists: (1) competition-based full four-year bachelor scholarships for Serbian secondary-school pupils; (2) internal merit scholarships for existing Metropolitan undergraduates in years 2–4, six per year, one per faculty per year level, with fourth-years able to continue tuition-free into a master; (3) a dual-education package created with A+Crowd of Toronto offering free study, EUR 100/month and a guaranteed job, aimed at school-leavers entering IT, management or design. None is open to an incoming foreign master applicant in music production. Anything else would have to be negotiated directly with upis@metropolitan.ac.rs.
entry: MATERIALLY CORRECTED — the previous record's claim that entry requirements are 'NOT PUBLISHED' is WRONG. They are published in full at https://www.metropolitan.ac.rs/upis/upis-na-master-akademske-studije/ under 'Opšti uslovi upisa na Master studije'. (1) BASE RULE: 'Na studijske programe Master akademskih studija mogu se upisati studenti koji su prethodno završili četvorogodišnje i ostvarili uslov od 240 ESPB' — a completed four-year bachelor with 240 ECTS, the same gate as Novi Sad. (2) BUT THERE IS A PUBLISHED ROUTE OUT, which Novi Sad does not offer: 'Studenti koji su završili tri godine osnovnih akademskih studija i stekli 180 ESPB bodova imaju mogućnost da upišu četvrtu godinu akademskih studija Univerziteta Metropolitan i nakon završetka iste steknu zvanje diplomirani, na taj način ostvarivši uslov za upis na Master studije' — a holder of a three-year 180-ECTS bachelor may enrol in the FOURTH YEAR of a Metropolitan bachelor programme, obtain the 'diplomirani' title, and thereby qualify for the master. That is directly relevant to him if his Tunisian licence is 180 ECTS, at the cost of an extra year and extra fees. (3) COGNATE vs NON-COGNATE: 'Iz srodne oblasti, određuju se predmeti programa za nastavu u trajanju od godinu dana. Iz nesrodne oblasti, komisija određuje uslove upisa, predlaže nastavni plan i program, utvrđujući broj diferencijalnih ispita koje kandidat mora da položi.' A non-cognate first degree is expressly provided for, via differential exams set by a faculty commission. (4) DOCUMENTS: certified copy of the diploma (or graduation certificate); certified copy of the transcript of passed exams (or diploma supplement); birth certificate showing citizenship; two identical 3.5x4.5 cm photographs; proof of payment of a 1,000 RSD administrative fee; proof of payment of the first tuition instalment; ŠV-20 form (completed at the faculty, not purchased). (5) FOREIGN NATIONALS: they submit a NOSTRIFIED diploma stating the ECTS achieved, or, if recognition is still running, a certificate that the procedure is under way.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — CORRECTED from the previous record's 'probably yes on marketing copy, UNVERIFIED'. It is published policy, not marketing: the master admission rules expressly contemplate applicants 'iz nesrodne oblasti' (from an unrelated field) and provide the mechanism — a faculty commission sets the admission conditions and the number of differential exams. The programme page separately states the studies are intended for 'muzičare, muzičke producente, izvođače, kao i sve zainteresovane kandidate koji žele da kreiraju ili unaprede sopstvenu karijeru u muzičkoj industriji'. So a software-engineering graduate is admissible in principle, subject to differential exams. What he cannot avoid is that those differential exams, like the degree, will be in Serbian.
portfolio: No portfolio required — this is now a confirmed published finding rather than an unknown. The official master admission page describes the full procedure (online application, then scanned diploma and transcript, then referral to the faculty commission which issues individual admission conditions) and no portfolio appears anywhere in it, nor on the programme page. For an applicant with no body of work yet, this is a genuine structural advantage over both Novi Sad programmes.
audition: No entrance exam or audition for master entry — confirmed by the published admission procedure, which routes the application to a faculty commission that sets conditions and any differential exams rather than testing the candidate. (The prijemni ispit and the 'direct enrolment without an entrance exam' offer advertised elsewhere on the site relate to bachelor admission.)
deadline: No published application deadline — rolling admission. The binding dates are financial and immigration ones, not academic: 20% deposit plus 20% first instalment by 1 October; 40% up front if enrolling after 1 September; 31 March for the 10% early-payment discount; and, dominating all of these, the visa D and residence-permit timeline plus the diploma-nostrification timeline, which he should start at least six months ahead.
opens: Rolling, online via the university's application portal. After the online application the candidate receives procedural instructions and submits scanned diploma and transcript; the file then goes to the faculty commission, which issues individual admission conditions and any differential exams. Practical planning date: pay the 20% deposit by 31 March 2027 to secure the 10% discount for a 2027/28 start.
duration: 1 year / 2 semesters, 60 ECTS. CONFIRMED on the official programme page. Note the university's generic master page markets 'master diploma in 10 months'.
languageReq: Not published for this programme — UNVERIFIED. The published master admission rules impose no language certificate. In practice, delivery is Serbian-only, so functional Serbian is a de facto requirement whatever the paperwork says. Ask upis@metropolitan.ac.rs in writing.
englishTest: Not published — UNVERIFIED, and irrelevant: the programme is not taught in English, so no IELTS/TOEFL band would help him here.
study: CONFIRMED verbatim from the official programme page. Semester 1: AD511 Muzička produkcija 1 (audio technology, music software, arranging, microphone placement, instrument miking, basic mixing and mastering); AD560 Kreativna radionica zvuka (creative sound workshop — practical sound-design projects, experimentation with digital audio tools, sound installations, history of music-scenic performance); AD570 Novi mediji i tehnologija u performansu; Elective block 1 (MK520 Kreiranje digitalnog brenda / MK525 Digitalne marketinške kampanje); Elective block 2 (AD535 Advertajzing / AD565 Digitalna kultura). Semester 2: AD512 Muzička produkcija 2 (theory of analogue and digital recording and sound processing, equipment and techniques, sound formats and carriers); MG525 Upravljanje inovacijama i tehnologijama; Elective 3 (MG535 Digitalno preduzetništvo / MG545 Strateški menadžment i liderstvo); AD591 Završni rad muzičke produkcije – SIR; AD592 Završni rad – izrada i odbrana. Roughly a third of the taught credits are management/marketing, which a software engineer would handle comfortably.
recommendation: This record needed substantial correction and the programme comes out of it looking better on paper and worse in practice than the previous assessment implied. Three corrections he must hear. FIRST, the previous warning that the price is unknown and probably higher for a non-EU national is WRONG: Metropolitan's own admission rules state that foreign nationals enrol under the same conditions and the same tuition-financing conditions as Serbian citizens, so he pays EUR 4,500 — the published figure, not a mystery. SECOND, the claim that admission requirements are unpublished is also WRONG: they are published in detail, and they are more accommodating than anything at Novi Sad — 240 ECTS required but with an explicit route for a 180-ECTS three-year graduate to complete a fourth Metropolitan bachelor year first; non-cognate first degrees expressly admitted via commission-set differential exams; no entrance exam; no portfolio; rolling admission; full document list published. THIRD, the accreditation is now nailed down: NAT register, accredited 3 June 2025, approved intake 20, in-person Serbian delivery. So it is a real, state-recognised, visa-supporting second-cycle degree — the AVOID verdict reserved for master-priced non-degrees does not apply. What actually blocks him is language and money, not admissions. The programme is accredited for Serbian-language in-person delivery only — the register carries no English-language flag, unlike Metropolitan's own IT and business masters — so an Arabic/French/English speaker cannot follow it in September 2027. And EUR 4,500 (EUR 4,050 with the March discount), or EUR 7,000+ if he must buy a fourth bachelor year first, is 2.5x the state Academy in Novi Sad for a private-university degree with no scholarship he can win. Action if he still wants it: one e-mail to upis@metropolitan.ac.rs asking (a) to confirm in writing that the EUR 4,500 rate applies to a Tunisian national given that the price table is headed for Serbian and ex-SFRY citizens, (b) whether his specific BSc counts as 240 ECTS or requires the fourth-year route, (c) how many differential exams a software-engineering graduate would be set, (d) whether any part of the programme can be followed in English, and (e) whether they issue the enrolment documents needed for a Serbian study visa D.

portfolio: None.

study: Ten modules, VERIFIED: (1) Sound and Capture; (2) Processors and Production Phases; (3) Capture History and Advanced Techniques; (4) Analysis Keys for Productions; (5) Introduction to Mixing and Mastering; (6) Mixer History and Studio Performance Optimisation; (7) Mixing Architecture; (8) Dynamic Control and 3D Depth Mixing; (9) Official Waves Level A Certification; (10) Mixing According to Musical Styles. It is also aimed at the wrong craft: pure studio engineering, with no synthesis, no sound design, no composition, no live performance and no DJ content anywhere in the ten modules. For a software engineer who wants Pro Tools and Waves credentials cheaply it has genuine, narrow utility — but that is a €4,000 skills purchase for someone already living in Madrid, not a postgraduate route into Europe for a Tunisian graduate. acceptsNonMusic: CHECK — leaning against him on the letter, but "or a related field" is a real opening. The rule requires a "BA (or equivalent) in Fine Arts, Sound Arts, Literary Writing and Literary Translation, Performance Art or a related field". A Software Engineering BSc is not obviously in that list, so he must argue relatedness — and the argument is genuinely available here because selection turns on the digital portfolio and the proposed artistic project rather than on a conservatory transcript, and because the strand itself teaches electronic music, new media and interactive work where coding is native. Send cap@hkb.bfh.ch a portfolio plus an eligibility question before investing in an application.
portfolio: PARTIALLY VERIFIED — the general spec is confirmed, the Sound Arts numbers are genuinely not published. Official wording for all specialisations: a "digital portfolio with a representative selection of your current and previous work", submitted with the online application. The ONLY precise quantity published anywhere on the page is for Literary Writing/Translation: "one or more of your literary texts of a minimum of 20 pages and a maximum of 50 pages". There is NO published number-of-tracks, duration or file-format limit for Sound Arts. Correction to the prior record: the published contact for this master is cap@hkb.bfh.ch (not soundarts@hkb.bfh.ch) — write there for the Sound Arts portfolio spec.
audition: CONFIRMED — an INTERVIEW, not an audition. "After application review, selected candidates are invited for an interview" in which "the presentation of a selected work from the portfolio, literary texts, musical works, live performances, etc. can be part of this discussion". No music-theory examination, no instrumental audition, no sight-reading. Whether the interview can be held remotely is NOT stated — ask cap@hkb.bfh.ch, since a trip from Tunis is otherwise required.

study: CONFIRMED: an interdisciplinary master across four specialisations — Fine Arts, Sound Arts, Literary Writing and Literary Translation, Performance Art — which you may combine multidisciplinarily. In Sound Arts you "design creative musical media projects and compositions and realise interactive pieces", working in "electronic music, sound art and new media" and investigating how "sound, image and space influence each other": electronic sound design, composition in media contexts and interactive sound installations. You develop your own individual or collective artistic project as the spine of the degree, taught by "competent musicians and guest lecturers" through to a final presentation. HKB's associated BA Sound Arts explicitly welcomes DJs, pianists, composers and sound artists — the same division teaches this MA strand.
recommendation: Still the least gate-kept artistic route in Switzerland for him: no theory exam, no instrument audition, an interview rather than a performance test, teaching available in English and French, 24/7 studio access, and a sound-arts culture whose sister BA openly welcomes DJs. Two caveats are now firmer than before. First, the money: the confirmed fee is CHF 2,550 per semester from AS 2026/27, roughly CHF 5,100 a year — no longer a cheap option, and the highest fee in this slice. Second, the framing: this is sound ART, not commercial dance-music production, so his DJ/producer ambition must be presented as an artistic practice with a real project proposal. Still the strongest Bern option for him, but only with funding secured.

NOTE TWO THINGS: (1) RECORDED works are accepted, not only written scores; (2) works may be UNFINISHED ('même inachevées'). NO minimum number of works, no length limit and no file format are specified anywhere in the document — this is the least prescriptive portfolio requirement found in the entire territory.
audition: NOT A PERFORMANCE AUDITION. VERBATIM, the full épreuve is: 'Présentation par le candidat de compositions écrites ou enregistrées, même inachevées. Évaluation par le jury du parcours artistique du candidat, de sa maîtrise suffisante des langages musicaux et des techniques instrumentales et/ou électroniques. Évaluation des connaissances générales. Entretien de 20' avec le jury d'admission, sur les motivations du candidat et ses aspirations.' So: portfolio presentation + jury assessment of musical-language and instrumental AND/OR ELECTRONIC technique + general knowledge + a 20-minute interview. The phrase 'et/ou électroniques' is important — electronic technique alone can satisfy the technical assessment, so no instrument is strictly required. But 'maîtrise suffisante des langages musicaux' still demands real musical literacy.

entry: CORRECTED and materially narrower than previously reported. The official 2025 curriculum grants DIRECT admission only to a BSc in Medialogy (Copenhagen). study: Confirmed structure from the official 2025 curriculum: semester 1 = project 15 ECTS + course 5 ECTS + two electives 10 ECTS; semester 2 = same shape; semester 3 = industry placement OR game production, 30 ECTS pass/fail; semester 4 = Master's Thesis 30 ECTS. "After the first semester, you must choose whether you want to continue in the Medialogy programme or specialise in Sound and Music Computing." Confirmed SMC-track modules: Immersive Sonic Experiences (15 ECTS), Sonic Interaction Design (5 ECTS), Sound and Music Perception and Cognition (5 ECTS, also available as a general-track first-semester elective). AAU's problem-based learning means every semester is built around a group project. recommendation: Still by far the best real option for him in the Nordics, but downgraded from A after verification. The second honest caveat is unchanged: this is sound and music COMPUTING - immersive audio, sonic interaction design, perception and cognition, project-based engineering work - not DJing, not mixing records, not A&R. It makes him an audio developer or technical sound designer who produces on the side. Use it as the funded backbone of his plan, with craft learned independently; if the scholarship does not land, EUR 15,490/yr is a hard self-pay number.

study: Semester 1: project 'Adaptive Media Systems' plus 'Machine Learning for Media Experiences', choosing two electives from Sound and Music Perception and Cognition (recommended for this specialisation), Real-Time Computer Graphics, Mobile and Wearable Computing, Narratives in Interactive Systems. Semester 2: project 'Immersive Sonic Experiences' plus the course 'Sonic Interaction Design', with two electives from Multi-Sensory Interaction and Media Cognition, Signal Processing for Interactive Systems, Embodied Interaction, Spatial User Interfaces, Game Research and Development. Semester 3: a company internship, DADIU Game Production (the Danish national game-production programme), a regular project, or a semester abroad. Semester 4: thesis only. Everything is problem-based group project work. Honest framing for him: this is audio ENGINEERING and interaction design — spatial audio, VR/AR sound, AI for sound, new interfaces for musical expression — not beat-making, mixing records or DJ craft.
recommendation: The previous entry's claim that this programme is dead is WRONG and must be corrected before he sees it. The old standalone smc.aau.dk / 'Sound and Music Computing' master URL does redirect into AAU's 'programmes without admission' area, which is what caused the false negative — but the content has moved: it is now a live 2-year, 120-ECTS, English-taught specialisation inside the MSc Medialogy at the Copenhagen campus, and it is open for application. This remains the single most natural destination in this whole slice for a computer-science graduate who wants to work in sound. Two real obstacles: (1) the hard ECTS gate — 10 ECTS each of programming, media technology and interaction design/UX, with no possibility of topping up, and no pre-assessment, so he is guessing until he submits; (2) money — EUR 7,745 per semester, about EUR 31,000 all in, with the only escape being one of roughly 15 government scholarships awarded across the whole university, which do at least pay tuition in full plus about EUR 1,500 a month. It will not, on its own, make him a DJ or a record producer; it will make him someone who can build audio technology and design interactive sound.

During the interview the panel "can test a candidate's knowledge in a narrower field of specialization as well as his or her general cultural knowledge. You will also be tested whether or not your English or Estonian language skills are sufficient." No numeric IELTS/TOEFL threshold is published on the admission pages.
acceptsNonMusic: Check — no music-degree requirement is published, and the MA admission page states no subject restriction at all. Contact katrin.puur@eamt.ee (study programme registrar) or admissions@eamt.ee before applying.
portfolio: Three requirements, verbatim: (1) "The applicant must present his electroacoustic compositions in a recording or live performance (a total of approximately 15 minutes)." (2) "Participate in an oral examination where the Board may assess the candidate's knowledge of their area of specialization and their understanding of related cultural issues (colloquium)." (3) "Submit a portfolio of their original works." Scores are required only for the classical Composition track, not this one. Assessment criteria: artistic mindset and originality of creative ideas; logic of development and expressiveness of the works; technical refinement and appropriate technical choices; fulfilment of length and genre requirements; understanding of cultural and specialty-specific issues. Graded 0–10.
audition: Entrance examination = presentation of the ~15 minutes of electroacoustic work (recording OR live performance) + an oral colloquium. Graded 0–10. Format: "EAMT prefers to audition you in person, but those foreign applicants, to whom traveling is not possible, are encouraged to submit an original video recording... candidates can only pass the entrance audition by video recording if the examination panel has no doubts about authenticity of the recording, the quality of the recording is sufficient for evaluation and the candidate's performance meets the highest standards, clearly exceeding the admission threshold." So remote is possible but held to a higher bar. Auditions/interviews last approximately 20–30 minutes.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The 2026/27 admission period ran 1 February – 3 July 2026 via DreamApply. No 2027/28 dates published as of July 2026.

duration: 2 years / 120 ECTS. EAMT states curricula are established on "the assumption that the standard volume is 30 ECTS per semester and 60 ECTS per academic year", and DreamApply gives 2 years — so 120 ECTS, though the figure is not printed on the programme page itself.
study: One curriculum with four fields: classical composition, electroacoustic composition, audiovisual composition, recording arts. Electroacoustic and audiovisual studies "combine musical, artistic and technical creativity", with the Academy's sound and multimedia studios and editing rooms "offering a learning environment under the guidance of acknowledged professionals". Creative mentorship model — students are not tied to a single professor. The curriculum collaborates with national and international art and music institutions and students take part in international festivals and workshops each year, including the annual COMMUTE Festival. Note EAMT's curricula page warns: "Applying for admission to a Master's curriculum in another field may require completing prerequisite subjects during Bachelor studies" — directly relevant to a software-engineering entrant.
recommendation: English-taught, in an active Northern European electronic-music scene, €7,700/year non-EU (moderate for a conservatory), €75 application fee, real studio access, and a portfolio spec a self-taught producer can actually meet — roughly 15 minutes of electroacoustic work presented as recordings, with no scores required for this track. Main obstacles: it is judged as composition, so club tracks alone will read poorly against criteria like 'logic of development'; the colloquium tests cultural and specialist knowledge; remote examination is allowed only where travel is impossible and is held to a higher bar; and there is no quantified funding for a Tunisian, so realistically this is €7,700/year self-pay plus living costs.

acceptsNonMusic: YES — and unusually explicitly so for this applicant. The only stated degree condition is "Relevant Bachelor's degree"; there is no music-degree, music-theory or conservatory requirement anywhere on the page. Decisively, the published evaluation criteria for Artistic and/or design practice state: "Demonstrations of artistic and/or design work related to sound, e.g. artistic or commercial projects, publications, performance/exhibition documentations or other works of art and/or design in the audible domain. Proven musical competence of any kind (e.g. violin playing, DJ'ing etc) is a plus." DJing is named, in Aalto's own words, as a positive. The programme also states it "brings together a multicultural group of students with very versatile skills and backgrounds", and the toolset it teaches (creative coding, physical computing, generative composition) presupposes technical entrants. Selection is portfolio-, motivation- and interview-driven. Aalto does not publish an enumerated list of "relevant" fields — that single point remains unverified; confirm with arts-admissions@aalto.fi.
portfolio: EXACT published spec: "The portfolio is presented and discussed during the application interview. The form and format of the portfolio is free; however, the portfolio should be online so that it can be accessed via Internet with a common web browser (Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox or Safari). The access to the portfolio might be password protected on the responsibility of the applicant. The portfolio may consist of individual art/design works, documentation of exhibitions and/or performances etc. The portfolio must showcase the applicant's previous academic, professional and/or scientific activity in a diverse and comprehensive manner. The applicant should be able to present the portfolio in 10 minutes." Maximum file size 1.0 GB; file named Portfolio-lastname-firstname.pdf; document language English. NOTE THE ODD HYBRID: Aalto asks for an online, browser-accessible portfolio AND names a PDF file — in practice submit a PDF that carries links out to hosted audio/video. NO fixed number of works, no per-track duration and no audio format are specified. Also required: motivation letter, max 4,000 characters, single PDF, English, explaining "why they wish to apply to the degree programme in question, what their particular areas of interest in this field are, and what their objectives and hopes are regarding the studies at the School of Arts, Design and Architecture"; and a CV (single PDF, English) with personal data, education, work experience, exhibitions, publications, awards and grants, study trips and positions of trust. "Lack of this application document will adversely affect the evaluation of the application."
audition: NO live audition and NO on-site test. Two-phase selection, both remote-capable. Phase I scores Suitability/Motivation letter plus Other areas of competence (CV); "the scoring and/or ranking of the first phase doesn't affect the final, 2nd phase scoring." Only the highest-ranked are invited onward, with at least 7 days' notice. Phase II: "applicants complete one or more assignments within the given time. The assignment(s) can be written or audible and is (are) based on the provided material and/or given topic. The assignment(s) is (are) submitted in electronic form as text file(s) with possible supporting graphs and images and/or as audio file(s)." Plus "a 30-minute interview" (Aalto states interviews "may be conducted remotely"), in which the portfolio is presented and discussed. Important caution published by the programme: "the application process aims at a balanced group of different kinds of students... even exceptional skills and talent in one field don't automatically guarantee that the applicant would be selected. Furthermore, the more there are applicants with a similar profile, the harder the competition is."

study: CORRECTED SCOPE (quoted from the official page). Aim: "to explore, discover and comprehend the emerging digital technology and its aural impact in society; to find and exploit the possibilities it opens to acoustic communication, sonic interaction and new interfaces for musical expression". Named areas: "sound and music computing, sound art and auditory culture, sonic interaction design, artificial intelligence applied to sound design and music, game audio and acoustic branding". Tools and skills explicitly listed: "creative coding, physical computing, digital fabrication, sonic interaction design, extended reality, generative composition methods and other emerging technologies" — note how directly a software-engineering BSc maps onto creative coding and physical computing. Teaching is "project-oriented, combining practice with theory, hands-on with minds-on", with "intensive workshops" and "tutored studio work". Every student writes a Personal Study Plan (PSP); year 1 is programme/major core, year 2 is electives, minors and the thesis. Research anchor: the Sound and Physical Interaction research group (SOPI). CONFIRMED CROSS-REGISTRATION: "Majority of our students take courses from the Sibelius Academy Department of Music Technology, and these studies can be included to the MA degree." Closest internal partners: Aalto Department of Signal Processing and Acoustics and the Master's Programme in Information Networks.
recommendation: The strongest Nordic option on the list by a wide margin, and the only one where the official evaluation criteria literally say "Proven musical competence of any kind (e.g. violin playing, DJ'ing etc) is a plus". No music degree, no instrument audition, no on-site test, no theory exam — a remote 30-minute interview plus a written-or-audio assignment. His software-engineering BSc is an asset rather than a liability here: the major teaches creative coding, physical computing and generative composition, and it sits next to Signal Processing and Acoustics. He can also pull Sibelius Academy Music Technology courses into the degree, which is the practical bridge from sound design toward music production. TWO REAL CAVEATS, which is why this is B and not A. First, money: EUR 20,000 per year, EUR 40,000 over the degree, with the only route to affordability being a competitive Excellence Scholarship that the programme is free to award to nobody — his admission and his funding stand or fall on the same application. Second, content drift: this is sound design, sonic interaction and sound art for media, installation and games, not club-music production or record mixing; the DJ/producer ambition is served obliquely. Practical plan: sit IELTS by spring 2027 at the latest (target 7.0 to leave headroom over the 6.5/6.0 floor), spend the next twelve months building a portfolio that pairs finished electronic tracks and DJ work with at least one technical/interactive sound project that shows the coding side, and note he can rank TWO study options on one form — pair this with a second Aalto or Finnish option rather than wasting the slot.

entry: CONFIRMED. The written test syllabus signals the content: cinema culture (films, professions, equipment), 'esthétique sonore et culture musicale', and applied science — powers/roots/logarithms, acoustic units, periodic and sinusoidal motion, Fourier's law, production and propagation of sound (reflection, absorption, diffusion, focusing, refraction, diffraction), microphones/amplifiers/loudspeakers, oscillating circuits, impedance, hearing and loudness (Fechner's law, Bel/Decibel/Phone, Fletcher diagram), DC/AC and Ohm's law. The document adds: 'C'est uniquement la « compréhension », le « principe » des notions énumérées ci-dessus, qui sont pris en compte.'
recommendation: The international concours is designed for exactly his nationality profile, and the diploma requirement is genuinely open to a software-engineering BSc. But everything else is against him: four years, French-only teaching and testing, €32,000 tuition with a solvency declaration required before he would even know if he is admitted, a cinema-culture and musical-culture written paper, and a maximum of 7 admitted per year ACROSS all seven departments. There is no music-production, record-mixing or electronic-music track. This is a prestige self-pay fallback, viable only if the French Embassy in Tunis funds him outright — not a primary target for a DJ/producer goal.

institution: Abbey Road Institute Germany

whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's; portfolio required, so build it

It is not a Bologna second-cycle qualification, it carries no ECTS-bearing master's status, and it is not a German staatlich anerkannter Hochschulabschluss. RULE IT OUT for a candidate whose objective is a master's degree and who needs a student visa: a German student residence permit is granted for study at a recognised Hochschule, and a private diploma course is a much weaker basis. Whether the diploma is staatlich anerkannt was NOT confirmed — UNVERIFIED, but nothing found suggests it is.
accreditation: Private institute founded by Abbey Road Studios; no German higher-education accreditation identified. UNVERIFIED.
tuition: €16,000–€18,000 FOR THE WHOLE COURSE. Verbatim from a German trade source citing the institute: 'Die Kosten für das Studium betragen circa 16.000 bis 18.000€', with 'zwei Zahlungsoptionen: Vorauszahlung und Ratenzahlung'. THIS IS BY FAR THE MOST EXPENSIVE OPTION IN THE ENTIRE SWEEP — five to eight times the total tuition of any public master here, for a qualification that is not a degree. FIGURE SOURCE: trade press, not read from an Abbey Road Institute fee page directly — treat as INDICATIVE, though a course-fees page exists at abbeyroadinstitute.de/kurse/advanced-diploma-music-production-sound-engineering/course-fees/.
otherFees: UNVERIFIED

scholarshipDetail: UNVERIFIED — none identified.
entry: Not published on the pages read — UNVERIFIED. Private institutes of this type typically require only a portfolio or interview and no prior degree.
acceptsNonMusic: YES in practice — no music degree is required. But the award is not a master's, so this does not answer the brief.
portfolio: UNVERIFIED — not published.
audition: NO AUDITION AND NO EAR-TRAINING EXAM published. UNVERIFIED.
deadline: UNVERIFIED — rolling intakes typical.

languageReq: Berlin: English throughout. Frankfurt: bilingual. No CEFR level published — UNVERIFIED.
study: Curriculum 'developed by renowned sound engineers from Abbey Road Studios and education professionals', covering three areas: 'Music Theory and Production', 'Sound Engineering and Acoustics' and 'Management and Business'. In pure content terms this is the closest thing in Germany to the record-making craft he actually wants — recording, mixing, studio practice, taught in English by industry engineers. The problem is the qualification, not the teaching.

institution: BIMM University
programme: MA Popular Music Practice (Production specialism)
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's; portfolio required, so build it
qualification: MA Popular Music Practice — CONFIRMED verbatim 'Awarding institution: BIMM University'. BIMM holds its own UK degree-awarding powers, so this is a genuine university master's rather than a validated diploma, including at the Berlin and Dublin campuses.
tuition: MAJOR CORRECTION — the Berlin and Dublin figures are now VERIFIED, resolving the biggest open question. UK CAMPUSES: UK/Irish £9,950 full-time (£4,975/yr part-time); EU/EEA/Swiss and non-EU both list at £15,950/yr, with an automatic £6,000/yr discount for EU/EEA/Swiss passport holders (not him) and a £2,000 Early Acceptance Discount for non-EU students who accept and pay the deposit by the published date — so c. £13,950 net for him. BERLIN (bimm-institute.de): German/EU/EEA/Swiss/UK €11,950/yr, International/Non-EU €16,950/yr with a €4,000 deposit, less the €2,000 Early Acceptance Discount = c. €14,950 net. DUBLIN (bimm.ie): EU/IE €8,450/yr, International €16,950/yr. So Berlin is cheaper than the UK campus but NOT dramatically so — the earlier assumption that the German operation would be materially lower is only partly right. Deposits: UK £4,000 self-funded / £1,000 if government-funded; Berlin €4,000 non-EU / €1,000 EU. Berlin remaining balance due 8 weeks before start; a payment plan spreads the balance over 8 monthly instalments Sept-April.
scholarshipDetail: MAJOR CORRECTION — BIMM's current scholarships page lists only THREE awards, not the long portfolio previously reported. (1) Launchpad Bursary — a tuition reduction for the duration of study, but only 10 students per year and explicitly 'across BIMM Music Institute's UK campuses', so it does NOT apply to Berlin or Dublin. (2) Open Day, Audition & Interview Travel Bursary — UK travel only. (3) Fair Access Fund — UNDERGRADUATE students only. The IDLES, Joan Armatrading, Fatboy Slim/Martlets, Jim Aiken, MusicMaker, Black Music Coalition x Wretch 32, Universal Music UK Sound Foundation and Creative Futures Bursary awards are NOT on the current page — treat them as lapsed. The International Hardship Bursary is confirmed CLOSED. BIMM Berlin states outright: 'BIMM University Berlin does not offer scholarships directly.' BUT Berlin signposts an external option he can genuinely use: the SBW Berlin Scholarship for International Students, which may cover shared student housing, a monthly living allowance, tuition fee support and travel assistance, for applicants aged 18-30 who show academic capability, financial need and social/community engagement; applications accepted year-round with no fees. The Creative Futures Discount (£1,000/€1,000) is BIMM-alumni-only and does not apply to him.
entry: CONFIRMED verbatim: 'A good degree (normally 2.2 or above) or significant experience in a relevant field.' And: 'Overseas students for whom English is not their native language may be required to meet a minimum English language requirement of an Academic IELTS 6.5. We require a minimum of 6.0 to be achieved in each band.' And: 'All applicants will be subject to interview and a portfolio may also be requested for Recognition of Prior Certified or Experiential Learning (RPCEL).' Contextual offers with reduced entry requirements exist for applicants meeting certain criteria. Tunisia does NOT appear in BIMM's international entry-requirements country table — he must email admissions for an equivalency ruling on the SMU MedTech BSc.
acceptsNonMusic: Yes — the most permissive degree-subject wording of any real master's in this slice. The requirement is 'a good degree (normally 2.2 or above)' with NO subject restriction stated anywhere on the page; the alternative is 'significant experience in a relevant field'. A software-engineering BSc satisfies the letter of the requirement. The real filter is the compulsory interview, not the degree subject.
portfolio: CONFIRMED verbatim and CONDITIONAL, not automatic: 'All applicants will be subject to interview and a portfolio may also be requested for Recognition of Prior Certified or Experiential Learning (RPCEL).' A portfolio is therefore requested when prior learning needs accrediting, not as standard. No number of works, duration or format is published — UNVERIFIED. In practice, for a Production-specialism applicant with no music degree, expect to be asked for a demo, so build one regardless.
audition: INTERVIEW IS MANDATORY for every applicant — verbatim: 'All applicants will be subject to interview.' No instrumental audition for the MA. Whether the interview runs online from Tunisia is not stated on the page — UNVERIFIED, but BIMM operates an international agent network and offers a UK travel bursary specifically for people attending auditions and interviews in person, implying both modes exist. Confirm remote interviewing with admissions.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. No MA application deadline is published for the UK campuses; admissions appear rolling. Two dated anchors in the current cycle: the Early Acceptance Discount cut-off of 06 August 2026 for non-EU students (worth £2,000 / €2,000, applies at UK, Berlin and Dublin), and BIMM Berlin's advertised final application deadline of 12 August. Expect equivalent early- to mid-August 2027 dates. Note Berlin also requires the balance of fees 8 weeks before the course starts.
opens: UNVERIFIED. Postgraduate entry is Apply Direct, not UCAS. BIMM Berlin's site currently shows a 'Final Application Deadline – 12 August' banner for the in-progress cycle, indicating a late-summer close in Berlin.
duration: Full-time one year (winter, spring and summer trimesters) or part-time two years. CONFIRMED verbatim: 'Credits: 180 FHEQ / 90 ECTS (EU)'.
study: Five modules across three trimesters, CONFIRMED: Popular Music Practice and Research (theory applied to your practice, research training, one-to-one mentoring); You and the Popular Music Industry (refine direction, audit skills, audience/market research, liaise with industry stakeholders); Popular Music & Technology (technology's role in creative practice and entrepreneurship, mentoring and workshops); Exploring Collaborative Practice (negotiation, leadership, teamwork; curate a symposium or run group project work); Major Project (the extended culminating piece). The Production specialism is described verbatim as: 'specialising in production will stretch your skills in recording, mixing, mastering and more. Get involved in extraordinary recording projects and build your portfolio for a sustainable career.'
recommendation: Still the best combination of accessibility and geography in this slice, and the Berlin fee question is now answered: c. €14,950/yr net after the Early Acceptance Discount, versus c. £13,950 in the UK — Berlin is cheaper and avoids the UK visa entirely, but it is not the bargain that was hoped. Strengths: any bachelor subject at 2:2 is acceptable, IELTS 6.5 is attainable with preparation, English-taught in Berlin, 90 ECTS, portfolio only conditional, and the same BIMM University award in Berlin, Dublin or the UK. Weaknesses: no BIMM scholarship reaches a non-EU student at Berlin or Dublin (Launchpad is UK-only, Fair Access is undergraduate-only), the interview is mandatory and is the real gate, and this is a project-supervision MA culminating in a Major Project rather than a taught mixing curriculum — he must arrive already able to produce. Chase the external SBW Berlin Scholarship for International Students; it is the only route to meaningful funding here.

institution: Catalyst – Institute for Creative Arts and Technology, Berlin (degree validated by Plymouth Marjon University…
programme: Creative Production (Music) MA

Full-time €6,028 per semester (two instalments per year) or €11,693 per year paid annually (3% discount). Part-time €3,678 per semester or €7,134 per year. Plus a non-refundable enrolment fee of €895 per study year, which includes visa support. So roughly €12,588 for the full-time year, or about €16,000 over two years part-time. Monthly and extended payment plans exist.

Only price reductions: €1,000 early-application/priority tuition discount, 3% discount for annual payment, a further discount for paying in full, and €500 off total tuition for combining a summer short course with a degree within two years.
entry: 'Bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline, with an Honours grade (e.g. 2:1 in the UK university system) or be in the final year of studies for one.' Non-standard entry exists: applicants lacking the minimum education requirement 'may be assessed on the strength of a professional CV and portfolio, which must demonstrate a solid background in artistic practice and research'. English at 'IELTS 6 (referred to as B2 in Germany and other EU countries)', evidenced either by an official certificate or by taking Catalyst's own online assessment — which is a real advantage given he has not sat IELTS. Submission is via an online portal: transcripts, portfolio with work samples, professional references, and a project proposal.
acceptsNonMusic: Check — likely yes, but not stated as such. The requirement is a bachelor's 'in a relevant discipline' at Honours level, and students are said to come 'from a wide range of backgrounds'. Software engineering is arguably relevant to creative coding and spatial audio, and the non-standard route offers a fallback, but the page does not name computer science and selection turns on the project proposal and portfolio. Ask Admissions directly whether an SE BSc satisfies 'relevant discipline'; the FAQ invites exactly that conversation.
portfolio: Not quantified anywhere public — UNVERIFIED as to number and duration. Confirmed components: a portfolio with work samples; a detailed project proposal framed as practice-led artistic research (the school runs free online prep workshops on artistic and practice-based research specifically to help applicants shape it, and offers to send a recent graduate's final project portfolio as a reference on request); a sample of research/academic writing; academic transcripts; professional references; and personal/educational documentation. The proposal, not the music, is the decisive artefact.
audition: None — confirmed: there is no interview or audition requirement; the assessment is a digital submission reviewed by admissions. A voluntary call with the Admissions team is offered and, given the 'relevant discipline' question, he should take it.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Published for the 2026 intake (start September 2026): priority deadline 28 February 2026 (early-enrolment bonus); visa-required applicants 30 April 2026; EU/visa-exempt 5 June 2026; late applications until 28 August 2026 'subject to availability'. For a September 2027 start expect the same pattern — priority around late February 2027 and a visa-required deadline around 30 April 2027 — but the 2027 dates are not yet published. As a Tunisian national he is bound by the EARLIER visa-required deadline, not the general one.
opens: Rolling, with a priority deadline that carries a €1,000 tuition discount for early enrolment.
duration: 1 year full-time or 2 years part-time. Credit total (UK credits or ECTS) is NOT published on the course page or fees page — it sits in the downloadable course guide/syllabus. UNVERIFIED.
study: Five modules forming one arc: Imagine (detailed research proposal, research contract and work plan agreed with a supervisor), Contextualise (critical review of existing concepts, literature, practices and methods in the field), Investigate (survey then depth), Present (creation, public presentation and documentation of outward-facing work), Synthesise (a substantial original work or body of works). Three concurrent year-long workshops: Creative Sound Practices — weekly sessions moving 'between modular synthesis, spatial sound, creative coding, field recording, improvisation and sound installation', with the explicit aim being 'not technical mastery but the development of a personal methodology'; Contexts of Listening (musicology, sound studies, philosophy, critical theory — Oliveros, Schaeffer, Attali, Fisher, Butler, Derrida and others); and Supervision (one-to-one plus group critique). Guest artists have included Nicolas Collins, Bob Ostertag and Kaffe Matthews. The page is emphatic and repeats the warning twice: 'This is not a studio engineering degree, a vocational production course or a genre-based music programme. It is postgraduate artistic research' and 'This programme is not suited to those seeking vocational production training, DAW certification or a genre-based music course.' Encouragingly for him, past students have come 'from various backgrounds, including songwriting, house, techno, folk, jazz ... experimental and electroacoustic music'.
recommendation: The best environment on this list for a would-be electronic producer and the only one with no language barrier: Berlin, the Funkhaus, English-taught, no audition, one year, and an English test he can sit through the school itself rather than booking IELTS. Two hard caveats. It costs about €12,588 for the full-time year with no funding he can access — label it the self-pay fallback and nothing else. And the school states twice, unprompted, that this is postgraduate artistic research and explicitly not vocational production training or a genre-based course; the admissions decision hinges on a practice-led research proposal, which is a genuinely unfamiliar genre of writing for a software-engineering graduate and the thing he would need months of preparation for (their free prep workshops exist for exactly this reason). Judged purely as a career move, the Berlin network, the Funkhaus studios, the symposium and the radio station may be worth more to a DJ career than any credential in this batch — but he would be buying access, not being funded into it.

institution: Consortium: IADT Dún Laoghaire (Dublin, coordinating school), Universidade Lusófona (Lisbon), Lithuanian Acad…

Submit either as a SINGLE hyperlink to a portfolio website or as ONE compiled audio or video file. The selection team states it can realistically review 10–15 minutes of material per application, so keep the total inside that. All documents in English.

Two honest caveats. First, competition — a maximum of 24 places worldwide, so this cannot be his only application. Second, and more important for his stated goal, the subject is sound design for MEDIA ARTS: screen sound, sonic arts, theatre and game audio. It will make him an excellent sound designer with strong production technique and a European network, but it will not on its own train him as a club/dance-music producer or DJ the way Berklee's elective tracks would. Apply for it as the funded anchor; treat the DJ/producer craft as something he builds alongside it.
