Because no spec is published, he should email the Music and Technology course coordinator via CSM.FullTimeCoursesCork@mtu.ie in autumn 2026 to ask precisely what evidence the panel expects — well before the 31 May non-EU deadline. This is the single highest-value email he can send.
audition: Not a formal instrumental audition. CONFIRMED: an interview in July/August for shortlisted candidates, 'if required', at which the applicant must display musical competence. deadline: CONFIRMED and CRITICAL. The course page states: 'Irish/EU: 31st August 2026. Non-EU: 31st May 2026' — PRIOR CYCLE, confirm the 2027 dates. Either way the pattern is unambiguous and decisive: THE NON-EU DEADLINE IS THREE MONTHS EARLIER THAN THE EU ONE. languageReq: CORRECTED — the prior record overstated its certainty. It claimed as 'VERIFIED' that Cork School of Music programmes sit in MTU's Level 2 band at IELTS 6.5 with no section below 6.0. The official MTU English-language page is INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT on this point. Under the heading 'Applicants to Courses at MTU CORK Campus' — and Cork School of Music is in Cork — the bands are given as: Level 1 = all undergraduate programmes plus postgraduate ENGINEERING, MATHEMATICS AND COMPUTER SCIENCE programmes (IELTS 6.0 with no section below 5.5); Level 2 = postgraduate MEDIA AND BUSINESS programmes (IELTS 6.5 with no section below 6.0). CSM is not named in the Cork list at all. It is only under the separate 'Applicants to Courses at MTU KERRY Campus' heading that Level 2 is defined as 'Postgraduate Media, Business, CCAD and CSM programmes' — which looks like an MTU copy-paste error, since CSM and CCAD are Cork institutions. So 6.5 with no band below 6.0 is the PROBABLE requirement and the safe planning assumption, but it is NOT verified for Cork, and there is a real possibility this CS-and-engineering-adjacent programme falls under Level 1 at 6.0/5.5. MTU's own page adds: 'Please note some programmes have a higher requirement in English Language. You should contact the International Office for further details.' HE MUST EMAIL AND CONFIRM — the difference between 6.0/5.5 and 6.5/6.0 is months of preparation for someone at a working-English baseline.
englishTest: Plan for IELTS Academic 6.5 with no section below 6.0 (Level 2), but CONFIRM IN WRITING with MTU International Office — the Cork-campus band table may place this programme at Level 1 (IELTS 6.0, no section below 5.5). NEW AND USEFUL: alternatives are confirmed for both levels. Level 2 accepts PTE Academic 63 (no section below 59), TOEFL iBT 90 (Listening 23, Reading 21, Speaking 22, Writing 23), Duolingo 120 with no individual section below 110, Cambridge English 176 (no section below 169). Level 1 accepts PTE 59, TOEFL iBT 80, Duolingo 105 with no section below 100, Cambridge English 169. The Duolingo option is materially cheaper and faster to sit than IELTS and was not flagged in the prior record. Test must be taken within 2 years of programme start; MTU accepts the IELTS One Skill Retake if retaken within 60 days of the original test.
study: CONFIRMED VERBATIM: 'The first two semesters (September-January and January-June) each have a 30-credit load, delivered through a combination of 5-credit mandatory and elective modules.' A full-time student normally studies SIX modules per semester. Independent work is undertaken over the final June–August period for a 30-credit project. Core studies: computer music, recording studio, acoustics and psychoacoustics, sound synthesis. Electives are drawn from multimedia, music performance, engineering and computer science — which is exactly where his software engineering background becomes an asset rather than a liability. Teaching staff span music performance and composition, art, multimedia, business, electronic engineering and computer programming, with integration discussed in computer-music classes and industry seminars. ACCS (Accumulation of Credits and Certification of Subjects) and part-time routes exist with flexibility on module load.
recommendation: STILL THE STANDOUT OF THIS SET — but two corrections to the prior record, one of them important. FIRST AND MOST IMPORTANT, the English requirement was stated with false confidence. The prior record said it was 'VERIFIED' that Cork School of Music sits in MTU's Level 2 band at IELTS 6.5 with no section below 6.0. It is not verified. MTU's official page defines the CORK campus bands as Level 1 (all undergraduate plus postgraduate engineering, mathematics and computer science) at IELTS 6.0/5.5 and Level 2 (postgraduate MEDIA AND BUSINESS programmes) at 6.5/6.0 — CSM is not named in the Cork list at all. CSM appears under Level 2 only in the KERRY campus table, which is almost certainly an MTU error since CSM is a Cork institution. Plan for 6.5 with no band below 6.0 as the safe assumption, but email the International Office to confirm, because if this programme is treated as Level 1 the bar drops to 6.0/5.5 and saves him months. MTU's page explicitly invites this query. SECOND, useful alternatives to IELTS were missed: Level 2 accepts Duolingo 120 with no section below 110, TOEFL iBT 90 with stated section minima, and PTE Academic 63 — Duolingo in particular is cheaper and faster to sit from Tunisia. THIRD, a small missing fee: a mandatory €7 USI membership levy payable before Semester 1, on top of the €500 deductible acceptance fee. Also note the page contains stale text giving the non-EU deadline as 31 May 2025 alongside the header figure of 31 May 2026 — ignore the stale line, but the 31 May pattern is the point. EVERYTHING ELSE CONFIRMS: €4,000 EU total and €13,500 non-EU, NFQ Level 9 with 90 ECTS verbatim, two 30-credit taught semesters of six 5-credit modules each plus a 30-credit June–August project, Honours 2.2 in a cognate area, the July/August musical-competence interview, and formal RPL with a direct instruction to contact the course coordinator. ACTION PLAN: (1) email CSM.FullTimeCoursesCork@mtu.ie this autumn asking two questions — which English band applies to CR_GMUTE_9, and what evidence of musical competence the interview panel expects; (2) confirm the course code is on the current ILEP; (3) sit the English test by March 2027; (4) submit by 31 May 2027, three months ahead of the EU deadline; (5) apply for the Government of Ireland International Education Scholarship in parallel. This is his primary target.

study: Composizione e pratica elettroacustica I/II in Max, Kyma and Pure Data (spectral modelling, time shifting, delay lines, Fourier analysis and resynthesis, spectral processing, Jitter); Laboratorio di improvvisazione e composizione interattiva I/II (real-time composition, ecosystemic procedures, immersive listening, OpenMusic/Bach/Cage from IRCAM); Live Electronics I/II (real-time processing interacting with voice and acoustic instruments on Max8, Kyma and Pure Data; the historical repertoire of Nono, Manoury, Di Scipio, Stroppa and David Tudor; software engineering, ecosystemic composition, machine learning); Linguaggi di programmazione I/II (SuperCollider, Processing, Arduino, JavaScript, and in the study plan C++ with the JUCE framework for building Audio Unit plug-ins); Sistemi interattivi e installazioni d'arte I/II (sensors, augmented instruments, Arduino, BITalino R-IoT, Raspberry Pi, hidden Markov chains and Gaussian mixture models, sound art, kinetic sculpture, multimedia performance); 9 CFA electives; thesis.
recommendation: The best intellectual fit and the worst admission odds - treat it as a stretch target, not the primary application. It converts his coding skill into a coursework advantage like nothing else in this batch, and it is an official MUR degree at about a third of NABA's price. But the earlier draft understated the gate badly: he would have to arrive able to present his own acousmatic or instrument-plus-live-electronics piece, discuss the compositional method of Stockhausen's Kontakte or Parmegiani's De Natura Sonorum, and pass a Max8 or Pure Data test. That is 18 months of deliberate study, in Italian-inflected art-music vocabulary. It is also worth saying plainly: this is installation and concert-hall electroacoustic music, not club or dance-floor work. If his goal is genuinely to DJ and release dance records, Music Production or Sound Design serve him better and admit him more easily; keep Live Electronics as a second-choice application only if he falls in love with the material during 2026.

study: Recording studio practice (microphone technique, critical listening, editing, mix setup, vocal, ensemble, string and brass recording); Mix (progressive supervised individual sessions, plug-ins, reverbs, effects, multi-stylistic professional sessions); Mastering both in the box and with dedicated outboard; Fondamenti di acustica degli strumenti musicali e della voce. recommendation: The safest admission and the wrong ambition - take it only as a deliberate career hedge. Everything about the gate suits him: no portfolio, no audition, a studiable written exam and a practical mix test on material the school hands him. And it produces a real MUR degree plus Pro Tools 210M/310M certification, which is directly employable. But it trains the engineer who serves other people's records, not the artist who makes his own - if the goal is to DJ and release music, Music Production is the same money for a far closer fit, and Sound Design is equally winnable with more distinctive skills. Only pick Mix & Mastering if he consciously wants a studio-technician day job to fund the DJ ambition. Before committing, get the price of the extra Pro Tools courses and the 210M/310M certifications in writing - it is the only figure in this batch the school refuses to publish.

scholarshipDetail: (1) SAINT LOUIS INTERNAL SCHOLARSHIPS — partial exemptions from the fees, worth €500 to €2,500 per year of the course for full-time attendance, restricted to first- and second-level academic courses. FIRST-YEAR criteria are two, jointly: an ISEE below €22,000 AND merit. For a student who has NOT come through Saint Louis pre-academic courses, the merit test is 'la media delle prove di ammissione deve essere pari o superiore a 26/30', with a 1-point penalty on the average for each subject carried as a debit. Application window 2-31 JULY each year. SECOND-YEAR renewal: ISEE still below €22,000, plus at least 50 CFA with a weighted average of 26/30 or higher by the September session. Not available for years fuori corso. AS A NON-EU APPLICANT HE WOULD NEED AN ISEE PARIFICATO built from consular-legalised Tunisian tax and property documents to prove the €22,000 test — the same exercise described in the IED entry, and it must be started months ahead. (2) *** PREMIO GIORGIA MILETO — CORRECTION: HE ALMOST CERTAINLY CANNOT WIN THIS. *** It is worth 40% to 100% of the annual fee, €2,000-€4,500 per awardee, but it is awarded 'tramite audizioni aperte a tutti i corsi di STRUMENTO E CANTO del Dipartimento di Jazz e di Popular Music', held as a LIVE CONCERT in a Rome venue with the candidate backed by a professional resident band; to reach the audition he must submit audio/video of two pieces played IN A GROUP (duo, trio, quartet). It is a performer's award, open to 'musicisti, cantanti e songwriter'. A sound-design student who does not perform is outside its scope. Do not budget for it. (3) BORSE DI COLLABORAZIONE — annual competition for student collaboration grants across all departments; amounts UNVERIFIED. (4) LAZIODISCO / DiSCo LAZIO REGIONAL SCHOLARSHIP — awarded through a separate regional call on income and merit. Non-EU students are eligible and, under Art. 13(3) d.p.c.m. 9/04/2001 (quoted verbatim in the IED entry), are automatically classified 'fuori sede', the highest-value bracket. Saint Louis confirms compatibility: 'Gli esoneri parziali dal versamento delle quote sono compatibili con le borse di studio LazioDisco, è possibile conseguire entrambi' — so a Saint Louis internal exemption AND a LazioDisco award CAN be stacked. This is the only genuine stacking opportunity found anywhere in this batch. LazioDisco amounts for Saint Louis students UNVERIFIED. (5) Convenzione with Sapienza and other partnership discounts — details UNVERIFIED. (6) FINANCING via Banca Sella and Intesa Sanpaolo 'per Merito': the Banca Sella application requires an Italian tessera sanitaria/codice fiscale and, above €7,000, an Italian income document from the borrower — effectively closed to him before he is resident.
entry: VERIFIED and quoted. 'Level II Academics: EU or NON-EU Citizens holding a Three-year University or Academic Diploma (or equivalent), obtained in Italy or in their home country, may apply for admission. Proof of a minimum of 15 years of schooling is also required.' The degree must be submitted as a scanned original with certified translation and a Declaration of Value (DOV) from the Italian Embassy or Consulate, or alternatively a CIMEA Diplome certificate. A Tunisian BSc after 13 years of school plus a 3-year degree gives 16 years — but he must count this precisely against his own transcripts, because falling short of 15 diverts him to Pre-Academic courses.
acceptsNonMusic: THIS IS THE REAL BARRIER, AND IT IS WORSE THAN PREVIOUSLY RECORDED. The programme page states: 'Bachelor of Sound Technician graduates gain access by right to one of the two-year degrees listed above. Graduates in other disciplines who have prior experience in phonics may enter upon entrance examination.' He is a graduate in another discipline WITHOUT prior experience in phonics (audio engineering). On the published wording he does not currently meet the alternative route. Compounding this, the international page warns: 'Students whose incoming preparation is NOT CONSIDERED SUITABLE for direct entry into Academic Level Courses will be eligible for more appropriate Pre-Academic Level Courses' — i.e. he risks being offered a pre-academic year instead of the biennio. GET A WRITTEN RULING FROM THE SEGRETERIA DIDATTICA BEFORE INVESTING IN THIS PATH, and use the year to 2027 to build demonstrable audio work.
portfolio: VERIFIED and favourable. The pre-selection route differs by department. For Jazz/Pop/Songwriting/Classical the candidate must record four songs performed, at least three in a group of at least a trio — that would be impossible for him. BUT for 'Composition/Electronic/Applied Music' the requirement is: 'Prepare a link containing Portfolio (video, audio, sheet music) of your most indicative and recent works.' A self-built production portfolio is therefore admissible on the correct track. For the Sound Technician course there is no pre-selection at all, only an aptitude interview. He must confirm which pre-selection route the Sound Design biennio follows.
audition: No performance audition on the portfolio track. After pre-selection there are ADMISSION TESTS — the course page says they run 'over two consecutive days'; the international page says they can be taken online between January and June on individually agreed dates, or in a single in-person session in June. Results feed a merit ranking (graduatoria). Test contents are published in the Course Catalog.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates for 2027 entry, but the pattern is stable and the dates are early. For a SEPTEMBER/OCTOBER 2027 START he should expect: applications 1 January - 30 APRIL 2027; Very Early Bird payment deadline 30 APRIL 2027 (15% off); Early Bird admission completed by 15 JUNE 2027 (10% off); registration fee €240 by 30 May 2027; internal scholarship application 2-31 JULY 2027; regular upfront payment by 5 September 2027. The binding constraint is 30 April 2027 — which means the portfolio, the DOV/CIMEA and the language evidence must all be ready by roughly March 2027.
opens: VERIFIED. Applications for admission to academic courses, complete with pre-selection links, are accepted each year from 1 JANUARY and no later than 30 APRIL. Late applications are considered individually at the discretion of management, subject to places. Admission tests: online between January and June on individually agreed dates, or a single in-person session in June; the course page also mentions June and September sessions. Scholarship applications: 2-31 July annually.
duration: 2 years, 120 CFA (Diploma Accademico di II livello). VERIFIED CONTACT HOURS: 'Approximately 300 hours of classes per year', with classes 'mostly held on a fortnightly basis', mandatory attendance of at least 80%. A part-time route exists and may extend the course beyond 3 years. 300 h/year is roughly 10 hours a week — LOW, and he must check that it satisfies the Italian study-visa full-time expectation before relying on it.
englishTest: IELTS is NOT the binding requirement and is not mentioned. Language proficiency is assessed in the aptitude interview, in 'English (or Italian)'. If the biennio is delivered in Italian he will need real Italian; if an English route exists, English suffices. CONFIRM WHICH — this is the highest-value single question to put to the Segreteria.
study: VERIFIED module list. Sound Design — techniques and concepts of sound design and audio post-production, recording, construction and manipulation of sound effects for film, TV series, video games and media, Pro Tools with a detailed focus on the audio post-production and sound-design workflow, plus other sound-manipulation software and plug-ins. Wwise Nonlinear Interactive Audio — audio nonlinearity in interactive video-game sound design using Audiokinetic Wwise. Audio Sampling and Post Production — Kontakt and its engine, modulators, envelopes, zones, groups, mapping, and building a custom sample library. Sound Branding — analysis, composition, implementation, mix and mastering of a sound brand. Technologies and Techniques of Audio Restoration — restoration and audio forensics from film to tape to digital, in specialised laboratories. Mix e Mastering — mix and mastering sessions finalising multimedia products. Students are also involved in projects with the Saint Louis Composition and Music Applied to Images departments and with the film/animation departments of RUFA, Vigamus and others. Career outcomes: Sound Designer, Sound Restorer, audio post-production sound engineer, Sound Designer for gaming.
recommendation: This remains the best SUBJECT fit in Italy for him and the cheapest genuinely accredited second-level route in this batch — a real Diploma Accademico di II livello in Sound Design and Audio Post-Production, taught on Pro Tools, Wwise and Kontakt, from a MUR-authorised music school with an AEC membership and a Sapienza relationship. But three corrections change the plan. FIRST, THE PRICE: it is not €2,800 a year. As an international student he pays €7,230 to €8,500 a year depending purely on how early he commits, plus €240-€290 registration, €140 regional tax a year, a €500 diploma exam fee and chargeable extra Pro Tools modules — about €15,700-€18,400 over two years. The €1,270-a-year gap between Very Early Bird and Regular instalments is the single easiest saving available to him anywhere in this batch: commit and pay by 30 April. SECOND, ADMISSION IS NOT ASSURED: the published rule gives access by right only to Sound Technician graduates, and admits 'graduates in other disciplines who have prior experience in phonics' by entrance examination. He has none. He must (a) get a written ruling from the Segreteria Didattica now, and (b) spend the year to April 2027 producing demonstrable audio work so that the 'prior experience' claim is real — the good news is that the Composition/Electronic/Applied Music pre-selection route accepts exactly that, 'a Portfolio (video, audio, sheet music) of your most indicative and recent works', with no group-performance requirement. THIRD, KNOW WHAT HE IS BUYING: this is sound design for film, TV, games and restoration, not electronic music production or DJing. If his goal is genuinely to become an international DJ/producer, this teaches him the professional audio craft underneath that ambition but not the ambition itself. Practical sequence: written ruling on eligibility and on teaching language first; then Italian to B2 if the answer is Italian; DOV or CIMEA started by autumn 2026; ISEE parificato paperwork started in spring 2027 for the 2-31 July scholarship window; application filed by 30 April 2027 to capture the 15%; and LazioDisco pursued in parallel, since the school confirms in writing that its own exemptions and LazioDisco awards can be held together.

acceptsNonMusic: YES, CONDITIONALLY — CONFIRMED, and this remains the single most important finding for him. The official rule, quoted verbatim from the how-to-apply page, is: 'A Bachelor's degree in Music, OR proof of an equivalent level of knowledge and skills tailored to the programme.' A BSc in Software Engineering plus a strong producer portfolio is precisely the case that second clause exists for, and the department operates a formal Preparatory Course Master as an explicit third admission outcome for applicants who audition below master level. A pure DJ with no keyboard will not pass.
audition: CONFIRMED EXACTLY, no corrections. Three stages. (1) PORTFOLIO of unlisted YouTube links (links only, never the files): candidate introduces him/herself in English at the start of the video, max 10 minutes; THREE own DAW productions (originals) — 'Show the entire production and then talk us through which tools and techniques you've used'; a video of the candidate playing his instrument, with 'jazz skills' shown where present — 'Playing (jazz) piano and/or guitar is a plus!'; optionally live-performance footage and notated/arranged scores via a shared cloud folder. (2) 'LIVE' AUDITION, may be held online, 20–45 minutes: discussion of the portfolio, presentation of the candidate's vision, demonstration of playing skills 'on your preferred instrument AND piano', and an EAR TEST ('The main subject teachers also may take time to test your ears, as this is an important tool of an emp-er!'). Stated priority: 'The most important focus, however, will be on the quality of your writing and your vision.' (3) MASTER INTERVIEW, ~20 minutes, with the jazz master coordinator on the Master Research Project, assessing investigative attitude and critical thinking. Audition documents/video due by the application deadline (1 March or 1 May depending on when you applied).

All must be taken AT A TEST CENTRE (home/online editions not listed). Exemptions: native English speaker (ID copy), or a Bachelor completed at a University/College with a full English programme. NOTE for him: his BSc at SMU MedTech Tunisia may well qualify for the exemption if it was fully English-taught — get a written statement from SMU and ask Team Admissions (bo.conservatoriummaastricht@zuyd.nl) whether it is accepted; that could save him the IELTS entirely. recommendation: VERIFIED AND STILL THE STRONGEST TARGET IN THIS SET. Every material claim in the previous record checks out against the official pages, and the two fee figures (€2,694 / €12,280) are now confirmed from Zuyd's own primary fee regulation rather than a calculator. It is a genuine NVAO-accredited, English-taught, publicly funded Dutch second-cycle Master of Music that fully supports a student residence permit, whose written entry rule explicitly admits 'equivalent level of knowledge and skills' instead of a music bachelor, and whose portfolio brief is literally 'three of your own DAW productions'. Two corrections to carry forward: (a) budget ~€12,700–€12,900/yr for a 2027-2028 start, not €12,280 — the rate is re-indexed annually; (b) he may not need IELTS at all if his SMU BSc was fully English-taught, which is a listed exemption — check this first, it is free. Action plan for September 2027: (1) email Team Admissions (bo.conservatoriummaastricht@zuyd.nl) NOW to ask whether an English-taught Tunisian BSc satisfies the language exemption, and otherwise book IELTS Academic for spring 2027 targeting 6.0+; (2) through 2026-27 produce at least three finished, fully mixed original tracks and rehearse narrating the production chain in English on camera; (3) START PIANO AND EAR TRAINING IMMEDIATELY — this is the one thing that will fail him, and it is the only part that cannot be crammed; (4) in autumn 2026 write to head of programme Irja Zeper (irja.zeper@zuyd.nl), state the software-engineering background plainly, and ask directly whether his profile is assessed as 'equivalent level' or whether he should apply for the Preparatory Course Master; (5) apply via Studielink before 1 MARCH 2027 and simultaneously apply for the Zuyd Excellence Scholarship, the NL Scholarship and the Educations.com €5,000 award. Go in with eyes open: this is a real degree at a real price, not a cheap option.

verdictWhy: This is the one door in the sweep whose published entry list actually names his degree — IADT writes "computational science" into the accepted bachelors — and there is no live audition, only an online interview after a scored file. Two things he must resolve first: he must sit IELTS and clear 6.0 (a low bar, but he has not taken it), and he must build three pieces totalling 10-15 minutes with written reflections, because the Erasmus Mundus scholarship that makes the €15,000 affordable is won on the strength of that portfolio alone. Without the scholarship the €15,000 plus three-country living costs is beyond what he said he can pay, so treat the scholarship as the whole point of applying.
correction: The record's cost band 'EUR 5k-15k/yr' is WRONG — €15,000 is the total for four semesters (€7,500/yr), not per year. The record's gate 'Portfolio + exam/interview' is right only in the sense of an ONLINE interview: there is no exam and no audition. Most importantly, the record does not flag that IADT's published entry list explicitly includes computational science, which makes this by far his strongest eligibility match; nor that no 2027 call is yet published. NOTE ON DUPLICATION: indices 47, 48, 50 and 51 are the SAME single Erasmus Mundus programme (ReSound, IADT code DL935) recorded four times under different spellings of the consortium — IADT Dún Laoghaire with Universidade Lusófona Lisbon and the Lithuanian Academy of Music and Theatre Vilnius. It was verified once and the identical verdict is written to all four; they should be collapsed into one row.
qualification: ERASMUS MUNDUS JOINT MASTER (EMJM) — 120 ECTS joint/multiple master's degree awarded by the consortium partners. A full, official 2nd-cycle degree, not a certificate.
accreditation: OFFICIAL, and the highest-quality accreditation signal in this entire batch. Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are selected and funded directly by the European Commission, and each partner's award is nationally accredited — Lusófona under A3ES (verified separately in this batch: R/A-Cr 34/2018/AL01 for its sister mestrado, and the institution is an accredited Portuguese university), IADT under Irish QQI, LMTA under Lithuanian accreditation. EMJM designation is itself an external quality endorsement that no purely private school can buy. There is no plausible scenario in which this qualification turns out to be worthless paper — which is precisely the risk that dominates the rest of this search.
tuition: €15,000 total for the four-semester programme (self-funded) — VERIFIED on the official consortium application page as '15,000 Euro' split into two payments of '7,500 EUR'. CONFLICT FLAG STANDS: Universidade Lusófona's own ReSound page quotes an average of roughly €2,250 per month for 30-ECTS semestral units (about €9,000 per semester), which does not reconcile with the consortium's €15,000 total. Treat resound-ma.eu as authoritative — it is the consortium's own page and the figure is unambiguous — but get the discrepancy resolved in writing before paying anything, because a €36,000 reading of the Lusófona page is not a rounding error.
otherFees: No application fee is mentioned on the application page — VERIFIED absence, though absence of mention is weaker than an explicit statement of zero. Travel, accommodation and living costs are explicitly excluded from tuition and estimated by the consortium at €600–€1,000 per month. HIDDEN COST HE MUST BUDGET FOR: three-country mobility means THREE separate immigration processes (Ireland — outside Schengen and with its own IRP regime — plus Portugal and Lithuania) and two inter-country relocations. Realistically €1,500–€3,000 across the two years in permit fees, flights and deposits. This is nowhere published — UNVERIFIED as a figure, but it is certain to exist and it disproportionately burdens a Tunisian passport holder.
totalCost: WITH an Erasmus Mundus scholarship: €0 tuition and a net-positive €1,400/month, i.e. the plan pays for itself. WITHOUT a scholarship: €15,000 tuition + roughly €14,400–€24,000 living over 24 months + €1,500–€3,000 relocation and permits — a realistic all-in €31,000–€42,000 over two years, front-loaded with €7,500 due before he starts.
scholarshipDetail: THE BEST FUNDING AVAILABLE ANYWHERE IN THIS SEARCH, AND HE IS ELIGIBLE AS A NON-EU NATIONAL. VERIFIED: Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders 'pay no tuition fees' and receive a stipend of '1,400 EUR per month'. Over 24 months that is roughly €33,600 in stipend plus €15,000 in waived tuition — around €48,600 of value, and it converts his entire plan from a €30,000+ outlay into a net-positive one. Awarded on merit. The number of scholarships is a limited share of the maximum 24 annual places, so it is genuinely competitive; EMJM calls typically reserve a substantial quota for Partner Country (non-EU) applicants, which is his category, though I could not verify the specific quota for this consortium — UNVERIFIED. This single line item is the most consequential fact in the entire Portuguese slice.

institution: ETIC – Escola de Tecnologias, Inovação e Criação (private school, Lisbon; Pearson BTEC Accredited Centre sinc…
programme: Sound Design for Live, Studio and Interactive Media
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's; portfolio required, so build it
verdictWhy: This is a Pearson BTEC Level 5 professional certificate from a school that says in writing it is not a higher education institution. Level 5 is below the BSc he already holds, so it is an academic step backwards and cannot support a master's-level student visa route. Bank loans are the only published funding.
correction: TWO corrections. (1) This is not a master's and was collected as though it were: the award is a 'Pearson BTEC Level 5 Professional Certification (240 CATS)' and the school states 'ETIC is not a higher education institution.' Level 5 is below bachelor's level. (2) Gate recorded as 'Portfolio + exam/interview' — wrong on the portfolio: the page states portfolio submission is 'not mandatory'. The real gate is a motivation letter plus an interview.
qualification: CORRECTED AND SHARPENED. The award is a "BTEC Higher National Diploma, Level 5, carrying a total of 240 CATS credits" — ETIC's own wording. The page also calls it a "Pearson BTEC Level 5 Professional Certification (240 CATS)". It is an HND: NOT a mestrado, NOT a pós-graduação, NOT a Portuguese degree, and NOT a bachelor's. ETIC states plainly on its own page: "Certification follows the British education system; ETIC is not a higher education institution." NEW FINDING: the optional 3rd year is a separate award — "ETIC / SOLENT UNIVERSITY RECOGNITION / 120 CATS", taking the total to 360 CATS, i.e. a UK bachelor's-level top-up recognised by Solent University (Southampton). So the 2-year route ends BELOW bachelor's; only the 3-year route reaches bachelor-equivalent — still nowhere near a master.
accreditation: NOT a Portuguese degree — VERIFIED IN ETIC'S OWN WORDS. It is NOT accredited by A3ES or DGES, is NOT a mestrado, and is NOT a pós-graduação in the Portuguese academic sense. It is a UK Pearson BTEC Higher National Diploma at Level 5, assigned its level "by Ofqual (Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation) under the Regulated Qualifications Framework (RQF), which forms part of the UK qualifications system", delivered in Portugal by a DGERT-certified vocational provider. ETIC states: "ETIC is not a higher education institution." It describes the programmes as "internationally recognised, enabling direct entry into the labour market as well as progression to further studies" — "progression to further studies" is the operative admission: an HND Level 5 is a stepping stone TOWARD a bachelor's, which is exactly what the optional Solent third year completes. For someone who already holds a BSc, the two-year award is a step DOWN and the three-year award is at best lateral.
tuition: CORRECTED to €11,640 for the full 2-year programme by instalments (24 x €485), or €11,058 if paid promptly in 2 x €5,529 with the 5% discount. The previously reported €11,200 was wrong. CRITICAL FOR THIS CANDIDATE: a separate line applies to him — "CITIZENS WITHOUT TAX RESIDENCE IN PORTUGAL: 1st instalment: €3,492 + 23 instalments: €354,26", totalling €11,639.98. Same total, but with a €3,492 lump sum demanded up front instead of €485. As a Tunisian national with no Portuguese tax residence, this is the schedule he would face. The table is dated 2025 and carries the warning "Prices and payment conditions may change until enrollment begins."
otherFees: MAJOR CORRECTION — application fees DO exist and were previously reported as absent. The published table states "APPLICATION: YEAR 1: 700€ | YEAR 2: 200€", footnoted "Amount to be paid upon enrollment and non-refundable, except in the case the course does not open." That is €900 in non-refundable fees on top of tuition. No separate materials, insurance or exam fees are published; UNVERIFIED whether a Pearson registration/certification fee is charged separately, and this should still be asked about explicitly. Cost of the optional Solent-recognised third year is UNVERIFIED.
totalCost: CORRECTED. Tuition €11,640 over two years (or €11,058 prompt-paid) PLUS €900 non-refundable application fees = €12,540 total to ETIC on the instalment route, or €11,958 prompt-paid. His first-year outlay as a non-tax-resident is front-loaded: €700 application + €3,492 first instalment = €4,192 due immediately, then €354.26/month. Add Lisbon living costs — the cheapest of the four capitals in this slice but now expensive for housing, realistically €900-€1,200/month. All-in over two years, tuition plus modest living: roughly €34,000-€41,000. ETIC publishes no living-cost estimate (UNVERIFIED).
scholarshipDetail: None published for this course — the only fee reductions are the 5% prompt-payment and 6% alumni discounts, neither of which he can use (he is not an alumnus, and prompt payment means finding €11,058 at once). ETIC's site carries an "Erasmus+ Scholarships" menu item and offers Erasmus+ international internship mobility after completion subject to performance, but that is a placement scheme, not a fee reduction. Net position: essentially no scholarship access.
entry: VERIFIED verbatim: a motivation letter outlining professional goals; a "portfolio or showreel" listed as OPTIONAL; attendance at an interview; and a "recommended english entry level: B1". Places are limited: "Enrolment in a specific timetable is limited to the number of available places" and "the opening of each course, class or timetable is subject to a minimum number of enrolments."
acceptsNonMusic: Yes, comfortably. VERIFIED: no degree, no music background and no formal prior qualification is required. Entry is by motivation letter, an OPTIONAL portfolio and an interview. His BSc sits far above the entry bar — which is precisely the problem.
portfolio: Portfolio or showreel is OPTIONAL — VERIFIED. This remains genuinely notable: with no portfolio yet built, this is one of the very few audio programmes across the four countries he could apply to today without producing a single finished track.
audition: Interview only. No audition, no test, no entrance exam. VERIFIED.
deadline: UNVERIFIED — no published application deadline. With a hard cap of 16 places, entry is effectively first-come. For a non-EU applicant the binding constraint is not ETIC's deadline but the Portuguese visa timeline, which ETIC itself warns "can take several months". PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
opens: UNVERIFIED — not published. Admission is enquiry-and-interview based: select the course, submit the application form, receive an email with interview dates, then enrol on approval.
duration: "Duration: 2 years + 1 (optional). Level: 5" — ETIC's own wording. 240 CATS after year 2 (BTEC HND, Level 5); a further 120 CATS with Solent University recognition in the optional year 3, totalling 360 CATS. CATS is a UK credit unit, NOT ECTS; 240 CATS is nominally 120 ECTS but the LEVEL is what matters, and Level 5 is below bachelor's.
englishTest: No IELTS required — VERIFIED. The published requirement is a "recommended english entry level: B1", and no standardised test is demanded at all. This is dramatically softer than Berklee Valencia's IELTS 7.5 or SAE's IELTS 6.0, and it is the single most accessible English requirement found in this research.
study: CORRECTED — the module content was previously UNVERIFIED and is now confirmed in detail from the official page, and it is not what a producer/DJ needs. Verified units: sound design for film, documentary and animation; adaptive audio systems for video games, virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR); sound design for installations, exhibitions and public spaces; technical installation and operation of Public Address (P.A.) systems including tuning and calibration; Lighting Control fundamentals covering the DMX system, cabling, projectors and digital lighting consoles; Broadcast and LUFS Standards (sound engineering for TV and radio, loudness measurement and regulatory volume standards); Sound for Arts, Theatre and QLab (setup, automation and playback control for live performance); Sound Systems for Museums and Installations (multi-channel and distributed audio design); and Sonic Interactivity and Prototyping using sensors and Arduino/Raspberry Pi. Stated career outcome: "Sound Designer specialising in recording and post-production for video games, film, theatre, advertising and sound installations." Schedule: Mon-Friday 14:00-18:00, in person, project-based, max 16 students. Erasmus+ international internships available on completion, subject to performance.
recommendation: Cheap, English-taught, visa-supported and genuinely accessible — and still the wrong course, for two independent reasons. First, LEVEL: the two-year award is a BTEC Higher National Diploma at Level 5, which is BELOW bachelor's. ETIC says outright it is not a higher education institution. Paying €12,540 and two years to obtain a sub-bachelor vocational diploma when he already holds a BSc is a downgrade, not a postgraduate step. The newly-verified optional third year (Solent University recognition, +120 CATS, 360 total) only brings him back up to bachelor-equivalent — still not a master, and now three years and considerably more money. Second, and previously unverified, CONTENT: the module list is now confirmed and it is media, live-event and installation sound design — film and documentary post, game/VR/AR adaptive audio, P.A. rigging and calibration, DMX lighting control, broadcast LUFS compliance, QLab theatre playback, museum multichannel systems, Arduino sensor prototyping. There is no music production, no electronic music, no DJing, and the stated career outcome is "Sound Designer specialising in recording and post-production for video games, film, theatre, advertising and sound installations". That is a different profession from the one he wants. Correct the money on the record: tuition is €11,640 not €11,200, the schedule is 24 x €485 not 10 x €560, there IS a non-refundable application fee of €700 in year one plus €200 in year two, and as a non-tax-resident he must pay €3,492 up front rather than a first monthly instalment — so his day-one cash requirement is €4,192, not €560. What still makes it worth keeping on the page: it is the only entry in this batch with a published price, English delivery, NO IELTS requirement (B1 recommended only), an OPTIONAL portfolio, and explicit written non-EU visa support including an AIMA enrolment letter. If his real constraint turns out to be that he cannot reach IELTS 7.5 or cannot build a portfolio in time for a 2027 master's, this is the fallback that would still take him — but he should choose ETIC's music production certification rather than this sound design one, because this one does not teach what he wants to do. And the honest structural finding stands: Portugal has no international private chain master's in this field at all, so if Portugal matters to him the search must move to private Portuguese universities such as Universidade Católica Portuguesa's Som e Imagem mestrado.

portfolio: MAJOR CORRECTION — the previous record described this only as 'a written project description' and called the full spec unpublished. It IS published, and it is far more demanding. audition: MAJOR CORRECTION AND THE DECISIVE FINDING ON THIS PROGRAMME. The previous record left the entrance examination as 'three components, detail UNVERIFIED'. The detail is published and it is a performing-musician audition held ON CAMPUS IN STOCKHOLM. TEST 2 — Musical performance ability: from an assignment given on the day, and TOGETHER WITH TWO MUSICIANS PROVIDED BY KMH, he must prepare and perform a short piece of music THAT INCLUDES IMPROVISATION. Structure: 30 minutes solo preparation, 15 minutes rehearsal with the two musicians, a performance of maximum 5 minutes, then oral reflection; about 60 minutes total, scored 0–6 on musical interpretation and artistic reflection. TEST 3 — Artistic reflection and musical expression: an on-campus interview of about 20 minutes discussing the Test 1 works, his creative process and his motivation, scored 0–6. Two consequences the previous record missed entirely: (a) he would have to perform live improvised music with professional musicians, which no amount of DAW portfolio work substitutes for; (b) Tests 2 and 3 are in person in Stockholm, so he must travel from Tunisia — and enter Schengen on a short-stay visa — BEFORE any admission decision exists.

study: CONFIRMED from the syllabus. Trains musicians and composers in music, artistic practices and interdisciplinary methods for cross-border collaboration. Practical foundation is artistic work in music related to sound art, composition, performance practice or improvisation, with an experimental approach central throughout. Theoretical base is artistic research; electives broaden toward interaction design, robotics, music and sound in computer games, narrativity and engineering. Students come from varied fields including composition, improvisation and music production, and each has a main teacher who follows them through four project courses (Project Lab 1–4). The student's project FROM THE APPLICATION is what is developed across the programme — so the project description is not a formality, it is the spine of the degree.
recommendation: THE PREVIOUS RECORD CALLED THIS THE BEST STRATEGIC FIND IN SWEDEN. After checking the official syllabus and the published entrance-test specification, it is BETTER THAN CLAIMED ON LANGUAGE AND MUCH WORSE THAN CLAIMED ON ADMISSIBILITY, and the second point governs. Resolved in his favour: the language of instruction is ENGLISH, stated verbatim in the KAIM1 syllabus — the previous record's biggest open question, now closed, and he should not waste the email asking it. Also confirmed: no music bachelor required, sound art and music in computer games are named parts of the remit, SEK 264,000/yr, SEK 900 application fee, roughly three full-tuition scholarships institution-wide (plus FAS+ insurance) decided only after May admission. Resolved against him, decisively: the entrance examination is not the written project description the previous record described. Test 1 demands three recorded works including one where he leads and one where he collaborates with other musicians or artists. Test 2 is an ON-CAMPUS live performance in Stockholm where he must prepare and perform improvised music with two musicians KMH assigns him, scored 0–6. Test 3 is a 20-minute on-campus interview. That is a performing-musician audition, and it is the sole basis of selection. A man with no conservatory training, no ensemble experience and no portfolio cannot pass it in one year of bedroom production, and he would have to fund travel and a Schengen visa to Stockholm to fail it. Add that KMH still has not published whether autumn 2027 is even an admission year. VERDICT: do not build his 2027 plan on this. One email to international@kmh.se is still worth sending, but ask only the two questions that remain unknown — is there admission for autumn 2027, and what IELTS band satisfies English 6. Do not ask about language; that is answered. Revisit AIM only if he ever acquires genuine live-improvisation ability, in which case it becomes a strong target because the degree itself is a real, English-taught, state-accredited master that does not require a music bachelor.

recommendation: STILL NOT A MASTER'S — but the correct verdict is now sharper than "unaccredited marketing". This means that we are now able to accept a limited number of international students who require a Student visa to study on the UK." He would pay £23,950 in full up front, with no work rights, to earn a Level 5 award — one level BELOW the BSc he already holds, and worth nothing towards a master's, a Level 7 recognition in Europe, or doctoral progression. The teaching and the Abbey Road access are probably excellent, and the portfolio bar ("we do not expect to receive high-quality productions") is realistically within reach for him. But as a step after a completed bachelor's, paying nearly £24k to move DOWN the qualification framework is hard to justify, especially with zero funding. RATED C for that reason, not because it is fake. If he wants the Abbey Road name cheaply, the 4-day Song Production Masterclass (10-13 Oct 2026, one day at Abbey Road Studios, three at Angel Studios, with Sylvia Massy) is the sane version of this.

A Tunisian national applying from Tunisia cannot take it. This is the most painful loss in the slice — £11,250 for a Falmouth-awarded MA, full-tuition scholarships, no audition, just a video call, an APEL route for non-relevant degrees, and forgiving IELTS sub-scores. Everything about the admissions design suits him except the one thing he cannot change. Included so he does not spend time on it.

institution: Iceland University of the Arts / Iceland Academy of the Arts (Listaháskóli Íslands, LHÍ), Department of Music
programme: Music Composition MA/M.Mus
whyChance: Names engineering or computing as a welcome background; portfolio required, so build it
verdictWhy: The gate suits him better than almost anything else here: no audition, no music degree strictly required, no IELTS, an explicit clause admitting people who can 'demonstrate a comparable knowledge, experience and technical ability', and a portfolio spec so clear it doubles as a work plan — five works in electronic composition and sound art, due early March. The condition is money: LHÍ introduced non-EEA tuition from autumn 2026 and has not published the figure, so he must email lhi@lhi.is and get the 2027 non-EEA amount in writing before committing, since it could be anything from a few hundred to several thousand euros.
correction: MAJOR CORRECTION ON COST. 'Under EUR 1.5k/yr' was true until this year and is now WRONG OR AT BEST UNKNOWN: LHÍ states 'From fall 2026 tuition fees will apply to applications from a country outside of EEA, Faroe Islands, Greenland and Switzerland.' A Tunisian starting in 2027 is squarely in the new fee-paying category, and LHÍ has not published the amount on any page I could reach. The old fee-free-plus-ISK-registration model no longer describes his situation.
qualification: MA / M.Mus
tuition: BLOCKING FINDING — the amount is now published and it is very large. From LHÍ's tuition-fee page, for the academic year 2026-2027, non-EEA students pay per academic year: Department of Music ISK 5,500,000 (also Performing Arts and Film ISK 5,500,000; Architecture, Fine Art, Design and Arts Education ISK 4,500,000). ISK 5,500,000 is roughly EUR 37,000-38,000 per year at mid-2026 rates, i.e. on the order of EUR 75,000 for the two-year MA — indicative conversion, verify at the time. LHÍ states the fees "reflect the actual cost of the studies and the amount may change between academic years", are charged in ISK by bank transfer, are non-refundable, and "must be paid in full before enrolment or continuation of studies can be confirmed. Failure to pay on time or in full may result in the loss of the study place." The ISK 100,000 annual registration fee does NOT rescue him: it applies to "students with citizenship within the EEA, the Faroe Islands, Greenland and Switzerland as well as all students regardless of nationality who started studying at LHÍ in the fall of 2025 or earlier." Only two exemptions exist, neither of which he meets: holding an Icelandic permanent residence permit (or one that can lead to it), or studying at LHÍ via an international university cooperation project, cooperation programme or university network. Separate application fee ISK 5,000, non-refundable, per application, not deducted from any other fee.
scholarshipDetail: None — and this is now an explicit institutional statement, not an absence of evidence. LHÍ's tuition-fee page: "IUA does not provide any scholarships for [tuition] fees or living expenses."
entry: NOW PUBLISHED AND CONFIRMED (previously logged as UNVERIFIED). General: "a bachelor's degree or equivalent university education that supports the applicant's ability to meet the [demands] of the MA Program", with certified academic transcripts. Programme-specific: "Applicants will have completed a BA degree in composition or the related fields of music theory or the arts. Non musical academic degrees are not excluded, especially on graduate and doctoral levels. Applicants who do not have a BA degree in composition can be recommended to the program provided they demonstrate a comparable knowledge, experience and technical ability in the field of musical composition." Language: "Students must be proficient in spoken and written English in the academic context. In case the admission committee has doubts regarding the applicant's competence, he/she may be required to submit evidence of English proficiency" — so no blanket IELTS/TOEFL requirement, but a test can be demanded. Documents: certified degree certificate(s) and transcript(s) (PDF); ONE reference, max one page, submitted directly by the referee via an emailed link (waived for former LHÍ students); letter of motivation in English (PDF); CV in English (PDF); portfolio. Non-refundable application fee ISK 5,000, payable per application; the application is not valid until both submitted and paid.
acceptsNonMusic: TECHNICALLY YES, PRACTICALLY DEMANDING. Quoted: "Non musical academic degrees are not excluded, especially on graduate and doctoral levels." But the same paragraph sets the real bar: an applicant without a BA in composition must "demonstrate a comparable knowledge, experience and technical ability in the field of musical composition" — i.e. the door is open only if the portfolio performs at conservatory-graduate level. With no music degree, no conservatory training and no professional audio experience, he would be asked to evidence exactly what he does not yet have. The sibling MMus in New Audiences and Innovative Practice (NAIP), described on the department page as suitable for musicians from diverse backgrounds with "innovative and interdisciplinary approaches to creating and communicating music", is the more permissive door — but it carries the identical Department of Music tuition, which is the real blocker.
portfolio: NOW PUBLISHED AND CONFIRMED (previously UNVERIFIED). Item 5, "Portfolio of works (PDF/URL)", compulsory: "Portfolio of 5 scores with or without audio files are required for applications in instrumental composition. Applicants in electronic composition and sound art must submit 5 works. Applicants for interdisciplinary studies (composing for film, theater etc.) must submit 5 original works." So his route would be the electronic-composition/sound-art stream: FIVE works, no notation obligation on that stream. No per-work duration, no audio format and no total runtime cap are specified. Submitted as PDF or URL.
audition: NO live audition and no on-site entrance test published. "An admission committee assesses applications on the grounds of assessment of the subject material, the applicant's motivation and aim with the study at the Iceland University of the Arts and the interview(s) with the applicant." Interview(s) form part of selection; the mode is not stated, so confirm whether they are held remotely. Additional risk on the official page: "If the number of applicants meeting the admission requirements for the study program falls below the minimum threshold, the program will not be offered for the upcoming academic year."
deadline: 2 March 2026, with results announced April 2026 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Only the 2026-intake cycle is published (open 14 Jan 2026, deadline 2 Mar 2026, answered Apr 2026). For a September 2027 start expect roughly mid-January to early March 2027, unconfirmed. The upside relative to Aalto is a much later and longer window; the downside is that it is irrelevant unless the funding problem is solved.
opens: 14 January 2026 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date (expect approximately mid-January 2027 for a September 2027 start, but this must be reconfirmed; nothing for the 2027 intake is published as of July 2026)
duration: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS — NOW CONFIRMED on the official programme page (previously logged as UNVERIFIED)
study: "The international MA program in composition enables the student to develop his/her artistic and theoretical activity in a stimulating creative and critical environment, with access to the staff's wide professional experience and theoretical knowledge and supported by an inspiring learning community." Structure, per the official page: one-to-one private lessons with a composition tutor plus collective composition classes; "the subject of composition is by far the largest item in the syllabus, generating almost half the credits in the first three terms"; first two terms also carry "a course in sound technology, either electronic or instrumental, a course on artistic research, a course on music analysis and an introduction to some recent issues [in] music composition", plus electives. Weekly seminars analyse notable compositions and discuss students' research. The school "collaborates with professional musicians who give workshops where students' works are heard and discussed". Master's project options: (a) 20-credit composition + 10-credit paper, (b) 10-credit composition + 20-credit paper, or (c) a 26-credit practical project + a 4-credit reflection. CONFIRMED on the official page (previously flagged as aggregator-sourced): "Students are offered the opportunity to have their final project performed by the Caput Ensemble at a graduation concert." No PhD in music yet, though one is in development.
recommendation: DOWNGRADED TO C — this is now a confirmed financial dead end, not merely an unverified one. LHÍ has published the number the earlier record could not find: from autumn 2026 a non-EEA student in the Department of Music pays ISK 5,500,000 per academic year, roughly EUR 37,000-38,000, about EUR 75,000 across the MA, with tuition due in full before enrolment can be confirmed, no refunds, and the institution stating flat out that it offers no scholarships for tuition or living costs — in Iceland, one of Europe's most expensive countries. The only two exemptions are Icelandic residency and inbound exchange/network mobility; neither is available to him as a direct-entry Tunisian applicant. Set the money aside and the fit is still weak: it is a contemporary art-music composition MA built around private composition tutorials, score-based work and a Caput Ensemble graduation concert, with electronics as one course and one application stream. The published entry rule is honest about the bar — a non-composition bachelor is "not excluded" but must "demonstrate a comparable knowledge, experience and technical ability in the field of musical composition", which is precisely the evidence he cannot produce this cycle. There is one genuine positive to bank: the electronic-composition and sound-art portfolio route asks for five works with no notation requirement, which is a spec he could realistically meet in a year — the same five-work package would serve the Aalto portfolio. Recommendation: do not apply. If Iceland matters for non-academic reasons, email lhi@lhi.is and registration@lhi.is to check whether the NAIP MMus route or any Erasmus/network mobility arrangement could bring him in under the cooperation-programme exemption, since that is the only published mechanism that removes the fee.

study: Year 1: design for the performing arts through critical theoretical research and interactive tools; stage writing; physical training in dedicated spaces; creation of audiovisual content that dialogues with space and bodies. recommendation: ADMISSIBLE, ACCREDITED, AND FINANCIALLY INDEFENSIBLE WITHOUT THE SCHOLARSHIP. Verification confirms every academic advantage: it is a real MUR-recognised laurea-magistrale-equivalent, there is no audition, no music prerequisite, no Italian requirement, an explicit written welcome for applicants from different backgrounds, IELTS at just 5.0 (General accepted), and a properly documented Universitaly/type-D visa route. For a Tunisian software engineer with no conservatory training, that combination is rare and valuable. But the money is brutal and the verification made it worse, not better: €22,250 per year with no income banding for non-EU students, €44,500 over two years, a scholarship that covers only the first year and caps at €6,000, and three compulsory fees whose amounts NABA simply does not publish. And it is not music production — it is performance and interaction design with sound as one component; he would graduate a performance technologist, not a producer. Apply ONLY through the portfolio-based scholarship competition, treat the €6,000 as a precondition rather than a bonus, get the application, pre-enrolment and thesis fees quoted in writing first, and have funds ready before results because winners must enrol within seven days. Without the award, this is not defensible for someone whose stated goal is club and electronic production.

recommendation: Best accreditation in the batch, wrong programme for this candidate — and the verification made the mismatch worse, not better. The widely repeated '€125,000 allocated for 2026–27 master's entrants' figure is NOT a general fund — it is Berklee Valencia's scholarship programme FOR VALENCIAN STUDENTS ONLY (application deadline 10 March, scholarship materials by 1 April). A Tunisian applicant CANNOT access it. Do not build a budget around that number. The general graduate eligibility page states only that applicants must have 'earned a bachelor's degree from an accredited college, conservatory, or university' with no field named. But the Berklee Valencia ENTRANCE REQUIREMENTS page is more restrictive for MPTI specifically: a bachelor's in music is PREFERRED, with 'other disciplines accepted with demonstrated musicianship', and applicants must show 'technological proficiency, musical excellence in performance and/or composition'. The programme page adds that the ideal candidate shows 'excellent musicality', 'facility with technology', 'success in artistic and academic settings' and 'prior accomplishment'. VERDICT: a software-engineering BSc is formally eligible and the technology half is a genuine strength for him, but he is an exception applicant who must prove musicianship through the portfolio. MPTI requires: (1) a self-produced video of MAXIMUM 3 MINUTES describing THREE thesis project ideas; (2) THREE recorded musical projects (audio or video); (3) optionally, musical scores. Formatting rule that fails applications: all portfolio material must be organised into ONE PDF with embedded links — WeTransfer, Dropbox and Google Drive links are NOT accepted. duration: CONFIRMED: one full academic year of three consecutive semesters (fall, spring, summer; summer term 6–7 weeks), September start. Optional fourth-semester internship. Minimum 32–33 US credits (33 with internship), maximum 37–38 (38 with internship). ECTS equivalence NOT published for MPTI — UNVERIFIED. (For comparison, the ANECA-verified Scoring master publishes 39–40 US credits = 60 ECTS, so US-credit-to-ECTS is not a linear conversion and must not be assumed.)

VERIFIED figure for MPTI and all programmes except Contemporary Performance: IELTS 7.5, TOEFL iBT 100 (for exams before 21 Jan 2026), Pearson PTE Academic 73. DISCREPANCY FOUND on Duolingo: the Berklee Valencia 'How to Apply' page states 130, while the Berklee college-wide eligibility page states 120 — assume the higher Valencia figure of 130 and confirm in writing. Berklee institution code 3107. THIS IS HIS BIGGEST PRACTICAL OBSTACLE: IELTS 7.5 is a demanding band (roughly C1) and he has not sat the test. He should book a diagnostic test in 2026, not 2027.
study: VERIFIED on the programme page. Core: Audio Engineering (Hybrid Recording), Studio Music Production, Music Video Production, Interactive Media (Max MSP Fundamentals), Electronic Music Production and Performance, Career Preparation Seminar, plus proficiencies in Pro Tools, Analog Audio and Music Theory. Final Project Module: three MPTI seminars ('Past, Present, Future') plus proposal, development and defence of a culminating experience. Electives (4+ credits): stereo mixing, DJing, live video production, sound design, advanced synthesis. Software named by the school: Ableton Live, Max, Pro Tools, Adobe Premiere. Career outcomes listed verbatim: 'artists, technologists, producers, DJs, electronic composers, educators, and software and/or hardware designers.'
recommendation: This is the best-matched programme in this batch and the only one that is simultaneously a real accredited master's degree, taught in English, aimed squarely at producers and DJs, and backed by a documented, functioning non-EU student-visa pathway. The curriculum literally contains Electronic Music Production and Performance and DJing electives, and the school names DJs among its graduate outcomes — that is his stated goal in the school's own words. His software-engineering background is a genuine asset here, not a liability: Max/MSP, interactive media and hardware/software design are core content, and Berklee explicitly lists 'software and/or hardware designers' as an outcome. Four hard realities. FIRST, money: roughly $67k–71k all-in for one year, billed in USD, plus an unpublished mandatory insurance cost. SECOND, the scholarship picture is weaker than commonly reported — the €125,000 figure is reserved for Valencian students and he cannot touch it; his realistic levers are the General Scholarship and the Diversity Scholarship (up to 50%), the latter requiring a deliberate 3-minute video or 500-word essay by 1 February, sent to a separate email address from the main application. THIRD, IELTS 7.5 from a standing start is a serious 12-month study target and should be booked as a diagnostic in 2026. FOURTH, the award is a US Master of Music, not a Spanish official master — excellent internationally and perfectly adequate for a production career, but it would need homologación if he ever wanted Spanish PhD entry or public-sector recognition. For a DJ/producer career that last point barely matters. VERDICT: worth the money ONLY if he lands 40–50%+ in scholarship AND spends the next twelve months building three finished tracks strong enough to carry the portfolio. At full sticker price this is poor value against simply building a catalogue independently. Concrete plan: sit IELTS by early 2027, produce the three portfolio tracks through 2026, and apply Early Action (1 Nov 2026) with the Diversity Scholarship submission prepared in parallel.

scholarshipDetail: STRONGEST FUNDING ROUTE IN THE ENTIRE NON-EUROPE SEARCH. Renewal: "Funding is renewed yearly, contingent on satisfactory academic and research performance, and alignment with research priorities." CITIZENSHIP: this is an internal RA appointment, not a citizenship-restricted award — TUNISIANS ARE FULLY ELIGIBLE. No separate scholarship application exists; admission IS the funding. Covers tuition AND living. Deadline = the admission deadline (15 December).
entry: "you must have completed your Bachelor's degree by the time you enroll in our Master's program." Application = Statement of Objectives, Personal Statement, Portfolio, transcripts, three recommendation letters. acceptsNonMusic: YES — emphatically. MAS is not a music degree and imposes no music prerequisite; MIT's FAQ requires only "a completed Bachelor's degree" with no field restriction. The Media Lab is famous for admitting engineers, designers and self-taught builders. A BSc Software Engineering is a mainstream, competitive background here. (No explicit sentence saying 'any field' is published, so the wording is inferred from the absence of any restriction — partially UNVERIFIED.)
portfolio: "Some research groups require the submission of a portfolio of relevant work, and most other groups will accept such portfolios for consideration. Applicants should consult the applicant information webpages of the research groups they are applying to for specific requirements." So there is NO single Institute-wide portfolio spec — it is set per research group. For Opera of the Future / Responsive Environments the de facto expectation is documented built work (instruments, software, installations, demo videos, code repositories), which a software engineer can assemble without any musical training. Exact per-group specs for the 2027 cycle: UNVERIFIED.
audition: NO AUDITION. There is no performance audition anywhere in the MAS process — this is an engineering/design school, not a conservatoire. Selection is by statement, portfolio, letters and (for shortlisted candidates) interviews with the research group.
deadline: 15 DECEMBER ("11:59pm ET on December 15 is the firm deadline for all applications") — i.e. 15 DECEMBER 2026 for September 2027 entry. AFTER September 2026, so still reachable. Decisions from late February.

However, year-to-year there is occasionally some fellowship support and/or TA positions available." There is no guaranteed package, no tuition waiver, and Stanford master's students are generally expected to self-fund. Knight-Hennessy Scholars (full funding, open to all nationalities including Tunisians, covers tuition + stipend) IS technically available for a Stanford master's — but it is one of the most competitive awards on earth (~100 places from ~10,000 applicants worldwide), deadline typically mid-October, and it requires a separate application plus admission to the degree programme. Fulbright would have been the realistic route, and the Tunisia 2027 cycle CLOSED 30 JUNE 2026. VERDICT: unaffordable for this candidate for September 2027.

acceptsNonMusic: Check — the phrasing is "a suitable field of study", which is not defined, but the third and fourth routes (3 years' professional creative-industries work, or a combination of qualifications and experiential learning) are explicitly designed to catch people whose degree does not match. Get a written ruling on whether a software-engineering BSc is "suitable".
portfolio: No portfolio specification is published on the course page — UNVERIFIED. What IS published is that successful applicants "will receive an invitation to audition/interview" and that assessment weighs experience "for currency, validity, quality and sufficiency". ACM maintains separate Audition Guides on its site; consult those for the production-specialism requirement.
audition: AUDITION/INTERVIEW REQUIRED — verbatim from the international application process: "If your application is successful, you will receive an invitation to audition/interview." Format (online vs on-site) not stated — UNVERIFIED and important to confirm from Tunisia.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. No master's application deadline published; ACM advises applicants "to start the application process as soon as possible" to leave time for admissions and the visa. Note the sequence: conditional offer → audition → visa documents → FULL FIRST-YEAR TUITION PAID → CAS issued. That means the entire £17,200 must be paid before the visa can even be applied for.
opens: UNVERIFIED. Applications go through UCAS (course code A48); UCAS postgraduate/undergraduate cycles typically open in the autumn preceding entry.
duration: 1 year (also available as a 2-year accelerated bachelor + 1-year masters integrated route, 540 FHEQ). Masters alone: 180 FHEQ credits, 8 level-7 modules.
study: Four level-7 modules: CIF-701 Professional Practice Frameworks (60cr, benchmark and upskill your applied technical and craft competencies against an external framework); CIF-703 Ideas Into Action (30cr, rapid prototyping and pitching); CIF-702 Creative Applied Research (60cr, across two terms — this is where you choose the MA or MSc pathway); CIF-704 Making Connections and Building a Community (30cr, stakeholder and network building). The Music Production specialism is explicitly NOT beginner training: "The course is not about relearning technical fundamentals... aimed at practitioners who already have a grounding in production."
recommendation: The Metropolis Studios link is genuinely valuable and the entry routes are flexible. But read the warning on the page carefully: this programme states it is for producers who ALREADY have a grounding and are consolidating toward senior roles — it is not where you learn to produce. Combined with £17,200 payable in full before the visa is issued and no verified scholarship for non-EU students, this is a self-pay option that only makes sense if his portfolio is already strong. Also note international students are restricted to the London campus.

Offers may be conditional or unconditional depending on prior experience.

But the substitute for the degree subject is DEMONSTRATED EXPERIENCE plus the two-to-three-piece portfolio, and 'proven experience' is the phrase used. He has neither yet.

'Your application should be accompanied by a portfolio of creative work... likely to contain a mix of film, sound design, music production, sound installation work, or similar. It is easiest to put the materials in a folder (Dropbox, Google Drive etc.) with a document listing what it contains, and links to any external work online. Typically, a portfolio consists of TWO OR THREE PIECES. Above all we'll be looking for the CREATIVE USE OF SOUND in your work.' International applicants submit the same online portfolio, and an online meeting with the course leader can be arranged. Course leader: Jan Meinema (j.meinema@bathspa.ac.uk).

PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. For an international applicant needing a visa, 31 July is far too late in practice — target spring.
opens: UNVERIFIED for the 2027 cycle; an 'Apply now' link to the Bath Spa apphub (course code MASODE) is live. Confirm with admissions@bathspa.ac.uk.
duration: 1 year full-time across three trimesters (UK full-time £9,705/year vs part-time £4,853/year implies a 2-year part-time route). 180 UK credits = 90 ECTS equivalent.
languageReq: For most postgraduate courses: IELTS 6.5 overall with a minimum of 5.5 in Listening, Speaking, Reading and Writing (a few PG courses require 6.5 with 6.0 in each, or 7.0 with 6.0 in each; a few require only 6.0 with 5.5). The course page does not specify which band applies to MA Sound Design — UNVERIFIED at programme level; ask admissions@bathspa.ac.uk to confirm which of the three PG bands applies before booking a test. TOEFL iBT equivalents published: 81 overall with minimums of L17/R18/W17/S20 for the IELTS 6.5 bands.
study: Trimester 1: Sound Skills (self-selected skills projects), Research and Practice, Creative Portfolio (sound design for narrative storytelling and sonic immersion, advanced sound sculpting and processing). Trimester 2: Advanced Audio Workflows — audio post-production for film/animation/TV, game audio implementation, sound and audiovisual installations, theatre sound design. Trimester 3: independent large-scale practical Major Project. Subject areas: sound sculpting, processing and synthesis; language and aesthetics of sound design; storytelling and dramaturgy; immersive audio. Practical skills available: sound editing/track-laying, dialogue editing, foley and field recording, dubbing mixing, multichannel speaker arrays, and spatial audio across 5.1, Dolby Atmos, ambisonics, VR and binaural. Assessment is majority practical coursework. Teaching includes a 'flipped classroom' model for Sound Skills.
recommendation: The most useful thing about this record is the portfolio brief: two or three pieces, in a shared Dropbox/Drive folder, with a contents document and links, judged above all on 'the creative use of sound'. That is a concrete, achievable target for his portfolio year and it transfers to nearly every other application in this list. The programme itself, though, points at screen/game/theatre sound design rather than club music and DJing, and at £18,755 it is the second-most expensive here. Recommend it as a portfolio-discipline template and a secondary application, not a first choice — and verify before the 2027 cycle that it has not been retired like its sibling MA Sound (Production).

The supporting statement must address: what you previously studied and what you learnt about music production; why you want to study MA Music Production at Leeds Beckett; who your influences are as a songwriter/performer/producer and why; what music you are currently listening to and why; the type of music you like to write/perform/produce and why; an example of something you found particularly challenging in previous studies and/or music production work and how you met it; what you want to do after your studies. You should also include a PDF document with an overview of each of the examples (i.e. when, where and for whom was the production completed?) and identify your role/s in the production process (Are you the performer, composer, producer or recording engineer?). Facilities in the new Leeds School of Arts building: dedicated music studios, Foley studios, dubbing and music recording studios, acoustic labs, post-production suites, a 220-seat Dolby Atmos-accredited cinema. Artist-in-Residence sessions have included Utah Saints, I Monster, Chris T-T, Ian Prowse, Tom Williams, Matt Deighton.

scholarshipDetail: UK FUNDING BASELINE FOR A TUNISIAN APPLICANT (applies to every UK entry in this file): (1) CHEVENING — Tunisia IS a Chevening-eligible country. Award is fully funded (tuition, living costs, travel). BUT three hard bars apply: it funds ONLY full-time TAUGHT master's courses that are UK-based, start in the autumn term and last 9–12 months ('Chevening will not support a course that is longer than 12 months in any form'; part-time, distance learning, PhD and research master's are excluded); the applicant must have at least TWO YEARS of work experience acquired AFTER the undergraduate degree, equivalent to 2,800 hours; and applicants must apply to three different eligible UK courses. DEADLINE IS A FULL YEAR BEFORE ENTRY: for September 2027 entry the Chevening 2027/2028 deadline is 6 OCTOBER 2026, 11:00 UTC. (2) GREAT SCHOLARSHIPS — NOT AVAILABLE. The 2026 GREAT Scholarships programme covers Bangladesh, China (mainland), Egypt, Ghana, India, Indonesia, Kenya, Malaysia, Mexico, Nigeria, Pakistan, Spain, Thailand, Turkey and Vietnam. Tunisia is NOT on the list. (3) COMMONWEALTH SCHOLARSHIPS — not available; Tunisia is not a Commonwealth country. Net effect: for this candidate the only realistic full-cost UK route is Chevening, and only if he has two years of post-graduation work experience by 6 October 2026 and picks a 12-month taught master's. Everything else must be covered by institution-specific awards, which are almost always partial fee discounts of £1,000–£7,000. MIDDLESEX-SPECIFIC (named on the course page): Chevening Scholarship (full fees) — accepted here; European Academic Awards £1,000–£7,000 (Europe-only, so not applicable to a Tunisian national); Regional/International Merit Awards up to £2,000; plus region-specific awards. VERDICT: an automatic merit award of up to £2,000 does not close a £21,200 gap. Realistic only with Chevening — and the MA is 1 year full-time, so it IS Chevening-eligible.
