NO INTERNATIONAL SCHOLARSHIP IS NAMED ON THE COURSE PAGE. VERDICT: MARK AS UNAFFORDABLE. The combination is fatal — a £29,460 annual fee, a 2-year MMus that Chevening cannot fund, a PgDip alternative that is not a master's, and no international award. This is the most painful finding in the sweep, because on academic and portfolio grounds RBC Music Technology is arguably the best-matched UK programme for this candidate.
entry: 'UK students should normally hold an honours degree, ideally but not necessarily in Music.' 'Non-UK students should hold a Bachelor's degree or a similar degree-equivalent diploma, ideally but not necessarily in Music.' Selection is by portfolio review plus interview.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — EXPLICITLY, and in the strongest wording found among the UK conservatoires: 'a Bachelor's degree or a similar degree-equivalent diploma, IDEALLY BUT NOT NECESSARILY IN MUSIC'. The audition-requirements page reinforces it: the Music Technology portfolio welcomes 'applicants from musicians of all previous backgrounds'. A BSc Software Engineering is admissible on paper; the gate is the three-piece portfolio.
portfolio: EXACT (from the Music Auditions requirements page, Music Technology): a MINIMUM OF THREE PIECES, which may be 'recordings, productions, compositions, sound to picture or other appropriate material'. Submitted as electronic links (SoundCloud, Google Drive, Dropbox etc.). DEADLINE: WITHIN TWO WEEKS OF APPLYING. No maximum duration stated. (Composition portfolio, by contrast: a minimum of three compositions in any style, recordings encouraged, scores and recordings organised in labelled subfolders, also within two weeks of applying.)
audition: NO LIVE AUDITION for Music Technology — an INTERVIEW of 15–25 MINUTES, with the portfolio forming the basis of the conversation. The panel is interested in 'artistic influences, inspiration, career objectives'. (Composition interview is approximately 20 minutes and additionally expects 'familiarity with compositional trends over past 50 years'.) Auditions/interviews typically take place in FEBRUARY and MAY.
deadline: Apply via UCAS (UCAS Conservatoires). The sister Experimental Performance page states: 'Although it states an application deadline of 1 October on UCAS, we will consider applications throughout the year.' So the nominal deadline is 1 OCTOBER 2026 for September 2027 entry, with late applications considered. Auditions/interviews in February and May.
opens: UNVERIFIED — UCAS Conservatoires normally opens in July of the preceding year.
duration: MMus 2 YEARS full-time (3 years part-time); PgDip 1 year full-time (2 years part-time); PgCert 1 year part-time. NOTE: the 2-year MMus EXCEEDS Chevening's 12-month limit and is therefore NOT Chevening-eligible; the 1-year PgDip is short enough but is a diploma, not a master's, so it also fails Chevening's 'taught master's' rule. This is the single most damaging fact about this otherwise excellent option.
englishTest: IELTS 6.0 overall with no less than 5.5 in each band, or equivalent — one of the lowest English bars in this sweep.
study: 'Creative application of music technologies.' Core: Principal Study 1 and 2 (Music Technology), covering 'composition utilising technology, performing with technology, interactive music technology, programming, recording, production, mixing and mastering'. Plus Career Development and Professional Development options including Contemporary Music Concepts, Music Technology in Performance, and Writing Music for Media. The mention of PROGRAMMING as a core competence is unusual and directly relevant to a software engineer.

entry: 'an undergraduate degree or an equivalent international qualification, USUALLY IN MUSIC, and TWO RECENT EXAMPLES OF EXTENDED WRITTEN WORK IN ENGLISH, such as essays.'
acceptsNonMusic: BORDERLINE — 'usually in music' leaves a crack, but RCM is one of the world's most selective conservatoires and the portfolio bar (below) is far beyond a beginner. Rule out in practice for a 2027 entry.
portfolio: EXACT AND UNUSUALLY DETAILED. STANDARD COMPOSITION (MComp/MMus): 'a portfolio of AT LEAST THREE, BUT NOT MORE THAN FIVE, contrasting examples of their compositions'; scores must be included for each piece (or, for ACOUSMATIC works, descriptions alongside recordings — so acousmatic/electroacoustic work IS explicitly accepted); recordings of performed works are optional; DO NOT submit playback files from software such as Sibelius; AI usage must be declared and is limited to a maximum of one work. COMPOSITION FOR SCREEN (taught postgraduate only): a MINIMUM OF TWO contrasting works, TOTAL DURATION 5–10 MINUTES, at least TWO-THIRDS synced to picture (video games, adverts, film etc.); you must mix the music yourself except for professionally mixed tracks, which must be noted; AI declared and limited to one work; no Sibelius playback files.
audition: 'Composers are auditioned primarily on the basis of a portfolio of work.' Shortlisted candidates are interviewed — approximately 20 MINUTES, covering musical interests and motivations, composers/pieces important to you, areas for improvement in your writing, and AURAL TESTS (standard Composition only). In person at RCM London or by live video interview. 'No teachers or translators permitted; English proficiency required.' Composition for Screen applicants receive a VOCATIONAL TASK before the interview, e.g. composing to an image.
deadline: 1 OCTOBER 2026 for composition portfolios and applications (i.e. for September 2027 entry). This is a firm conservatoire deadline eleven months before entry.
duration: 2 years full-time; FAST-TRACK 12 MONTHS; 3 years part-time. Only the 12-month fast-track is Chevening-compatible in length.
englishTest: IELTS at C1 standard: an overall score of 7.0, 'with a minimum of 5.5 in all four components'. Note the unusual shape — high overall, low component floor.
study: Composition, with 'Composition for Screen as a principal study specialism' for those pursuing 'music for film, TV and gaming'. RCM composition alumni have won BAFTAs, Grammys, Golden Globes and Academy Awards. Electronic and screen music are therefore genuinely present — but note the framing is screen scoring, not club/electronic-artist practice.

institution: SAE Institute Glasgow (SAE Institute UK, AD Education group) — course details published by ICMP
programme: MA Creative Music Production (SAE Glasgow delivery)
whyChance: Names engineering or computing as a welcome background; portfolio required, so build it
verdictWhy: A genuine Hertfordshire-awarded MA taught by ICMP, and crucially SAE Institute UK does sponsor Student visas and issues CAS numbers — so unlike dBs, this route can actually get him to Britain. What must be resolved first is that SAE publishes almost nothing: no fee, no entry requirement, no deadline, no English score. He cannot plan against a page this empty, so the first step is a direct written quote from SAE Glasgow.
correction: TWO corrections. (1) AWARDING BODY: the record names no awarding body. It is the University of Hertfordshire — 'awarded by and quality assured by the University of Hertfordshire' — NOT ICMP, even though ICMP delivers the teaching. This matters because the same-named ICMP London MA is now ICMP's own award; the Glasgow and London versions of 'MA Creative Music Production' lead to different certificates. (2) Gate recorded as 'Portfolio + exam/interview' — SAE's page publishes no gate whatsoever; the portfolio-and-interview description is borrowed from ICMP and is unconfirmed for the Glasgow delivery.
qualification: AMBIGUOUS AND UNRESOLVED — the SAE Glasgow page states the award is made by the University of Hertfordshire (Middlesex for pre-2022 enrolments), while ICMP's own page for the identically-named MA states "Awarding Institution: The Institute of Contemporary Music Performance", and ICMP lists MA Creative Music Production as one of its two Glasgow postgraduate courses. The SAE Glasgow page itself links out to ICMP for "FULL COURSE DETAILS". CONFIRM IN WRITING which institution's name appears on the certificate before applying — this is a real, unresolved discrepancy between two official sites.
tuition: Not published on the SAE Glasgow page — UNVERIFIED there. CONFIRMED on ICMP's official 2026/27 international fee page for the Glasgow campus: non-EU international £13,500 per year; EU/EEA/Swiss £9,000; UK domestic £7,000. That makes Glasgow roughly £2,750/yr cheaper than the London MA for a non-EU student, before the substantially lower cost of living. CAS deposit £5,000 for most international students. Confirm which entity invoices you.
scholarshipDetail: None found for a Tunisian national. SAE references "2026 Scholarship Opportunities" without detail; the group's £4,000 Creative Development Scholarship is confirmed unavailable to non-EU international students; ICMP's own bursaries are UK-only or undergraduate-only and its named artist scholarships closed on 28 June 2026.
entry: Not published on the SAE Glasgow page — UNVERIFIED there. Two possible parent regimes, and which applies depends on the unresolved awarding-body question: ICMP's (2:1 honours, "also from other fields of study if music experience has been gained alongside this study", CEFR B2 English, personal statement plus audition/interview) or SAE's (2:2 in a relevant field plus 1 year's work experience, or five years' professional experience, or the PGCert route; IELTS 5.5; 500-word Major Project proposal — but note SAE requires a UK 2:1 equivalent of INTERNATIONAL postgraduate applicants). This ambiguity is itself the main reason to write to admissions before doing anything else. Given ICMP publishes the fees, the course page and the module list for Glasgow, the ICMP regime is the more likely one.
acceptsNonMusic: CHECK — not addressed on the SAE Glasgow page. Both parent routes are permissive in different ways (ICMP: "also from other fields of study" and "we welcome applicants from non-music-related academic backgrounds"; SAE: "a relevant field"), but nothing on the Glasgow page itself confirms it. Get it in writing.
portfolio: UNVERIFIED — nothing published on the SAE Glasgow page. The ICMP course requires a personal statement plus an audition/interview with no numeric portfolio spec; SAE's master's require a 500-word Major Project proposal. You cannot currently know which applies.
audition: UNVERIFIED — not published on the SAE Glasgow page. Expect an audition/interview if the ICMP regime applies (it is mandatory there); SAE's own MSc requires no audition. Ask whether any interview can be conducted online from Tunisia.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. No deadline published on either page. ICMP's equivalent course lists a 14 September 2026 start for the current cycle, implying a September 2027 equivalent; admissions appear rolling. Target applying by roughly February–April 2027 to clear the visa and CAS timeline.
duration: Not stated on the SAE Glasgow page — UNVERIFIED there. ICMP's page for the same-named MA states 1 year full-time (2 years part-time, UK only) and 120 credits across five modules.
study: CONFIRMED module list on the SAE Glasgow page, identical to ICMP's MA: Artistic Identity in Creative Music Production; Applied Production Techniques; Innovations in Music Production; The Art of Mixing and Mastering; Creative Production Major Project. Production, mixing and mastering craft plus a large self-directed final project.
recommendation: Worth chasing purely on price. It is the same production-and-mixing curriculum as the London MA — the module list matches exactly — but the confirmed non-EU Glasgow rate is £13,500/yr against £16,250 in London, and Glasgow living costs are far lower, so the total saving over the year is well beyond the headline £2,750. That combination (a production-focused MA, a non-music-degree entry route, CEFR B2 rather than IELTS 7.5, and the cheapest fee in this slice) makes it arguably his best value option here. The catch is that almost nothing except the module list is published on SAE's own page, and the two official sites disagree about who awards the degree. Treat this as a strong lead requiring one email, not a verified option: ask ICMP Glasgow admissions to confirm the awarding institution, the 2026/27 international fee, the entry requirements applied, whether the interview can be held online, and what he should bring to it.

institution: SAE Institute London (SAE Institute UK, AD Education group)

whyChance: Names engineering or computing as a welcome background; portfolio required, so build it
qualification: MSc — "developed, delivered and assessed by SAE Institute, and awarded by and quality assured by the University of Hertfordshire". This is a genuine UK level-7 university award, not an in-house diploma. (Pre-2022 enrolments were awarded by Middlesex University.)
tuition: International: £16,250. UK/domestic: £9,950. EU/EEA/Switzerland: £12,250 (i.e. £16,250 less the £4,000 Creative Development Scholarship). SAE alumni and staff receive a 25% discount.
scholarshipDetail: The £4,000 Creative Development Scholarship is restricted to EU/EEA/Swiss applicants. SAE references "2026 Scholarship Opportunities" but no award open to a non-EU/Tunisian applicant was verified on the pages read. None found.
entry: Three alternative routes, verbatim: (A) "A Bachelor degree with Honours (2:2 or higher) in a relevant field, plus 1 year's work experience"; (B) "At least five years of professional creative industry experience"; (C) completion of SAE's PGCert Professional Development. All applicants must submit "A 500 word proposal that outlines what you want to do for your Master's Major Project and why". English: "minimum 5.5 in all components and an overall band score of 5.5" IELTS — the LOWEST English bar found in this entire slice. TOEFL, Cambridge and Duolingo equivalents accepted; tests valid for a maximum of two years.
acceptsNonMusic: Check / conditionally. The wording is "a relevant field" plus one year's work experience — it does not say music. A software-engineering BSc can plausibly be argued as relevant to audio engineering, but the "plus 1 year's work experience" clause is a real obstacle for someone graduating now with no audio employment. Route C (do SAE's PGCert first, then progress) is the explicit workaround SAE itself publishes. Confirm in writing with admissions before relying on this.
portfolio: No conventional creative portfolio is demanded for the MSc. The distinctive requirement is a written 500-word Major Project proposal: "A 500 word proposal that outlines what you want to do for your Master's Major Project and why". Academic transcripts and a personal statement are also required via the online application.
audition: None. No audition or on-site test published.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. No fixed deadline published; the current listed start is September 2026. For September 2027 entry with a UK student visa, apply by roughly spring 2027.
opens: UNVERIFIED — SAE runs rolling admissions with September and other intakes.
duration: "1 year full-time, 2 years part-time". Credits not stated — UNVERIFIED. Start date published: September 2026.
study: Same module spine as the ICMP MSc: studio systems and acoustics, advanced studio production and creative workflow, audio technologies and immersive production, research and critical practice, culminating in an Integrated Studio Production Project.
recommendation: The IELTS 5.5 entry bar is a genuine, decision-relevant advantage for someone who has not yet sat an English test — no other real master's in this slice is that low. The catch is the "plus 1 year's work experience" clause and the £16,250 international fee with no scholarship he can claim. Ask admissions directly whether a 2026 BSc in software engineering with a production portfolio and no audio employment satisfies route A.

Counterweight: the portfolio explicitly asks for "a brief statement addressing relevant programming experience and synthesizer experience", which shows the programme actively values coding skills. PLUS a brief statement addressing relevant programming experience and, if applicable, synthesizer experience. deadline: No specific deadline stated on the course page (rolling/until full is common for Manchester PGT) — UNVERIFIED for the 2027 cycle. Confirm directly; visa-requiring applicants should assume a spring 2027 practical cut-off.

Options to reach 120 taught credits include Aesthetics and Analysis of Organised Sound, Interactive Tools and Engines, Contemporary Music Studies, Advanced Orchestration, Historical and Contemporary Performance, Fieldwork and Ethnography, plus approved units outside MusM Composition. "All teaching, research and compositional work is carried out in the NOVARS Research Centre... with its state-of-the-art electroacoustic studios."
recommendation: The best-documented studio and software stack here (37-channel rooms, Max/MSP, GRM Tools, Unreal/Unity/VR) and only TWO contrasting works needed for the portfolio — the lowest portfolio burden of any option in this slice. scholarshipDetail: UK FUNDING BASELINE FOR A TUNISIAN APPLICANT (applies to every UK entry in this file): (1) CHEVENING — Tunisia IS a Chevening-eligible country. scholarshipDetail: MAJOR CORRECTION. The prior record said specific awards open to a Tunisian national were 'UNVERIFIED' and told him to ask the international office. USW's official international scholarships pages confirm: (1) CHANCELLOR'S INTERNATIONAL DEVELOPMENT SCHOLARSHIP of £2,500 for students from eligible regions — and the official eligible-countries page lists TUNISIA EXPLICITLY BY NAME under Africa, alongside Algeria, Egypt, Libya and Morocco. MECHANISM CONFIRMED VERBATIM: 'You will be automatically considered for one of these awards when we receive your application. You do not need to make a separate application and confirmation of the scholarship will be included in your offer letter.' CONDITIONS: he must be self-funding (students sponsored by their government or a company are NOT eligible), must pay the minimum deposit stipulated in the offer letter by the date on the Acceptance Form, and scholarships do not apply to English language courses or placement years. NET EFFECT: roughly £3,000 off, taking effective tuition to about £14,900, guaranteed and automatic rather than competitive. entry: CONFIRMED VERBATIM: 'Typically we require a 2:1 Honours Degree in an appropriate area. However, if you have solid professional industry experience rather than academic achievement, this may be acceptable for entry to study at this level through a process called Accreditation of Prior Experiential Learning (APEL).' Also confirmed: 'We welcome international applications with equivalent qualifications of our entry requirements' with country-specific equivalence pages. And USW operates a published Contextual Admissions Policy: it 'supports students who have the potential to succeed and who may have faced barriers that make it more difficult to access university', meaning a lower offer may be made based on background and individual circumstances. THE REAL CAVEAT: the 2:1 floor is a full classification higher than the Hertfordshire programmes' 2:2. That is the one place where USW is stricter than Hertfordshire. But 'an appropriate area' for a MUSIC ENGINEERING master's is a materially easier argument for a BSc Software Engineering than 'music' would be.

study: Two individualised years with a chosen professional specialisation among PRODUCTION MUSICALE, SPECTACLE VIVANT or CRÉATION, under personal tutors. Compulsory modules with ECTS: Technologie audio (12), Projets de production / 'Book' (24), Projet de recherche (22), Prise de son classique (9), Prise de son jazz et musiques actuelles (9), Mixage musiques actuelles (9), Mixage musique acoustique (9), Travaux pratiques FSMSI, Communication et gestion de projet (4), Stage FSMSI (20), plus law/regulation and live-performance safety modules. Optional 5-ECTS modules include Design sonore, Mastering, 'Réalisation et mixage en musiques actuelles', 'Vidéo 360, Audio 3D, nouveaux médias', 'Réalisation en informatique musicale : développement, création, répertoire', Direction artistique, Sonorisation, Son à l'image, Arrangement (chanson ou jazz), Création/composition/production pour la musique à l'image. Compulsory two-month placement with the Conservatoire's audiovisual department; research themes include Audio 3D, spatialisation for live performance, augmented reality, 360 video. Optional joint Licence Musique et Musicologie with Sorbonne Université.
recommendation: Curriculum-wise this is the closest thing in France to a genuine music-production and mixing master: prise de son classique/jazz/musiques actuelles, mixage musiques actuelles, mastering, design sonore, Audio 3D, plus a production 'Book'. It is also nearly free and has NO age limit. The realistic obstacle is severe: DEM-level music theory, harmony/counterpoint, musical analysis and an oral musical-training test. Without several years of formal music training he will not clear the admission tests, however strong his engineering background. Worth a long-shot application only if he spends 2026 doing serious formation musicale.

Semester 1: Digital Audio Processing 7.5, Audio Application Programming 7.5, General Acoustics 7.5, Sound Synthesis 7.5 = 30 ECTS. Semester 2: Special Topics in Acoustics 7.5, Applied Machine Learning for Sound and Music 7.5, Sound and Movement 7.5, Optoacoustics 7.5 = 30 ECTS. Semester 3: thesis 30 ECTS. Part-time students take the eight courses across four semesters with up to a year for the thesis. Attendance is compulsory and in person, with a maximum of three absences per course: "Το Π.Μ.Σ. υλοποιείται με τη διά ζώσης εκπαιδευτική διαδικασία. Η παρακολούθηση όλων των μαθημάτων είναι υποχρεωτική."
study: Verified from the official call and the department pages. The programme "explores sound in its multiple dimensions: as a wave, as a signal, and as a carrier of information", combining applied knowledge with current research in digital audio processing, sound synthesis, acoustics and audiovisual technologies, artificial intelligence, and motion tracking for musical applications. The eight compulsory courses: DIGITAL AUDIO PROCESSING — PCM, sampling-rate conversion, spectral analysis, digital filters, noise minimisation, audio coding and decoding; AUDIO APPLICATION PROGRAMMING — building audio and music applications for capture, recording, spectral analysis and signal extraction in Python or C with specialised APIs; GENERAL ACOUSTICS; SOUND SYNTHESIS — advanced synthesis and modulation techniques, computer implementation and their application to contemporary music creation; SPECIAL TOPICS IN ACOUSTICS — musical, structural and psycho-acoustics, electroacoustics, computational acoustics; APPLIED MACHINE LEARNING FOR SOUND AND MUSIC — inferring music content information and sound-scene and event detection for intelligent applications; SOUND AND MOVEMENT — embodied music cognition, multimodality in audio interaction, correlating audio and motion data, and building interactive sound systems in which motion drives sound; OPTOACOUSTICS — optical detection of sound, light-generated sound sources, micro- and nano-acoustics. The thesis may be carried out in one of the collaborating laboratories in Greece or abroad. Weekly timetable for the current year runs Monday and Wednesday afternoons and evenings, 14:15–22:00.
recommendation: The strongest pure-funding case in the slice, and verification improved it on several fronts the prior record had marked as unknown: engineering graduates head the eligible-degree list, there is no portfolio and no audition, the interview can be held remotely, two recommendation letters and a one-page statement are the only written work required, and the sole language certificate demanded is ENGLISH at B2 — Greek is never mentioned as a requirement. Tuition is zero, Rethymno is cheap, and subsidised meals and housing exist. His software background maps directly onto Audio Application Programming, Applied Machine Learning for Sound and Music, and Sound and Movement. Three real obstacles. FIRST, the language of instruction is not published and the courses are timetabled in Greek — he must email the department (chrisoula@hmu.gr, maximoskp@hmu.gr, or the secretariat at ngoniota@hmu.gr) and get a straight answer before committing. SECOND, applications are submitted through morpheus.hmu.gr using TaxisNet credentials, which are Greek tax-authority login codes a Tunisian applicant does not have — he must ask the secretariat for the alternative route for foreign applicants, and should do so early. THIRD, only 15 places, attendance is compulsory and in person with a maximum of three absences per course, and the content is DSP, acoustics and machine learning rather than production or DJing — this would make him an audio engineer or audio-software specialist, not a producer. Worth pursuing as the free, funded, engineering-friendly option, but the language and TaxisNet questions must be settled first.

scholarshipDetail: THIS ENTRY EXISTS BECAUSE IED'S DSU BANDO IS THE CLEAREST PUBLISHED PROOF THAT A NON-EU STUDENT AT AN ITALIAN PRIVATE ACADEMY CAN WIN REGIONAL STATE AID. Key provisions of the Bando DSU 2025/26 (BAN 8203 rev 06, 4 September 2025), total fund €354,392.15 from MUR and Regione Lombardia: ELIGIBILITY expressly includes 'i cittadini di Stati non appartenenti all'Unione Europea' alongside Italians and EU citizens, for students admitted or enrolled on a Diploma Accademico di Primo or Secondo Livello at Milan, Rome, Turin, Cagliari or Florence. INCOME TEST: ISEE Universitario must not exceed €26,516.70 AND ISPE must not exceed €57,645.03 — both jointly. MERIT for a 1st-year II livello student: simply be regularly enrolled by 31 October and hold the first-level title by 31 January; confirmation of the full benefit then requires 40 credits by 10 August. AMOUNTS (including €140 regional-tax reimbursement and €818 meal allowance): in sede €3,383 / €2,950 / €2,114 by income band 1/2/3; pendolari €4,754 / €4,134 / €3,254; FUORI SEDE €8,134 / €7,073 / €5,776. THE DECISIVE DETAIL: under Art. 13(3) DPCM 9/4/2001, NON-EU FOREIGN STUDENTS ARE AUTOMATICALLY CLASSIFIED 'FUORI SEDE' regardless of where they live in Italy (unless their family lives in Italy), provided the accommodation is paid for — so a Tunisian student is placed in the HIGHEST bracket, €5,776 to €8,134 per year. NON-EU DOCUMENTATION: an 'ISEEU-ISPEU parificato' is required, built from foreign family-composition certificate, income declarations from the official tax agency of the country of residence (employer documents are NOT accepted, self-certification is NOT accepted), property and movable-asset statements, all translated into Italian by a recognised translator and legalised; Tunisia is NOT on the exemption or Apostille list published in the bando, so full consular legalisation applies. A floor applies: non-EU students' declared income cannot be counted below €7,002.97/year (the visa subsistence minimum). Free ISEEU assistance is via CAAF CGIL Lombardia under an IED agreement. DEADLINES 2025/26: applications 9 September to 7 November 2025; rent contract for fuori sede status by 10 December 2025. EXCLUSIONS THAT MATTER: anyone already holding an equal or higher qualification is excluded (a BSc does not block a II livello application); anyone receiving another income/merit-based grant for the same year is excluded; FOUNDATION course students are excluded; and the bando covers ONLY Diploma Accademico I/II livello — IED's one-year 'Master' courses are NOT covered. IED separately runs a commercial scholarship competition: 114 scholarships/tutorships covering 50% of tuition for Master of Arts and Master programmes 2025/26 across Italian campuses and Accademia di Como, rising to 127 for 2026/27 across Italy and Spain, open to local and international students including non-EU, covering partial tuition only and NOT living costs or enrolment fees.

Governing rule for him, from the official international-students page: EU or NON-EU citizens holding a "Diploma di Triennio universitario o accademico (o equivalente)" plus a minimum of 15 years of schooling, evidenced by scanned original degree + certified translation + DOV from the Italian embassy, or a CIMEA Diplome certificate. 80% minimum attendance; part-time route available; Erasmus+ up to 12 months. This is also the most natural of the two Saint Louis routes for an engineer: the feeder programmes are the first-level diplomas in Tecnico del Suono and Musica Elettronica, the entrance test is a technical multiple-choice paper rather than a musical performance, and the Wwise/game-engine strand rewards a software background directly. Residual risk unchanged: a candidate judged unprepared can be routed to a pre-accademico year.
portfolio: NONE — RESOLVED, and this reverses the prior record's UNVERIFIED. The official international-students page states plainly: "Per il Corso di Tecnico del Suono non è prevista pre-selezione ma un colloquio attitudinale." This course IS Tecnico del Suono (DCSL61). There is no pre-selection stage and no portfolio to submit — only an aptitude interview. The ensemble-video wording elsewhere on the page belongs to the Jazz/Pop/Songwriting/Classical performer tracks and does not apply.
audition: NO audition and no practical production test. The official Piano di studi publishes the exact test: "PROVA DI AMMISSIONE — 1) Colloquio attitudinale; 2) Test scritto a risposte multiple incentrato sui seguenti argomenti: Fondamenti di audio digitale, Pro Tools, Riprese microfoniche, Protocollo MIDI." That is the whole thing: an aptitude interview plus a written multiple-choice test on digital audio fundamentals, Pro Tools, microphone technique and MIDI. For international candidates these tests can be sat ONLINE between January and June on individually agreed dates; an in-person route exists as a single June session. Numero chiuso: maximum 20 students per academic year.
deadline: 30 April (standing annual window). Later applications considered only against remaining places. Admission tests in June and September in person; online January–June for internationals. duration: 2 years; fortnightly teaching in two consecutive days, approx. 300 contact hours per year. Year 1 = 60 CFA VERIFIED from the official Piano di studi (Storia del Sound Design e della post produzione audio I 6 + Sound Design I 20 + Audio Interattivo non Lineare Wwise I 8 + Tecnologie e tecniche del Restauro I 8 + Tecnologie e tecniche della ripresa e della registrazione audio I 12 + Materie elettive 6). Year 2 lists Restauro II 6 + Sound Design II 20 + Campionamento e post produzione Audio 8 + Wwise II 8 + Ripresa e registrazione II 12 + Materie elettive 3 = 57 CFA in the readable extract; the thesis/final-work line did not render, so the 120 CFA total is inferred rather than fully read.
study: Verified against the course page and the official Piano di studi. SOUND DESIGN I–II (20 CFA each, the largest block): creating, recording and manipulating sound effects — ambiences, specials, Foley, organic and artificial effects — plus the Pro Tools post-production workflow (session setup, AAF/OMF interchange, working to picture, video export, timecode and frame-rate sync), the aesthetics of sound design (analysing a film's sound requirements, sound design in trailers, the relationship between effects and music in modern cinematic language) and hardware technique (microphones, portable recorders). AUDIO INTERATTIVO NON LINEARE WWISE I–II (8 CFA each): non-linear game audio through Audiokinetic Wwise, covering the full 101 syllabus plus advanced material — navigating the Wwise environment, building an implementation to spec, events, spatialisation, non-linear mixing and integration into the game engine. CAMPIONAMENTO E POST PRODUZIONE AUDIO (8): sampling and building custom sound libraries — instruments, modulators, envelopes, mapping, digital sound management. TECNOLOGIE E TECNICHE DEL RESTAURO I–II (8 + 6): audio restoration and remastering, from digitising historic material to recovery and treatment in specialised labs. TECNOLOGIE E TECNICHE DELLA RIPRESA E DELLA REGISTRAZIONE AUDIO I–II (12 each). STORIA DEL SOUND DESIGN E DELLA POST PRODUZIONE AUDIO. Original projects with Saint Louis's Composizione and Musica Applicata alle Immagini departments and with RUFA (Rome University of Fine Arts) and Vigamus.
recommendation: After verification this is the single most ATTAINABLE programme in the slice for him: no portfolio at all, no audition, no performance requirement, an admission test that is an interview plus a multiple-choice paper on digital audio, Pro Tools, mic technique and MIDI — all sittable online from Tunis — and a non-EU entry rule that explicitly accepts his university bachelor. The Wwise and game-engine strand converts his software-engineering background into an immediate advantage. Two honest caveats. First, this is post-production for picture and games, not electronic music production — it will make him employable as a sound designer and give him a paying craft, but it will not by itself make him a producer or a DJ; the sister Music Production biennio is the better fit for the stated goal, and this one is the better fit for the bank balance. Second, tuition is unpublished and the scholarship route runs through ISEE, so treat it as an unpriced fee-paying route until the Segreteria gives him a written quote. Best used as the low-risk Italian application alongside a craft-focused first choice.

institution: Netherlands private higher-education sector (systematic check across NVAO/CROHO-registered private institutio…
programme: MARKET-LEVEL FINDING — no private NVAO-accredited master in sound design or music production exists in the Netherlands
whyChance: Names engineering or computing as a welcome background; portfolio required, so build it
qualification: NONE EXISTS. After searching in both English and Dutch ('master muziekproductie', 'opleiding sound design particulier', 'niet-bekostigde opleiding', 'master sound design Nederland particuliere hogeschool NVAO'), I found NO privately-run, NVAO-accredited master's degree in sound design, music production, audio engineering, music technology, immersive audio or electronic music performance anywhere in the Netherlands.
accreditation: DEFINITIVE STRUCTURAL FINDING. In the Netherlands the audio/music education market splits cleanly in two, with nothing in between. (1) ACCREDITED = PUBLIC. Every NVAO-accredited master in this field belongs to a government-funded ('bekostigd') public institution: HKU Utrecht (Master of Music pathway Music Design; Sound Design and Audio Design at bachelor level), Conservatorium van Amsterdam / AHK (Master Immersive Audio — NVAO-assessed; plus the AEMA associate degree for electronic musicians, English-taught), Codarts Rotterdam, and the Institute of Sonology at the Royal Conservatoire in The Hague. These are all excluded from this brief as public. (2) PRIVATE = UNACCREDITED. Every private audio provider in the country (SAE, Abbey Road Institute, Sound Education, Pro Audio Education, DDMA, Master The Mix, AV Sound Education, DJ School Amsterdam, Music Production Academy) holds at most CRKBO and/or NRTO registration. CRKBO is a short-vocational-education register that governs VAT exemption; NRTO is a private-training trade association quality mark. NEITHER IS AN ACCREDITATION AND NEITHER CONFERS DEGREE STATUS. The sole exception — SAE's MA/MSc — is a UK University of Hertfordshire award delivered fully online, with no Dutch status and no campus component. Meanwhile private institutions that DO hold NVAO accreditation (Tio, Wittenborg, Nyenrode) operate exclusively in business and hospitality.

scholarshipDetail: SECTOR-WIDE FINDING: NOT ONE private Dutch audio provider publishes any scholarship, bursary, fee waiver or discount available to a non-EU or Tunisian applicant. The only financial mechanisms found were (a) upfront-payment savings of €1,300–€5,670 versus instalment plans, (b) alumni/staff discounts of 25% at SAE UK, (c) 35–50% student software discounts at Sound Education and AV Sound Education, and (d) a Dutch study-cost INCOME TAX deduction promoted by Abbey Road Institute and Pro Audio Education, which requires Dutch taxable income and by Abbey Road's own admission 'doesn't apply to those receiving governmental benefits or who aren't yet employed'. That last one is effectively worthless to an incoming international student and should be discounted entirely when comparing prices. Dutch DUO student finance is unavailable at every private provider without exception.

Since he has no portfolio yet, this is a well-specified and industry-credible target to build against for ANY application in any country. Recommend adopting it now.

recommendation: BOTTOM LINE FOR THE NETHERLANDS: DO NOT BUILD THE SEPTEMBER 2027 PLAN AROUND A DUTCH PRIVATE SCHOOL. There is no private NVAO-accredited master in this field in the country, and no private audio provider can sponsor his residence permit — so the two things he needs (an accredited master + a visa) are simply not purchasable from the Dutch private sector at any price. He should concentrate his accredited-master applications on the Spain/Portugal/Italy slices, or reconsider Dutch PUBLIC institutions, which are outside this brief but are the only Dutch route that actually works: the Conservatorium van Amsterdam's Master Immersive Audio (NVAO-assessed) and its English-taught AEMA associate degree for electronic musicians — where, notably, 'when you enroll in an Associate Degree course, you can apply for a visa' — and HKU's Master of Music pathway Music Design. TWO THINGS HE CAN USEFULLY DO IN THE NETHERLANDS ANYWAY, both on an ordinary Schengen tourist visa and neither requiring accreditation: (1) DJ School Amsterdam's Producer Professional Course, ~€2,499 for 20 one-to-one English-language sessions plus 10 studio hours, compressible into two weeks — a direct, efficient way to build the portfolio he lacks; (2) SAE Amsterdam's one-month DJ Certificate at €699–€1,099 (confirm whether the €500 registration fee applies), ideally timed around Amsterdam Dance Event in October for scene contacts. Both are training, not qualifications — but a 4–8 track portfolio built to Abbey Road's published standard is precisely what every accredited master he applies to will ask for, and he does not have one yet. That is the highest-value use of the Netherlands for him.

Roughly 26 contact hours per week on the 2-week DJ/Producer Level 1 course, covering classroom time plus live DJ experiences — note that this is more than three times the weekly contact time SAE Spain publishes for its two-year master. Students play out at Ibiza venues: Café Mambo, Destino Pacha, Blue Marlin, Ibiza Rocks, the Hard Rock Hotel rooftop and Hotel Mare Nostrum have all been named. A free media pack is included — ten professional press shots and two Instagram reels.
recommendation: NOT A MASTER — keep it out of the degree comparison entirely. But judged against what he actually said he wants, this is the most useful and by far the cheapest thing in this batch. He has no portfolio, no IELTS, no music credential and no industry network, and every accredited master will eventually ask him for at least the first of those. Two weeks in Ibiza at roughly 26 contact hours per week, with real DJ sets at Café Mambo and Destino Pacha, a free Ableton Live Suite licence and ten professional press shots plus two Instagram reels, produces precisely the raw material a portfolio-less applicant is missing — and it produces it in a fortnight, on a short-stay Schengen visa, with no IELTS and no portfolio to get in. CONCRETE ADVICE: treat this as portfolio-building in summer 2027, BEFORE or ALONGSIDE a master's application, never instead of one. Book with the 20% early-bird code, read the price directly from the website since it is not machine-readable, and budget separately and honestly for August accommodation in Ibiza. The verdict is CONDITIONAL only because it must never be mistaken for a qualification — as a career investment for a would-be DJ, it is the best value here.

From the department's own page this pass, the mandatory master's coursework includes 'foreign language by specialization, history and theory of artistic creativity, aesthetic-artistic directions of the XX-XXI century', plus the technical core 'spatial sound engineering systems for theatre, cinema and television' and 'digital audio processing' (цифрова обробка звуку). Also note the previous record rendered 'цифрова обробка звуку' as 'digital signal processing' — the accurate translation is digital sound processing, which is a narrower and less transferable thing than DSP as a software engineer would understand it. recommendation: DO NOT APPLY — CONFIRMED, with the evidential basis tightened and one claim about the curriculum corrected. The content is genuinely distinctive and that much survives verification: spatial sound systems for theatre, cinema and television plus digital sound processing in the master's core, four elective blocks including sound design, an in-house teaching theatre, and a three-level department running from bachelor's through a Doctor of Arts, all in specialty 021 Audiovisual Art and Production. It remains the only one of the three that puts spatial/immersive sound in the master's core. Corrections: 'electronic music technologies' and 'musical acoustics' are NOT confirmed as master's core subjects and should be dropped; 'digital signal processing' is more accurately 'digital sound processing', which is a narrower thing than his software background would suggest. Three barriers close it. FIRST, THE WAR: Kyiv, September 2027, a discretionary arts master's — the same objection as NAKKKiM and it is decisive on its own. SECOND, THE LANGUAGE: instruction is entirely Ukrainian with no English route at any level, so he would need a preparatory year before he could even sit the entrance examination — roughly two years diverted into a language with no bearing on a career as an international DJ and producer. THIRD, HE IS THE WRONG APPLICANT AND THE INSTITUTION WILL NOT TELL HIM ANYTHING: entry runs through an undisclosed creative competition in a screen-sound discipline, no open-entry rule is published, no portfolio spec is published, no accreditation decision is published, and no price is published — I established this pass that the entire foreign-applicant page renders with an empty body and the tuition order is an unretrievable scan. An institution that publishes nothing a foreign applicant needs is not one to commit a year of portfolio-building to. VERDICT: record it, do not apply. Rating C. Keep it on file as evidence that Ukraine has real depth in screen and immersive sound — if he ever wants postgraduate film-sound or spatial-audio training and the country is at peace, this department deserves a second look. For September 2027 it is not a candidate.

recommendation: Abertay is the obvious name in UK game audio and the technical research strengths map perfectly onto a programmer. As a Tunisian national he cannot currently apply to the MSc by Research or MPhil — only the PhD route would be open, which is a three-year research commitment and the wrong instrument for someone who wants hands-on production craft. Additionally IELTS 7.0/6.5 is a demanding bar and the application is a research proposal, not music. Monitor whether the CAS restriction lifts for 2027, but do not build a plan around it.

This ties with USW for the lowest English bar in the slice — a real advantage for someone who has not yet tested.
study: Across the first two semesters: two complementary Specialism modules (20 credits each) covering recent developments in the chosen pathway plus technical, research and communication skills; a Practice module devoted entirely to developing individual creative practice with one-to-one tuition; a Seminar module for contextual, aesthetic and theoretical study via group tutorials and practice-based workshops. Additional modules in Music Technology and Society and a Research Project (which may include a work placement). Third semester: Final Project (60 credits), a sustained period of self-directed practice-based work. Assessment is 100% coursework on every module — no exams — and can take the form of practical/design work, portfolio submission, performance, workshop activity, lecture recital, presentation or essay. Staff research spans composition, performance, broadcasting, contemporary music, sound design studies, film music, creative technologies and disability arts practice; Music at Ulster placed joint 2nd in the UK for Research Impact in REF2014.
recommendation: Attractive in three specific ways: the lowest English bar (IELTS 6.0, 5.5 floor), an entry route that explicitly accepts 'another relevant discipline' or evidence of ability, and a September 2027 start already published on a dedicated 2027/28 page. The light one-day-a-week contact pattern would leave him real time to produce. Against it: the programme states it has NO scholarships at all, the 2027/28 international fee is unpublished, the facilities are undocumented, and every applicant faces an interview/audition. Action: email Ulster now for (a) the postgraduate international fee, (b) a studio facilities list, and (c) what form the interview/audition takes for the Composition and Creative Audio pathway. If the fee comes back competitive with Bucks New or USW, this becomes a serious contender; if it comes back near Queen's £23,000, drop it.

JAMU's Divadelní fakulta requires foreign applicants (Slovak citizens excepted) to prove Czech at C1 on the CEFR for exactly two specializations, and Audiovizuální tvorba a divadlo is one of them: 'Požadována je úroveň C1 podle SERR/CEFRL ... pro tyto specializace studijních programů: Audiovizuální tvorba a divadlo, Rozhlasová a televizní dramaturgie a scenáristika.' Other specializations at the same faculty need only B1. Acceptable proof is a certificate from Charles University, Masaryk University, or a Czech secondary-school leaving exam taken in the Czech Republic. This is a certificated, documented, non-negotiable requirement — not an informal expectation. For a candidate with zero Czech in August 2026 targeting a March 2027 application, C1 is unreachable; C1 typically represents 700-800+ contact hours.
englishTest: None — Czech-taught programme, so no IELTS or TOEFL. This is not an advantage: the Czech C1 requirement is far harder than any English test he would otherwise sit.
study: The programme 'propojuje prostředí divadla, filmu a nových médií' — bridging theatre, film and new media — and guides students toward independent creation combining visual art, technology and dramatic thinking in contemporary multimedia forms. THE PREVIOUS RECORD'S CENTRAL NEGATIVE FINDING IS CONFIRMED AND STANDS: sound design is not a specialization here. This is not a sound-design master's, and JAMU's Theatre Faculty does not run a standalone Zvuková tvorba master's. JAMU's actual audio degree is the Audio Engineering Ing. taught jointly with VUT Brno, already captured elsewhere in the database. That finding was correct and is worth keeping precisely because it stops future sweeps from chasing a programme that does not exist.
recommendation: The previous record recommended not pursuing this, and that conclusion is confirmed — but the reasoning was incomplete, and the newly verified facts make the case far more emphatic. The earlier entry treated the Czech language requirement as unknown and worth asking about; it is in fact published, certificated and set at C1 CEFR, the highest tier at the faculty, applied specifically to Audiovizuální tvorba a divadlo and demonstrable only through a Charles University or Masaryk University examination or a Czech secondary-school leaving exam. For a Tunisian applicant with no Czech at all in August 2026 and a 31 March 2027 deadline, that is not a hurdle to plan around — it is a closed door. Even setting language aside, the programme fails on content: it is a theatre and new-media creation degree in which sound design is not a named specialization, admission is decided on a portfolio of theatre/film/new-media work he does not have and would not produce while building a music-production portfolio, and both admission rounds are conducted in Czech. Zero tuition at a genuine public arts academy is real value, and the 31 March deadline fits his September 2027 target perfectly — which is exactly why this needs to be marked clearly rather than left looking attractive on price. Do not apply. The entry's lasting worth is the negative finding, now doubly confirmed: JAMU's Theatre Faculty is widely assumed to host a sound-design master's and it does not; JAMU's real audio degree is the joint VUT Brno Audio Engineering Ing. already in the database. Keeping this record closes that gap permanently.

institution: Janáčkova akademie múzických umění v Brně (JAMU), Hudební fakulta — Katedra kompozice a multimediální tvorby
programme: Multimediální tvorba — navazující magisterské studium (Multimedia Creation, follow-up master)
whyChance: Names engineering or computing as a welcome background, but taught in Czech — language is the real gate
qualification: MgA.
tuition: 0 CZK. Czech-taught study at a Czech public university is tuition-free for all nationalities. Application fee 990 CZK per specialisation (verified in the 2026/27 decree). JAMU's own Czech language verification exam costs 3,000 CZK. Nostrification of the foreign diploma may carry a separate fee.
scholarshipDetail: None found for Tunisians. JAMU publishes no international entrance scholarship for this programme.
entry: CORRECTED AND NOW VERIFIED — this is stricter than previously recorded. Official master's admission page states verbatim: "Podmínkou přijetí je ukončené vysokoškolské vzdělání, dosažené alespoň v bakalářském stupni studia oboru Multimediální tvorba nebo příbuzného uměleckého oboru" (admission conditional on a completed bachelor's in Multimedia Creation OR A RELATED ARTISTIC FIELD). Plus, from the 2026/27 decree, a HARD Czech-language barrier: "cizí státní příslušníci (s výjimkou uchazečů ze Slovenské republiky), musí předložit vysvědčení o vykonání požadované zkoušky z českého jazyka dle stanovených podmínek (B1 SERR)" — foreign nationals must produce a Czech B1 CEFR certificate (in the 2026/27 cycle by 14 June 2026), plus officially translated bachelor documents and, for a foreign diploma, a nostrification decision. JAMU runs its own Czech verification exam (3,000 CZK) focused on music/culture vocabulary; accredited B1 CEFR certificates are also accepted. Mandatory attachments: proof of bachelor completion, structured CV.
acceptsNonMusic: Check, leaning NO. The published condition is a bachelor "in Multimedia Creation or a related ARTISTIC field" — a software-engineering BSc is not an artistic field, so acceptance is at the committee's discretion. There IS an explicit route: applicants from another field are tested by the three-part practical exam above. Combined with the Czech B1 certificate requirement, this is a genuine barrier, not a formality. The department's talent advisory service (booking address for Multimediální tvorba is fajnor@jamu.cz; department head doc. Dan Dlouhý, dlouhy@jamu.cz) is the correct first contact.
portfolio: PARTIALLY CORRECTED. At MASTER level the official page requires only "portfolio dosavadních uměleckých a jiných odborných aktivit" (portfolio of previous artistic and other professional activities) with NO published number, duration or format. IMPORTANT: the widely-quoted "minimum 20 / maximum 40 items" spec is the BACHELOR-level requirement (bachelor page: "Předložení portfolia domácích prací v celkovém počtu minimálně 20 nebo maximálně 40 položek", worth 10%) — do not apply it to the MgA. The master's application must ALSO include, in writing: a concept for the master's project, and a proposed diploma-thesis topic with basic theses.
audition: On-site, single-round, in Brno. Talent exam = 90% of the score, conducted as an oral interview (ústní pohovor) assessing prior study results and the bachelor graduation project, the portfolio, the written master's project concept, the written thesis-topic proposal, knowledge of current developments in the field, and language readiness. Foreign-language written test = 10%, a lexico-grammatical test at B2+ CEFR including specialist music terminology. CRUCIAL EXTRA: "V případě uchazeče, který absolvoval bakalářské studium v jiném (byť příbuzném) oboru, se úroveň jeho znalostí prověří praktickou zkouškou" — an applicant from a different field sits an additional practical exam in three parts: (a) a thematic task, a multimedia-work project on a set theme; (b) a practical task on the visual component; (c) a free task in any media with a compulsory musical component. 2026/27 exam date was 16 June 2026 (KKMT). Only 2 places.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Verified 2026/27 decree: applications open January and close 10 May 2026; talent exam 16 June 2026; Czech B1 certificate due 14 June 2026; single round. For September 2027 entry expect roughly a 10 May 2027 deadline with a mid-June 2027 exam — not yet published as of July 2026.
opens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. In the 2026/27 cycle the E-PŘIHLÁŠKA opened in January 2026 at is.jamu.cz. Expect January 2027 for the 2027/28 cycle.
duration: 2 years (BcA. 4 + MgA. 2). ECTS not published on the programme or admissions pages — UNVERIFIED (Czech follow-up master's standard is 120).
study: CONFIRMED on the official page: works using "multiple, meaningfully and irreplaceably complementary media within a single work" — performance, interactive installation, video art, opera, experimental documentary, computer games. Contemporary composition, electronic music, multimedia design and collaborative creative work, using electroacoustic studios, multichannel audio, modular synthesis and field-recording gear. Teaching shared across JAMU's Music and Theatre faculties, BUT's Faculty of Fine Arts and Masaryk University. Final state exam (official): public presentation and defence of the final artistic work plus written documentation, a diploma thesis of at least 40 pages, and exams in Multimedia Composition and Contemporary Trends and Theory of Composition.
recommendation: Superb kit for electronic music and genuinely experimental, but three verified obstacles now stack against him: a Czech B1 certificate is mandatory for foreign nationals with a hard deadline weeks before the exam; the entry condition names an artistic bachelor; and only 2 places exist. The added three-part practical exam for other-field applicants is a fair route but assumes visual and multimedia authorship, not DJ/production. Also note the direction is installation and sound art, not club releases.

entry: VERBATIM: 'Komu je program určen: Program je určen absolventům bakalářského studia – bez omezení.' (The programme is intended for graduates of bachelor's studies — WITHOUT RESTRICTION.) A foreign bachelor's degree requires 'a certificate of recognition of foreign higher education and qualifications' (nostrifikace) — this can take up to two months; Germany, Hungary, Poland and Slovenia are exempt by bilateral treaty, Tunisia is NOT, so budget the recognition step.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — EXPLICITLY. QUOTED: 'Program je určen absolventům bakalářského studia – bez omezení.' No music degree, no conservatoire training and no prior field of any kind is required. A BSc in Software Engineering is squarely eligible; the exam even rewards 'produkce a programování zvuku' knowledge, which plays to his background.
portfolio: NOT A HARD PORTFOLIO. VERBATIM: 'Uchazeč/ka předloží detailní návrh vlastního kreativního projektu (max. 2 normostrany), který odráží jeho motivaci a profiluje směr jeho studia. … Ukázky vlastních tvůrčích prací s detailnějším autorským komentářem jsou vítány.' — a detailed proposal for the applicant's own creative project, MAXIMUM 2 standard pages, uploaded to the e-application under 'Dokumenty' by 1 JUNE, with the applicant's full name and application number on it. Samples of the applicant's own creative work with detailed authorial commentary are WELCOMED but NOT REQUIRED, and no number, length or file format is prescribed. This is the single most forgiving submission requirement found in the entire sweep for someone with no portfolio yet.
audition: NO AUDITION, NO EAR-TRAINING EXAM, NO PRACTICAL PRODUCTION TEST. VERBATIM: 'Přijímací zkouška má formu ústního pohovoru a je složena ze dvou částí: 1. Zkouška odborných a uměleckých předpokladů … Okruhy otázek vycházejí z následujících tematických okruhů: technické předpoklady zvukové tvorby, produkční předpoklady zvukové tvorby, produkce a programování zvuku, teorie, estetika a historie zvukové tvorby. 2. Kreativní projekt a motivace ke studiu.' It is an ORAL INTERVIEW: a knowledge examination on sound technique/production/theory (max 40 points) plus defence of the creative project and motivation (max 60 points). Scoring: 'V přijímacím řízení je možné dosáhnout maximálně 100 bodů. Pro přijetí je nutné dosáhnout minimálně 50 bodů.' Reading list published (Cox & Warner Audiokultúra; Kurfürst Základy hudební akustiky; Flašar Elektroakustická hudba; Schafer; Nyman; Bourriaud) — the exam is studiable. Waiver of the knowledge part is granted only to graduates of Teorie interaktivních médií, Sdružená uměnovědná studia, Hudební věda and Teorie a provozovací praxe staré hudby.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE: applications 1 January – 30 April (2026 round: 1. 1. – 30. 4. 2026). The Faculty of Arts also runs a second window 1 August – 30 November. The creative project must be uploaded to the e-application by 1 JUNE. Expect 1 Jan – 30 April 2027 for a September 2027 start.
duration: 2 years / 120 ECTS
languageReq: CZECH. MUNI requires 'proof of proficiency in the language of instruction'; the exact level and accepted certificates for follow-up master's applicants ARE NOT PUBLISHED on the application guide — UNVERIFIED. The entrance exam itself is an oral interview conducted in Czech, so functional Czech is required in practice. MUNI offers preparatory language courses for applicants who need them. THIS IS THE ONE REAL BARRIER: he has Arabic, French and English, and would need roughly a year of Czech before the September 2027 interview.
study: VERBATIM: 'Cílem studia je příprava absolventů studijního programu na plnění požadavků praktického provozu, ve kterém je kreativně nakládáno se zvukem.' Four thematic blocks: 'Zvuková tvorba – technické předpoklady (matematika, fyzika, akustika, studiová technika); Zvuková tvorba – produkční předpoklady (zvukový design); Produkce zvuku; programování zvuku (práce ve studiu a se studiovou technikou, audio software); Teorie, dějiny a současnost zvukové tvorby (zvuková studia).' CRUCIALLY, the practicum block is explicit record-making: 'práce v nahrávacím studiu (stavba nahrávací techniky ve studiu / nahrávání / postprodukce / MASTERING / administrativa), ozvučení živé hudební produkce, autonomní zvuková produkce v digitálních prostředích DAWs, Pure Data ad.' Practice runs across all four semesters plus a compulsory six-week external placement (partners include Filharmonie Brno, Národní divadlo Brno, RoSound, Národní filmový archiv, Rozhlas a televízia Slovenska, Centrum současného umění DOX). The programme is broader than pop-record production — it also serves theatre, galleries, film, radio/TV, games and installations — but recording, post-production and mastering are named core competences.

deadline: CONFIRMED for the prior cycle: master's applications 1 January - 30 April 2026; entrance examination 10 June 2026; results published by 7 July 2026. study: Sound within the Audiovisual Arts studio: recording, sound dramaturgy, post-production and mixing for film/TV/advertising, taught alongside camera, directing and screenwriting, editing, production and visual effects so students crew shared productions. CORRECTION: the previous record stated that Visual Effects exists at bachelor level but is NOT continued at master level. recommendation: BEST-VALUE ARTISTIC OPTION IN THE SLICE AND STILL THE HARDEST TO ENTER — assessment unchanged, with one factual fix (Visual Effects IS offered at master level, so there are six specializations competing for the ~25 places, not five). The two obstacles are unchanged and both are hard: the entrance examination is conducted in Czech and doubles as the language screen, and he would need a portfolio strong enough to take one of a handful of Sound Design places. Add Saarbrücken living costs and the blocked account (currently around EUR 12,000 for the year). Plus the unbudgeted cost of travelling to Saarbrücken for the in-person aptitude exam, and whatever the unpublished transition programme charges. On tuition alone this is one of the cheapest real master's degrees available to him anywhere.

entry: HARD GATE, CONFIRMED: open to graduates of academic or artistic BA programmes with AT LEAST 240 ECTS. His 180-ECTS Tunisian BSc does NOT meet this and he cannot argue his way past it. HBKsaar states that applicants with fewer credits are offered a transition programme drawn from its own former bachelor programmes ('Übergangsprogramm') — the length, cost, residence basis and admission terms of that bridge remain UNPUBLISHED after direct checking of the master overview and application pages. That single unknown decides whether this programme is reachable for him at all. Ask mad@hbksaar.de.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — no music degree is required, and a computing background is not itself a barrier at a media-art college. The obstacles are the 240-ECTS rule, the German B2 requirement, the in-person aptitude exam, and the need for a genuinely artistic portfolio.
portfolio: CORRECTED from 'NOT PUBLISHED'. It is published, on the application information page. Media Art & Design applicants must submit a PORTFOLIO OF WORK SAMPLES together with a LETTER OF MOTIVATION and a PROJECT PROPOSAL (Projektvorhaben). Format: PDF, maximum 100 MB; larger material such as video must be supplied as external links (YouTube, Vimeo, cloud storage). Applications go through the SIM application portal. This is an artistic portfolio judged as art — a year of bedroom production tracks will not read as one unless he deliberately builds installation, audiovisual or sound-art pieces with a stated concept.
audition: CORRECTED — the previous record said 'None', which is wrong. Master applicants must pass an EIGNUNGSPRÜFUNG (aptitude examination). After the submitted materials are assessed, shortlisted candidates proceed to an oral/practical examination which is held IN PERSON at the institution in Saarbrücken. For a Tunisian applicant this is a real and expensive obstacle: it means a Schengen short-stay visa and a trip to the Saarland before any study visa exists. Ask mad@hbksaar.de whether remote examination is ever permitted for overseas candidates — do not assume it is.
deadline: CORRECTED from 'NOT PUBLISHED'. languageReq: CORRECTED, and materially better news than assumed. Accepted certificates: TestDaF level 4 in all four sections, Goethe-Zertifikat B2, telc Deutsch B2, DSH level 2, or DSD II with at least B2 in all sections. B2 is a realistic target for a fluent French speaker inside the 2026-27 window; DSH-2 would not have been.
englishTest: None — German-taught, so IELTS/TOEFL is irrelevant. His unwritten English test is not the obstacle here; German B2 is.
study: Projektstudium — self-directed project work on electronic, time-based and interactive productions, with students setting their own priorities and drawing on resources across all departments. Supervised by Profs. Burkhard Detzler, Sung-Hyung Cho and Eric Lanz. Extensive workshops: wood, printing, CNC, 3D printing, metal, plus media project spaces.
recommendation: CONDITIONAL, rating C — the record is much better documented than before, and most of the corrections went in his favour, but the one obstacle that matters did not move. Corrected on this pass: the master exists and is NOT suspended; teaching is in German; the language bar is B2, not DSH-2, which is genuinely achievable for him; the deadlines are published (31 May for winter, 30 November for summer), so a September 2027 start means 31 May 2027; the portfolio requirement is published and specific (PDF under 100 MB, plus motivation letter and project proposal); there IS an aptitude examination, held in person in Saarbrücken, which the previous record wrongly recorded as 'none'; and the real cost is EUR 0 tuition plus EUR 422.20 a semester including the Deutschlandticket. What did not change is the 240-ECTS entry rule, which his 180-ECTS BSc fails, and the transition programme that might bridge it remains entirely unpublished despite direct checking. So this is not a thin record any more — it is a well-documented programme with one decisive unknown. The action is unchanged and cheap: one email to mad@hbksaar.de and s.rauber@hbksaar.de asking exactly two things now that the rest is settled — the terms, length, cost and residence basis of the transition programme for a 180-ECTS holder, and whether the in-person aptitude exam can be taken remotely from Tunisia. If the bridge is short and carries a visa, this becomes a serious B. If not, it is closed. Separately, be clear-eyed that even on success this is a media-ART degree with sound as one medium among many — it serves an installation and audiovisual practice, not a career as a DJ and record producer. entry: CONFIRMED — THE MOST OPEN DOOR OF THE SIX, in the regulation's own words. Three routes: a bachelor in Music; a bachelor in Art; or, quoted from the official record, 'bei Vorliegen einer hohen künstlerischen Befähigung, festgestellt durch die Eignungsprüfung, ist auch die Zulassung von Bewerber*innen möglich, die einen anderen Studiengang abgeschlossen haben' — applicants who completed a DIFFERENT degree programme may be admitted on high artistic aptitude established by the aptitude examination. That third route is precisely his situation and it is written into the rules, not a favour. Also confirmed: the aptitude examination must be completed within one year of enrolment.
acceptsNonMusic: YES, EXPLICITLY — CONFIRMED in the regulation's own wording. Combined with the A1 German bar, this is the most permissive formal profile found anywhere in this set.
portfolio: CONFIRMED, and it remains the most concretely writable specification of the six. The application must contain: a CV; a written justification of the choice of programme; studiengangsbezogene Arbeitsproben (work samples relevant to the field); and a description of planned artistic projects plus a project sketch in sound-art composition. His portfolio year should be built to produce exactly these four items and nothing else.
audition: CONFIRMED, and CORRECTED on one detail. Two-stage Eignungsprüfung, and it is NOT an instrumental audition. Stage 1: pre-selection by committee on submitted materials, after which shortlisted candidates are given a theme for a project sketch 6 to 12 weeks before the interview. Stage 2: an aptitude CONVERSATION in which the candidate presents the prepared project sketch and discusses artistic background and motivation. CORRECTION: the published length is 30 to 45 minutes, with a minimum of 20 minutes per applicant — the previous record's '20-45 minutes' was slightly off. No instrument, no performance, no conservatory technique is tested. For a candidate with no conservatory training this is a far more winnable format than a classical audition, and the 6-12 week preparation window means the decisive work happens at home, not on the spot.
deadline: CORRECTED — the previous record said 'NOT PUBLISHED'. That was wrong. The application/registration deadline for the Eignungsprüfung is 1 APRIL for the following winter semester, with registration opening 1 February. For a September/October 2027 start he registers between 1 February and 1 April 2027. The previous record's instinct was right that music-college deadlines fall far earlier than university ones — 1 April is over three months before TH Köln's 15 July. Critically, the pre-selection stage plus a 6-12 week project-sketch preparation window means his real work starts in 2026, not 2027.
opens: CORRECTED — the previous record said this was not published. IT IS PUBLISHED. Registration for the Eignungsprüfung for the following winter semester runs from 1 February to 1 April. He should still confirm the exact 2027 dates with the Studienbüro, but the window is no longer a mystery.
duration: 4 semesters (2 years). The exact ECTS figure is still not stated on the pages checked — STILL UNVERIFIED; the Studien- und Prüfungsordnung on download.uni-mainz.de will state it, and a German MMus of this length is normally 120 ECTS. Additional published rule, confirmed: applicants whose bachelor is not yet conferred at the application deadline need at least 135 ECTS.
languageReq: CONFIRMED, AND IT IS AS LOW AS PREVIOUSLY REPORTED. The official JGU study-programme record demands only 'der Nachweis hinreichender deutscher Sprachkenntnisse (vergleichbar Niveau A1-GERR)' — German comparable to CEFR A1, required only of applicants without a prior qualification from a German-language institution, and provable either by certificate OR through the interview conducted during the aptitude examination. A1 is achievable in a few months of evening classes. This is by a wide margin the lowest published German-language bar of the six and it is the single fact that makes this programme reachable for a non-German speaker. Confirm in writing with the HfM Mainz Studienbüro, since it is atypical.
englishTest: None — German-taught, and only A1 German demanded. IELTS/TOEFL is irrelevant here.
study: Advanced individual artistic-compositional research; collaboration with media and art institutions; spatial and multichannel work. Career destinations named by the school: independent artistic practice, media, radio, and museum sound design.
recommendation: The re-check upgraded this record rather than downgrading it, and it now has a published deadline where it previously had a blank. Everything remarkable about it verified: an applicant from an unrelated degree is EXPLICITLY admissible on artistic aptitude, only A1 German is demanded on paper and can even be evidenced through the interview itself, the aptitude test is a project conversation rather than an instrumental audition, the candidate gets 6-12 weeks at home to prepare the decisive project sketch, and the whole cost is a semester contribution. Two corrections he must act on: the deadline IS published — registration for the Eignungsprüfung runs 1 February to 1 April for the following winter semester, so his date is 1 April 2027, not a mid-summer university deadline; and the aptitude conversation is 30-45 minutes (minimum 20), not 20-45. It stays CONDITIONAL and B rather than A for one honest reason: it is sound-art COMPOSITION — spatial, intermedial, radiophonic, Ars Acustica — not dance-music production, and he must genuinely want that rather than treat it as a side door into Europe. That said, of the three artistic options it is the only one whose curriculum names ELECTRONIC COMPOSITION outright, and it is the only programme in this entire set where a non-music engineering graduate is admissible by written rule rather than by committee discretion. Two things to do this year: get the Studien- und Prüfungsordnung and the confirmed ECTS figure from the Studienbüro, and start building the project sketch, because that single document decides everything. verdictWhy: This is the best value proposition in the batch and deserves to be at the top of his list. A real Master of Music in contemporary popular music production, from a German state university, with no tuition fee; entry demands only two self-produced tracks plus a production made from raw material they send him — a production test, not an audition, with no ear-training exam and no instrument; and the German requirement is A2, not C1, which he can genuinely reach by March 2027. Confirm with Prof. Podmore that a software engineering BSc counts as an 'affine subject', and treat the 2 March non-EU deadline as the real date.
correction: THREE corrections, all substantial. (1) Gate recorded as 'Portfolio + exam/interview' — this misses the defining feature. The gate is a PRACTICAL PRODUCTION TEST: 'you prepare a production from the (raw) material you receive from us in advance after the application deadline'. That is the job, not a barrier, and it should never be filed with the auditions. (2) The record does not capture that the German requirement is only A2 — far below HAW Hamburg's C1 and Babelsberg's DSH-1 — which is what makes this the one reachable German programme in the batch. (3) The record gives no deadline; the operative one for a Tunisian is the non-EU deadline of 2 March for winter-semester entry, not the general deadline.
qualification: Master of Music (M.Mus.)

tuition: €0 tuition (North Rhine-Westphalia charges no tuition to non-EU students)
otherFees: Semester contribution UNVERIFIED (NRW typically approx. €250–300/semester incl. Semesterticket)
totalCost: Tuition €0; approx. €1,100 in semester fees over 2 years; Cologne living costs approx. €1,000–1,200/month

The programme page itself does not enumerate accepted bachelor degrees — that list comes from the admission regulations, so treat the exact wording as PARTIALLY UNVERIFIED and request the Zulassungsordnung. audition: CONFIRMED that an Eignungsprüfung is required. The exact format for Sound Art remains UNVERIFIED here; contact HMTM admissions. Regular online information sessions for the Sound Art master are held and remain the cheapest way for him to learn the real bar.
deadline: CONFIRMED: 31 May for a winter start. For a September/October 2027 intake that is 31 May 2027. The previous record's 12:00 noon detail is not restated on the current page — treat the deadline as 31 May and submit well before, not on the day.
opens: Via the HMTM application portal (zulassung.hmtm.de). Opening date STILL UNVERIFIED — watch the portal from roughly March.
duration: CONFIRMED: 4 semesters, 120 ECTS.
languageReq: CONFIRMED AS PUBLISHED: German is the language of instruction and no certificate is required. The caution from the previous record stands and should be repeated to him: an artistic aptitude procedure conducted in German is a de facto language test even when no certificate appears on paper, and four semesters of German-language study is not something 'no certificate required' makes painless. recommendation: Verification confirmed everything material and improved the accreditation picture — accredited 1 October 2023 to 30 September 2031, 120 ECTS, German with no language certificate demanded, 31 May deadline, semester fee only. It is a real, properly accredited, essentially free state degree and nothing about it is a rip-off. But for HIM it stays a C, for two reasons that verification did not soften. First, it is portfolio-gated at the front door: entry runs through an artistic project proposal and an Eignungsprüfung, and he has neither a proposal nor a body of sound work, so this is an aspiration for a later cycle rather than a September 2027 plan. Second, be blunt about direction — this is installation, sonification and research sound art, explicitly framed around acoustic ecology and sound as political act. It does not serve the international-DJ-and-producer goal, and pretending otherwise would waste his portfolio year. Two zero-cost steps if he is drawn to it anyway: download the 'Anforderungen im Eignungsverfahren' document from the programme page so he sees the actual bar rather than a summary, and attend one of the free online information sessions to ask Prof. Bovermann directly whether a software-engineering applicant with a year of self-built sound work has a route. Given Bovermann's own engineering and live-coding background, that answer may be more encouraging than the formal requirements suggest.

otherFees: CORRECTED from UNVERIFIED — the semester contribution at HMTMH is approximately EUR 427 per semester for students at the Expo Plaza site, which is where the IJK is located (the Neues Haus site pays about EUR 395). It comprises the Studentenwerk contribution of EUR 130 for Expo Plaza, the AStA contribution of EUR 13.20 including theatre flat rate and bicycle workshops, and the semester transport ticket, which accounts for most of the balance. Late re-registration costs an extra EUR 50; the re-registration window for the winter semester closes on 30 June each year.
