entry: CORRECTED AND DECISIVE — the previous record described this as 'ambiguous' and it is not. The rule requires a bachelor in communication science, media studies, musicology, or a music-related artistic-academic programme, OR another academically related prior degree, that contains AT LEAST 60 ECTS OF CREDIT IN MUSIC, COMMUNICATION, MEDIA OR SOCIAL SCIENCE COMPONENTS. That 60-ECTS subject quota is the real gate, and it is the fact the previous record missed. A BSc Software Engineering from SMU MedTech will not carry 60 ECTS in those fields — a computing curriculum is mathematics, programming, systems and engineering. Half a year's worth of media, music or social science credit simply is not there to point at. Note also that the phrase 'another academically related prior degree' is what admits, say, a sociology or marketing graduate; it does not dissolve the 60-ECTS quota that follows it. He fails on credit content, not on the absence of a music degree.
acceptsNonMusic: CORRECTED — the honest answer is EFFECTIVELY NO, for him. No music degree is required and no instrument is needed, which sounds welcoming, but the 60-ECTS subject quota in music/communication/media/social science does the excluding instead. A software engineering graduate does not clear it. He could submit the prior-study form and argue the case into a 17-place cohort, but he would be asking for a discretionary exception on the single criterion the programme uses to filter.
portfolio: None. Required documents are proof of the relevant bachelor or first degree, a transcript of records with grades (translated where necessary), a CV, and German language proof at TestDaF 4. Optional but recommended: evidence of vocational training, internships, work experience and intercultural experience, plus a prior-study form which the institute specifically recommends for applicants whose background differs from communication, media or music studies — that form would be his only avenue for arguing the 60-ECTS point.
audition: None — CONFIRMED, and worth stating plainly: there is no entrance examination and no interview. Selection is made on submitted documents alone. It is also explicitly confirmed that playing an instrument is NOT a requirement for this programme. The barrier is entirely the academic credit profile.
deadline: CORRECTED from 'NOT published'. It is published: 15 JUNE for the winter semester and 15 JANUARY for the summer semester. For a September 2027 start his deadline would be 15 JUNE 2027, well outside the October 2026-February 2027 window he has been planning around.
opens: CORRECTED — the online application window for the winter semester runs from approximately 20 May to 15 June. Applications are submitted through the institute's online platform.
duration: CORRECTED from UNVERIFIED — 120 ECTS over 4 semesters, modular, confirmed. Only 17 places are awarded per year, making this a very small and competitive cohort.
languageReq: CORRECTED from UNVERIFIED — now on record. German at TestDaF level TDN 4 minimum is required, and it is required ONLY of applicants who do not hold a German higher-education entrance qualification. As a Tunisian applicant he falls squarely in that group, so TestDaF 4 is mandatory for him. Note this is TDN 4 across the board, a higher bar than HBKsaar's B2.
englishTest: None — German-taught. His unwritten IELTS/TOEFL is irrelevant here; TestDaF 4 is what he would need.
study: CONFIRMED as a research and management degree with no studio craft whatsoever. The reformed structure runs six study modules plus an examination module, including three research projects, advanced methods training completed by the end of the third semester, strategic management in media and music, an individual profiling module, and a master thesis with defence. He would be studying the music industry as an object of research, not learning to make records in it.
recommendation: AVOID for his stated goal, rating C — and the verification pass turned the previous record's 'ambiguous' entry assessment into a clear no. The programme is real, genuinely prestigious, costs EUR 0 in tuition and about EUR 427 a semester, and carries an unproblematic student visa. Corrections made on this pass: it is 120 ECTS over four semesters, not an unknown quantity; the deadlines are published at 15 June for winter and 15 January for summer, so a September 2027 entry means 15 June 2027; German is required at TestDaF TDN 4 for anyone without a German school-leaving qualification, which includes him; there is no entrance exam, no interview and no instrument requirement, selection being on documents alone; and the semester contribution is about EUR 427 at the IJK's Expo Plaza site. The decisive correction is the entry rule: admission requires a prior degree containing at least 60 ECTS in music, communication, media or social science subjects. That quota, not the absence of a music degree, is what excludes him — a software engineering curriculum does not contain half a year of such credit, and he would be seeking a discretionary exception on the very criterion used to rank a 17-place cohort. Even setting that aside, the fit is wrong in kind: this degree researches the music industry and teaches strategic management of it, in German, with no studio craft anywhere in the seven modules. Nothing in it moves him toward producing records or DJing. Reconsider only if his ambition genuinely shifts from making music to researching or managing the business of it, in which case it becomes a strong option worth learning German for. Take it if he wants Cologne, a recognised credential, near-zero cost and creative freedom — not if he wants production drills.

entry: Bachelor's degree or equivalent; German B2 (Goethe); aptitude assessment based on a portfolio, a motivation letter and a detailed project proposal for the chosen focus area. No numerus clausus. Aptitude-test fee €50 (first application; €10 per further application). Application via muvac; links open about one month before the deadline.
acceptsNonMusic: Yes — explicitly, and this remains the clearest published welcome to a non-music graduate of any German programme in this batch. Official page: 'Musical practice is not bound to musical instruments; it encompasses many approaches to art and research. Accordingly, the master's program is open to students from all disciplinary backgrounds.' A software-engineering BSc qualifies on paper, and his coding ability is directly relevant to the algorithmic strand (the programme is co-led by Prof. Julian Rohrhuber, known for live-coding/SuperCollider work).
portfolio: NOW EXACT (from the official German Anforderungen page). Three documents, uploaded with the aptitude-test registration in the online portal: (1) 'ein Portfolio mit bereits realisierten Projekten' from the chosen focus area (Transmediale Formen or Epistemische Medien) — no number, duration or format limit is published; (2) a motivation letter expressing the applicant's interest in that specific focus area; (3) 'eine ausführliche Beschreibung eines Projektvorhabens mit detailliertem Zeitplan sowie konkreten Ideen zur Mitarbeit von Mitstudierenden in diesem Projekt' — a detailed project proposal WITH a detailed timetable AND concrete ideas for how fellow students would contribute to the project. That last element is unusual and easy to miss: the proposal must be designed as collaborative work.
audition: No audition, no on-site test, and — importantly — the assessment is REMOTE: 'Das Projekt muss anschließend der Auswahlkommission in einer Online-Präsentation vorgestellt werden. Darauf folgt ein Online-Bewerbungsgespräch mit der Kommission. Die Präsentation und das Gespräch dauern zusammen maximal 60 Minuten.' An online presentation of the project to the selection panel followed by an online interview, together max 60 minutes. No travel to Germany is needed to apply.
deadline: 31 October, published as a standing annual rule: 'Die Bewerbungsfrist ist stets der 31. Oktober' (and the central deadlines page confirms 'Der Bewerbungsschluss zum Sommersemester ist der 31. Oktober'). Aptitude tests are held for the SUMMER SEMESTER ONLY: 'Für den Masterstudiengang Klang und Realität gibt es Eignungsprüfungen ausschließlich zum Sommersemester.' Courses start at the beginning of April. CONSEQUENCE FOR HIM: a September 2027 start is impossible. The reachable options are apply by 31 October 2026 for an April 2027 start, or 31 October 2027 for April 2028.
opens: About one month before the deadline: 'Die Bewerbungslinks werden in jedem Jahr etwa einen Monat vor dem jeweiligen Bewerbungsschluss freigeschaltet' — so roughly late September each year, via muvac.
duration: 4 semesters / two years, full-time. The '120 ECTS' figure is NOT stated on the official programme page or the Modulplan page — UNVERIFIED.
study: Project-driven master integrating performative, compositional and algorithmic forms of contemporary art. The student's own project sits at the centre and is re-conceptualised across two years on the basis of critical, multi-perspectival peer feedback. Two focus areas (Studienschwerpunkte), and the application is made to ONE of them: Epistemic Media (art as a method of enquiry — acoustic research, documentary film, algorithmic composition) and Transmedia Forms (performance, sound art, installation, digital media). CONFIRMED on the official page, including that 'Musical practice is not bound to musical instruments'.
recommendation: By far the easiest German conservatory door for him to open: open to all disciplinary backgrounds in the school's own words, no audition, no on-site test, assessment by a 60-minute online presentation and interview, and no tuition. His coding background is a genuine asset for the algorithmic strand. Three real caveats. First, German B2 is required — though the Kollegstudierender route lets him produce the certificate during year one, which is the softest German requirement of any RSH programme. Second, the intake is April only, so this cannot serve a September 2027 target; the nearest realistic entry is April 2027 (apply 31 October 2026 — that is roughly three months from now) or April 2028. Third and most important for his actual goal: this is artistic-research and transmedia practice, not production craft. He would graduate with a conceptual sound-art practice and a strong European network, not with mixing, mastering or dance-floor production chops. Best used as a funded, low-barrier route into a German art scene if he is genuinely drawn to experimental and algorithmic work — not as a producer's apprenticeship.

entry: Verbatim: 'Studierende, die an der KUG/TU Graz das Bachelorstudium Elektrotechnik - Toningenieur abgeschlossen haben, erfüllen die Aufnahmevoraussetzungen.' External applicants need a 'gleichwertiges und zur Zulassung berechtigtes Studium' (equivalent qualifying prior degree); up to 30 additional ECTS from the bachelor programme may be prescribed. External applicants must also pass an admission examination and submit 'certificates of your musical-artistic background' to the KUG Studien- und Prüfungsabteilung by 30 June.
acceptsNonMusic: YES IN PRINCIPLE, conditionally. The rule is 'gleichwertiges und zur Zulassung berechtigtes Studium' judged by the dean, with 'up to 30 additional ECTS from the bachelor program may be required' — an engineering/computer-science bachelor is the natural equivalence route here, unlike the pure music schools. BUT the candidate must still pass the KUG artistic aptitude test and produce 'certificates of your musical-artistic background', which he does not have. This is the single most engineering-friendly entry in the DACH territory for a software-engineering BSc.
portfolio: No track portfolio. Instead: bachelor transcript/diploma plus certificates of musical-artistic background, submitted to KUG by 30 June.
audition: APTITUDE TEST, not a performance audition and not a production test. Three written components: (1) Seashore Test, ~40 min — discrimination of frequency, intensity and duration, plus timbre and rhythm memory; (2) Ear Training Test, ~20 min — melodic and rhythmic dictation, interval, chord and instrument recognition; (3) Music Theory Test, ~15 min — intervals, scales, rhythm notation. Held online.
deadline: Documents to KUG by 30 June; application to the admission exam by 3 June, exam 27 June (dates shown for the 2027 exam cycle on the KUG page — treat as indicative, reconfirm). Study starts winter semester.
duration: 4 semesters / 120 ECTS
study: Inter-university Tonmeister/audio-engineering master combining electrical engineering and IT coursework with music practice, recording studio work, acoustics, audio signal processing and sound engineering. Taught jointly by TU Graz and KUG (home of the IEM).

External applicants must hold 'ein gleichwertiges und zur Zulassung berechtigendes Studium' (an equivalent degree conferring admission eligibility); equivalence is assessed by the Dean of Studies, and 'je nach Vorbildung und zur Erlangung der vollen Gleichwertigkeit' up to 30 ECTS of courses and exams from the bachelor programme may be prescribed. All externals must pass the admission examination. German C1, or A2 at application plus the supplementary German exam. Documents: bachelor diploma and final certificate, transcript of records, all with official German or English translations and possibly diplomatic legalisation, via KUGonline.
acceptsNonMusic: YES, by design — the clearest technical-entry route in Austria. Official wording: 'Externe Studienwerber*innen, die kein Bachelorstudium der Studienrichtung Elektrotechnik-Toningenieur an der KUG/TU Graz absolviert haben, müssen über ein gleichwertiges und zur Zulassung berechtigendes Studium verfügen', with 'bis zu 30 ECTS aus dem Bachelorstudium Elektrotechnik–Toningenieur' potentially prescribed. A software-engineering BSc is a plausible base, but the Dean of Studies rules on equivalence and an SE degree is not an electrical-engineering degree — the 30-ECTS top-up is likely.

audition: No artistic audition. A written admission examination at IEM in three parts: (1) Seashore hearing test over headphones, approx. 40 minutes — paired-comparison thresholds for frequency, intensity and tone duration, timbre discrimination, tone and rhythm memory (sample tests with solutions are published on Moodle); (2) second written aural test, approx. 20 minutes — melodic and rhythmic dictation, recognition of modes, time signatures, triads and instruments, plus spotting errors in a printed score; (3) written music-theory test, approx. 15 minutes — interval and scale construction, rhythm. Confirmed on the page: 'Die Zulassungsprüfung für das Wintersemester 2027/28 findet online statt' — the WS 2027/28 admission exam is ONLINE. Results normally 2 days later via KUGonline.
deadline: 3 June, with the next admission test given as 'xx. Juni 2027'. This is already the WS 2027/28 cycle, but the exact test DAY is an unfilled placeholder on the official page — treat 3 June 2027 as the working application deadline and confirm the exam day once KUG fills it in.

duration: 4 semesters / 120 ECTS (Studienkennzahl UV 066 413)
study: Official text: an interdisciplinary synthesis of technology and music, science and art. 'Based on a well-founded scientific and music-theoretical foundation, followed by specialisation with a choice among electrical/information-technology, music-practical and audio-technical areas.' Courses are held at Institute 17 — Electronic Music and Acoustics (IEM). Chairs: Robert Höldrich (recording and reproduction technology, electronic music), Alois Sontacchi (acoustics and audio engineering), Franz Zotter (acoustics and audio engineering). Graduates are aimed at the audio industry, acoustics and multimedia.
recommendation: The only affordable, portfolio-free route in this slice, and the online WS 2027/28 admission exam removes the travel barrier entirely. Two hard obstacles: German at C1 (or A2 plus a supplementary German exam that must be passed before regular studies begin), and the musical-aptitude battery — Seashore test, melodic/rhythmic dictation and music theory — which needs roughly a year of deliberate ear training. Also be honest about the content: this is an engineering degree in audio, not a DJ/producer degree, and the equivalence ruling on a software-engineering BSc is a genuine unknown.

institution: USTP – University of Applied Sciences St. Pölten (formerly Fachhochschule St. Pölten), Department of Media an…
programme: Digital Media Production (Master), Master Class "3D Audio & Sound Design"
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's, but taught in German — language is the real gate
qualification: CORRECTED: Diplom-Ingenieur (Dipl.-Ing.) — NOT an MA. An optional Dual Degree with HAW Hamburg (one extra semester plus a second master thesis) additionally yields a Master of Arts from HAW Hamburg.
tuition: CORRECTED and confirmed on USTP's official costs page. Standard tuition €363.36 per semester, BUT: "third-country nationals are charged a tuition fee of EUR 1,500.00 plus the ÖH fee" (ÖH €26.20 per semester). A Tunisian citizen on a student residence permit pays €1,500 + €26.20 per semester, i.e. roughly €6,100 over four semesters. Additional master costs: €100 copy costs and €20 Campus Card fee. USTP also "collect[s] a deposit of EUR 200 from students from third countries". The €363.36 rate applies only to holders of other permits (Permanent Residence – EU, Family Member, Red-White-Red Card, etc.). The previously suspected €4,385/semester figure indeed belongs to a different continuing-education programme and does not apply.
scholarshipDetail: CONFIRMED: none available to him. USTP's tuition-fee-waiver scheme for third-country nationals with higher tuition (best 20% of each semester receive a refund of the increased fee) applies ONLY to Creative Computing, Cyber Security and Resilience, Digital Innovation and Research, Citizen-Centered Digital Health and Social Care, and Gamified Reality Applications (GRACE) — Digital Media Production is explicitly not on that list. What DMP does have is small project grants: "Each semester, selected project teams of the degree programmes Media Technology, Digital Design, Digital Media Production, and Interactive Technologies are awarded grants" — departmental financial aid and equipment for student projects, not tuition relief. Ukrainian nationals get a fee waiver; Tunisians do not.
entry: CONFIRMED on USTP's general admission page: for a master degree programme, either completion of a relevant bachelor at a university of applied sciences, or completion of an equivalent programme at an accredited Austrian or foreign post-secondary institution with at least 180 ECTS and a duration of at least six semesters. Where equivalence is only partly established, the Academic Director may tie recognition to examinations taken during the master programme. Plus German B2 for all non-native speakers. Third-country applicants must upload their residence permit during the online application.
acceptsNonMusic: Yes in principle — CONFIRMED there is no music-degree requirement anywhere. This is an applied-sciences media/technology master; the requirement is a relevant bachelor of at least 180 ECTS and six semesters, with the Academic Director able to prescribe supplementary examinations where equivalence is only partial. A software-engineering BSc is a plausible fit for the technical side (programming, signal processing, real-time systems). The blocking condition is language and money, not musical background.
portfolio: Portfolio required; the specification is deliberately open. Official FAQ, verbatim: "For your application, you can submit a variety of projects that demonstrate the manifold facets of your work. These could be projects of your bachelor programme, projects from your professional work, or even private projects that match your chosen masterclass. Be creative and opt for projects that showcase your skills, interests, and your aptitude for the study programme of your choice." No fixed number, duration or format is published — UNVERIFIED at that level.
audition: No musical audition. A standard FH admission procedure with scheduled admission dates: for the 2026/27 cycle the admission date for the master classes "3D Audio & Sound Design" and "Animation & Visual Effects" was a fixed date (a separate 15/06/2026 date applied to "Film & TV"), "and thereafter by appointment". Whether the admission appointment is on-site or remote is not stated for this programme — UNVERIFIED.
deadline: CONFIRMED status as of today: "The application deadline for the winter semester 2026/27 has expired. An application is currently not possible. Applications for the winter semester 2027/28 will be possible from autumn 2026." PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Third-country applicants at USTP face an earlier cut-off than the general one (for comparison, in the WS 2026/27 cycle the general master window ran from autumn to late spring while third-country nationals had to apply by late February) — he must check the third-country deadline specifically as soon as the 2027/28 window opens in autumn 2026.
opens: CONFIRMED forward-looking: "Applications for the winter semester 2027/28 will be possible from autumn 2026." That is exactly his intake.
duration: CONFIRMED 4 semesters, full-time, delivered in block teaching. 120 ECTS is reported by Austrian study portals but is not stated on the official page — treat the ECTS figure as UNVERIFIED. 20 study places per year; studies begin in calendar week 37.
study: CONFIRMED from the official course-contents and master-class pages. Core: economy, law, management and scientific work, plus TV, video and audio production, storytelling, video/audio/studio technology, media coding, digital imaging, information visualisation, 360-degree video, AR and VR. You then choose one of three master classes — Animation & Visual Effects, 3D Audio & Sound Design, or Film & TV. The Audio master class runs four independently designed, developed, planned, implemented and evaluated projects across four semesters: semester 1 Design Thinking, project on sound design in animation; semester 2 Prototyping & Implementation, project on Sonic Interaction; semester 3 Evaluation & Testing, project on 3D Audio & Virtual Realities; semester 4 a group project. In-depth courses: Audio System Design; Film & Location Sound & Post Production; Film & Game Sound Design; Prototyping & Implementation; Coaching & Consulting. Software focus: Pro Tools Ultimate with Dolby Atmos Production Suite, Nuendo, Reaper, Ableton Live, Max4Live, Max8, Pure Data, Unity 3D with Wwise, Python, IRCAM SPAT5, IEM Plugin Suite, Sparta VST, Zylia Studio Pro, EASE 4, Tsugi GameSynth, iZotope RX. Students can 'buy' skills they lack (e.g. programming, graphic design) from students in other master classes, paying in ECTS credits. Regular field trips to Tonmeistertagung (VDT), next_generation (ZKM), klingt gut! (HAW Hamburg), ICSA and AES Conventions.
recommendation: On subject matter this is arguably the best technical fit in the whole batch for a software engineer who wants immersive-audio craft — Atmos, Ambisonics, Wwise/Unity game audio, Max/Pure Data, four self-run projects, four studios, AES links, and a dual degree with HAW Hamburg. But verification turned two soft caveats into hard blocks: (1) German B2 is required for admission because the degree programme is German-taught, and he has no German at all; (2) as a Tunisian third-country national he would pay €1,500 per semester (~€6,100 total) plus a €200 deposit, with the university's own third-country tuition-waiver scheme explicitly not covering this programme. The one genuinely good piece of news is timing: the 2027/28 application window — his intake — opens in autumn 2026. If he were ever to spend two years reaching German B2 and could self-fund, this would jump to an A; as of today it is C.

entry: For Montaža the published prerequisite is a 'trogodišnji sveučilišni ili stručni prijediplomski studij, 180 ECTS bodova' — a three-year university OR professional undergraduate degree of 180 ECTS. Croatian-language competence is expected in speech and writing; ADU requires no certificate but 'Povjerenstva Prijamnih ispita imaju pravo eliminirati kandidata ... ako ocjene da kandidat ne poznaje hrvatski jezik u mjeri koja je potrebna za uspješno studiranje'. Non-EU nationals compete in a separate foreign-nationals quota with its own priority list.
acceptsNonMusic: YES on paper. The prerequisite is stated purely as a 180-ECTS undergraduate degree, university or professional, with no field named — so a BSc in Software Engineering meets the formal condition. The direct-admission ('izravni upis') shortcut is reserved for ADU's own Montaža undergraduates, so an external applicant simply takes the full entrance exam. The genuine filter is the exam's assumed knowledge of film and music history, not the bachelor subject.
portfolio: EXACT, from the official 2026/27 entrance-exam document. Stage (A) submission, all eliminatory: (1) životopis (CV); (2) motivacijsko pismo — motivation letter, up to 2 'kartice' of text (~3,600 characters); (3) an audiovisual work for which the candidate conceived the sound picture or participated in creating it; (4) a written analysis of that submitted audiovisual work explaining the sound-picture concept AND listing the origin of the noises, music, sound effects and computer programs used in sound post-production. Positive evaluation of BOTH the audiovisual work and the written analysis is a precondition for reaching stage (B). (An older ADU booklet additionally specified DVD-video format in at least 3 copies and three copies of the analysis — check the current submission format.)
audition: Yes — on-site, three-part, out of 100 points, with a hard 80/100 pass threshold. (1) klauzurni rad (supervised in-house practical exam) up to 20 points; (2) izlaganje koncepta zvučne slike za zadani predložak — presentation of a sound-picture concept for a given template/brief, up to 30 points; (3) razgovor s povjerenstvom (interview) up to 50 points. The commission assesses knowledge of film history, film-music history and music history, and recognition of musical forms, styles and genres. Recommended reading includes Sonnenschein, 'Sound Design: The Expressive Power of Music, Voice and Sound Effects in Cinema', and Weis & Belton, 'Film Sound'.
deadline: 2026/27 CYCLE (Sept 2026 entry), NOT 2027 — confirm 2027 dates. NOTE: for the Snimanje department ADU ran a SEPARATE EARLIER WINDOW FOR FOREIGN NATIONALS (23–25 June 2026, exam 1 July 2026) — check whether an equivalent early foreign-national window applies to Montaža in 2027.
opens: 2026/27 cycle opened 1 September 2026 for Montaža. Foreign nationals should check for an earlier June window. 2027/28 dates not yet published.
duration: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS
study: Though formally a module of the Montaža (Editing) master, it is 'largely conceived as an independent program'. It aims to educate creative and professional practitioners who acquire sound knowledge and skills through artistic, theoretical and professional subjects, for film and television as well as for other performing, broadcast and stage arts. Courses dealing with film sound are tied to practical work, individual and team-based: sound-design students realise film, television, radio and stage works produced by ADU's other departments and collaborate with other University of Zagreb faculties. Teaching staff are working sound recordists, sound editors, music editors, re-recording mixers and sound designers. Graduates work across film, television, theatre, radio, performing arts, multimedia projects and video games.
recommendation: Formally open to him — a 180-ECTS engineering degree satisfies the entry level — and the entrance exam is transparent and well documented, which is rare. But it is an extremely narrow gate (one foreign place), it is taught and examined entirely in Croatian, and the submission requires an audiovisual work whose sound he designed, which he does not yet have. Realistic only after a year of building a picture-based sound portfolio and learning Croatian.

tuition: NOW VERIFIED (prior record said unpublished): "Einschreibegebühr: 400€" plus course fees either as "24 Zahlungen à 485€" (monthly, = €11,640) or "4 Zahlungen à 2.838 €" (per semester in advance, = €11,352). entry: NOW VERIFIED, under the heading "Zugangsvoraussetzungen": (1) "Berufsqualifizierender Hochschulabschluss" — a professionally qualifying higher-education degree, (2) "mindestens 180 ECTS", (3) "Künstlerische Eignung" — artistic aptitude, assessed via a test (see auditionSpec). And, listed FIRST under Zugangsvoraussetzungen: "Teilnehmende aus der EU (deutschsprachig)" — participants from the EU, German-speaking. His BSc would satisfy (1) and (2); the EU-residency and German-language conditions are what stop him.
acceptsNonMusic: Formally YES on the academic side — the requirement is only a "berufsqualifizierender Hochschulabschluss" with at least 180 ECTS, with no subject restriction, and the project fields are deliberately broad ("Musik, Film, Video-, Installations- und Medienkunst, Sound-Art, bildende Kunst, Fotografie, Game-Art"). Admission is portfolio- and project-led, not subject-led, so a software-engineering BSc is not itself a barrier. He would, however, have to pass the artistic aptitude test on the strength of a proposed master project and prior creative work — which he does not yet have.
portfolio: NOW VERIFIED in substance, and it is unusual: there is no conventional Mappe. The application is a WRITTEN PROJECT PROPOSAL. Verbatim: "Ablauf des künstlerische Eignungstests: Der/Die Bewerber/in bewirbt sich mit einer schriftlich verfassten Idee für ein künstlerisches Masterprojekt. Daraufhin findet auf Basis der Projektidee ein Kolloquium statt, um den/die Bewerber/in, dessen bisherige Werke/Tätigkeiten und das Projekt besser kennenzulernen." Existing works may be shown at the colloquium but are not the formal submission.
audition: YES — an artistic aptitude examination in the form of a colloquium before a joint panel. Verbatim: "Wie ist die künstlerische Eignungsprüfung aufgebaut? Hierbei handelt es sich um ein Kolloquium, in dem du deine Projektidee einer Prüfungskommission, bestehend aus Mitgliedern des SAE Instituts und der Folkwang UdK, vorstellst. Natürlich kannst du in diesem Kolloquium auch bestehende künstlerische Arbeiten von dir vorstellen, um der Kommission einen Einblick in dein bisheriges Schaffen zu geben." This is a defence of a project idea in German before an academic panel — not a performance audition, but a substantial hurdle.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. No application deadline is published. The only published date is the intake month: "Starttermin: Oktober" (Bochum, annually). For an October 2027 start, expect a first-half-of-2027 deadline, but nothing is currently published.
opens: UNVERIFIED. SAE publishes generic "Bewerbung & Zulassung", "Kosten & Zahlungspläne" and "Internationale Bewerber·innen" pages but no dated application window for this programme.
duration: 24 months. ECTS NOW VERIFIED from the module list (prior record said unpublished): MA-PMC-1 Projekt I 20 ECTS, MA-PMC-2 Projekt II 20 ECTS, MA-PMC-3 Wahlpflicht I 20 ECTS, MA-PMC-4 Projekt III 20 ECTS, MA-PMC-5 Wahlpflicht II 10 ECTS, MA-PMC-6 Abschlussarbeit 30 ECTS = 120 ECTS total. CRITICAL STRUCTURAL FINDING: the compulsory modules run as weekend blocks — "Da die Pflichtmodule am Wochenende in Blockform am SAE Institute in Bochum statt finden... ist es möglich, neben dem Studium einen Beruf auszuüben." It is explicitly designed to be done alongside a job, which is a poor basis for a German student residence permit.
study: A two-year, supervised, self-directed artistic master project, developed across three project modules (artistic practice and reflection, project planning and goal-setting, narration, project marketing, project and event management), 30 ECTS of electives taken at SAE or Folkwang (one week of SAE electives = 1 ECTS, documented in a logbook), and a 30-ECTS final thesis consisting of the realised project plus its public release. "Alle Inhalte dieses Masterstudiengangs führen zur öffentlichen Aufführung des Abschlussprojekts." Sound art and music are legitimate project fields, but this is an interdisciplinary media-art master's, not a music-production or mixing course.
recommendation: RULED OUT ON TWO CONFIRMED GROUNDS, one of which is new and harder than language. (1) ELIGIBILITY: the programme's own Zugangsvoraussetzungen block restricts it to "Teilnehmende aus der EU (deutschsprachig)" — EU participants. That is a nationality/residency restriction, not merely a language note, and a Tunisian national is outside it. (2) LANGUAGE: delivery and the admission colloquium are in German, which he does not speak; reaching the required level by autumn 2027 is not realistic from a standing start. (3) A third practical problem even if the first two vanished: compulsory modules run as weekend blocks explicitly so students can hold down a job, which is a weak basis for a German student visa. Add that the content is self-directed media art culminating in a public performance, not the hands-on production, mixing and sound-design craft he wants. The attraction — a genuinely state-recognised German MA at only ~€12,000 all-in with 120 ECTS — is real but not available to him. If he still wants Germany, look for English-taught, non-EU-open master's at public Hochschulen instead; SAE's other master's (Professional Practice, University of Hertfordshire, online) carries the same "EU (deutschsprachig)" restriction and is no help.

recommendation: AVOID — CORRECTED FROM 'BEST-FITTING GREEK OPTION' TO A CLOSED FILE. The previous record hedged that the programme 'often means it has stopped admitting'; reading the programme's own site directly turns that hedge into a finding. The last call for applications was for 2021-22, closing 23 September 2021. Five consecutive admission cycles have passed with no call. The application-dates menu stops at 2021-22. Every announcement, timetable and results page is frozen at 2021-22. The site has no valid HTTPS certificate and a 2018 copyright footer. Its 'International Students' link points to the blog of TEI Piraeus, an institution abolished in 2018. Its fee regulation still cites Ν.4485/2017, repealed by Ν.4957/2022, under which every Greek ΠΜΣ had to be re-established — with no sign this one was. And the department's own MSc page shows the sibling programmes carrying live 2025-26 and 2026-27 calls while this one carries none. That is a dead programme with a stale directory entry, not a dormant one. This is doubly unfortunate because it was, on paper, the best academic fit in the whole set for him: an audio and broadcast ENGINEERING master requiring no portfolio and no audition, selecting on file plus interview weighted equally, at €700 a semester in a public university, where his software-engineering degree would have been an advantage rather than an oddity. Two things killed it anyway even if it revived: everything is in Greek, which he does not speak, and there is no evidence of English-medium delivery. Action: one cheap email to eee@uniwa.gr and mscavb@uniwa.gr asking whether the ΠΜΣ will admit for 2027-28 and whether it has been re-established under Ν.4957/2022. Expect no reply or a negative one. tuition: CORRECTED — the "0 PLN" is misleading for him. The programme page does show a semester fee of 0 PLN, but that reflects the standard full-time Polish-track rate for those entitled to free study. AGH's International Students Office publishes separate fees for foreigners: roughly €1,000–2,750 per semester for full-time study depending on programme and level, with engineering programmes in the €1,250–2,750 band. Exemption from tuition is available on defined grounds, including a NAWA decision (which is how Banach delivers free study), and notably also for holders of a C1 Polish-language certificate on full-time Polish-taught programmes. scholarshipDetail: Banach NAWA Programme — genuinely available here, and for a better reason than previously stated. CONFIRMED from the Banach 2026 call (Announcement No. 16/2026 of 13 April 2026): Tunisia is an eligible country and sits in Group 3 (with Angola, Jordan, Kenya, Lebanon, Palestine, Rwanda, Senegal, Tanzania). CORRECTION: the call imposes NO field-of-study restriction on any group — the earlier claim that Group 3 is limited to engineering, agricultural and natural sciences does not appear in the current call. What the call DOES restrict is the institution: it funds studies "conducted at universities supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education that have concluded a framework agreement with NAWA." AGH is such a university, which is precisely why Banach works here and fails at every Polish music academy in this slice. Other eligibility conditions he meets or must watch: no prior master's degree; no previous NAWA second-cycle scholarship; first-cycle degree obtained no earlier than 2024 (he graduates 2026, so fine); and documented B2 in the language of instruction (B2 Polish for the Polish track, or B1 Polish if he takes the funded one-year preparatory course first).
entry: CORRECTED AND MORE DEMANDING THAN PREVIOUSLY RECORDED. Prior degree: LICENCJAT for the summer round (4 semesters, includes a compensatory semester), INŻYNIER for the winter round (3 semesters) — a Tunisian BSc in Software Engineering would most plausibly map to the inżynier route, subject to AGH's recognition assessment. There IS an entrance examination: AGH computes a recruitment index WR = wE·E + wS·S, where E is the entrance-exam score on a 0–100 scale ("scores below 30 disqualify candidates"), S is the standardised first-cycle GPA, and the weights sum to 10; the programme page shows both weights at 5, i.e. exam and GPA count equally. Maximum index 1000 points ("Maksymalna wartość wskaźnika rekrutacji wynosi 1000 pkt"). Foreign applicants must additionally document language of instruction at B2. Recruitment fee: the programme page shows 100 PLN; AGH's general 2026/2027 schedule lists 85 PLN where the AGH mathematics exam is not taken and 100 PLN where it is.
acceptsNonMusic: Yes, by design — it is an engineering degree and a software-engineering bachelor is a natural feeder. This remains the one programme in the slice where his degree is an asset rather than an obstacle. The qualifying constraints are the entrance exam and B2 Polish, not his subject.
portfolio: None — this is a technical programme and admission turns on the entrance-exam score plus first-cycle GPA, not on creative work. CONFIRMED: no portfolio appears anywhere in the qualification formula.
audition: None — no audition, no creative test, no audiometry. But note this is NOT the same as "no examination": a written qualification exam scored 0–100 is part of the recruitment index, with a disqualifying floor of 30 points. Its subject content for inżynieria akustyczna could not be confirmed and should be requested from wkr-imir@agh.edu.pl.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for both. Banach NAWA 2026 closed 8 May 2026 at 15:00 Warsaw time "or until 300 applications are submitted in each of country groups no. 1-3" — note the quota can close the call EARLY, so a 2027 application should go in on day one. IMPORTANT TIMING POINT: the Banach 2026 call funds studies starting in the winter semester 2026/27, so for a September 2027 start he needs the Banach 2027 call, expected around April–May 2027 — which lines up well with his target intake.
opens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. AGH runs summer and winter recruitment rounds; the general 2026 admission window ran from 1 June to 11 September 2026, and 2027 dates were not published as of July 2026. The Banach NAWA 2026 call opened 13 April 2026.
duration: CONFIRMED from the AGH recruitment page: winter recruitment 3 semesters (entry requirement INŻYNIER); summer recruitment 4 semesters (entry requirement LICENCJAT). The 90 ECTS figure for the 3-semester track is consistent with AGH's programme documents but is not stated on the recruitment page itself.
study: Two master specialisations: "Drgania i hałas w technice i środowisku" (Vibrations and Noise in Technology and Environment) and the relevant one, "Inżynieria dźwięku w mediach i kulturze" (Sound Engineering in Media and Culture). Graduates are trained as sound-system designers, sound engineers in media, and audio programmers in IT companies, and are explicitly prepared for supporting cultural and artistic institutions and participating in art-creation processes. This is the technical/engineering route into professional audio, not an artistic one.
recommendation: Still the only credible fully-funded, degree-compatible route found in Poland: his software-engineering BSc fits the entry requirement, there is no creative audition or portfolio, and Banach NAWA is genuinely reachable here — Tunisia is eligible, there is no subject restriction, and AGH is the right kind of institution, unlike every music academy in this slice. Downgraded from an unqualified recommendation to B because verification exposed two real hurdles the earlier note missed: he must pass a written entrance exam with a disqualifying floor, and he must certify B2 Polish (or take the funded NAWA preparatory year first, which pushes the start to 2028). And the deeper caveat stands — this trains a competent audio engineer or audio programmer, not a producer or DJ. Best treated as the funded pragmatic option with music production pursued alongside.

It is not a mestrado and not a pós-graduação. Its DGERT certification attaches chiefly to the 8-semester Curso Profissional de Música Moderna; the Produção Musical offering is fee-paying tuition, not a certified programme in its own right — UNVERIFIED whether the production course itself falls inside the DGERT scope, and he should ask. It teaches CUBASE with a MIDI keyboard, which is the wrong toolchain for electronic music, DJing and live performance; he would be buying skills and software he then has to replace. And it enrols from age 12 over a 1-to-4-year, 3-level structure, which is a children's-and-hobbyists' music school cadence, not a professional intensive. Against that, the honest counterpoint stands: he has NO music training at all, and that — not gear, not software — is his real weakness for a portfolio-weighted selection like ReSound or Lusófona. Where it COULD genuinely help: if he takes the Lusófona or UCP route and is already lawfully resident in Lisbon, a 170-hour evening course at €19:00–23:00 three nights a week is a cheap, practical way to add hands-on production craft alongside an academic master's — and its portfolio-plus-motivation-letter entry process is trivial for him. That is its only sensible role: a supplement AFTER residence, never the reason for it.

VERIFIED ABSENCE, AND IT IS DECISIVE: there are NO dedicated sound-engineering, recording, mixing, mastering, synthesis, sound-design or electronic-music modules published anywhere in the plan. Not one. Compare this with the Lusófona mestrado, which has five sound-specific units in its first semester alone. recommendation: DO NOT PRIORITISE — RIGHT COUNTRY, RIGHT ACCREDITATION, WRONG SUBJECT. Let me be blunt, because the accreditation being genuine is exactly what makes this dangerous: a real A3ES degree, real visa eligibility and a real quantified scholarship can all be true while the programme still teaches him nothing he wants. He wants music production, mixing, sound design and electronic music. This degree teaches digital journalism, infographics, transmedia and web labs, in Portuguese, with one shared sound studio and zero audio modules. Paying around €12,000 plus two years of his life for that would be a poor use of a budget-sensitive candidate's money when the Lusófona mestrado, in the same city, teaches acoustics, capture, synthesis, sound design and studio practice for less. Three further practical cautions: the exact tuition and emolumentos figures could NOT be verified from the official PDF and must be obtained in writing; the merit scholarship threshold for him is the FOREIGN-institution bar of 16.5/20, not 15.5, and the two official sources disagree on both threshold and percentage; and every scholarship and the 11-instalment plan require a Portuguese direct debit he cannot set up before arriving. Keep it only as a distant fallback if UCP, Lusófona and ReSound all fail AND he decides he wants an accredited Portuguese degree for immigration reasons more than he wants sound training — which would be an honest choice, but he should make it with his eyes open rather than mistake this for a sound course.

study: Year 1 S1 (30 ECTS): Projeto/Produção I — Exterior e Estúdio (12), Produção de Som para Videojogos (5), Produção Eletrónica (5), Artes e Tecnologias do Som (5), Investigação em Som e Imagem (3). Year 1 S2 (30 ECTS): Projeto II — Pós-Produção/Design de Som (12), Banda Sonora (5), Projeto Interdisciplinar (5), Seminário Interdisciplinar (3), Interfaces Tangíveis e Computação Física (5). Year 2: Portfólio e Showreel (3) plus Dissertação/Projeto/Estágio (27+30). Covers microphone technique, studio recording and mastering, surround mixing for cinema, live sound, game audio and sound art. Curricular internship option of minimum 24 weeks. NOTE THE PROPORTION: exactly ONE 5-ECTS unit ('Produção Eletrónica') out of 120 touches electronic music production. This is a film/game/media sound-design degree with strong studio craft — it is not an electronic-music or DJ programme, and no amount of framing changes that.
recommendation: THE STRONGEST PORTUGUESE OPTION ON PAPER — BUT THE LANGUAGE MAKES IT CONDITIONAL, NOT AUTOMATIC. It is the only entry in this batch that is simultaneously a genuine A3ES/DGES master's degree, explicitly open to an engineering bachelor in its own published wording, visa-safe, and cheap (€13,140 for the whole degree). The accreditation question that the draft left open is now closed in its favour. Two things must be said bluntly. First, it is taught in Portuguese and he does not speak it — that is a 12-month project he must start NOW if he wants the Feb–Apr 2027 phase-1 window, and if he will not do it, this entry is unworkable and he should put everything into ReSound instead. Second, it will not make him a DJ. It will make him a competent film and game sound designer with real studio craft and one 5-ECTS brush with electronic production. If he is honest that the accredited degree is the visa-and-craft vehicle and the DJ career is built in parallel on evenings and weekends, this is excellent value. If he expects the degree itself to deliver the DJ career, he will be disappointed and out €35k.

qualification: Mestrado (2nd-cycle master, 120 ECTS)

entry: Bachelor's degree (licență) plus diploma supplement, or a faculty certificate for 2026 graduates. audition: CORRECTED ORDER AND DETAIL. Exam 1 is ORAL, 15 minutes, graded 1-10: a discussion based on his portfolio of representative works. Final grade is the average of the two; minimum 6.00. Both conducted in Romanian. The written paper requires him to draw/diagram design concepts, not just write — an additional skill barrier the previous entry missed.
deadline: CONFIRMED AND EXPANDED: registration closes 9 September 2026; document verification 10-11 September; EXAMS 15-20 SEPTEMBER 2026; results per the exam schedule. Scholarship deadlines are far earlier — about 31 March. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm all 2027 dates.
opens: 4 August 2026 for the 2026-27 cycle — CONFIRMED. PRIOR CYCLE, expect early August 2027 for his target intake.
duration: CONFIRMED: 2 years, 120 ECTS, full-time (învățământ cu frecvență).
languageReq: CONFIRMED via UNATC's own foreign-citizen admission page: non-EU applicants must complete a Romanian preparatory language year UNLESS they hold a minimum B1 Romanian certificate or have completed 4 years of prior study in Romanian. IELTS/TOEFL are irrelevant here — his untaken English tests neither help nor hurt.
study: Lighting and sound design for stage. CORRECTED/SHARPENED: the official page describes the 3-hour written exam as two tasks involving analysis of lighting/sound design drawn from PLAYS (dramatic texts) plus graphic projection of design concepts. So the discipline is text-driven theatre design — reading a play and designing its light and sound — not studio production or electronic music.
recommendation: CONFIRMED AS REAL, BUT DOWNGRADED — AND I HAVE FOUND HIM A STRICTLY BETTER PROGRAMME AT THE SAME UNIVERSITY. Everything structural checks out: it is a genuine ARACIS-accredited 120-ECTS second-cycle master's, the domestic tuition of 8,000 lei/year is confirmed verbatim in the Senate decision, the admission fee is 400 lei, and it is eligible for Romanian government scholarships whose Romanian-only teaching rule actually suits it. But it is a poor fit for HIM and I am rating it C rather than treating it as a serious second application. Four reasons. First, it is half lighting design, examined in a 3-hour written paper in Romanian that requires analysing plays and producing graphic design projections — a skill set he has no route to in one year. Second, the portfolio must be a live performing-arts project with a 3-5 page theoretical argument; club music and studio work do not qualify. Third, there are 6 places in total. Fourth and most importantly: THE SAME UNIVERSITY RUNS 'Interactive Technologies for Performing and Media Arts', a 120-ECTS MA taught entirely in ENGLISH, which explicitly welcomes applicants from science and engineering backgrounds, whose second admission test is a practical software demonstration in Processing, Max/MSP, TouchDesigner, Unity or Blender, and which accepts a 1500-2000 word English essay IN PLACE OF a portfolio for candidates who do not yet have one. That programme is 13,750 lei/year with 3 budget and 4 fee places, needs no Romanian at all, and its non-EU admission runs 10-27 June with an ONLINE exam option. For a Tunisian software engineer with no portfolio and no Romanian, that is a categorically better application than this one. He should apply to ITPMA and treat Design lumină și sunet as, at most, a throwaway second option only if he has by then genuinely built stage-sound credits.

institution: Universitatea Națională de Artă Teatrală și Cinematografică „I.L. Caragiale“ București (UNATC), Facultatea de…
programme: Arta sunetului de film (The Art of Film Sound), studii universitare de masterat
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's, but taught in Romanian — language is the real gate
verdictWhy: This is the best-shaped gate on the whole list for him — no audition, any 180/240-credit bachelor accepted, a portfolio of his own sound work plus a DAW session, and tuition of only about EUR 2,750/yr. The blocker is Romanian: the programme is taught in Romanian, the written exam is on a Romanian bibliography, and as a Tunisian he must produce a B1 Romanian certificate from a recognised issuer or do a preparatory year. Resolve the Romanian-language route (ICR certificate or preparatory year, which pushes entry to 2028) before spending anything else on it.
correction: Input said cost 'Under EUR 1.5k/yr'. Wrong — the Senate schedule sets 'Arta sunetului de film' at 13.750 lei/yr, about EUR 2,750/yr, plus a 400-lei registration fee. Input also said gate 'Portfolio only'. Wrong — there is a compulsory written exam (Proba 1) on a Romanian film-culture bibliography and technical sound-design knowledge, sat in person, in addition to the portfolio colloquium.
qualification: Diplomă de master — CONFIRMED a genuine state-recognised second-cycle degree (ciclul II) under Legea învățământului superior nr. 199/2023. Supports a student residence permit for a third-country national via the Ministry of Education Letter of Acceptance.
accreditation: CONFIRMED. ARACIS-accredited state university; the programme is listed on the official 2026/2027 admissions site, on the dedicated foreign-citizens master's admission page, and in Annex 1 (II.2, Faculty of Film) of the Senate fee decision.
tuition: STILL NOT PUBLISHED — the previous record's caution was correct and I confirm it. I extracted the full text of Hotărârea Senatului nr. 290/2026: it contains no euro figure and no reference to 'cont propriu valutar', 'străin' or 'terțe' anywhere. All figures are in lei and apply to the domestic fee-paying regime. Romanian non-EU tuition is set per institution above a Government Ordinance 22/2009 floor and is normally quoted in EUR per month; comparable Romanian arts faculties sit around €750–950/month payable nine months a year. DO NOT assume the 13,750 lei figure applies to him. Ask study@unatc.ro and secretariat.film@unatc.ro in writing for the euro rate for a non-EU master's student in Arta sunetului de film — and note that if he wins a Romanian government scholarship the question becomes moot, because scholarship holders occupy budget places.
otherFees: CORRECTED — previously UNVERIFIED, now confirmed from the same Senate decision. Master's admission registration fee: 400 lei (Annex 1, TAXE DE ÎNSCRIERE, item 2), payable online in the admission application. Optional admission preparation courses: 150 lei per course (15% discount if paid in full). Document legalisation/apostille, authorised translation, credential recognition and Letter of Acceptance processing are additional. Bucharest living costs additional — UNATC's own page points candidates to Numbeo rather than publishing a figure.
totalCost: Two scenarios. SELF-FUNDED: unquantifiable until UNATC publishes or states the non-EU euro rate; if it lands in the €750–950/month band typical of Romanian arts faculties, roughly €6,750–8,550 per year over two years, plus a Romanian preparatory year, plus Bucharest living, plus 400 lei registration and legalisation costs. SCHOLARSHIP: tuition, preparatory year and accommodation covered, a monthly stipend paid, and registration and aptitude-test fees waived — his cost collapses to visa costs, travel, document legalisation and the gap between the stipend and Bucharest living costs.
scholarshipDetail: CONFIRMED WITH IMPORTANT CORRECTIONS. (1) Romanian Government / MFA scholarships via scholarships.studyinromania.gov.ro, under Government Decision 288/1993 — open to citizens of ALL non-EU countries, so a Tunisian national qualifies; requires an average of the study years for the last graduated school of at least 7/10 or equivalent 'Good'; excludes only Medicine, Dental Medicine and Pharmacy; at master's level beneficiaries study ONLY IN ROMANIAN, with a fully financed Romanian preparatory year for non-speakers. Covers: exemption from registration, language-testing and aptitude-test fees; tuition for the preparatory year; tuition for the degree; a monthly stipend during both the preparatory year and the degree; and dormitory accommodation subject to availability. 2026/2027 cycle: applications 16 February – 31 March 2026, results announced around 15 July 2026, then the Ministry issues the Letter of Acceptance. TWO CAVEATS THE PREVIOUS RECORD MISSED — the Ministry expressly reserves the right to assign a DIFFERENT university in the same field if the candidate's choice cannot be honoured, and later requests to change field or university are refused; and the scholarship does not waive UNATC's own aptitude test, so he must still pass Proba 1 and Proba 2 in Romanian and place within three budget seats. (2) ARICE scholarships — CORRECTED AND DOWNGRADED. 40 scholarships for 2026/2027, files emailed 11 May – 12 June 2026 to burse2026@arice.gov.ro, Romanian-taught with a free preparatory year to B1. But ARICE explicitly PRIORITISES economics and business administration, agricultural sciences, technical sciences, and oil and gas; other fields are considered only 'to the extent of the places available'. Film sound is not a priority field, so ARICE is a long shot, not a parallel route of equal weight.
entry: CONFIRMED. A completed bachelor's degree worth 180 or 240 credits, with NO field restriction for this programme (contrast Arta imaginii de film on the same page, which requires graduates 'ai facultăților de profil'). Plus a Europass CV, the portfolio, proof of registration-fee payment, baccalaureate diploma, birth certificate, passport valid 6+ months, foreign-credential recognition certificate, a medical fitness certificate from a family physician, and the GDPR declaration. Minimum admission average 6.00/10 for both budget and fee-paying places. Registration is exclusively online via the 2BitsEDU/Edubits platform; portfolios are uploaded to a secure institution-provided folder issued only after registration.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — CONFIRMED. The published condition is simply a completed bachelor's of 180 or 240 credits, with no field restriction and no music-degree clause. His BSc Software Engineering is an acceptable academic qualification. The barriers are the portfolio, the Romanian language, and six seats.
portfolio: MANDATORY AND SUBSTANTIAL — CONFIRMED, and the binding practical constraint for him. Required at registration: a portfolio of artistic projects with sound design created by the candidate himself (digital copies of films or other relevant sound-design-for-film-and-media projects), plus a Europass CV. At Proba 2 he must present an actual DAW session file from one portfolio piece and be able to open, run and discuss it; candidates are explicitly responsible for verifying the completeness and functionality of the DAW project. He has none of this today. Building it is a genuine twelve-month project and must be spent sound-designing SHORT FILMS, not producing club tracks — the portfolio must show film-sound work.
audition: CONFIRMED. Single stage, two exams, each marked 1–10, final mark the arithmetic mean. Proba 1 — written: film-culture test based on the competition bibliography plus technical sound-design knowledge. Proba 2 — oral: a colloquium on one project of the candidate's choice from his portfolio, presented with the openable DAW session. Tie-break is decided on Proba 2, then Proba 1. No appeals are admitted against oral or practical exams. Both exams are in Romanian.
deadline: Expect an August–September 2027 registration window for a September 2027 start. The operative deadline for him is far earlier: the Romanian Government / MFA scholarship closes around 31 March 2027, roughly five months before the university's own window, and the preparatory-year requirement means a scholarship awarded in July 2027 would put him into the Romanian language year in September 2027 and into the master's proper in September 2028.
opens: 2026/2027 cycle, Romanian-taught route (which is the route for this programme, including for foreign citizens): online registration 4 August – 9 September 2026; file verification 10–11 September; admission exams 15–20 September 2026. Separately, the English-taught non-EU route ran 10–27 June 2026 with file verification 28–30 June and exams 1–8 July 2026 — that route does NOT include Arta sunetului de film. PRIOR CYCLE — confirm 2027 dates.
duration: 2 years, 4 semesters, 120 ECTS, full-time (cu frecvență) — CONFIRMED on both the programme page and the foreign-citizens page.
languageReq: CORRECTED AND SHARPENED — this is stricter than the previous record implied. UNATC's own foreign-citizens page states that foreign nationals may be enrolled in the admission contest / aptitude test only AFTER completing the Romanian-language preparatory year („Cetățenii străini pot fi înscriși la concursul de admitere/testul de aptitudini după absolvirea anului pregătitor de limba română“). Exemption requires one of: Romanian study documents or school records showing at least FOUR consecutive years of study in Romanian within the Romanian national system; or a certificate of linguistic competence of minimum CEFR level B1 issued specifically by an accredited Romanian higher-education institution that organises the Romanian preparatory year, by a Romanian language-and-culture lectorate at a foreign university, by the Institutul Limbii Române, or by the Institutul Cultural Român. A generic B1 certificate from any other provider does not qualify. No IELTS/TOEFL anywhere in this admission.
englishTest: None required or accepted for this programme. His untaken IELTS/TOEFL is irrelevant to Arta sunetului de film — but it WOULD be needed for UNATC's English-taught master's programmes, which is a reason to sit it anyway.
study: Film sound as an art form: sound design, recording, editing and post-production for cinema, worked through DAW projects. The competition bibliography is the professional film-sound canon: Yewdall 'Practical Art of Motion Picture Sound', Sonnenschein 'Sound Design', Chion 'Film, A Sound Art' / 'Audio-Vision' / 'The Voice in Cinema', Murray 'Sound Design Theory and Practice', Holman 'Sound for Film and Television', Purcell 'Dialog Editing for Motion Pictures', Ament 'The Foley Grail', Viers 'The Sound Effects Bible' and 'The Location Sound Bible', Rumsey & McCormick 'Sound and Recording', Schafer 'The Soundscape', Weis & Belton 'Film Sound: Theory and Practice'. Toolchain: Avid Pro Tools, Steinberg Nuendo, Cockos Reaper, Adobe Audition, Adobe Premiere Pro, Fairlight/DaVinci Resolve.
recommendation: STILL THE BEST PROSPECT OF THE SIX, AND NOW THE ONLY ONE THAT IS BOTH A GOOD FIT AND OPEN TO HIM — BUT NARROWER THAN THE PREVIOUS RECORD SUGGESTED. Everything structurally good about it holds up under verification: a real 2-year, 120-ECTS, ARACIS-accredited degree at Romania's national film school; no music-degree requirement; the professional film-sound toolchain and canon; and a Romanian government scholarship a Tunisian national genuinely can win, which covers tuition, a free Romanian preparatory year, accommodation and a monthly stipend. Four corrections tighten the picture. First, the programme admits only SIX students a year — 3 on budget, 3 fee-paying — so this is a highly competitive seat, not a place he walks into. Second, the language rule is stricter than reported: foreign nationals may sit the admission exam only after completing the Romanian preparatory year, unless they hold a B1 certificate from a specific short list of Romanian issuers (an accredited Romanian HEI running the preparatory year, a Romanian lectorate abroad, the Institutul Limbii Române or the Institutul Cultural Român) — an ordinary B1 certificate will not do. Third, the MFA scholarship does not buy him admission: he must still pass a written film-culture exam and an oral DAW colloquium in Romanian and place in the top three, and the Ministry reserves the right to send him to a different university in the same field if UNATC cannot take him. Fourth, ARICE is a much weaker parallel route than described — film sound is outside its four priority fields and is considered only if places remain. The non-EU euro tuition rate genuinely is unpublished; I extracted the full Senate decision and it contains no euro figures at all, so the previous record's refusal to guess was right. Concrete plan for a realistic 2028 master's start via a 2027 preparatory year: (a) confirm his SMU MedTech average converts to at least 7/10 — this is a hard eligibility gate, check it first; (b) start Romanian now and aim for a qualifying B1 certificate from an accepted issuer; (c) redirect the portfolio year to sound-designing student short films, not DJ tracks, and finish with an openable, functional Pro Tools or Reaper session he can walk a panel through; (d) email study@unatc.ro and secretariat.film@unatc.ro for the non-EU euro rate and for confirmation of the number of places open to non-EU candidates; (e) apply to the MFA scholarship in the 16 February – 31 March 2027 window, and treat the university's own August–September 2027 registration as the second gate, not the first. One additional option worth putting in front of him: UNATC's English-taught non-EU master's route — in particular Interactive Technologies for Performing and Media Arts (digital control of sound, light, image and code) and Art of Game Design, both 2-year, 13,750 lei, admitted on a separate June–July calendar with an English-language file competition and no Romanian required. Those are not funded by the MFA scholarship, which is Romanian-only at master's level, but they are the same university, the same faculty, adjacent to his interests, and they play directly to a software-engineering background. That is the pairing to research next.

Core: Супервизија звука (Sound Supervision, 2+4 weekly hours — by far the heaviest course); Драматургија савременог филма; Режија - анализа и синтеза; Авангардни филм; Завршни рад and Завршни рад - истраживање. Electives, choose 12 ECTS: Аудиовизуелна артикулација; Звук у филмској уметности; Постпродукција филмске слике; Светлосна артикулација у визуелним медијима; Продукција музике за нове медије (Production of Music for New Media); Филмска и телевизијска продукција; Имерзивне игре (Immersive Games); Видео арт. Note the sibling MAS Музичка продукција (also 1 year / 60 ECTS) is far closer to club/electronic production — its courses include Музичка продукција, Звук и музика на филму, Савремене тенденције у музичкој продукцији 1 and 2, Историја електроакустичке музике and Историја популарне музике — but its entry is restricted to a four-year degree in the artistic field Музичка продукција or a cognate programme, so it is closed to him.
recommendation: Substantially better than previously assessed: entry is explicitly field-neutral (unlike every sibling module), foreign nationals are admitted 'under the same conditions as domestic', it is one year / 60 ECTS, and tuition for foreigners is a confirmed €1,800/year. The electives (Продукција музике за нове медије, Имерзивне игре) are genuinely interesting for him. Two real obstacles remain: he must have a FOUR-YEAR bachelor (240 ECTS) — a 3-year licence disqualifies him — and he must produce documented proof of Serbian-language knowledge plus formal Serbian recognition of his diploma. Content is film/AV-sound-led rather than club/electronic. Worth one concrete e-mail asking for the Dizajn zvuka Informator and whether his specific degree meets the four-year condition.

entry: THE EXCEPTION CLAUSE IS THE POINT. HSLU master admission normally requires, verbatim, 'a Bachelor's degree from the Lucerne School of Music' with preparatory modules, or 'a Bachelor's degree from a music conservatory or comparable educational establishment'. BUT, verbatim and specific to this major: 'For the Music and Digital Creation major specifically, a Bachelor's degree obtained at a university of applied sciences (sur-dossier admission) is sufficient – REGARDLESS OF THE DEGREE PROGRAMME.' Separately, the master overview page states verbatim: 'Für Studierende ohne einen Bachelor-Abschluss einer Schweizerischen Musikhochschule kann eine Standortbestimmung Theorie angeordnet werden. Je nach deren Verlauf muss im ersten Studiensemester Master ein Auflagenmodul erfolgreich absolviert werden, in dem die Zielkompetenzen des Bachelor-Abschlusses der Hochschule Luzern – Musik erarbeitet werden. Vom Bestehen des Auflagenmoduls ist die Fortsetzung des Studiums über das erste Semester hinaus abhängig.' So a music-theory placement check can be imposed, with a remedial module in semester one that you must pass to continue — a real risk for someone with no theory background, but it is remedial teaching, not an entry exam.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — EXPLICITLY AND UNIQUELY. Quoted verbatim: 'a Bachelor's degree obtained at a university of applied sciences (sur-dossier admission) is sufficient – regardless of the degree programme.' This is the only programme found in Switzerland that states in terms that ANY bachelor subject qualifies. A BSc Software Engineering is exactly the profile the major was built for — HSLU publishes a separate curriculum variant for entrants who already hold an informatics bachelor.
portfolio: NO TRACK PORTFOLIO REQUIRED. Instead, verbatim: applicants must 'submit a project description (one A4 page) three weeks before the exam, outlining a music and IT project to be realized during studies'. ONE A4 PAGE. That is the entire submission — no finished tracks, no recordings, no scores. For a candidate with no portfolio yet, this is decisive: he can apply on an idea rather than on a back catalogue.
audition: NEITHER AN AUDITION NOR AN EAR-TRAINING EXAM. Verbatim: this major has 'no ear training test or traditional instrument audition'; the assessment is 'a jury conversation focusing on project goals, program expectations, training content and aims'. It is an interview about a written project idea. ONE CAVEAT, quoted: 'For applicants without a Music Bachelor, additional practical/theory assessment occurs in their musical specialization' — the scope of that additional assessment is not published and is UNVERIFIED; it may be where a music-theory shortfall surfaces, and it links to the Standortbestimmung Theorie / Auflagenmodul mechanism above. (For comparison, HSLU's Major Komposition also has no ear-training component but demands 'three scores in different instrumentation and recordings' plus a 30-minute written analysis — a much harder ask for him.)
deadline: 28 FEBRUARY, verbatim: 'the deadline is 28 February (in a leap year on 29 February)'. This is a standing annual deadline, not a prior-cycle date, so 28 February 2027 for a September 2027 start. NOTE the portfolio timing: the one-page project description is due 'three weeks before the exam', which is later than the application deadline itself.

duration: Master of Arts in Music, 4 semesters, 120 ECTS (HSLU standard). Two published curricula exist — one 'for students without a BA in Computer Science' and one 'for students with a BA in Informatics'; HE WOULD FOLLOW THE COMPUTER-SCIENCE TRACK, which is shorter on IT foundations and longer on music.

study: Verbatim: the major 'aims to build Information and Communications Technologies competencies and their connection with musical content. It provides students with a conceptual and operational toolkit to strategically leverage digital transformation. In addition to mandatory foundational knowledge and basic competencies, students acquire in-depth competencies in the areas of DATA SCIENCE and DIGITAL CREATION. Students are enabled to integrate new digital, artistic, and pedagogical possibilities into their own repertoire of action and expression.' Related minors available at HSLU that lean toward his interests: Minor Groove und Electronics, Minor Media Composer, Minor Electronic Music Composition, Minor Digitale Kompetenzen für Musik, Bildung und Kultur.
