qualification: Master of Arts in Music, Major Music and Digital Creation. 4 semesters, 120 ECTS — CONFIRMED ('A Master's programme comprises 120 ECTS-Credits and typically consists of a Major and a Minor'). A genuine second-cycle Swiss degree.
accreditation: CONFIRMED. Real, state-recognised second-cycle Swiss degree, institutionally accredited under the HFKG. Supports a Swiss student residence permit (B permit for studies) for a non-EU national, subject to cantonal quota and proof of funds.
tuition: CHF 1,300 PER SEMESTER — CONFIRMED verbatim: 'CHF 1'300.– for international students (for students with foreign citizenship who enter or have entered Switzerland for the purpose of studying).' CHF 2,600 per year; CHF 5,200 over the 4-semester master. The surcharge exists because students entering Switzerland to study do not attract cantonal FHV subsidies.
otherFees: All CONFIRMED on the official fee page, and they are substantial. PER SEMESTER on top of tuition: module examination CHF 150, photocopying flat rate CHF 45, service fee CHF 45, university sport CHF 25 — CHF 265 per semester. ONE-OFF: enrolment CHF 390, HSLU Card CHF 50, degree and certification CHF 220. ADMISSION: CHF 200 per entrance examination (credited on enrolment) plus CHF 390 for two practical examinations. OTHER: break from studies CHF 200/semester, student exchange application CHF 200, additional one-to-one lessons CHF 500.
totalCost: Fees only, over 4 semesters: tuition 4 × CHF 1,300 = CHF 5,200; compulsory per-semester extras 4 × CHF 265 = CHF 1,060; one-offs CHF 1,250 (enrolment 390 + practical exams 390 + admission 200 + card 50 + diploma 220). Institutional total ≈ CHF 7,510, of which the CHF 200 admission fee is credited back on enrolment, so ≈ CHF 7,310 net. Living costs in Lucerne dominate and are not published — Switzerland is by far the most expensive country in this set, and the Swiss student permit requires proof of sufficient means (figure set cantonally — UNVERIFIED; confirm with the Swiss representation in Tunis and the Kanton Luzern migration office).
scholarshipDetail: Nothing published at programme level. The relevant instrument remains the Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships — Art Scholarships stream, which funds a first master's at a Swiss music university for a foreign national. Tunisia's inclusion in the ART-stream country list (narrower than the research-scholarship list) changes yearly and must be confirmed on the SERI/FCS official list for the 2027 call. UNVERIFIED for this programme. Note that unlike the Lugano conservatory (see below), HSLU publishes no internal scholarship fund of its own.
entry: MAJOR CORRECTION, AND THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING IN THIS RE-CHECK. The official Studienreglement für die Ausbildung (Musik), section on master admission, states: 'Für den Master of Arts in Music, Major Music and Digital Creation gelten, weil es sich um ein interdisziplinäres Angebot in Zusammenarbeit mit der Hochschule Luzern – Informatik handelt, gesonderte Zulassungsvoraussetzungen: a. das Bachelor-Diplom EINER FACHHOCHSCHULE (Sur-Dossier-Aufnahme); b. das Bestehen des Zulassungsverfahrens (Praxis, Theorie, Gespräch), mit dem die Eignung für die musikspezifischen Module abgeklärt wird; c. das Erbringen der für die verschiedenen musikspezifischen Ausrichtungen zusätzlich formulierten Zusatzqualifikationen. Die Voraussetzungen a–c müssen kumulativ erfüllt sein.' The public admission page puts it more simply: 'Für den Major Music and Digital Creation genügt ein an einer Fachhochschule erworbener Bachelor-Abschluss («Sur-Dossier-Aufnahme») – EGAL IN WELCHEM STUDIENGANG' — a UAS bachelor in ANY subject suffices. So NO music degree is required for this major. The previous record's flat 'NO, not realistically' was correct for Major Komposition and wrong for the programme he should actually be looking at. THE ONE REAL UNKNOWN: 'Bachelor-Diplom einer Fachhochschule' means a university-of-applied-sciences diploma. His BSc is from SMU MedTech, a private Tunisian university, not a Swiss-style FH. Whether HSLU treats it as equivalent under the sur-dossier route is THE decision-changing question and must be asked in writing before anything else.
acceptsNonMusic: YES FOR THIS MAJOR — REVERSING THE PREVIOUS RECORD'S 'NO'. The Studienreglement grants Major Music and Digital Creation a sur-dossier admission route on the strength of a Fachhochschule bachelor in ANY subject. No music degree, no conservatory bachelor. He must still pass the practical/theoretical music examination and the interview, and satisfy any additional major-specific qualifications, all three cumulatively — but the door is open in a way it is emphatically not for Major Komposition. THE OPEN QUESTION IS INSTITUTIONAL, NOT MUSICAL: does a Tunisian private-university BSc count as 'ein an einer Fachhochschule erworbener Bachelor-Abschluss'?
portfolio: CORRECTED — no conventional portfolio and no score dossier is required for this major (that requirement belongs to Major Komposition, which demands three scores plus recordings, none older than two years). For Music and Digital Creation the official exam-contents page requires: 'At the latest three weeks before the entrance exam, a short description (ONE A4 PAGE) must be submitted outlining a project combining music and computer science that the candidate wishes to realise within the major studies.' That is the entire written submission. For a software engineer with a year to think, this is an extraordinarily low-friction entry document — but it must be a genuinely good idea, because the whole interview turns on it.
audition: CORRECTED — no conservatory audition, but not nothing either. Official exam contents, verbatim: 'Candidates with a Bachelor of Arts in Music — Examination interview with the jury on the candidate's project description, expectations of the programme, training content and objectives, and previous knowledge of computer science / IT. Candidates with NO Bachelor of Arts in Music («sur dossier») — PRACTICAL AND THEORETICAL EXAMINATION ADDRESSING THE CANDIDATE'S MUSICAL ORIENTATION, plus examination interview with the jury on the candidate's project description, expectations of the programme, training content and objectives, and previous knowledge of MUSIC.' So he faces a practical and theoretical music examination — but one framed around HIS OWN musical orientation, not a fixed classical repertoire. A serious electronic-production practice, demonstrated live and discussed knowledgeably, is a legitimate answer to it. Ask Daniella Gerszt exactly what the practical part looks like for an electronic-music applicant; this is not published.
deadline: 28 FEBRUARY ANNUALLY (29 February in a leap year) — CONFIRMED verbatim on the official application page: 'The application deadline for ALL degree programmes is 28 February.' A standing annual rule, not a cycle-specific date. Confirmed independently on the Major Music and Digital Creation page. THIS IS ONE OF ONLY TWO PROGRAMMES IN THIS SET WHOSE DEADLINE FALLS INSIDE HIS OCTOBER 2026 – FEBRUARY 2027 WINDOW: for a September 2027 start he applies by 28 February 2027. Note the one-A4-page project description is due at the latest three weeks before the entrance exam, not at the deadline.
opens: Not published as a fixed opening date — UNVERIFIED; online registration runs up to the 28 February deadline. Fees are due at online registration.
duration: 4 semesters, 120 ECTS, full time — CONFIRMED. NOTE ON THE PREVIOUS RECORD'S 'THEORY PLACEMENT' WARNING: it is real but overstated. The official exam-contents page describes the master 'theory assessment' as something candidates complete only 'under certain conditions', where 'the result determines their PLACEMENT IN THE THEORY MODULES' — a streaming test, not a pass-or-leave gate. Whether he must sit it is 'communicated upon admission to the entrance examination'. Content, if required: two harmonic dictations with secondary dominants and altered chords, a two-part polyphonic dictation, and analysis of a Viennese Classical movement. That is still hard for a self-taught producer and he should prepare for it, but it does not by itself end the application.
languageReq: MAJOR CORRECTION — THE PREVIOUS RECORD OVERSTATED THIS BADLY. It claimed B1 German must be certified before studies begin. The official admission-requirements page (German original) says the opposite for Master's programmes: 'das Beherrschen der deutschen Sprache (im ersten Studienjahr A2-Niveau, danach B1-Niveau)' — A2 in the FIRST YEAR of study, rising to B1 from the second year. Higher levels apply only to other majors (B2 from the start for Instrumental/Vocal Pedagogy; B1 then B2 for Church Music; C1 from the start for Musiktheorie and Schulmusik II; C1 English from the start for Artistic Research — none of which is his). And 'knowledge of German is not required for the entrance examination'. NO English certificate is required for this major. Practical effect: he can sit the entrance exam with no German, and only needs A2 — a genuinely low bar, a few months of evening classes — during his first year. This turns German from a blocker into an errand.
study: Data science and digital creation applied to music; independent development, planning and execution of projects; elective modules in music practice, pedagogy or theory. Stackable Master minors confirmed from the official minors index: Electronic Music Composition, Groove und Electronics, Media Composer, Digitale Kompetenzen für Musik/Bildung/Kultur, Komposition, Jazz, Improvisation, Music Research and 13 others. Teaching is split across Lucerne School of Music (Arsenalstrasse 28a, Luzern-Kriens) and Lucerne School of Computer Science (Campus Zug-Rotkreuz).
recommendation: PROMOTED FROM 'FILE IT, DO NOT CHASE IT' TO A LIVE TARGET — the previous record assessed Major Komposition and reached a verdict that does not apply to the major he should actually pursue. Corrected picture: HSLU's Major Music and Digital Creation is a joint Musik/Informatik master, expressly built for computing graduates, with a published curriculum variant for holders of a computing bachelor, an admission rule that accepts a UAS bachelor in any subject sur dossier, an entrance submission consisting of ONE A4 PAGE describing a music-plus-computing project, German at only A2 in year one, and a standing 28 February deadline that lands inside his planning window. On top of the major he can stack Minor Electronic Music Composition, Minor Groove und Electronics or Minor Media Composer — the closest thing to electronic-music-production training in central Switzerland. THE REAL CAVEATS, and they are why this is B and not A. (1) He must pass a practical AND theoretical music examination as a sur-dossier candidate — soft compared with a composition audition, but not a formality for someone with no training at all; he needs a year of serious, demonstrable practice. (2) The 'Fachhochschule bachelor' wording may not stretch to a Tunisian private university — unresolved and decisive. (3) Cost: ~CHF 7,300 institutional plus Lucerne living costs, the highest in this set, with no funding he is known to qualify for beyond the Swiss Government Excellence Art Scholarships, whose country list must be checked. (4) Entrance exams are on site only, so budget for a separate exam visa. (5) The major leans data science and digital creation, not DJing or record production. THREE EMAILS TO SEND NOW, all free, all decision-changing, to Daniella Gerszt (Studienkoordinatorin, +41 41 249 26 05) and musik@hslu.ch: (a) does a BSc from a private Tunisian university satisfy the 'Bachelor-Diplom einer Fachhochschule' sur-dossier condition; (b) what exactly does the practical and theoretical music examination consist of for an applicant whose musical orientation is electronic production; (c) how much of the major is taught in English at Campus Zug-Rotkreuz. If (a) comes back yes, this becomes his strongest non-Austrian option and he should build the year around the one-page project idea and the practical exam.

qualification: Master of Arts FHNW in Komposition/Musiktheorie, Studienrichtung Audiodesign — full second-cycle degree, 120 ECTS
accreditation: Public Fachhochschule (FHNW). Governed by the 'Studienreglement Master of Arts FHNW in Komposition/Musiktheorie' in force 1 December 2024, whose §1(2) names the three Studienrichtungen verbatim: 'Komposition, Audiodesign, Theorie der Alten Musik'.
tuition: CHF 1,250 PER SEMESTER = CHF 2,500 PER YEAR for a Tunisian, under FHNW's published three-tier scale 'Semestergebühr 750 CHF (CH) | 1000 CHF (EU/EFTA-Länder) | 1250 CHF (Nicht-EU/Nicht-EFTA)'. A third-country national pays CHF 500/semester more than a Swiss student and CHF 250/semester more than an EU student.
otherFees: Application fee CHF 200 (FHNW HSM standard). Cost of the Goethe/telc B1 certificate. Compulsory Swiss health insurance.
totalCost: Tuition CHF 2,500/yr + CHF 200 one-off + Basel living approx CHF 20,000–24,000/yr (UNVERIFIED). Two-year total roughly CHF 45,000–53,000.
scholarshipDetail: One named internal prize, verbatim: 'Eduard Brunner Composition Award: Every year, one of our students is awarded a composition prize worth CHF 5,000 as part of an internal sonic space basel competition.' That is a prize for enrolled students, not entry funding. General FHNW scholarship pages exist but were not read — UNVERIFIED.
entry: Verbatim: 'In order to enter the FHNW Master of Arts in Composition/Music Theory programme with an Electronic Music Major, applicants must be awarded a Bachelor in Audio Design or equivalent as well as they must have passed the entrance exam and were offered a free place at the Academy (limited places). Applicants who have submitted all the necessary registration documents in time will be invited to the online entrance exam by mail and online meeting.' And: 'The FHNW Master of Arts in Composition/Music Theory with an Audio Design Major is aimed at holders of a Bachelor degree in sound design, electronic music, composition or equivalent qualification.' REQUIRED SKILLS, verbatim: 'Good skills in recording, producing and sound technology'; 'Good in handling diverse editing software (ProTools, Logic, Nuendo, Ableton Live etc.)'; 'Basic knowledge about an audio programming environment (PD, Max/MSP, Supercollider or Csound)'. Governing regulation §4(2) delegates to the Studienrichtungsreglement 'die Anforderungen an den Nachweis bei ausserordentlicher künstlerischer Begabung gemäss § 3 Abs. 1 StuPO' — i.e. there is an exceptional-talent route for applicants who lack the nominal degree; its detailed terms were NOT located and are UNVERIFIED.
acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY, AND ON SKILLS RATHER THAN ON A DEGREE. Quoted verbatim: 'aimed at holders of a Bachelor degree in sound design, electronic music, composition OR EQUIVALENT QUALIFICATION' and 'applicants must be awarded a Bachelor in Audio Design OR EQUIVALENT'. The published gate is not 'a music bachelor' but a bachelor in an audio/sound field or equivalent, and the required-skills list is entirely technical — recording, producing, sound technology, Pro Tools/Logic/Nuendo/Ableton, and an audio programming environment (Pd, Max/MSP, SuperCollider, Csound). A BSc Software Engineering plus demonstrable DAW and Max/MSP or SuperCollider work is a far more plausible 'equivalent' here than at any conservatoire Tonmeister course. The FHNW study regulation also preserves an 'ausserordentliche künstlerische Begabung' route under StuPO §3(1). NOT GUARANTEED — but this is the most argueable non-music entry in Switzerland.
portfolio: NOT PUBLISHED IN DETAIL ON THE PROGRAMME PAGE — the required-documents accordion is loaded dynamically and its contents could not be read. UNVERIFIED: the number of works, their length, and the file formats. What IS stated verbatim: 'Applicants who have submitted all the necessary registration documents in time will be invited to the online entrance exam by mail and online meeting' — so a submitted dossier gates the exam. Contact klassik.hsm@fhnw.ch or +41 61 264 57 32 for the exact list.
audition: NOT AN AUDITION AND NOT AN EAR-TRAINING EXAM — a remote, portfolio-and-interview assessment. Verbatim: 'Applicants ... will be invited to the ONLINE entrance exam BY MAIL AND ONLINE MEETING' (German page: the Eignungsabklärung takes place 'per Mail und Videokonferenz'). No instrument performance is demanded anywhere on the page; no Gehörbildung/aural test is published; no live attendance in Basel is required. This is the most accessible admission gate found in Switzerland for someone applying from Tunis — the whole assessment can be done from Tunisia. The precise exam content is UNVERIFIED beyond the format.
deadline: 1 MARCH. Verbatim: 'The registration window is open from 15th December to 1st March.' NOT a prior cycle — the page already lists the start date 13.9.2027, so for September 2027 the window is 15 December 2026 – 1 March 2027, with the German B1 certificate due by 31 May 2027.
opens: 15 December (15 December 2026 for the September 2027 intake).
duration: 4 semesters, 120 ECTS, at Campus Musik-Akademie Basel. NEXT START PUBLISHED AS 13 SEPTEMBER 2027 — his exact intake.
languageReq: German B1 (CEFR), all four skills tested separately, ALTE-Q-Mark certificate only (Goethe or telc), submitted by 31 May of the entry year — i.e. AFTER admission. Exceptions at the programme head's discretion.
study: Three specialisation fields are offered inside the major, verbatim: 'electro-acoustic composition / live performance / sound and media installation / performance of electroacoustic music'; 'RECORDING/PRODUCTION'; 'audio design & software development'. The second and third are squarely in field for him; the first is the electroacoustic/installation strand this search excludes, so the programme is only a fit if he takes the recording/production route. Graduate competences listed verbatim include: 'compose, produce, perform electronic music'; 'compose and design film/video audio tracks (incl. music, sound effects, speech)'; 'RECORD AND PRODUCE ANY GENRE OF MUSIC IN A PROFESSIONAL RECORDING STUDIO'; 'devise and develop music software to generate, transform and analyse sound'. Taught at the Elektronisches Studio Basel: 'This study programme is geared as closely as possible to practice and dovetails with the production and research activities of the Electronic Studio. From a very early stage, students are involved in the activities of the Electronic Studio and are also required to initiate and carry out their own projects.' Lecturers: Volker Böhm, Svetlana Maraš. The software-development strand is a direct use of his BSc.

institution: Hochschule für Musik Basel, FHNW (Musik-Akademie Basel)
programme: Master of Arts in Komposition/Musiktheorie — Major AUDIODESIGN (sonic space basel)
whyChance: Names engineering or computing as a welcome background, but taught in German — language is the real gate
qualification: Master of Arts (MA)
tuition: CHF 1,250 per semester for non-EU/non-EFTA students (CHF 750 Swiss residents, CHF 1,000 EU/EFTA), plus a CHF 200 application fee.
scholarshipDetail: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships ART category (initial master's at a Swiss conservatory/university of the arts; up to CHF 2,450/month; 2027–28 applications open 20 August 2026). Art scholarships cover a restricted list of countries published only in August 2026 — Tunisia's eligibility for the ART category is UNVERIFIED.
entry: "A Bachelor in Audio Design or equivalent" plus a passed entrance exam and an offer of one of a limited number of places. Stated prerequisite competences: strong recording and sound-technology skills; proficiency with editing software (Pro Tools, Logic, Nuendo, Ableton Live); and BASIC KNOWLEDGE OF AUDIO PROGRAMMING (Pd, Max/MSP, SuperCollider, Csound). German B1 by the start of studies.
acceptsNonMusic: Check — the published rule is restrictive but the expected skill set is technical. Entry requires "a Bachelor in Audio Design or equivalent", so an equivalence argument must be made; however, the listed prerequisites (Pro Tools/Logic/Nuendo/Ableton plus basic Pd/Max/SuperCollider/Csound) and the "audio design and software development" focus area are squarely in a software engineer's territory. Worth a direct equivalence enquiry rather than an assumption.
portfolio: UNVERIFIED at the level of number/length of works. FHNW states that individual entrance exams are designed "for each study programme direction" and that portfolio/aptitude details are specified in each programme's admission-procedure regulations. Request the Audiodesign Eignungsabklärung regulations from the Hochschule für Musik Basel admissions office.
audition: An Eignungsabklärung (aptitude assessment) / entrance exam specific to the Audiodesign direction. Applicants who submit complete registration documents on time are invited by mail — FHNW music admissions describe invitations to an ONLINE entrance exam via online meeting, which would remove the travel requirement, but this should be confirmed for Audiodesign specifically (UNVERIFIED for this major).
deadline: Registration window 15 December – 1 March (the Audio Design page states 15 December to 1 March; the general FHNW music page gives 15 December to 15 February with programme-specific exceptions). Studies start 14 September 2026 for the current cycle. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm both the window and which date applies to Audiodesign.
duration: 4 semesters / 120 ECTS, full-time, on-site
study: Creative music technology and electronics inside the sonic space basel platform and the ~50-year-old Electronic Studio Basel (a recording, production, experimental and research studio). You choose one of three focus areas: (1) electroacoustic composition and performance, (2) recording and production, or (3) AUDIO DESIGN AND SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT. Work culture is modular, collaborative and project-based, with composition students, performers and electronic musicians working together on and off campus.
recommendation: Content-wise the best Swiss blend of studio production, electroacoustic practice and audio software development — the "audio design and software development" track could turn his SE degree into an asset rather than a handicap. Obstacles: the "Bachelor in Audio Design or equivalent" wording, German B1 by start of studies, and an unpublished portfolio spec. Contact the school early with his production work and an equivalence request.

entry: Verbatim: 'Die Voraussetzungen für die Zulassung zum Studium und Immatrikulation sind der Rahmenordnung der ZHdK (RO § 19 bis 24) zu entnehmen. Zusätzliche Voraussetzungen inklusive der erforderlichen Sprachkenntnisse für die Zulassung zum gewählten Major-Studienprogramm sind der Studienordnung für den Masterstudiengang in Composition and Theory der Zürcher Hochschule der Künste (StO MA Composition and Theory § 4 ff.) zu entnehmen. In Ausnahmefällen kann die ZHdK Personen ohne Bachelorabschluss oder gleichwertigen Abschluss einer anerkannten und akkreditierten Hochschule zulassen.' StO §4(1) verbatim: 'Zum Studium wird zugelassen, wer a. die Zulassungsvoraussetzungen gemäss den Bestimmungen der übergeordneten fachhochschulspezifischen Erlasse erfüllt, b. einen positiven Entscheid des Aufnahmeverfahrens über die Zulassung zum Studium vorweist, c. nachweist, dass sie oder er über die für den jeweiligen Studiengang erforderlichen Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse verfügt.' StO §4(2): 'Die Zulassung zum Aufnahmeverfahren «sur dossier» ist ... möglich.' StO §4(3): 'Die Zahl der Studienplätze ist beschränkt. Die verfügbaren Studienplätze werden im Rahmen des Aufnahmeverfahrens aufgrund einer Bestenliste vergeben.' A medical AUDIOGRAM no older than 2 months must be submitted with the application.
acceptsNonMusic: YES IN PRINCIPLE — the regulation demands only a bachelor from a recognised, accredited higher-education institution, never a music bachelor, and §4(2) explicitly opens the aptitude procedure 'sur dossier'. But the application page attaches an explicit penalty clause, quoted verbatim: 'Zusatzprüfung bei fehlendem Bachelorabschluss in Musik — Instrumentale Praxis: Beherrschung eines Instruments auf einem Niveau, das es der/dem Kandidierenden ermöglicht, sich durch das Instrument musikalisch auszudrücken. Prüfungsinhalt: Performance auf einem Instrument von zwei verschiedenen Stücken; kurzes Partiturspiel. Gehörbildung: Darstellen und Erkennen von Intervallen, Klängen, Akkordstrukturen, Rhythmen, Harmoniefolgen. Musikalische Allgemeinbildung: Kurzanalyse von zwei stilistisch verschiedenen Stücken.' So a BSc Software Engineering is admissible on paper but triggers a supplementary instrument audition AND an ear-training exam. For this candidate that is the decisive obstacle.
portfolio: Verbatim: 'Dossier mit eigenen Aufnahmen (max. 1.95 GB): Reiche 3 verschiedenen Stücke oder Ausschnitte von insgesamt ca. 10 Minuten Länge ein (Partituren/Texte/Bilder als pdf, Audio als mp3, Video als mp4 Datei).' So: EXACTLY 3 pieces or excerpts, ~10 minutes TOTAL (not each), audio as mp3, video as mp4, scores/texts/images as pdf, whole dossier zipped, ZIP under 1.95 GB. Plus 'Gib eine Einschätzung zu diesen Aufnahmen ab (max. zwei A4-Seiten)' saved as 'Einschätzung.pdf' — a written self-assessment of your own recordings. Optional 'Links.pdf' with personal website / SoundCloud / Bandcamp / Vimeo links. Filenames must carry surname+first name and must not contain special characters or umlauts. Also required: Motivationsschreiben max. 2 A4 pages (German or English), tabular CV, passport copy, passport photo min. 320x400 px, and the audiogram. 'Der Einsatz von künstlicher Intelligenz (KI) ist erlaubt und muss bei der Einreichung der Anmeldung angegeben werden.'
audition: THREE-WAY BREAKDOWN. (1) PORTFOLIO — the 3-piece dossier above, screened first: 'A Schriftlich — Mit der Anmeldung reichen die Kandidierenden ein Motivationsschreiben sowie ein Dossier mit eigenen Aufnahmen ein. Bei positiver Beurteilung werden die Kandidat:innen zur mündlichen Eignungsprüfung eingeladen.' (2) PRACTICAL PRODUCTION TEST — FAVOURABLE, this is the job: a take-home assignment emailed to you ('Einreichen einer Hausaufgabe ... innerhalb der gesetzten Frist ... Umfang: Maximal zwei A4 Seiten'), then 'Tonmeisterliche Praxis (Dauer 25 Minuten). Es steht eine Vorbereitungszeit von 60 Minuten zur Verfügung. Musikübertragung — Themenfelder: Routinierte Bedienung der Infrastruktur (DAW, Peripherie); Klare Vorstellung der Abläufe bei einer Musikproduktion; Zielgerichtetes Mikrofonieren, Editieren und Mischen; Klangästhetische Vorstellung und Fähigkeit, diese umzusetzen; Grundlagen der Aufnahmeleitung. Prüfungsinhalt: Die Kandidierenden bringen eine Session auf dem eigenen System mit, die sie an der Prüfung präsentieren und mit dem Experten diskutieren.' Studiotechnik: 'Anhand der mitgebrachten Produktion werden aufnahmetechnische Fragen diskutiert ... Alternativ oder zusätzlich erhalten die Kandidierenden präparierte Audioclips mit typischen Fehlern oder Artefakten, die gemeinsam diskutiert werden.' NOTE this is a production/engineering test, NOT an audition. (3) TECHNICAL WRITTEN/ORAL EXAM — 'Technische Fächer (Dauer 25 Minuten)' covering Elektrotechnik (charge/current/voltage, network analysis, bipolar transistor and op-amp circuits, filters, microphones and loudspeakers, measurement practice, design and build a simple circuit), Digitale Audiotechnik (sampling and reconstruction, A/D and D/A, data compression, FFT, z-transform, digital filters), Akustik (room acoustics, absorption, reverberation-time measurement, ray tracing, eigenmodes), and Mathematik/Informatik (trigonometric/exponential/log/polynomial functions, Fourier transform, complex numbers, system equations, frequency response, impulse response, differentiation and integration, simple differential equations). A software-engineering BSc is an ASSET here. (4) EAR-TRAINING EXAM + INSTRUMENT AUDITION — applies to him because he has no music bachelor: 'Gehörbildung: Darstellen und Erkennen von Intervallen, Klängen, Akkordstrukturen, Rhythmen, Harmoniefolgen' and 'Performance auf einem Instrument von zwei verschiedenen Stücken; kurzes Partiturspiel'. HE CANNOT PASS THESE. This is the gate that closes ZHdK Tonmeister.

Alle Dateien sind mit Nachname_Vorname_Komponist_Werk zu bezeichnen.' The naming convention (Komponist_Werk) shows they expect performances of repertoire. So 3 TO 4 works, ~10 minutes TOTAL. Each must be commented: 'Kommentiere jede dieser Arbeiten (Konzept, Bedeutung, Entstehungsprozess etc.). Fasse diese Kommentare (max. zwei A4-Seiten) in einer einzigen pdf-Datei zusammen. Benenne diese Datei «Kommentare.pdf».' PLUS a separate application video: 'Bewerbungsvideo (max. 3–5 Minuten / max. 1 GB / Format mp4), in dem du dich in deiner eigenen kreativen Arbeitsumgebung präsentierst.' Optional 'Links.pdf'. Plus the non-music-bachelor performance video (max 15 min). Recording quality spec given for video items: 'HD Video (720p; 1080i; 1080p) mit 265 kbit/s Klangauflösung, Format mov oder mp4. Max 1.95 GB'; 'Verwendung eines Stereo-Mikrofons ist erwünscht.' All zipped into one ZIP under 1.95 GB.
audition: MIXED — one favourable gate and one fatal one. PRACTICAL PRODUCTION TEST (FAVOURABLE — this is the job, not a barrier), verbatim: 'Praktische Prüfung — Sound Design-Aufgabe (90 Minuten Vorbereitungszeit, 20 Minuten Präsentation und Diskussion)' and 'Mündliche Prüfung Analyse einer kurzen Filmszene, eines Game-Levels, einer Klangszene etc. (60 Minuten Vorbereitungszeit, 10 Minuten Präsentation und Diskussion)' plus 'Mündliche Präsentation / Kolloquium anhand einer der eingereichten Arbeiten (10 Minuten)'. You are handed material and asked to make something — exactly the format that suits a self-taught producer. EAR-TRAINING EXAM (HE CANNOT PASS), verbatim: 'Musikalische Eignungsprüfung — Mündliche Theorieaufgaben (Gedächtnisübung; Darstellen von Rhythmen und Melodien; Intervalle und Akkorde erkennen, benennen und schreiben können; harmonische Aufgabe; Kurzimprovisation), Dauer 30 Minuten.' Recognising, naming and WRITING intervals and chords by ear, plus a short improvisation, is conservatoire aural skill. Combined with the non-music-bachelor performance video, ZHdK Sound Design is also effectively closed to him.

scholarshipDetail: CONFIRMED — and this is the decisive advantage. entry: CONFIRMED verbatim from the official 2025-26 exam guide admission table: ALES Puanı Şartı = 'Aranmaz' (not required); Yabancı Dil Taban Puanı = 'Aranmaz' (not required); Mezuniyet Taban Notu = 2.50/4.00 or 65/100 or 3.1/5.00; Programa Kabul edilen Mezunlar = 'Herhangi bir lisans programından mezun olmak' (graduation from ANY bachelor's programme). acceptsNonMusic: YES — EXPLICITLY AND CONFIRMED. The official guide states the accepted graduates are 'Herhangi bir lisans programından mezun olmak' — any bachelor's programme whatsoever. A BSc in Software Engineering is formally, unambiguously eligible. This remains the single most important fact about this programme for him. portfolio: REQUIRED and CONFIRMED in detail. Weighted 10% of the entrance score (dosya değerlendirmesi). The candidate must upload to the designated area on the university site by 23:59 on the closing day, AND hand the jury three (3) printed copies of a file containing: (A) ONE single work he produced himself reflecting his interest/aptitude in the area he intends to study, in sound recording, sound programming, instrument making, sound electronics or acoustics — supplied as (a) a digital copy on CD/DVD/external USB and (b) an explanatory text describing the work's content; (B) a digital copy (CD/DVD/USB) of his other personal works in the field with the associated audio files, software and/or written documents plus an index of those materials; (C) his CV. audition: Two-stage entrance exam, entirely in Turkish — CONFIRMED in full. STAGE I (60% of the entrance score), six assessed areas with exact point weights: Müziksel İşitme (musical ear-training — distinguishing musical elements in a played recording and describing them in technical language) 27 pts; Mesleki İşitme (technical listening — analysing, classifying and describing played sounds) 27 pts; Mesleki Bilgi (professional technical/theoretical knowledge) 9 pts; Problem Çözme 9 pts; Analitik Düşünme 19 pts; Akademik Araştırmaya Yatkınlık 9 pts. For that last component candidates must read IN ADVANCE a named Turkish journal article on determining the acoustic properties of small-scale popular-music production spaces (dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/203754), answer a question on it in writing in the first part of the exam, then defend that written answer orally. Electronic devices of any kind are banned from the exam. STAGE II (30%): oral examination on the submitted file — Ana Çalışma Yeterliği (command of his main submitted work) 57 pts, Yazılı Sınav Değerlendirmesi (review of his written exam) 28 pts, Genel Değerlendirme 15 pts. ENTRANCE SCORE = 10% file + 60% Stage I + 30% Stage II. PASS MARK 60/100. FINAL RANKING = 70% entrance-exam score + 30% bachelor GPA. Appeals within 2 working days, decided within 3.

study: CORRECTED. The previous record attributed the wrong syllabus to this programme. The official 2026/2027 interview конспект for Мениджмънт на музикалните индустрии is: (1) types of music organisations in Bulgaria by genre and mode of financing; (2) foreign models of financing and organising musical life; (3) specifics of organising musical events; (4) organisations in Bulgaria financing music-culture projects; (5) the diversity and specifics of professions in the music industries; (6) the role of the public sector in cultural life — state and municipal cultural institutes. Recommended reading is Bulgarian arts-management literature (Върбанова, Георгиев, Томова) plus lex.bg, the Ministry of Culture, National Culture Fund and IJMBR. The 'record labels / copyright / Tommy Swindali' syllabus the previous record quoted belongs to a DIFFERENT programme — Музикално продуцентство — not to this one.
recommendation: THE ONLY BULGARIAN DOOR STILL OPEN TO HIM — AND IT LEADS TO THE WRONG ROOM. Now that the game-audio specialty has closed to non-music graduates, this is the sole programme at either Bulgarian academy that a software-engineering graduate can legally enter. It is a real, accredited, state-recognised master's; no music degree, no audition, no portfolio. But the verified syllabus is narrower and more local than the previous record suggested: it is about how Bulgarian music organisations are financed and run, the role of Bulgarian state and municipal cultural institutes, and the professions of the Bulgarian music sector — assessed in a Bulgarian-language interview plus a motivation discussion. It teaches him nothing about sound design, production craft or electronic music, which is what he says he wants and what his portfolio year is meant to build. Add €8,500/year with no scholarship he can win, mandatory certified Bulgarian, and an application window that closes five days before term starts. Keep it on the list only as evidence that Bulgaria has been checked properly, not as a plan.

tuition: CRITICAL AND NEW. Décret n°2026-385 of 19 May 2026 (part of the 'Choose France for Higher Education' plan), effective 1 September 2026, changes how differentiated fees work at French PUBLIC UNIVERSITIES. Reference amounts (2025-2026 basis; 2026-2027 amounts 'not yet known' per service-public.gouv.fr): LICENCE €2,895/yr vs €178 standard; MASTER €3,941/yr vs €254 standard. EXEMPTION QUOTAS: universities may exempt at most 30% of their non-EU students in 2026-2027, 25% in 2027-2028 (THE CANDIDATE'S ENTRY YEAR), and 20% long-term. Previously universities exempted non-EU students en masse, making the regime largely theoretical; that is no longer safe to assume. Students already exempted keep the exemption to the end of their cycle. Exempt by right: EU/EEA/Swiss nationals, Canadians resident in Quebec, students enrolled since 2018/2019, doctoral students, holders of a French government scholarship (bourse du gouvernement français), refugees/subsidiary protection, legal French residents. A TUNISIAN IS NOT EXEMPT BY RIGHT. IMPORTANT: this regime targets universities; Ministry-of-Culture establishments (CNSMD Paris/Lyon, ENSATT, ENS Louis-Lumière, Le Fresnoy, écoles nationales supérieures d'art) charge their own low flat fees (€300–€760/yr observed) and no differentiated non-EU rate was found for them.
otherFees: CVEC approx. €105/yr at French institutions. Campus France Tunisie procedure fee: 400 TND to validate the application file.
totalCost: Budget approx. €4,000/yr in tuition for a public UNIVERSITY master vs approx. €300–800/yr for a Ministry-of-Culture school. This is the single biggest cost variable in this sweep and it points the candidate towards the Culture-ministry schools and Belgium.
scholarshipDetail: EIFFEL: candidates must be 29 or younger at selection for the 2027 campaign; dual French nationals ineligible; CANDIDATES CANNOT APPLY DIRECTLY — only French institutions may nominate, so the candidate must ask each target institution about its internal Eiffel procedure. Eiffel is restricted to specific disciplinary fields (sciences/engineering, economics/management, law/political science and related) and ARTS AND MUSIC MASTERS ARE GENERALLY NOT ELIGIBLE — meaning the only Eiffel-plausible entries in this whole sweep are the SCIENCE masters (AMU Ingénierie et conception sonore, Sorbonne ATIAM, Brest Ingénierie du son, Le Mans Acoustique). UNVERIFIED against the official 2027 Eiffel call. INSTITUT FRANÇAIS DE TUNISIE: offers scholarships targeting culture, arts and humanities, 'often with less competition than Eiffel' — the appropriate route for the artistic programmes in this list; amounts and deadlines UNVERIFIED. BOURSE DU GOUVERNEMENT FRANÇAIS: confers exemption from frais différenciés by right — the highest-leverage funding target. ARES (Belgium) development-cooperation scholarships: Tunisia eligibility for arts masters UNVERIFIED.
deadline: ÉTUDES EN FRANCE / CAMPUS FRANCE TUNISIE (mandatory for a Tunisian resident applying to a connected French institution): campaign opens 1 OCTOBER of the year before entry; MASTER 1 / MASTER 2 APPLICATIONS CLOSE ~15 JANUARY; institutions reply by ~30 APRIL; the candidate must reply by ~31 MAY ('the absence of response is considered a refusal'). Six-step process: identify connected formations; complete the online file; register for French language certification exams; validate the file and pay 400 TND; attend an interview at the Campus France office with original documents; confirm the final choice and book the visa appointment. FOR SEPTEMBER 2027 ENTRY THIS MEANS THE FILE MUST BE READY BY ~15 JANUARY 2027 — much earlier than monmaster.gouv.fr (late Feb–March), which is the EU/resident route. Institutions not connected to Études en France are applied to directly (procédure HDAP).

institution: LEPL Vano Sarajishvili Tbilisi State Conservatoire (TSC)
programme: Music Technology (Master of Arts) — English-language stream
whyChance: Music degree is the named route, but technical subjects count as comparable — ask
qualification: Master of Arts, a genuine second-cycle degree. Georgia is a full EHEA member and a Lisbon Recognition Convention party, so the award is Bologna second-cycle and recognisable in the EU through ENIC-NARIC. The programme sits in the Composition and Musicology Faculty. Nothing found this pass contradicts this.
accreditation: PARTIALLY CORRECTED — the previous agent overstated this. (1) Georgian state accreditation is solid and independently evidenced: the institution is an LEPL under the national quality system and it distributes state-funded master's places, which I verified in the official quota PDF. (2) THE MusiQuE CLAIM COULD NOT BE RE-VERIFIED. I searched tsc.edu.ge for an accreditation or quality-assurance page and found none — the URL the previous agent's reasoning implied (tsc.edu.ge/en/accreditation-2/) returns HTTP 404, and the English homepage contains no reference to MusiQuE or to a 31 March 2025 decision. What IS visible on the official site is that TSC lists the AEC (Association Européenne des Conservatoires) among its international partners, which is consistent with but not proof of a MusiQuE accreditation. TREAT 'MusiQuE-accredited, 31 March 2025' AS AN UNCONFIRMED CLAIM, not as the strongest accreditation signal available. Ask ir.office@tsc.edu.ge for the MusiQuE decision letter in writing. This matters: it was the previous agent's main argument for the programme's international standing.
tuition: 3,423 EUR per year; 6,846 EUR total for the two-year degree. CONFIRMED VERBATIM — I extracted the text layer of TSC's own PDF at https://tsc.edu.ge/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/2.Program-Cost-per-year-MA.pdf. Its heading reads 'Program Cost per Year with a 20% Fee Increase (euro)' and the line reads 'Technology MA – 3,423 euro per year (total cost: 6,846 euro)'. For context from the same table, Composition MA is 2,827 EUR/yr and Piano MA is 4,154 EUR/yr, so Music Technology is mid-range. THIS FIGURE IS THE 2026-2027 RATE AND ALREADY INCLUDES A 20% INCREASE — a further rise before September 2027 is plausible; budget headroom.
otherFees: Exam/audition participation fee 50 EUR (or the GEL equivalent) for applicants applying WITHOUT the Unified Master's Exam, which is his category; applicants applying WITH the Unified Master's Exam pay 50 GEL instead. CONFIRMED on the official page. Bank details at https://tsc.edu.ge/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Transfer-Details.pdf. Foreign-language documents must be translated into Georgian and notarised — cost UNVERIFIED. Accommodation, health insurance and residence-permit fees are not published — UNVERIFIED.
totalCost: Verified hard costs: 6,846 EUR tuition + 50 EUR exam fee = 6,896 EUR across two years. Living costs, residence permit, insurance and notarised translations are not published by TSC — UNVERIFIED. Tbilisi is cheap by European standards but do not budget on an unpublished number; ask ir.office@tsc.edu.ge for cost-of-living guidance.
scholarshipDetail: NONE HE CAN WIN — CONFIRMED VERBATIM. TSC's own fee PDF ends with the footnote: '*Scholarships and institutional funding are not available for international students.' The 5 state-funded places shown against English-language Music Technology sit in the quota table for applicants applying WITH the Georgian Unified Master's Exam, i.e. the domestic route. I opened the other table — the one covering applicants WITHOUT the Unified Master's Exam, which is his route — and it has no funding column at all; it says only 'Shall not exceed 5% of the maximum student enrollment capacity (for all programs)'. So the 5 funded places are structurally unavailable to him. This is fully verified and it is the programme's defining weakness.
entry: CONFIRMED VERBATIM AND STILL THE CENTRAL PROBLEM FOR HIM. The official page states: 'The prerequisite for admission to Master's degree programmes is a Bachelor's academic degree, higher academic musical education.' Read literally, that demands a music bachelor, which he does not have. Against it: the Music Technology entrance has no instrumental and no music-theory component at all — only a project, a portfolio and an English interview — which is the structure of a programme built for technologists. Required documents, confirmed on the official page: registration form, citizenship/ID document, 3x4 JPG photograph, exam-fee payment receipt, English B2 evidence, and for non-Unified-Exam applicants the bachelor's diploma plus academic records; foreign documents need notarised Georgian translations; for Music Technology specifically, the master's project description and portfolio. HE MUST ASK enrollment@tsc.edu.ge IN WRITING WHETHER A BSc IN SOFTWARE ENGINEERING SATISFIES THIS RULE, in autumn 2026, before spending a year building a portfolio for it.
acceptsNonMusic: UNCERTAIN, DECISIVE, AND STILL UNRESOLVED. The stated prerequisite is 'a Bachelor's academic degree, higher academic musical education', which on its face excludes him. Against that, the Music Technology entrance contains no musical test of any kind — a project, a portfolio and an English interview, which is a structure built for people who make things with computers. This one email determines whether Georgia belongs on his list at all. Write to enrollment@tsc.edu.ge and ir.office@tsc.edu.ge in October 2026.
portfolio: Two electronic deliverables: (1) a written description of the Master's Artistic Project, i.e. what he proposes to make across the two years, and (2) a portfolio of past artistic activities. CORRECTION TO THE PREVIOUS RECORD: it claimed 'Changes to the Artistic Project and Portfolio are permitted up to 25 June of the admission year.' That is not in the Music Technology requirements document — I read its complete text and it contains no such sentence. The 25 June date on the MA-Admission page is the deadline for changing the SELECTED PROGRAMME, and the date by which the exam schedule is published. Do not rely on a portfolio-revision window that the official documents do not grant. No format, length, duration or track-count spec is published anywhere — still UNVERIFIED; ask the Music Technology department for one. For him the Artistic Project is the lever: it is a forward-looking proposal, not a back catalogue, and a software engineer can write a strong one.
audition: CONFIRMED VERBATIM — I downloaded and read the full one-page document 'Master's Degree Educational Programme of Music Technology — Requirements for the Admission/Exam/Audition Round'. It states: assessment on a 100-point system, passing score range 71-100; the candidate 'must undergo an exam/audition round in the specialty (for English-Language Programme) and a General Master's Exam (for Georgian-Language Programme)'; the round comprises '(A) a written description of the applicant's artistic project (electronical File / folder) and submission of portfolio of past artistic activities (electronical File / folder)' and '(B) an English-language interview on project-related issues, during which the applicant provides a presentation of the project and answers to the questions of the commission members.' There is NO instrumental audition and NO music-theory paper. Document: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1dfV5yDgkkFwWVWQTrHFew3a78tD8fjCi/view
deadline: 2026-2027 cycle, CONFIRMED on the official page: registration closed 3 June 2026; audition/exam rounds 6-18 July 2026; exam schedule published by 25 June 2026; deadline for programme changes 25 June 2026. ALL PRIOR CYCLE — confirm 2027 dates. Expect registration late May to early June 2027 and interviews early-to-mid July 2027.
opens: Registration for exam/audition rounds ran 21 May – 3 June 2026 for the 2026-2027 year — CONFIRMED on the official page. PRIOR CYCLE; expect roughly late May 2027 for a September 2027 start. Usefully, this is LATER than the European October 2026 – February 2027 call season, so TSC does not compete with those deadlines and can be held as a late fallback decided in summer 2027.
duration: 2 years (4 semesters) — CONFIRMED on the official page, which states all Master's programmes span 2 years / 4 semesters. TOTAL ECTS IS STILL NOT PUBLISHED — I re-checked and the official page carries no credit figure. The Georgian second-cycle norm is 120 ECTS but TSC does not say so on its own domain. Get the ECTS total in writing; he will need it for any later EU recognition file.
languageReq: CONFIRMED VERBATIM, including the escape clause the previous agent flagged. The official page reads: 'applicants must submit an internationally recognized certificate confirming English language proficiency at a minimum of B2 level (CEFR), including IELTS, Cambridge English PET, Pitman ESOL International, TOEIC, or TOEFL, or any other official document issued by an accredited educational institution confirming at least B2-level proficiency in English.' That final clause is real and is on the official page. It means a letter or transcript from SMU MedTech evidencing English-medium instruction at B2 may satisfy the rule without an IELTS sitting. Confirm in writing with enrollment@tsc.edu.ge before paying for a test. No Georgian required for the English stream.
englishTest: B2 CEFR minimum. IELTS, Cambridge English PET, Pitman ESOL International, TOEIC and TOEFL are named as acceptable, but the official wording also accepts 'any other official document issued by an accredited educational institution confirming at least B2-level proficiency in English' — CONFIRMED VERBATIM. Since he has not sat IELTS, this alternative may spare him the test entirely. Get it confirmed in writing.
study: The admission document I read in full defines the centre of gravity: the candidate is admitted on a self-authored Master's Artistic Project and spends the two years realising it. NO MODULE LIST AND NO ECTS BREAKDOWN IS PUBLISHED ANYWHERE ON THE OFFICIAL SITE — I checked the MA-Admission page and its full document index (quotas, costs, transfer details, evaluation system, per-programme admission requirements, registration forms, exam schedules) and there is no curriculum or syllabus document among them. STILL UNVERIFIED. Request the silabusi from enrollment@tsc.edu.ge or ir.office@tsc.edu.ge before committing.
recommendation: CONFIRMED AS THE STRONGEST OF THESE THREE AND THE ONLY ONE TAUGHT IN ENGLISH — but downgraded from the previous record's assessment on two counts. What survives verification intact: no instrumental audition, no theory exam, entry on a written artistic project plus portfolio plus an English interview, a B2 English rule with a genuine non-test escape clause, and 3,423 EUR/year (6,846 EUR total) — cheap enough that self-paying is realistic for him. What I corrected: FIRST, the MusiQuE international accreditation claim could not be re-verified — there is no accreditation page on tsc.edu.ge, the expected URL 404s, and the English site never mentions MusiQuE. That was the previous agent's headline argument for the programme's international standing, and he should now treat it as unproven and ask for the decision letter. SECOND, the claimed 25 June portfolio-revision window does not exist in the official document; 25 June is the programme-change deadline. What remains true and hard: zero funding, stated in writing by TSC, so this is a pure self-pay decision; the entry rule literally says 'higher academic musical education' and he has a software engineering BSc; no studio inventory is published, which for a technology degree is a serious gap; and Georgia sits outside the EU and Schengen, so this advances his craft and his credential but not his European residence position. Rating B rather than A for exactly those reasons — good fit, real caveats. Sequencing: TSC registration opens in late May, well clear of the Oct 2026 – Feb 2027 European rounds, so he should chase funded European programmes first and hold Tbilisi as a paid fallback decided in summer 2027. Actions for October 2026, by email to enrollment@tsc.edu.ge and ir.office@tsc.edu.ge: (1) does a non-music BSc satisfy the entry requirement for Music Technology; (2) what exactly must the portfolio contain, and is there a revision deadline; (3) what studios and equipment does the department have, with photographs; (4) what is the total ECTS; (5) can a letter from SMU MedTech confirming English-medium study satisfy the B2 rule; (6) please send the MusiQuE accreditation decision. Then spend the year drafting the Master's Artistic Project — that document, not his back catalogue, is what he is admitted on.

entry: CONFIRMED and stricter than previously recorded: an internationally recognised first degree (Bachelor, Diplom, First State Exam or equivalent); the programme "builds on a bachelor's degree in media technology or design" and expects approximately 210 ECTS — with fewer credits "eine individuelle Prüfung hinsichtlich der Anerkennung von Kompetenzen" (individual competency review) is carried out, with up to 30 ECTS potentially credited. Applicants must evidence at least 15 ECTS in engineering fundamentals ("Mathematik, Informatik, Physik, Nachrichtentechnik, Elektronik") AND at least 15 ECTS in media-related applications ("visuelle Gestaltung, Bild-/Ton-/Textkonzeption, Sounddesign"). German C1. The NC "lay in recent years approximately in the range of 2.2" (German grading), varying annually.
acceptsNonMusic: Check — half yes, half no. No music degree is required and the FAQ lists many qualifying bachelors from engineering, film and design fields "oder andere ähnlich geartete Studiengänge/Hochschulen", so non-media backgrounds are not excluded outright. His BSc easily covers the 15 ECTS in engineering fundamentals (mathematics, informatics). The problem is the second, equally mandatory 15 ECTS in media-related applications — visual design, image/sound/text conception, sound design — which a software-engineering curriculum almost certainly does not contain, plus a 180-vs-210 ECTS shortfall triggering an individual competency review. Formally arguable, practically weak without documented media/sound coursework.
portfolio: No artistic portfolio is required — CONFIRMED. Optional supporting documents can improve the procedure grade by up to 0.5 grade points: a motivation letter of maximum 2 pages, evidence of two or more years of post-bachelor professional experience, letters of recommendation from universities or employers, and evidence of engagement in politics, culture, sport or social activities.

study: Three profiles: 3D Audio and Music Technology, Visual Media Creation, and Computer-Generated Imagery, each with mandatory core modules plus electives. The programme combines research, design and engineering, with students developing audiovisual concepts, prototypical media applications and scientific solutions for the media industry. The 3D Audio and Music Technology profile works on current audio-technology questions with a focus on 3D audio applied to sound design, radio drama (Hörspiel) and interactive audio installations, in modern studios. Engineering- and research-flavoured, not track production.
recommendation: On the surface this is the ideal technical route: no portfolio, no audition, no artistic gatekeeping, and a 3D-audio and music-technology profile where a CS degree is an advantage. In practice three things block him. German at C1 (Telc C1 / TestDaF 16 / Goethe C1) is mandatory and he has none. The admission rules demand 15 ECTS of documented media/design/sound coursework in addition to the engineering 15 ECTS, which his BSc almost certainly lacks, and his 180 ECTS falls short of the ~210 expected, triggering an individual review. And it costs €1,500 per semester plus fees as a non-EU student. Even if all that were solved, the content is 3D audio, Hörspiel and installations — engineering for the media industry, not producing and performing tracks.

entry: SPO §4(1) verbatim: 'Voraussetzung für die Zulassung zum Studium dieses Studiengangs sind ein fachlich affiner erster Hochschulabschluss sowie das Bestehen der Aufnahmeprüfung. In begründeten Fällen können auch hervorragende berufliche Leistungen als Qualifikation ganz oder teilweise anerkannt werden.' The Immatrikulationssatzung annex is stricter, verbatim: 'Das Aufbaustudium mit dem Studienziel Master (M.A.) im Fach Musikinformatik setzt den erfolgreichen Abschluss des grundständigen Studiengangs Musikwissenschaft/Musikinformatik B.A. an der HfM Karlsruhe oder eines entsprechenden Studiengangs an einer anderen Hochschule voraus, wobei die HAUPTFACHNOTE 2,5 ODER BESSER sein muss.' And then the crucial escape clause, verbatim: 'Absolventen eines Bachelor-Studiengangs anderer Hochschulen, die das Aufbaustudium Musikinformatik M.A. belegen wollen, aber KEINEN entsprechenden Bachelor-Abschluss im Fach Musikinformatik oder Musikwissenschaft/Musikinformatik haben, müssen entsprechende gleichwertige Kenntnisse nachweisen und in einer ERWEITERTEN AUFNAHMEPRÜFUNG bestätigen.'
acceptsNonMusic: YES, VIA TWO EXPLICIT ROUTES. First, SPO §4(1) requires only 'ein fachlich affiner erster Hochschulabschluss' — a SUBJECT-AFFINE first degree, not a music degree; a computing degree is plainly affine to Musikinformatik. Second, and unusually, 'In begründeten Fällen können auch hervorragende berufliche Leistungen als Qualifikation ganz oder teilweise anerkannt werden' — outstanding professional achievement can substitute wholly or partly for the degree. Third, the annex provides for entrants without the nominal bachelor: they 'müssen entsprechende gleichwertige Kenntnisse nachweisen und in einer erweiterten Aufnahmeprüfung bestätigen'. The trade-off is an EXTENDED entrance exam, whose extra parts the commission sets case by case: 'Sofern Abweichungen von den Zulassungsvoraussetzungen vorliegen und der Bewerber einen Antrag auf Ausnahmeregelung gestellt hat, kann die Kommission zusätzliche Prüfungsteile festlegen. Diese müssen dem Bewerber mindestens 3 Wochen vor dem Prüfungstermin schriftlich mitgeteilt werden.' You get three weeks' written notice of whatever extra is demanded — so the risk is knowable, not blind.
portfolio: REMARKABLY BROAD, AND SOFTWARE COUNTS. SPO §4(3) verbatim: '1. ein Motivationsschreiben, in dem auf maximal zwei Seiten die persönlichen Erwartungen an das Studium und die Gründe für die beabsichtigte Aufnahme des Studiums dargelegt werden sollen; 2. MINDESTENS ZWEI ARBEITSPROBEN IN DER FORM VON TEXTEN, AUDIO- ODER VIDEODATEIEN, SOFTWARE O.Ä.; DIES KANN AUCH PER LINK ERFOLGEN; 3. Nachweis über Kenntnis und sichere Beherrschung der deutschen Sprache.' So: AT LEAST TWO work samples, and they may be texts, audio files, video files OR SOFTWARE — submittable by link. No track count, no duration, no audio format prescribed. A candidate with no music portfolio but a GitHub history and two audio experiments can satisfy this literally. The motivation letter is capped at two pages.
audition: NO AUDITION, NO EAR-TRAINING EXAM, NO PRODUCTION TEST — a single interview. Verbatim, SPO §4(2): 'Die Aufnahmeprüfung besteht im Regelfall aus einem ca. 20-minütigen Eignungsgespräch, bei dem fachspezifische Vorkenntnisse, Sprachgewandtheit in der deutschen Sprache sowie die Studienmotivation überprüft werden. Für die Aufnahmeprüfung bildet der Prüfungsausschuss des Instituts eine Prüfungskommission.' The Immatrikulationssatzung annex gives the duration as 'ein Eignungsgespräch von ca. 25 Minuten Dauer' for Musikinformatik. Nothing is played, nothing is sung, no intervals are identified. THE ONLY CAVEAT is the 'erweiterte Aufnahmeprüfung' for entrants without the nominal bachelor — its content is set by the commission and is UNVERIFIED, but it is notified in writing three weeks in advance. Note the interview itself is a German-language test.
deadline: 15 JUNE annually for the entrance examination (application deadline). Winter-semester start only. This is a LATE deadline by German standards and gives him far more runway than the February–March Swiss dates.
opens: UNVERIFIED — deadline is fixed at 15 June.
duration: 4 semesters. Winter-semester start; SPO §4(4): 'Der Studienbeginn erfolgt zum Wintersemester. In begründeten Ausnahmefällen kann eine Aufnahme zum Sommersemester erfolgen.' ECTS not read from the SPO — UNVERIFIED (a German M.A. of this length is normally 120 ECTS).

englishTest: None required — UNVERIFIED whether English is assessed at all.
study: Music informatics at IMWI — the computational side of music. FIT CAVEAT, AND IT IS A REAL ONE: IMWI Karlsruhe is oriented to computer music, algorithmic composition, music software and musicology rather than to recording, mixing and mastering. It sits close to the 'sonology' territory this search excludes. tuition: SELF-PAY, now CONFIRMED — this is the biggest correction. The programme page's 'Keine Studiengebühren für EU-Bürger:innen bei Erstmaster' does not help him. Baden-Württemberg's LHGebG applies: 'Studiengebühr Internationale Studierende: 1.500 € pro Semester gem. § 3ff LHGebG für Studierende aus Ländern außerhalb der EU / des EWR ohne inländische Hochschulzulassungsberechtigung ... für alle Bachelor- und konsekutiven Master-Studiengänge'. Over four semesters that is €6,000, plus Verwaltungskostenbeitrag €80.00 and Studierendenwerksbeitrag €58.60 per semester (as of May 2026) — about €6,554 total. Exemptions exist under §§5–7 LHGebG (e.g. permanent domestic residence, spouses/children of EU/EEA nationals) and a waiver 'aufgrund besonderer Begabung gemäß § 6 Abs. 4 LHGebG' is possible on application; waiver applications are due 21 January / 21 June for the following semester.
scholarshipDetail: None from the institution — stated plainly on the school's own page for international applicants: 'Die Trossinger Hochschule kann keine finanzielle Unterstützung leisten', with only small Förderverein grants (e.g. competition travel) on application. It adds that German partial scholarships from the ministry or DAAD 'können erst nach einigen Semestern erfolgreichen Studierens beantragt werden' and go to very few students. A special-talent tuition waiver under § 6 Abs. 4 LHGebG is the one real lever. DAAD study scholarships normally require full-time enrolment, which a 50% part-time master does not satisfy — treat DAAD as unavailable here unless DAAD confirms otherwise.
entry: No specific bachelor subject is mandated. The page invites entrants from 'Architektur, Design, Musik, Medien, Informatik, Pädagogik oder Wissenschaft' and lists 'Einstieg aus vielen Bereichen und Disziplinen möglich' as a selling point. Submit: a motivation letter with a chronological account of prior musical and/or design background plus any publications or competition results; certificates (Zeugnisse); the Zulassungsantrag; proof of the transfer (fee payment); further documents per the Zulassungsantrag; and the media materials described below. German B2 per the Immatrikulationssatzung, deferrable to the third-semester re-registration deadline. The legally binding text is the Immatrikulationssatzung.
acceptsNonMusic: Yes — explicitly, and computer science is named. The official page opens with: 'Ob in Architektur, Design, Musik, Medien, Informatik, Pädagogik oder Wissenschaft: hier verbindest du dein bisheriges Fachgebiet mit auditiven Perspektiven' ('Whether in architecture, design, music, media, COMPUTER SCIENCE, education or science: here you connect your existing field with auditory perspectives'), and lists 'Einstieg aus vielen Bereichen und Disziplinen möglich'. A software-engineering BSc is squarely in scope, and the assessment is of the idea, not of musicianship: 'Wir bewerten das Potenzial deiner Idee.'
portfolio: EXACT, confirmed verbatim, and note the delivery mechanism. In the portal, where a 'Link für die erste Phase' is requested, you literally enter 'USB-Stick' and then POST a USB stick containing: (1) the exposé of the project idea — 'Kurzes (Selfie-)Vorstellungsvideo zum Vorhaben (max. 2 Minuten)', a written account of 'max. 3 Seiten', and any early media sketches; (2) 'Eine Auswahl deiner bisherigen Arbeiten (max. 7)' — up to SEVEN previous works showing the full breadth of his output, each described in 'max. 1/2 Seite pro Arbeit', stating the year of creation, the idea/concept behind it, how it was realised, and the team involved if any. Separately uploaded via the portal's upload button: motivation letter, certificates, Zulassungsantrag, payment confirmation.
audition: No on-site entrance examination — 'Es gibt keine Aufnahmeprüfung in Präsenz.' Shortlisted applicants get 'ein kurzes Gespräch per Videochat (ca. 15 Minuten)'. Note: separately, applicants without a German Abitur may face a Begabtenprüfung (a two-hour handwritten essay in German plus a 10–15 minute oral exam in German) — that route is described for applicants lacking a higher-education entrance qualification, so it should not apply to a completed BSc, but confirm.
deadline: 1 March to 1 April, a standing annual window for the winter-semester intake — confirmed both on the programme page ('Vom 1. März bis 1. April reichst du deine Bewerbung über das Bewerbungsportal ein') and on the school's general Bewerbung page ('01.03. bis 01.04. für das Wintersemester'). The programme itself launches in October 2026; for an October 2027 start the window should be 1 March – 1 April 2027 — confirm when the portal opens (today is July 2026).
opens: 1 March (the school's standing application window for the winter semester is 01.03.–01.04.; for the summer semester 01.10.–01.11., but this programme has a winter start only).
duration: 4 semesters (Regelstudienzeit), part-time at 50% workload / 60 ECTS total (15 ECTS per semester) — CONFIRMED in the page's 'Facts' box. Max 10 on-site days per semester; supervision otherwise mainly remote.
study: CONFIRMED on the official page: 'Development of audio experiences at the intersections of music, sound, language, technology, design, user experience and design research.' Semesters 1–2 centre on the applicant's own project, supported by design-research seminars, individual supervision (mostly remote) and up to four subject-specific workshops per semester with external experts, plus one smaller interdisciplinary project with students from the other part-time masters. From semester 3 the master's project takes over (it may but need not build on the first-year work). The page is unusually blunt about what this is not: 'This is not music production. Bei Audio Experience Design gestaltest du Klang als Erfahrung, nicht nur Tracks.' and, as a tagline, 'Stop producing. Start designing. Sound ist Material. Sound ist UX'. New programme, first intake October 2026, up to 10 students per year.
recommendation: The entry process is the friendliest anywhere in this batch — computer science named as a welcome background, no on-site exam, a 15-minute video interview, up to seven free-form works, and a German requirement he can defer to his second year. But almost everything after entry works against him. The school itself says 'This is not music production' and 'Stop producing. Start designing' — the deliverable is audio UX and design research, not tracks. It is 50% part-time and only 60 ECTS, which is a serious problem for a Tunisian national: German study visas and residence permits are premised on full-time study, so the part-time structure puts the whole immigration basis in doubt and should be checked with the German embassy before anything else. As a non-EU student he pays €1,500 per semester (about €6,554 all-in over two years) with no institutional funding and DAAD effectively off the table. And Trossingen is a village in rural Baden-Württemberg, roughly the opposite of a DJ's environment. Pursue only if he genuinely wants to become a sound designer for interfaces, installations and spatial experiences — and only after the visa question is answered.

institution: Moholy-Nagy Művészeti Egyetem (MOME) / Moholy-Nagy University of Art and Design
programme: Sound Design — szakirányú továbbképzés (postgraduate specialist training). WARNING: THIS IS NOT A MASTER'S DEGREE.
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's, but taught in Hungarian — language is the real gate
qualification: NOT A MASTER'S DEGREE — CONFIRMED. The award is a szakirányú továbbképzés (postgraduate specialist training) qualification. It requires a prior degree to enter and does issue an oklevél, but it does NOT confer a mesterfokozat (second-cycle master's degree) and sits outside the Bologna second cycle. WATCH THE MARKETING: Hungarian press coverage launched it as 'Magyarország első diplomát adó Sound Design képzése' — Hungary's first degree-granting sound design programme. In Hungarian usage 'diploma' here means the specialist-training oklevél, NOT a master's degree. Anyone reading that headline in translation will be misled. A two-semester szakirányú továbbképzés is typically 60 credits, half a master's volume.
accreditation: A genuine accredited Hungarian szakirányú továbbképzés at a state-recognised university — not a scam. But categorically outside the Bologna second cycle. It is marketed in English under a menu called 'Programmes' alongside genuine MA courses, which is exactly how a careful applicant gets caught.
tuition: The SAME 790,000 HUF per semester. MOME publishes a single self-funded rate for this course with no separate international tier, so his rate as a Tunisian national is 1,580,000 HUF total. This does not make it accessible — the barriers are language, format and immigration status, not price.
otherFees: A non-refundable special procedure fee of 5,000 HUF per application; non-payment excludes the applicant from the admission procedure entirely. NEW WARNING — A SECOND, SEPARATE TRAP AT THE SAME UNIVERSITY: MOME Open (open.mome.hu/sound-design) sells a DIFFERENT and much weaker 'Sound Design' short course at 450,000 HUF + 27% VAT = 571,500 HUF gross. It consists of 10 theory sessions (Mon/Wed 17:00-20:30), 4 practical workshops and 6 weeks of personalised practice, entry requires only a secondary school diploma plus basic solfège and basic DAW skills, and it is NOT a szakirányú továbbképzés and NOT accredited higher education at all. Its lower price and lower entry bar make it look like an easier way in. It is not — it is a paid short course with no qualification value and no immigration value whatsoever. He must not confuse the two.
totalCost: 1,580,000 HUF tuition plus 5,000 HUF application fee, plus Budapest living costs, plus whatever it costs to reach functional Hungarian — with no degree and no residence permit at the end of it. Not a viable expenditure.
scholarshipDetail: NONE for this course. Stipendium Hungaricum does NOT fund it. Tunisia IS an eligible Stipendium Hungaricum sending partner — the Tunisian Republic is named in the official 2026/27 Call with the Ministère de l'Enseignement Supérieur as sending partner, deadline 15 January, covering a monthly stipend, an accommodation contribution, a tuition waiver and medical insurance — but the Call restricts postgraduate specialist training and partial study to particular frameworks, and applicants may apply only in the study fields fixed in the Hungary-Tunisia bilateral educational cooperation programme. A Hungarian-taught, part-time, non-degree evening course is not a realistic Stipendium Hungaricum target. Check the Tunisia entry at stipendiumhungaricum.hu/partners/ for the exact agreed fields, since that route may still be worth pursuing for a genuine MA elsewhere in Hungary.
entry: Formally: a completed bachelor's, master's, or university/college-level degree ('Alap- vagy mesterfokozat, illetve egyetemi vagy főiskolai szintű végzettség'), so his BSc satisfies the paper condition. SUBSTANTIVELY he is excluded: applicants must already be familiar with at least one DAW at working level (Pro Tools and Ableton are the taught tools), must already have sound-design and music-theory fundamentals, and must supply a professional portfolio. The programme is explicitly aimed at people already working in sound, media, filmmaking, game development or creative fields, plus career-changers who already hold visual/media arts or design qualifications.
acceptsNonMusic: Formally yes, substantively no. Any bachelor's satisfies the paper condition and no music degree is named, so his BSc technically qualifies. But he must already possess sound-design and music-theory fundamentals, already work fluently in a DAW, and already hold a professional showreel or body of musical work. This is a specialisation course for practising professionals, not an entry route.
portfolio: MANDATORY. Required uploads: motivation letter (max 1 A4 page), CV, a PROFESSIONAL PORTFOLIO of existing work — explicitly a showreel or previous musical works, maximum 100 MB — and a scanned degree certificate. He has no portfolio and could not submit an application today. Unlike UNATC ITPMA and UBB Digital Interactive Arts, there is NO essay or proposed-project alternative.
audition: Three stages: (1) online application form; (2) document upload; (3) admission interview in Hungarian. For the 2026 intake interviews were held 3-4 September 2026, with only the strongest applicants invited on the strength of motivation letters and portfolios. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates.
deadline: 24 August 2026 for the 2026 intake. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
opens: Application form deadline 24 August 2026; document upload deadline 27 August 2026; interviews 3-4 September 2026 (2026 intake). PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates.
duration: 1 year / 2 semesters, delivered as an EVENING course (esti) — CONFIRMED by both MOME's own English page and independent Hungarian press, which describe flexible weekly contact hours specifically so the course can be completed alongside employment. Credit total not published — UNVERIFIED, but a two-semester szakirányú továbbképzés is normally 60 credits. Part-time evening delivery is by itself disqualifying for a Hungarian study residence permit.
languageReq: Hungarian. No formal certificate level is published — UNVERIFIED — but the motivation letter, CV and admission interview are conducted in Hungarian, so functional Hungarian is required in practice. IELTS and TOEFL are irrelevant and will not help him.
study: CONFIRMED. Three core areas: film sound, video game sound design, and spatial sound composition, taught through practical projects so participants build a portfolio during the course. Combines industry-standard software training with theoretical grounding in art history, positioning graduates as 'applied artists'. Led by sound artist Krasz Ádám (director of MOME TechPark) and Hajnóczy Csaba DLA. Instruction covers Pro Tools and Ableton.
recommendation: CONFIRMED IN FULL — DO NOT PURSUE. I re-verified every load-bearing fact and the previous assessment holds without correction: szakirányú továbbképzés not a master's, Hungarian-only, evening/part-time, 790,000 HUF per semester, professional portfolio and working DAW skills required on entry. AVOID is the right verdict, and the reason matters: MOME charges 1,580,000 HUF — genuine master's money in this region, more than a year at UNATC's English-taught MAs — for something that is NOT an accredited second-cycle degree and will NOT support a student residence permit. That is the exact pattern the brief asks to be called out. It will surface prominently in any search he runs: marketed in English, on a well-known university's site, under a menu called 'Programmes', launched with press coverage calling it 'Hungary's first degree-granting sound design programme', covering precisely his interests with genuinely excellent spatial-audio facilities. It fails on four independent grounds, any one of which ends it: not a master's; taught wholly in Hungarian with a Hungarian interview; part-time evening delivery that blocks the visa; and an existing professional showreel plus working Pro Tools and Ableton skills he does not have and cannot fake. ONE NEW WARNING I ADD: MOME Open separately sells a cheaper 571,500 HUF 'Sound Design' short course requiring only a secondary school diploma. It is not accredited higher education at all and is an even worse trap precisely because it looks easier to get into. He should engage with MOME only for its full MA programmes, where Stipendium Hungaricum money is genuinely available to Tunisian nationals — noting that MOME's Média design MA is not offered in English, and Budapest Metropolitan University's Media Design MA states plainly 'We do not offer this course in English'. Hungary is largely closed to him for audio at master's level; Romania, via UNATC's English-taught MAs, is not.

Classified by CPM as 'Pre-Accademico', a foundation course positioned BELOW first-degree level and designed to prepare students for entry into the academic diploma programmes.
