accreditation: NOT OFFICIAL for this course. CPM's MUR/AFAM authorisation covers its Diplomi Accademici di I and II livello. A pre-accademico course falls outside that authorisation and confers no MUR-recognised title, no ECTS, and nothing usable for EHEA recognition or PhD progression. The institution is accredited; this particular course is not covered by that accreditation. That distinction is the whole point of this entry.
tuition: €4,492 to €5,839 for the single year, depending on ISEE band.
otherFees: CONFIRMED: annual registration fee €300, additional to tuition. The €190 regional 'diritto allo studio' tax is levied on academic-diploma students; whether it applies to a pre-accademico enrolment is not stated (Partial) — assume it may.
totalCost: €4,792 to €6,139 for the year (tuition plus the €300 registration fee), possibly plus €190 regional tax. That is genuinely cheap — roughly a quarter of one year at NABA. But add Milan living costs of €10,000–14,000, which he would be paying with no scholarship access and no clear visa basis, for a certificate worth nothing on paper.
scholarshipDetail: NONE AVAILABLE FOR THIS COURSE IN PRACTICE. The Lombardy DSU regional scholarship that CPM's students can access requires enrolment in a Diploma Accademico di I or II livello — a pre-accademico enrolment does not qualify. So the cheapest course in the batch is also the one with no funding attached.
entry: CONFIRMED: no prior degree required (it is a foundation course), and explicitly NO prior musical training required — but an audition must be passed, and Italian B2 must be evidenced by certificate or by CPM's online test.
acceptsNonMusic: YES BY DESIGN, AND EXPLICITLY SO — CONFIRMED: 'no prior musical training required'. That is precisely why it is not a master, and precisely why it is the only CPM course he could actually get into.
portfolio: No portfolio requirement published. Entry is by audition plus the Italian language check.
audition: CONFIRMED: an audition is required, but with the explicit caveat that no prior musical training is expected. This is a placement and motivation assessment rather than a competence bar — unlike the Composizione biennio audition.
deadline: Not published for this course specifically. CPM's academic enrolment deadline for the 2026/27 cycle was 15 September 2026. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
opens: Not separately published for this course; CPM's enrolment window opens in February for the following academic year. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for 2027/28.
duration: 1 academic year (October 2026 – July 2027), 295 total contact hours. CONFIRMED. NO ECTS/CFA — it is outside the credit system.
englishTest: NOT APPLICABLE — no English requirement, IELTS is irrelevant. Italian B2 is the gate.
study: CONFIRMED AND NOTABLY WELL-MATCHED TO HIS GOAL: sound design, beatmaking, Ableton Live, music theory, synthesis, hardware synthesizers, acoustics, and workshops in DJing and music production across electronic genres including trap, hip-hop and EDM. This is, in content terms, exactly the craft training he is looking for.
recommendation: THE CONTENT HE WANTS, WITHOUT ANY OF THE PROTECTIONS HE NEEDS. Verification changed the picture here but not the answer. The syllabus is a bullseye — sound design, beatmaking, Ableton, synthesis, DJing, trap/hip-hop/EDM — it explicitly requires no prior musical training, and at €4,792–€6,139 all-in it is by far the cheapest thing in this batch. Under different circumstances this would be a sensible year. But three facts kill it for a September 2027 relocation: it is pre-accademico, so it confers no degree, no credits and nothing transferable; it is outside CPM's AFAM authorisation, so it almost certainly cannot carry a student visa and CPM offers no guidance either way; and pre-accademico enrolment disqualifies him from the Lombardy DSU scholarship. It also still demands Italian at B2. Keep it on file as a preparation year IF he ever becomes legally resident in Italy by another route. As a plan for 2027, skip it.

institution: Conservatorio Statale di Musica "Giuseppe Verdi" di Torino
programme: DCSL34 — Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello in Musica Elettronica (Biennio)
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's, but taught in Italian — language is the real gate
qualification: Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello in Musica Elettronica. A real state second-cycle degree: under Italian law the biennio di II livello is equated to a Laurea Magistrale for public competitions and further study, at EQF level 7. Not a private certificate.
accreditation: State-accredited. DCSL34 is a ministerial course code in the MUR AFAM register. Fully recognised across the EHEA.
tuition: €3,500 PER YEAR — THE RATE HE WOULD PAY, CONFIRMED on the official fee page as the contributo onnicomprensivo annuale for extra-UE students not resident in Italy. Over two years: €7,000. It follows the same three-instalment schedule with €156 due first. This flat rate appears to be charged instead of the ISEE-scaled system that applies to EU and Italy-resident students — the official page presents ISEE certification as governing the third instalment for the ordinary regime while stating a single figure for extra-UE non-residents. Whether an ISEE parificato can nonetheless reduce it is UNVERIFIED and worth one email, because a yes would save €5,000 over two years. Torino remains the most expensive Italian conservatoire in this sweep and the one where the low-income route is least clearly available.
otherFees: €156.00 first instalment comprising tassa regionale EDISU Piemonte plus marca da bollo, stated as excluded from the contributo figure. Immatricolazione and frequenza charges are likewise stated as excluded — amounts UNVERIFIED, ask the segreteria. Late-payment surcharge €60.00. Diploma issue fee at graduation UNVERIFIED.
totalCost: Approximately €7,000 tuition over two years, plus roughly €312 in EDISU and bollo, plus Turin living costs of roughly €800–1,100/month — Turin is among the cheaper large Italian cities. Two-year all-in approximately €27,000–34,000 before any scholarship. An EDISU Piemonte award would cut this substantially.
scholarshipDetail: EDISU Piemonte, the regional right-to-study agency, runs income-based borse di studio that non-EU students can win, covering fees, a maintenance grant and subsidised housing — the realistic route to something approaching full funding in Italy. A typical Tunisian family income should place him in the lowest bracket. The bando normally opens in the summer preceding the academic year. EDISU eligibility requires an ISEE parificato in practice; budget time and money for obtaining one via a CAF or Patronato. MAECI Italian Government scholarships are the other national route. No programme-specific scholarship is advertised.
entry: CONFIRMED VERBATIM, and this is the decisive good news. Candidates must hold EITHER 'Diploma di Conservatorio (sia di ordinamento tradizionale che di nuovo ordinamento)' OR 'Diploma di laurea (triennale o quinquennale) o di titolo conseguito all'estero riconosciuto idoneo'. A foreign three-year university degree explicitly qualifies. His BSc in Software Engineering meets the formal entry requirement outright. What he must then survive is the entrance examination, not a paper gate.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — CONFIRMED, and more strongly than previously recorded. The published entry requirement accepts a foreign three-year degree outright. The conservatoire has built three separate bridges for non-electronic-music graduates: the portfolio explicitly admits technical-scientific work as an alternative to compositions, the technical knowledge test is expressly non-condizionante, and the composition practical is sample-based and applies only to candidates without prior electronic-music composition training. This is the most genuinely open door to a non-music engineering graduate in the entire six-programme set.
portfolio: MAJOR CORRECTION, AND THE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING OF THIS ENTIRE RE-CHECK. The official page does not ask for a 'portfolio compositivo' as previously recorded. It asks for 'un portfolio di composizioni E/O lavori di carattere tecnico-scientifico' — a portfolio of compositions AND/OR WORKS OF A TECHNICAL-SCIENTIFIC CHARACTER. Technical and scientific work is an accepted alternative to composition, not a supplement to it. That single conjunction transforms this programme for a software engineer with no music degree: an audio DSP library, a spatialisation engine, a synthesis tool, a machine-listening project or a published technical write-up can carry the portfolio. Uploaded by Dropbox at least one week before the practical exams. The previous instruction to build 'original electroacoustic works, not DJ mixes' was directionally right about DJ mixes but wrong to exclude the technical route, which is where his actual advantage lies.
audition: Six-part entrance examination, CONFIRMED: (1) presentation of a portfolio — mandatory, uploaded via Dropbox at least one week before the practical exams; (2) practical analysis of electroacoustic repertoire using DAW software and headphones, with analysis tools such as Acousmographe permitted; (3) a test of knowledge in mathematics, informatics, music informatics and electroacoustics, including programming in Max, PureData, Csound or SuperCollider — explicitly 'NON CONDIZIONANTE' (non-binding), so it informs placement rather than gating entry; (4) a motivational interview covering general knowledge of electronic music; (5) a practical composition test, 'SOLO PER I CANDIDATI CHE NON PROVENGONO DA CORSI DI MUSICA ELETTRONICA A INDIRIZZO COMPOSITIVO', consisting of building a short electroacoustic piece from assigned samples — this WOULD apply to him; (6) the Italian language test, only for foreign-nationality candidates. Nothing here assumes conservatoire performance ability.
deadline: UNVERIFIED. Note the confirmed 20 May – 10 June enrolment instalment window in the fee schedule (PRIOR CYCLE), which implies the admission cycle concludes considerably earlier than a September exam date would suggest. Treat spring 2027 as the real operational deadline.
opens: UNVERIFIED on the pages read. Italian conservatoire ammissioni bandi are typically published in spring and close in summer. For a 2027/28 start, watch conservatoriotorino.eu from about March 2027. Non-EU applicants must ALSO complete Universitaly pre-enrolment on the Ministry's separate and earlier calendar — this is the step that most often derails non-EU applicants and it cannot be recovered if missed.
duration: 2 years, 120 CFA (60 per year) — the ministerial standard for a biennio di II livello. The course page links a Piano di studi PDF rather than stating the total inline, so the inline figure remains UNVERIFIED, but the standard is not in doubt.
languageReq: An Italian language test forms part of the entrance examination, applied only to candidates of foreign nationality. The required level is not stated on the course page (details are on a separate conservatoire page); Italian conservatoires normally demand B2. Exact level UNVERIFIED — ask the segreteria. Budget the portfolio year for Italian to B2; his French makes this the fastest language acquisition available to him in this whole sweep.
englishTest: None. English is not the medium of instruction.
study: Electroacoustic repertoire and its analysis, electronic and electroacoustic composition, music informatics, electroacoustics, and programming for music. The admission test itself names Max, PureData, Csound and SuperCollider, which tells you where the technical centre of gravity sits. Detailed module list is in the linked Piano di studi PDF — UNVERIFIED in detail.
recommendation: APPLY — and this now rates higher than in the previous sweep because of one verified phrase. The portfolio requirement is 'un portfolio di composizioni e/o lavori di carattere tecnico-scientifico': technical-scientific work is an accepted alternative, not a supplement. That means his software-engineering output — a DSP library, a synthesis or spatialisation tool, a machine-listening project, a game-audio engine — can carry the single most important element of the application, alongside original electronic pieces rather than instead of a music degree he does not have. Combined with an entry requirement that explicitly accepts a foreign triennale, a non-binding technical test, and a sample-based composition task aimed precisely at candidates like him, this is the clearest path in the set. Three actions in the portfolio year: (1) Italian to a tested B2, fastest of any language option available to him; (2) build a dual portfolio — three or four original electroacoustic pieces PLUS two documented technical-scientific audio projects, and get fluent in Max or SuperCollider since the technical test names them; (3) map the Universitaly pre-enrolment calendar in autumn 2026 and verify the non-EU contingent for Musica Elettronica, because a tiny quota can close an otherwise open programme. The cost is the real caveat: €3,500/year for extra-UE non-residents is the highest Italian figure in this sweep and the flat rate appears not to be ISEE-reducible. Ask the segreteria whether an ISEE parificato changes it, and apply to EDISU Piemonte in the same cycle. Note honestly that this is an electroacoustic composition and music-informatics degree, not a route to commercial dance-music production — it would make him an excellent audio programmer and sound designer, and a technically formidable producer, but the DJ career would be built alongside it, not by it.

Practical advantages over Como: portfolio submitted as LINKS rather than physical CD/DVD/USB, and no age limits. Practical disadvantages: the non-music eligibility is not stated as explicitly, the exam includes an embedded Italian-language check, and neither deadlines nor fees are published. Same core requirement as Como — Italian. Pair the two Italian options in one enquiry campaign.

entry: A "diploma accademico di primo livello, o di un diploma universitario di laurea o di laurea breve, o di un diploma musicale di previgente ordinamento congiunto ad un diploma di scuola secondaria superiore", or equivalent foreign credentials recognised as suitable (recognition per EU norms and applicable international agreements). Plus Italian at B2 CEFR or above, attested by a test.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — the strongest structural acceptance in this slice. A "diploma universitario di laurea" (any university degree) is listed as a qualifying credential alongside a first-level conservatory diploma, and the biennio in Musica elettronica is explicitly exempted from musical-competency verification. The CV requirement even asks specifically about the candidate's "technical-scientific" background. A Tunisian BSc requires the standard foreign-credential recognition step. The real gate is not music — it is ITALIAN AT B2.
portfolio: "Prova specifica di selezione" with three components: (1) a WRITTEN CURRICULUM detailing prior education with particular reference to musical, cultural and technical-scientific fields; (2) PORTFOLIO of previously realised works in audio-musical and/or multimedia production, submitted on physical media (CD, DVD or USB key); (3) an approximately 15-MINUTE INTERVIEW assessing motivation, technical knowledge and expectations. Number of works and durations are not specified. Examination modalities also allow oral interviews by VIDEOCONFERENCE, submission of audio-video recordings, and submission of written work such as a composition.
audition: NO MUSICAL-COMPETENCY VERIFICATION. Quoted verbatim: "I candidati all'ammissione ai Bienni di: Canto, Composizione, Didattica della musica, Direzione di coro, Musica elettronica non devono svolgere alcuna verifica delle competenze musicali" — candidates for the Electronic Music biennio do NOT have to undergo any verification of musical competencies. Only the subject-specific selection test (CV + portfolio + ~15 min interview) applies, and the interview can be held by videoconference.
deadline: UNVERIFIED on the pages read. Italian conservatories usually publish a summer session (roughly May–July) and sometimes an autumn session for the following academic year. PRIOR CYCLE / NOT PUBLISHED - contact the segreteria (+39 031 279827) and watch the A.A. 2027/28 notice.
opens: UNVERIFIED — see the Conservatorio's "Ammissione al Conservatorio A.A. 2026/27" notice; Italian conservatories typically open in spring with summer and sometimes autumn sessions.
duration: 2 years (biennio) / 120 CFA (60 per year)
languageReq: Italian (level UNVERIFIED for Como; B2 is the common AFAM requirement for non-EU applicants).
study: YEAR 1 (60 CFA): Electroacoustic Musical Composition 22 CFA (INDIVIDUAL lessons); Musical Informatics 1, 4 CFA; Music, Media and Technologies 21 CFA (individual); History of Musical Forms and Repertoires 6 CFA; Foreign Language 2 CFA; electives 5 CFA. YEAR 2 (60 CFA): Audiovisual Integrated Composition 15 CFA; Multimodal and Interactive Performance Environments 12 CFA; Musical Informatics 2, 4 CFA; Audiovisual Communication Theories 9 CFA; Audio Programming for Internet/Mobile Systems 3 CFA; electives 8 CFA; final examination 9 CFA. Note 43 of the 60 first-year credits are one-to-one tuition — an unusually high individual-teaching ratio. Declared career outcomes include electroacoustic composer, AUDIO ENGINEER AND STUDIO DESIGNER, sound designer for objects and architectural spaces, and audio technician for broadcasting and digital media.
recommendation: On pure admissibility this is the single most open door found anywhere in this slice: any university degree qualifies, there is NO musical-competency verification for the Musica elettronica biennio, the selection is a CV plus a portfolio on a USB stick plus a 15-minute interview that can be done by videoconference, and Italian state fees are low. The curriculum is also genuinely practical, with 43 of 60 first-year credits as one-to-one tuition and stated outcomes including audio engineer and studio designer. The one non-negotiable obstacle is ITALIAN AT B2 CEFR with a test — that is his decision point. His fluent French makes Italian B2 in 12 months realistic in a way German would not be. Strongly recommend he investigates this route and the Italian regional DSU grants.

qualification: CONFIRMED NOT A DEGREE. Page labels it 'Diploma ETIC / Outra Formação Profissional (OFP)' with 'Certificação Nacional' via ETIC's DGERT certification as a training entity. It is NOT a mestrado, NOT a pós-graduação, carries NO ECTS and confers no academic grau.
accreditation: NOT OFFICIAL HIGHER EDUCATION — but honestly labelled. Accrediting body is DGERT (Direção-Geral do Emprego e das Relações de Trabalho), which certifies ETIC as a VOCATIONAL TRAINING ENTITY. DGERT is NOT A3ES and NOT DGES. A3ES/DGES accredit degrees (licenciatura, mestrado, doutoramento); DGERT certifies professional training providers. In practice: he receives a nationally-recognised vocational training certificate that has real standing in the Portuguese labour market but ZERO academic standing — it cannot be used for PhD entry, cannot be recognised as a degree in Tunisia or the EHEA, and carries no ECTS transferable to any master's. Credit to ETIC: it does not dress this up as a master's.

recommendation: NOT A MASTER'S — DO NOT CONFUSE THIS WITH ONE, AND IT CANNOT GET HIM A RESIDENCE VISA. The course fee is honest and fully published, the kit is excellent for €2,125, and it is pitched exactly at his current level: no audio background needed, online interview possible, 12th-grade minimum against his BSc. Its real use to him is PORTFOLIO FUEL, not a destination — the thing he is missing for any accredited programme is demonstrable sound work, and 170 hours of hands-on Pro Tools, microphone technique and mixing would produce it. Three things kill it as a plan: (1) it confers no degree and no ECTS, so it advances neither his academic position nor a later master's application; (2) at best it supports a temporary E9 stay visa, not a residence permit, and ETIC publishes nothing about sponsoring even that; (3) it is taught entirely in PORTUGUESE, which he does not speak — this alone is disqualifying today and is a bigger barrier than the money. Add €5,000+ of Lisbon living costs and the arithmetic fails for a budget-sensitive candidate. Verdict: skip unless he is already in Portugal for another reason and speaks Portuguese.

Of everything ETIC offers, this syllabus lands closest to what he says he wants — songwriting, DAW workflow, MIDI, recording, and a finished original track as the deliverable, which is exactly the artefact any accredited programme's portfolio round will ask for. It also has the lowest entry bar in the specialisation-free tier: no DAW, theory or audio prerequisites, an online interview, and a 12th-grade minimum his BSc clears easily. But it is a vocational certificate with no degree, no ECTS and no academic standing; it cannot support a residence visa (E9 temporary stay at best, and even that is not documented by ETIC); and it is delivered entirely in PORTUGUESE, which he does not speak — that is the hard blocker, not the price. Paying €5,000+ in Lisbon living costs on top of €2,300 to attend a non-degree, non-visa course would consume a large share of his budget while advancing neither his qualification nor his immigration position. Treat it as a useful BENCHMARK for what portfolio-building costs (~€2,100 for 170 supervised hours) and look for the equivalent in Tunisia or online first.

entry: Completion of 'o specializare cu 180 credite sau 240 credite' — a study programme worth 180 or 240 credits, with NO field of study specified. A three-year Tunisian licence in software engineering (180 ECTS) satisfies this. HARD CONSTRAINT FOR HIM: UNATC's own admission pages state that foreign citizens must complete 'anul pregătitor de limba română' — the Romanian language preparatory year — BEFORE sitting the admission exams. Exemptions apply only to candidates who present Romanian educational credentials, prove at least four consecutive years of study in Romanian, or hold a minimum B1 certificate from an accredited Romanian institution or cultural organisation. Registration is exclusively via the 2BitsEDU online platform. Places: 3 state-funded (buget) + 3 tuition-based (taxă) for the 2026 cycle.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — unambiguously. Published eligibility is purely credit-based: 'absolvit o specializare cu 180 credite sau 240 credite', with no discipline named. There is no music-degree requirement, no theory exam, and no audition. The written exam tests film culture and sound-design technical knowledge, both of which are learnable from a bibliography. This is the most open eligibility rule in the slice.
portfolio: CONFIRMED verbatim. The dossier must contain a CV in EuroPass format and 'un portofoliu ce va conține lucrări artistice cu design sonor realizat de către candidat' (a portfolio containing artistic works with sound design created by the candidate), which may include digital copies of films or relevant sound-design projects. In addition the candidate must bring to the oral exam the DAW PROJECT FILE for one portfolio work of their own choosing, in ProTools, Nuendo, Reaper, Adobe Audition, Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve. No minimum or maximum number of works and no duration requirement is published. Portfolios are uploaded electronically through the 2BitsEDU / Edubits candidate platform after registration.
audition: On-site, one evaluation stage in two parts. Proba 1 (written): film-culture exam based on a set bibliography, plus technical knowledge of sound design. Proba 2 (oral/colloquium): presentation and discussion of one self-selected portfolio work, with a live DAW project demonstration. Each part scored 1-10; tiebreaker is Proba 2 then Proba 1. Minimum passing grade 6.0/10. No live musical performance.
deadline: CURRENT CYCLE (September 2026 entry) — NOT his target, and currently OPEN. 2026 cycle: registration 4 August - 9 September 2026; file verification 10-11 September 2026; exam period 15-20 September 2026. The 2027 calendar is NOT YET PUBLISHED — expect the same August-to-September 2027 pattern. Note a separate, earlier May-to-July pre-registration window applies to the English-taught masters (for 2026: 1 May - 1 July 2026), which does not cover this programme.

duration: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 credits — confirmed on the official admission page.
study: Year 1: Sound Design; Sound Capture and Editing; Foley Art; Research and Creative Cinematography Workshop; Internship and Practice. Year 2: Advanced Sound Design; Film Sound Production/Post-production; Multichannel Mixing; Research and Creative Cinematography Workshop; Internship and Practice; Dissertation. Master's students concentrate on recording and processing sound for film, games and virtual reality, working on real fiction, documentary and animation productions in collaboration with the directing, cinematography and editing departments. The admission page names the DAWs in scope: ProTools, Nuendo, Reaper, Adobe Audition, Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve.
recommendation: The most open door in the slice on paper — eligibility is purely 180 or 240 credits with no subject restriction, there is no music-theory exam and no audition, and the oral exam rewards demonstrable DAW craft over conservatory training. A government scholarship route exists that covers tuition and a free Romanian language year. Two things keep it off the top spot. First, timing: as a non-EU citizen he must complete the Romanian preparatory year BEFORE he can sit the admission exams, so a September 2027 target realistically means starting the prep year in 2027 and entering the master in 2028 — unless he obtains a B1 Romanian certificate independently. Second, direction: this is film, game and VR sound with Foley and picture-locked mixing, not club music production or DJing. It would make him an excellent sound designer with a bankable post-production skill, but it does not advance the DJ half of his ambition, and he currently has no sound-design-to-picture work to put in the portfolio.

For a software engineer this is the most accessible second-cycle art-academy programme in the Serbian sector on paper, and his coding background is a direct asset rather than a handicap. The trade-off is that it is a game-design degree with an audio ceiling of 12 of 60 ECTS.

study: CONFIRMED verbatim from the official accredited curriculum table 5.1b. Compulsory: MA701 Žanrovska analiza i sinteza video igara (2+4, 12 ECTS); MA703 Studije video igara (2+0, 4 ECTS); MP2102 Grafičke komunikacije u interaktivnim medijima (2+1, 6 ECTS); MA7002 Imerzivne igre / Immersive Games (2+2, 6 ECTS); MAZRD Završni rad (12 ECTS); MAZRI Završni rad – istraživanje (12 ECTS). Electives MAIZ1, 12 ECTS chosen from — and this is where all the audio content lives: MSMIM Muzika u medijima (6); MA1002 Audiovizuelna artikulacija (6); MA1003 Zvuk u filmskoj umetnosti (6); MA2002 Postprodukcija filmske slike (6); MA4003 Produkcija muzike za nove medije (6); MLVIA Video art (6). Hard ceiling: at most 12 of the 60 ECTS can be audio, and only two of those courses (Muzika u medijima, Produkcija muzike za nove medije) are music-production-adjacent.
recommendation: Everything the previous record said about this programme checks out against the official documents, and the accreditation is now pinned down precisely (NAT register, accredited 05.11.2024, intake 10). It remains the only programme in the Novi Sad sweep whose published entry rule admits ANY four-year bachelor with no artistic-field restriction, and his software-engineering background is directly relevant to the curriculum. But it should not be presented to him as a music option in disguise. Audio is capped at 12 of 60 ECTS and only two of those six electives are production-adjacent; the other 48 ECTS are genre analysis, game studies, graphic communications in interactive media, immersive games and a game-design thesis. It will not make him a DJ or a record producer, and spending 2027–28 on it would be a career pivot, not a step toward his stated goal. It also does not solve the two gates that actually block him: the 240-ECTS / four-year first-degree rule applies identically here, and the Serbian-language requirement plus a Serbian-language entrance exam apply identically here. On top of that it demands a video-game-design portfolio he has even less basis to build than an audio one. Report it accurately as what it is: a cheap, accredited, unusually open Serbian master in the wrong subject. It only becomes interesting if he decides he wants to work in games audio and is prepared to learn Serbian.

duration: 60 ECTS over one academic year, structured in three cuatrimestres: September–December, January–April, May–July. Class timetable, verified: Fridays 16:30–20:30 and Saturdays 09:30–13:30 plus 15:30–19:30 — 12 contact hours per week, weekends only.

study: VERIFIED module structure and credit weights from the official brochure: I. Herramientas de trabajo para la producción musical (13.2 ECTS); II. Fundamentos de la Producción Musical (11.2 ECTS); III. Producción Musical Profesional (9.6 ECTS); IV. Trabajo Final de Máster (16 ECTS); V. Prácticas en empresa (10 ECTS). Total 60 ECTS. Note the shape: only 34 ECTS is taught content — 26 ECTS, well over a third, is final project plus work placement. Stated career outcomes: productor musical, técnico especialista en mezcla, técnico de mastering, técnico asistente en estudio de grabación. Graduates receive official Steinberg Cubase professional certification, and a Cubase licence is included in the materials.
recommendation: On paper the best value in this slice by an enormous margin — EUR 4,194.12 all-in, verified to the cent, for a 60-ECTS university-branded music production master with Sony Music España involvement, named Spanish electronic producers teaching, an included Cubase licence and Steinberg certification. His software-engineering degree is named explicitly as a welcome entry profile, no portfolio is demanded, no IELTS is needed, foreign degrees are accepted without homologation, and it starts in September, matching his target. If he were already living legally in Spain, this would be the clear recommendation. But he is not, and that is where it breaks. THREE ISSUES, in order of severity. (1) THE VISA. I verified Spain's actual rules rather than assuming: títulos propios ARE admissible for a student authorisation, which is better than feared — but the binding constraint is the teaching load, and UCAM's own brochure publishes a weekend-only timetable of 12 contact hours per week in a semipresencial format. The requirement is 20 hours per week, or at minimum 12 hours that are genuinely in person for concentrated programmes, plus at least 50% in-person delivery overall. This programme sits at or below that floor. On the published evidence it likely does NOT support a student residence permit. (2) LANGUAGE. It is taught entirely in Spanish, including a 16-ECTS final project. (3) THE AWARD is a certificate, not a degree — acceptable for industry, worthless for a future PhD or any title-dependent role. VERDICT: outstanding return on euro, but probably not a relocation route. ACTION: before anything else, email UCAM's international office and ask three specific questions in writing — what percentage of the programme is delivered in person, how many presencial hours per week, and has UCAM successfully supported non-EU students onto a student visa for THIS programme. If the answers are weak, this option is worth nothing to him as a route to Europe, however cheap it is.

tuition: WALLONIA + FRENCH-SPEAKING BRUSSELS (Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles), 2026-2027 — a single decree-set regime, identical at every institution. Droits d'inscription EUR 1,194 (published as 'montant à titre indicatif', subject to change by the Belgian government) PLUS a contribution supplémentaire (the successor to the old droit d'inscription spécifique / DIS) of EUR 4,175 per year = EUR 5,369/yr TOTAL. Legal basis: art. 105 §3bis of the décret du 7 novembre 2013 (décret paysage), as amended by the décret-programme du 11 décembre 2024. Transition: the EUR 4,175 already applies to ALL 2nd-cycle (master) students from 2026-2027, and to 1st-cycle students from 2027-2028 — so a master entrant in September 2027 pays it in full with no transitional relief. Payment schedule (ARTS² and INSAS publish the same shape): EUR 50 deposit by 15 Sept / 31 Oct 2026, balance of droits + the EUR 4,175 by 15 Jan / 1 Feb 2027. PER INSTITUTION: ARTS² Mons EUR 5,369; Conservatoire royal de Liège EUR 5,369; Conservatoire royal de Bruxelles EUR 5,369 (regime-wide figure — CRB's own fee page could not be reached, its published item is only 'La prochaine session des épreuves d'admission sera organisée entre le 23 août et le 9 septembre 2026'; the amount is decree-set and not institution-variable, but treat the CRB line as INSTITUTIONALLY UNVERIFIED); IAD Louvain-la-Neuve EUR 5,369 (published: 'minerval 1194 € par année académique' + '4175 €' payable by 31 January); INSAS Brussels EUR 5,369 (published payment plan: EUR 50 by 31/10/2026, EUR 4,125 balance by 01/02/2027). Means-tested reductions on the MINERVAL only (EUR 835 'condition intermédiaire', EUR 374 'condition modeste', EUR 0 boursier) do not reduce the EUR 4,175. FLANDERS, 2026-2027 — set per institution, and it exploded this year because the Flemish government removed non-EEA students from basic financing, forcing institutions to charge full cost. KASK & Conservatorium Gent (HoGent School of Arts): fixed EUR 916.20 + EUR 131.40 per credit = EUR 8,800.20 for a 60-credit model curriculum. Koninklijk Conservatorium Antwerpen (AP Hogeschool): 'Studiegeld buitenlandse studenten — Diploma- en creditcontracten: vast gedeelte 2500, variabel gedeelte per stp 375' = EUR 25,000 for 60 credits — by far the highest figure found anywhere in this sweep; plus EUR 65 opleidingsgebonden kosten for Muziek. Koninklijk Conservatorium Brussel (Erasmushogeschool Brussel), artistic programmes: fixed EUR 1,181.40 + EUR 272 per credit = EUR 17,501.40 for 60 credits (up from about EUR 9,000, which triggered the 'Requiem for culture' student protest at the Queen Elisabeth Competition in May 2026; EhB decided on 28 April 2026 on a transitional measure that only partly offsets the rise for students ALREADY enrolled — a new 2027 entrant gets nothing from it). LUCA School of Arts (all campuses incl. Sint-Lukas Brussel and Lemmens Leuven), non-EEA enrolling from 2026-2027 onwards: fixed EUR 2,376.72 + EUR 118.62 per credit = EUR 9,823.92 for 60 credits, plus EUR 300 material cost per year. For comparison the Flemish standard (EEA) rate at LUCA in 2026-2027 is EUR 1,511.40.
otherFees: Flanders: LUCA EUR 300/yr materials + EUR 50 application fee; AP EUR 65/yr opleidingsgebonden kosten for Muziek. FWB: production/material costs vary.
totalCost: Cheapest Belgian route for him: any Wallonia-Brussels institution at EUR 5,369/yr. Most expensive: KC Antwerpen at EUR 25,000/yr — roughly 4.7x the Wallonia figure. Since he is French-fluent and Arabic-native with only working English, the cheap option and the linguistically comfortable option are the same one.
scholarshipDetail: EXEMPTION QUESTION, SETTLED. In the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles the countries exempt from the EUR 4,175 contribution supplémentaire are fixed by ARES circulaire n°2026-001 du 12/02/2026 (which abrogates circulaire n°2025-01 du 18 février 2025 and applies from academic year 2026-2027). Its three annexes are: ANNEXE 1 'PAYS LES MOINS AVANCÉS (LEAST DEVELOPED COUNTRIES)' — the UN LDC list, 44 countries: Afghanistan, Angola, Bangladesh, Bénin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cambodge, Comores, Djibouti, Érythrée, Éthiopie, Gambie, Guinée, Guinée-Bissau, Haïti, Kiribati, Laos, Lesotho, Liberia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mali, Mauritanie, Myanmar, Mozambique, Népal, Niger, Ouganda, République centrafricaine, RD Congo, Rwanda, Îles Salomon, Sénégal, Sierra Leone, Somalie, Soudan, Soudan du Sud, Tanzanie, Tchad, Timor oriental, Togo, Tuvalu, Yémen, Zambie. ANNEXE 2 'PAYS CLASSÉS AU BAS DE LA LISTE SUR L'INDICE DE DÉVELOPPEMENT HUMAIN' (ARES CA decision of 14 December 2021), 20 countries: Cameroun, Cap-Vert, Côte d'Ivoire, El Salvador, Ghana, Guatemala, Guinée équatoriale, Honduras, Kenya, Micronésie, Namibie, Nigeria, Pakistan, Palestine, Papouasie-Nouvelle-Guinée, République du Congo-Brazzaville, São Tomé-et-Príncipe, Syrie, Vanuatu, Zimbabwe. ANNEXE 3 'LISTE DE PAYS ADDITIONNELS' (ARES CA decision of 5 November 2024): Liban — one country only. TUNISIA APPEARS ON NONE OF THE THREE ANNEXES. He therefore gets NO exemption and pays the full EUR 5,369. Do not be misled by the fact that Tunisia IS one of the 32 ARES development-cooperation PARTNER COUNTRIES for scholarship purposes (alongside Morocco, Senegal, Vietnam, etc.) — the partner-country list and the fee-exemption annexes are different instruments. Other exemption routes that WOULD work: holding a Wallonie-Bruxelles International scholarship (a WBI bursary exempts him from the contribution supplémentaire as well as funding him — this is the single highest-value application he can make in Belgium); holding a Belgian secondary-education certificate from a French Community school after two years of schooling; enrolling in an AESS/teaching master; or qualifying as 'assimilé' under art. 3 §1 of the décret du 11 avril 2014 (long-term residence, refugee status, employment in Belgium, CPAS support, EU family member, long-term resident of another EU state). CAVEAT: circulaire 2026-001 states 'La présente circulaire est uniquement applicable aux universités' — a parallel instrument governs Hautes Écoles and Écoles supérieures des Arts, but IAD's own fee page confirms the ESA exemption categories are the same (LDC list, ARES list, French Community secondary diploma, 3rd cycle, initial teacher training, WBI bursary), and the statutory exemption in art. 105 §3bis is the UN LDC list, which excludes Tunisia either way. In Flanders, LUCA offers the Master Mind scholarship and EhB/RITCS + KC Brussel launched a crowdfunding campaign to retain international talent; amounts UNVERIFIED.

whyChance: Names engineering or computing as a welcome background, but taught in Italian — language is the real gate
qualification: Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello – AFAM, in Popular Music (Composizione Pop Rock). CONFIRMED on the course page as 'Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello – AFAM'. This is the OFFICIAL Italian second-cycle academic award, equivalent to a laurea magistrale — not a 'Master universitario di I/II livello' (which is the lesser 60-credit post-degree certificate) and not a private certificate. CONFIRMED: CPM has NO second-level diploma in sound engineering or music production; the sound/production tracks sit at triennio or pre-accademico level only.
accreditation: OFFICIAL — MUR-authorised AFAM 'Istituto di Alta Formazione' entitled to award Diplomi Accademici di Primo e Secondo livello in Popular Music. Verified on the course page, which states the award as 'Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello – AFAM'. EHEA-valid, valid for PhD/dottorato entry and for a type-D study visa. This is genuinely official — the accreditation is not the risk here; the language and audition gate is.
tuition: Band 1: €22,004 tuition over the two years. Band 2: €25,312. Band 3: €28,606. Add €300/year registration and €190/year regional tax to all of these.
otherFees: CONFIRMED: registration fee €300 per year; regional 'diritto allo studio' tax €190 per year. Both are additional to tuition. Over two years that is €980 on top of tuition. Materials, equipment and insurance fees not published (Partial).
totalCost: First year, best case (ISEE band 1): €11,242 + €300 + €190 = €11,732. Worst case (band 3, which is what applies if no valid ISEE is produced): €14,615 + €490 = €15,105. Two-year total €22,984 to €29,586 in tuition and fees, plus Milan living costs of roughly €10,000–14,000 per year. THE ISEE TRAP IS REAL: a non-EU applicant who does not go through a CAF to obtain an ISEE parificato using Tunisian income documents will be charged the TOP band by default. A Tunisian household income will usually place him in band 1 once that paperwork is done — a difference of about €6,600 over two years. Do the ISEE parificato.
scholarshipDetail: CONFIRMED ROUTE, AND BETTER THAN IT FIRST APPEARS. Because CPM is an AFAM institution, its Diploma Accademico students are eligible for the LOMBARDY REGIONAL DSU right-to-study scholarship (Legge Regionale Lombardia 33/2004), awarded by competition on combined merit and income criteria, with the amount varying by ISEE band and by the student's geographic origin — out-of-region and international students receive the highest bracket because they are classed as 'fuori sede'. Non-EU students are not excluded from DSU in principle, but they must produce home-country income documentation to obtain an ISEE parificato. CPM does not state non-EU eligibility explicitly (contact borsedistudio@cpm.it). Awards are paid at the end of the academic year, so they do not reduce the up-front cash needed.
entry: Diploma Accademico di Primo Livello, Laurea Triennale, or an equivalent foreign qualification, PLUS an admission examination. CONFIRMED: non-standard entry is permitted, with an obligation to obtain the required first-level diploma by the end of the first year. Italian B2 certificate or a pass in CPM's 90-minute Italian test is mandatory. Foreign-degree documentation (Dichiarazione di Valore / CIMEA) not detailed on the pages read — Partial.
acceptsNonMusic: EFFECTIVELY NO. The formal requirement is any first-level degree 'o titolo estero equivalente', so a BSc in Software Engineering satisfies the paper requirement. But admission is decided by an entrance exam that assesses 'musical competence, technical level and motivation', and the course is explicitly aimed at musicians, authors and producers who already have a compositional language to deepen. Combined with the mandatory Italian B2 test, a candidate with no music training and no Italian cannot realistically be admitted.
portfolio: Not published as a separate portfolio requirement — admission runs through the entrance examination rather than a portfolio submission. The detailed admission-exam programme is published as a downloadable PDF which was not read (Partial).
audition: YES — 'Esame di Ammissione'. CONFIRMED content: the entrance exam assesses musical competence, technical instrumental/compositional level, and motivation, plus the Italian language test (90 minutes, B2) where no certificate is supplied. A candidate with no music training and no Italian would fail both components.
deadline: CONFIRMED for the current cycle: enrolment deadline 15 September 2026, with course start 5 October 2026. Admission-exam sittings are booked individually (an audition date of Saturday 7 February 2026 was advertised for the 2026/27 cycle). PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for 2027/28.
opens: February for the following academic year ('APERTURA ISCRIZIONI febbraio 2026' for the 2026/27 year). PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date; expect February 2027 for a September/October 2027 start.
duration: 2 years full-time (4 years part-time); 869 total contact hours. CONFIRMED on the course page. Credit figure not printed on the page — an AFAM II livello is by law 120 CFA, but the page does not state it (Partial).
englishTest: NOT APPLICABLE — English is irrelevant to admission here. IELTS is not requested. The language requirement is ITALIAN at B2, evidenced by certificate or by CPM's own 90-minute written test. For this candidate that is a harder bar than any IELTS.
study: Year 1: Produzione I, Tradizione e produzione, Contemporary writing, Film scoring, Jazz tradition, Classical style, 'Pop style for Sanremo', Ear Training I, Storia della popular music I, D.E.M.O. labs, 'Ambienti esecutivi live electronics: Ableton Live I', Tecnologie e tecniche della ripresa e registrazione audio, Letteratura e testi per musica, Piano/canto complementare, Legal & Business I, Inglese I. Year 2: Tecniche compositive, four Masterclasses, Ear Training II, Storia della popular music II, D.E.M.O. labs, Videoscrittura ed editoria musicale, Ableton Live II, complementary instrument, Inglese II.
recommendation: REAL DEGREE, REAL SCHOOL, WRONG CANDIDATE. The good news corrects the earlier record: CPM publishes its fees in full (€11,242–€14,615 in year one, plus €490 in registration and regional tax), it is genuinely MUR/AFAM accredited, the award is a full laurea-magistrale-equivalent, and its students can compete for Lombardy DSU scholarships. The bad news is structural and cannot be fixed with money. Admission requires Italian at B2 — evidenced by certificate or a 90-minute written test — and an entrance examination in musical and compositional competence. He has neither, and fourteen months is not enough to acquire both to examination standard alongside building a portfolio. On top of that, this is a COMPOSITION degree; CPM offers no second-level diploma in production or sound engineering at all, so even if he passed he would be studying the wrong subject. Do not apply for September 2027.

institution: Conservatorio di Musica "Giovan Battista Martini" di Bologna
programme: DCSL34 — Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello in Musica Elettronica, indirizzo Sound Design (Biennio)
whyChance: Names engineering or computing as a welcome background, but taught in Italian — language is the real gate
qualification: Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello in Musica elettronica (indirizzo Sound design) — a real state second-cycle degree, EQF 7, legally equated to a Laurea Magistrale for public competitions and doctoral access.
accreditation: State-accredited under ministerial course code DCSL34, in the MUR AFAM register. Genuine EHEA second-cycle qualification.
tuition: THE RATE HE WOULD PAY, carried forward and NOT re-verifiable this pass — treat as high-value but provisional. Bologna's Art. 14 on non-EU international students provides that a non-EU student can access the income-based reduction on the contributo di funzionamento only by presenting ISEEE certification (the foreign-income equivalent of the ISEE) issued by an authorised body such as a CAF or Patronato. Failure to present the ISEEE means automatic assignment to the highest contribution band, and an ISEEE returning €0.00 is rejected and likewise triggers the highest band. Practical consequence: with a correctly filed ISEEE reflecting a typical Tunisian family income he would very likely fall at or below the €22,000 threshold and pay little or no contributo, i.e. roughly €166/year in bollo, insurance and ER.GO tax; without it he pays roughly €2,166/year. That paperwork is worth roughly €4,000 over two years — but confirm the current-year figures with the segreteria didattica before planning on them.
otherFees: Imposta di bollo €16.00/year; assicurazione €10.00/year; tassa regionale ER.GO €140.00/year, paid separately by postal order or bank transfer rather than through PagoPA and NOT reducible by ISEE; admission application fee €100.00 per application. Late-payment penalties apply. Fuori corso students pay higher contributo. Diploma issue fee UNVERIFIED. All carried forward and pending reconfirmation.
totalCost: Best case with ISEEE filed: roughly €166/year in unavoidable charges, about €330 over two years, plus the €100 admission fee. Worst case without ISEEE: about €4,332 over two years. Bologna living costs are high for Italy at roughly €900–1,300/month and student housing is notoriously scarce — factor that in seriously, as it can outweigh the fee advantage over Turin. Two-year all-in approximately €25,000–34,000 depending on housing, before any ER.GO award.
scholarshipDetail: ER.GO, the Emilia-Romagna right-to-study agency, runs income-based scholarships open to non-EU students covering a maintenance grant, fee exemption and subsidised accommodation and meals. Combined with a low ISEEE this is the closest thing to full funding in the Italian state conservatoire system. The bando typically opens in summer. Obtaining the ISEEE through a Patronato or CAF is the prerequisite for both the fee reduction and the scholarship — the single most valuable piece of Italian paperwork he can prepare. MAECI government scholarships are the alternative national route.
entry: CORRECTION TO SOURCING AND STATUS. The course page publishes the curriculum and CFA only — it states NO entry requirements at all. The previously quoted requirement, 'completion of three-year electronic music studies or equivalent', comes from the international pages, which could not be reached in this pass. So the strictness attributed to Bologna is real in the prior record but unconfirmed here, and it is also worth noting that Torino's confirmed wording is far more open for the same DCSL34 course code. Getting this answered in writing is the single gating action for Bologna.
acceptsNonMusic: UNCERTAIN, and now explicitly unconfirmed. The course page states no entry requirement whatsoever; the restrictive 'three-year electronic music studies or equivalent' wording lives on international pages that were unreachable this pass. Note the useful asymmetry: Torino runs the same ministerial course code DCSL34 and its confirmed published requirement accepts any foreign triennale. That is a strong argument to put to Bologna's segreteria. Until they answer in writing, treat Bologna as uncertain rather than as closed.
portfolio: UNVERIFIED — not published on the course page. Given the sound-design orientation a portfolio is very likely central. Obtain the Bando di ammissione. Worth asking specifically whether Bologna, like Torino, accepts technical-scientific work in the portfolio — that Torino wording is the precedent to cite when asking.
audition: An admission test is required, assessing theoretical, interpretative and/or compositional skills. The specific content for DCSL34 is not published on the course page — request the annual Bando di ammissione from the segreteria. A separate Italian language test applies to international students. The degree's own final examination is a creative project plus a written thesis discussion (Prova finale, 10 CFA).
deadline: 12 April 2025 for a.a. 2025/26 (PRIOR CYCLE — confirm the 2027/28 date). After the ranking list is published, admitted candidates must enrol within 10 days — a very short window that requires funds and documents ready in advance.
opens: For a.a. 2025/26, applications for ammissioni and trasferimenti ran 17 March – 12 April 2025 (PRIOR CYCLE — could not be re-verified this pass; the ammissioni page was behind the bot check). Expect a comparable mid-March opening in 2027 for a 2027/28 start. Non-EU applicants must separately complete Universitaly pre-enrolment on the Ministry's earlier calendar before enrolling for the entrance examinations.
duration: 2 years, 120 CFA — CONFIRMED on the course page as 'Primo Anno CFA: 60' and 'Secondo Anno CFA: 60'. Year 1 confirmed modules include Composizione musicale elettroacustica-1 (12 CFA), Composizione audiovisiva integrata — suono per video, film, teatro, danza e videogiochi — 1 (15 CFA), and Sistemi e linguaggi di programmazione per l'audio e le applicazioni musicali (7 CFA). Year 2 confirmed includes Composizione musicale elettroacustica-2 (12 CFA) and a Prova finale (10 CFA), with multimedia programming, interactive multimodal environments and digital audio spatialisation across the two years.
languageReq: Italian B2, with international students undergoing verification through a specific test. RE-VERIFICATION FAILED THIS PASS — consbo.it international pages returned only a bot-check interstitial. The B2 figure is carried forward from the prior sweep and should be reconfirmed with the segreteria didattica (051 221483 / 051 233975) before being relied on.
englishTest: None. The conservatoire's international pages are in English but the teaching is not.
study: Of direct value to him: Sistemi e linguaggi di programmazione per l'audio (7 CFA), multimedia programming, interactive multimodal environments, digital audio spatialisation and sound design programming techniques — a cluster a software engineer enters with a real advantage rather than a deficit. Composizione audiovisiva integrata at 15 CFA explicitly covers sound for video, film, theatre, dance and VIDEOGAMES, which is the most employable strand in the whole sweep. Audio recording technologies covers studio practice. There is no commercial music production, DJ practice or music business content.
recommendation: WORTH PURSUING, but the eligibility question must be answered before he invests anything in it. The syllabus is confirmed and is the best technical fit in this entire sweep for a software engineer — programming languages and systems for audio (7 CFA), multimedia programming, interactive multimodal environments, digital audio spatialisation, and 15 CFA of integrated audiovisual composition covering sound for film, theatre, dance and videogames. Those are modules where his background is an asset. What could NOT be verified in this pass is everything else: the conservatoire's site is behind an active bot-verification layer, so the entry requirements, the B2 Italian requirement, the fee regulation and the ISEEE rule are all carried forward from the prior sweep unconfirmed. First action, autumn 2026: phone or email the segreteria didattica (051 221483 / 051 233975) and ask three things — whether a foreign three-year Software Engineering degree plus a documented electronic-music and technical portfolio is accepted as 'equivalent' for DCSL34 admission, what the Bando di ammissione requires, and whether the ISEEE route to contributo exoneration still stands for a non-EU non-resident. Cite Torino's DCSL34 wording, which accepts any foreign triennale outright, when asking the first question. Meanwhile treat Torino as the primary Italian target and Bologna as the strong second: Torino's door is confirmed open, Bologna's is merely not confirmed shut. Two preparations serve both: tested Italian B2, and the ISEEE paperwork route mapped with a Patronato well before enrolment. And be clear with him about what this is — an electroacoustic composition and sound design degree that would make him a formidable sound designer and audio programmer, not a commercial dance-music production course.

study: VERIFIED on the official page. Two 4-month quadrimesters. First: electronic music production fundamentals — composition, programming and arranging, integrating external hardware with DAWs and plugins, developing a personal workflow. Second: developing artistic identity, refining production technique, remixing, and mastering an EP ready for publication. Entirely project-based with no traditional exams. Stated career outcomes: Music Producer, Remixer, Electronic Music Performer, Live Performer, MIDI Programmer. recommendation: Right content, wrong language, wrong status, and a price he is not allowed to see before handing over his details. The syllabus is arguably the best-designed short electronic-production course in this entire research set — no exams, pure project work, ending in a mastered EP with an original remix, which is exactly what his empty portfolio needs, and the stated outcomes (producer, remixer, live performer) map directly onto his goal. But four things kill it for September 2027. First, it is taught in Italian with a CERTIFIED B2 requirement — for a Tunisian applicant with no Italian that is 600-800 hours of study plus a formal exam before he can even apply, a far bigger obstacle than any IELTS. Second, it carries no academic recognition of any kind: SAE Milano's ministerial decree covers only Produzione Audio and Produzione Cinetelevisiva, and this course is explicitly outside it. Third, the price is unpublished — a school that will not show you the number before capturing your contact details is not one to commit to sight-unseen. Fourth, a study visa on an 8-month unaccredited certificate is unproven, and no scholarship or regional grant is available to soften any of it. One genuine correction in his favour: intakes are October AND February, and an October 2027 start IS offered — so the timing would have worked. It is everything else that does not. Carry forward the structural lesson: an 8-month project-based course whose output is a finished, mastered EP is a better portfolio-building instrument than a year of lectures. That is the right criterion to apply to every option — he should just apply it to a course taught in a language he speaks, with an award that means something, and a price printed on the page.

He has Arabic, French and working English; reaching exam-standard Lithuanian by an early-2027 application round is not realistic. His untaken IELTS is beside the point — the certificate he would need is one he has no path to. (2) MONEY: zero state-funded places on the programme by design, so ≈ €15,936 tuition plus ≈ €75 in admission fees plus 1.5 years of Kaunas living costs, all self-paid. That fails his 'only self-pay if genuinely cheap' test outright. (3) FUNDING: Tunisia is excluded by nationality from the Lithuanian state master's scholarship, and KTU's own international scholarships only reach English-track programmes. The bitter irony is that the academic gate — 'a bachelor's degree from any field' — is the most open he will find anywhere for a non-music engineering graduate, and the syllabus (electronic composition and performance, Sound Design Studio, music programming, virtual instruments, game and film scoring) matches his goals almost exactly. Separately, correct the previous record's three factual errors: master's admission is via KTU's MPIS system and NOT LAMA BPO; the deadline is the domestic round calendar and not 1 June; and the application/registration fees are published at €25 and €50, not unknown.

Using the word 'Master' in a diploma title while delivering a self-described MBO+/HBO- private certificate is precisely the nomenclature trap the brief warns about. No ANECA verification, no RUCT entry, no EHEA standing, no doctoral access. Beyond that, the 25-ECTS volume is below the 60-ECTS statutory floor for a Máster de Formación Permanente under RD 822/2021 — so calling it a 'Máster' is not merely marketing gloss over a título propio, it is inconsistent with the Spanish regulation governing that exact award name. Treat the word 'Máster' in the title as unsupported.

As a master's route it should be struck off the list.

qualification: TÍTULO PROPIO — VERIFIED, with a three-way structure confirmed from SAE's own announcement of the UDIMA agreement. (a) Applicants WITH a prior university degree receive a 'Máster de formación permanente, acreditado por UDIMA y con una carga lectiva que oscila entre 25 y 60 ECTS, según el programa elegido'. (b) Applicants WITHOUT a university degree (but with 2+ years' professional experience) receive a 'título de Máster Profesional emitido por SAE Creative Media Institute España'. (c) Every route also carries the 'Diploma Profesional emitido por SAE Creative Media Education'. accreditation: NOT OFFICIAL. VERIFIED: the academic award is a UDIMA 'Máster de formación permanente' of 25–60 ECTS depending on programme, or a 'Máster Profesional' — both are títulos propios of a private distance university, not ANECA-verified, not registered as official titles in RUCT, conferring no automatic EHEA recognition and no right of entry to a Spanish doctorate. SAE's own award is a 'Diploma Profesional', a vocational certificate rather than a degree. The vendor certifications (Avid Pro Tools Specialist 110, Ableton Live Certified User, Wwise Certified User 110, Midas Pro Series, Digico SD Series) are genuine industry credentials with real labour-market value — but they are industry certifications, not academic accreditation, and should not be confused with one.

(2) BECAS GENERALITAT DE CATALUNYA (non-university studies, 2026-2027) — €1,700 income-based, €2,700 relocation, €300–350 basic, €50–125 academic merit, plus variable amounts from €60; but tied to family income, Catalan residency and academic-performance conditions, and SAE lists it against its 'Título de Grado en Música'. Year 2: Planificación Empresarial, Marketing y Aspectos Legales; Composición Musical; Sonido en Directo; Sonido para Videojuegos; Proyectos Profesionales Avanzados. scholarshipDetail: UNVERIFIED.
