An unquantified 'we offer scholarships' is not a scholarship — treat as zero until he has a name and a number in writing.
entry: Aimed at 'técnicos/as de sonido, músicos/as, DJs, compositores/as o productores/as autodidactas', audio editors and career changers. TAI requires 'familiaridad con DAWs, procesos básicos de grabación y lenguaje musical/técnico' — familiarity with DAWs, basic recording processes, and musical/technical language. Admission process, verified: (1) book an appointment on +34 91 167 20 62 or admision@taiarts.com; (2) submit required documentation; (3) sit an in-person or video interview; (4) receive a written decision; (5) pay a place-securing deposit; (6) formalise enrolment.
acceptsNonMusic: YES in principle — TAI explicitly names 'productores/as autodidactas' (self-taught producers) and 'DJs' among its target profiles, so the absence of a music degree is not disqualifying and a software-engineering BSc is no obstacle. BUT the published expectation of 'familiaridad con DAWs, procesos básicos de grabación y lenguaje musical/técnico' is a real bar, and it is tested at a live interview. He must arrive with demonstrable DAW competence and finished work. Twelve months of self-study before autumn 2027 makes this comfortably achievable.
portfolio: No formal portfolio spec is published, but 'documentación requerida' plus a mandatory interview function as one. Given the stated DAW-familiarity expectation, assume he will be asked to play and discuss his own tracks.
audition: A mandatory admission interview, in person or by video. This is the only programme in this batch with a compulsory individual interview — a mild positive, since it means the cohort is at least filtered.
deadline: No published deadline; admission by appointment until places fill for the October start. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for October 2027.
opens: Rolling, by appointment with the admissions team. 40% of TAI's student body is international, so the process is well-worn.
duration: 1 academic year; 60 ECTS.
englishTest: No IELTS and no English test. Instruction is in Spanish; Spanish proficiency is the operative requirement. He should be at roughly B2 before starting.
study: MUCH richer than previously recorded — 13 core subjects, VERIFIED: AVID Pro Tools Certification (101/110), professional studio recording, creative mixing and mastering, audio editing in DAWs, artistic direction, sound design, co-writing and creative development, and marketing and industry projection. The programme is built around producing real projects, with professional pitching sessions to Sony Music and MercaderLab, and studio visits to reference facilities including MercaderLab and Sonobox.
recommendation: On CONTENT this is the strongest programme in the batch — 13 subjects, Pro Tools 101/110 certification, named industry faculty, and Sony/Universal/MercaderLab access are a materially better offer than anything else here, and TAI explicitly welcomes self-taught producers and DJs, which is exactly him. Two things hold it back. First, no one will tell you the price: for a budget-sensitive self-payer, committing to an unpublished number is not acceptable. Second, the good news I can give him is a correction — his non-EU administrative fee is €677.60, not the €1,440 previously assumed, because that higher tier applies only to official degrees. Send ONE email to admision@taiarts.com asking four things in writing: (a) total tuition plus reserva de plaza for a non-EU student on the 2027-28 intake; (b) whether a título propio at 60 ECTS supports a Spanish estancia por estudios and whether the €560 propio advisory package includes visa tramitación or only residency paperwork; (c) the name, amount and deadline of any scholarship he could actually receive; (d) whether the Avid PT101/110 exam fees are included. If tuition comes back above roughly €9,000, or if any of the four answers is vague, walk away — the award is not official and there are cheaper título propio options in the same city.

institution: UAX — Universidad Alfonso X el Sabio
programme: Máster en Gestión de la Música en Directo (Live Music Management)
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's, but taught in Spanish — language is the real gate
qualification: TÍTULO PROPIO — verified verbatim. The programme page carries the literal text "Título propio" in its qualification field, alongside "60 ECTS". This is UAX's own diploma, NOT a Máster Universitario Oficial.
accreditation: NOT OFFICIAL. Confirmed título propio: no ANECA verification, not registered in RUCT as an official title, no automatic EHEA recognition, no PhD access, no value for Spanish public-sector oposiciones or homologation. NOTE THE NAMING TELL, which he should learn to read across all Spanish private universities: UAX's official awards are named "Máster Universitario en ..." (e.g. the Máster Universitario en Gestión de la Cultura, el Deporte, los Medios y el Entretenimiento launched alongside it), while this one is named "Máster en ..." with no "Universitario" — that word is the difference between an official degree and a school certificate. Some UAX marketing and press coverage loosely calls the whole Live Nation family "official degrees"; the programme page itself says título propio, and the programme page governs.
tuition: UNVERIFIED. Must be requested from UAX admissions in writing, with the non-EU price specifically confirmed.
otherFees: UNVERIFIED. No application fee, reserva de plaza, enrolment fee, materials fee or insurance figure is published anywhere on the UAX site. Spanish private universities typically charge a separate non-refundable reserva de plaza; assume one exists until told otherwise.
totalCost: UNVERIFIED — no price is published, so no honest total can be given. On top of tuition he must budget Madrid living costs (realistically EUR 1,000–1,400/month) and satisfy the Spanish student-visa proof-of-funds requirement, which is pegged to 100% of IPREM (approximately EUR 600/month, i.e. roughly EUR 7,200 for a year, held in his own name).
scholarshipDetail: No true scholarship identified for a non-EU applicant. The advertised "25% de ayuda hasta el 15 de agosto" is a rotating promotional discount (a price cut, not a merit award), and it belongs to the current cycle — PRIOR CYCLE for his purposes. UAX separately advertises excellence scholarships and continuity-of-studies aid of up to 25%, but neither their criteria nor their availability to non-EU or título-propio students is published — UNVERIFIED. Assume he pays close to full price with at most a promotional discount.
entry: NOT PUBLISHED on the programme page — UNVERIFIED. The page describes the audience as professionals and graduates seeking to work in live music production and event management, but states no formal degree requirement, no grade threshold and no language requirement. The normal standard for a UAX título propio is a university degree in any discipline plus an admissions interview. He must obtain the written requirements from admissions.
acceptsNonMusic: ALMOST CERTAINLY YES, but the formal wording is UNVERIFIED because no entry requirements are published. The page's own framing is occupational rather than disciplinary — it addresses people who want to "liderar proyectos reales desde dentro de la industria: producción de conciertos, management, logística, presupuestos, negociación" — with no reference to musical training, an instrument, or a music degree. Live-music management programmes routinely admit business, law, marketing and technology graduates, and a software-engineering background is an asset for ticketing and data roles. This is the one programme in this batch whose admissions bar he plausibly clears today.
portfolio: None published. No portfolio, no demo reel, no track submission required — consistent with a management programme.
audition: None. No audition, no performance test, no instrumental requirement.
deadline: No published application deadline — admission is rolling until the cohort fills. UNVERIFIED for the 2027 intake. The "15 de agosto" date is a discount cut-off, not an application deadline.
duration: 60 ECTS, 9 months, presencial. Confirmed in the page's own analytics metadata: duration 9 meses, mode presencial, campus Madrid Chamberí.
englishTest: Not applicable — the programme is in Spanish, so IELTS is irrelevant. The real language barrier is SPANISH: he would be studying negotiation, contracts and legal frameworks in Spanish, in a Spanish-language cohort. No Spanish-level requirement is published (UNVERIFIED), but functioning in this programme without solid Spanish (realistically B2) would be very difficult.
study: Verified from the live page: concert production, artist management, logistics and operations, budgeting, negotiation with artists and promoters, legal aspects, marketing and creativity applied to marketing, sponsorship and audience development, ticketing, and project management — delivered through real projects. Masterclasses by Live Nation, Ticketmaster and Superstruct Entertainment executives, plus practical workshops on negotiation and event production. Faculty verified to include working industry figures (e.g. Pedro Martínez-Vega, of Resonance Projects, previously involved in the Grupo Pacha/Trilantic transformation and the Woomoon and Toyroom brands — genuinely relevant to the electronic-music/Ibiza economy). ZERO studio, DAW, mixing, mastering, synthesis or DJ-technique content.
recommendation: AVOID as a route to becoming a DJ/producer — the decisive reason is that it teaches none of the craft he asked for. Nine months and (probably) five figures buy him concert logistics, contracts, ticketing and sponsorship; he would not touch a DAW, a console or a studio. Two further problems compound it: the award is a título propio, so he would pay master-level money for a school certificate with no ANECA verification, no EHEA recognition and no PhD access; and UAX publishes no price at all, which for a budget-sensitive self-payer is disqualifying on its own — never commit to a programme that will not tell you what it costs. FLAG IT TO HIM ANYWAY, honestly, as a strategic alternative, because it solves the two problems no production school solves for him: it needs no portfolio and no musicianship proof, so his admissions weaknesses vanish; and the Live Nation, Ticketmaster, Superstruct and Mad Cool relationships are the most commercially valuable industry links anywhere in this Spanish slice, with faculty drawn from the Pacha/Woomoon/Ibiza electronic economy. If his true goal is "work in international electronic music" rather than "be the person at the desk", this is a real door — and his software-engineering degree is a genuine asset in ticketing and music-data roles. Two hard conditions before he would ever consider it: get the total non-EU price in writing, and get written confirmation that UAX will issue a carta de admisión supporting a student visa for a título propio. Also note he would be studying negotiation and contract law in Spanish, which without B2 Spanish is not survivable. If the official-degree route matters to him more than the subject, the sister Máster Universitario en Gestión de la Cultura, el Deporte, los Medios y el Entretenimiento (Málaga) is the one genuinely ANECA-official title in this family.

institution: UDIMA — Universidad a Distancia de Madrid
programme: Máster Profesional en Producción Musical (título propio, delivered in person by DJP Music School)
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's, but taught in Spanish — language is the real gate
qualification: TÍTULO PROPIO. CONFIRMED VERBATIM on udima.es: the award is a "Título propio de la Universidad a Distancia de Madrid", classified as "Enseñanza no reglada y sin carácter oficial" under Decreto 84/2004 of the Comunidad de Madrid. DJP's own page repeats it: these are "enseñanzas no conducentes a la obtención de un título con valor oficial". 60 ECTS are awarded, but they are título-propio ECTS.
accreditation: NOT OFFICIAL — and stated as such by the awarding university itself, in plain Spanish, on its own programme page. This is NOT a Máster Universitario Oficial, is NOT ANECA-verified, carries no EHEA official status, and gives no access to a Spanish or European doctorate. VERIFIED that the same UDIMA badge sits behind several Madrid private-school 'masters', including SAE Institute Spain's four music/audio masters (SAE-UDIMA agreement confirmed on sae.edu) and DJP's Máster en Producción Musical. THE DECODER RULE, now confirmed at source: when a Spanish 'máster' is described as accredited/awarded by UDIMA, or as a 'Título Propio', or as a 'Máster de Formación Permanente', it is the institution's OWN diploma. Only the exact phrase 'Máster Universitario Oficial' denotes an official Spanish degree.
tuition: €5,900 paying in full, or €6,100 across instalments, for the whole 9-month programme. UDIMA itself publishes no price — every figure here comes from DJP Music School.
otherFees: No application fee, materials fee or insurance charge is published. The €1,200 matrícula is separate from and additional to the tuition figure, so do not read €4,700 as the total. UDIMA contact: informa@udima.es, (+34) 918 561 699. DJP contact: info@djpmusicschool.com, (+34) 91 819 5390.
totalCost: €5,900–€6,100 in fees, plus roughly €1,000–€2,000 for laptop/DAW/hardware, plus Madrid living costs of about €900–€1,200 per month over 9 months (€8,100–€10,800). Realistic first-year outlay: €15,000–€19,000 — for a certificate with no official status and no visa basis.
scholarshipDetail: None published, by either UDIMA or DJP. Nothing available to a Tunisian or other non-EU applicant.
entry: No formal academic prerequisite is published. UDIMA describes the audience as anyone "interesado en desarrollar habilidades en la producción musical, ya sea desde cero o desde un nivel intermedio" — from scratch or from an intermediate level — naming musicians, composers, producers, sound engineers and DJs. DJP publishes no entry requirements at all. Open access.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — unambiguously. The published wording "ya sea desde cero o desde un nivel intermedio" ("whether from scratch or from an intermediate level") explicitly admits complete beginners. His BSc in Software Engineering is no obstacle; equally, no academic screening happens at all, which is a quality signal in itself.
portfolio: None published by either UDIMA or DJP. No portfolio is required — convenient given his portfolio is unfinished, but it also means no selection is taking place.
audition: None. No audition, interview or practical test is published.
deadline: No published deadline — enrolment runs until places are filled for the September start. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
opens: Not published. DJP operates rolling enrolment until the September cohort fills. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for 2027.
duration: 9 months, 60 ECTS (título-propio credits) — CONFIRMED on the DJP page. UDIMA's own page still does not state duration or ECTS, which is itself telling.
englishTest: No IELTS and no English-language route. Teaching is entirely in Spanish, so functional Spanish is the real language barrier. Nothing about DELE or any Spanish-proficiency evidence is published either.
study: Seven modules, CONFIRMED on both the UDIMA and DJP pages: music creation; musical theory and composition; sound design; implementation of music in live settings; introduction to mixing and mastering; and digital marketing / music promotion. Note the wording — mixing and mastering is an 'introduction' only. For someone who wants to work as a producer this is broad-but-shallow, and the technical depth a software engineer would find satisfying is not there.
recommendation: Keep this entry as the decoder ring for the whole Spanish private-school market rather than as a place to apply. The single most useful test he can carry into every Spanish offer: if the words 'Máster Universitario Oficial' do not appear, it is not an official Spanish degree. 'Título propio', 'Máster de Formación Permanente', 'acreditado por UDIMA', 'titulación propia' and '60 ECTS' all fail that test — and the SAE Institute Spain masters in his shortlist fail it too, via the same UDIMA agreement. On the programme itself: €5,900–€6,100 buys nine months of evening classes, four evenings a week, with an unfiltered intake, undisclosed facilities and an introductory-level treatment of mixing and mastering. It cannot support a Tunisian student visa, which makes the rest academic. If he ever ends up in Madrid on some other legal basis and wants a structured part-time course, it is defensible; as the reason to move to Spain, it is not.

institution: Universidad Francisco de Vitoria (UFV)
programme: Postgrado en Producción Musical y Artística (with The Music Station)
whyChance: Names engineering or computing as a welcome background, but taught in Spanish — language is the real gate
qualification: TÍTULO PROPIO, and specifically a 'Postgrado' of 30 ECTS lasting THREE MONTHS. VERIFIED on the official UFV page, which labels it 'Título Propio', '30 CTS', 'Duración 3 meses'. THIS IS NOT A MASTER. It is a short postgraduate certificate issued by UFV under its own authority.
accreditation: NOT OFFICIAL. A UFV título propio at postgraduate-course level. Not ANECA-verified, not an official master, no RUCT entry, no doctoral access. At 30 ECTS it carries half the credit weight of a 60-ECTS master and one quarter of a 120-ECTS one. It should not be compared with the master's-level programmes elsewhere in this slice despite being marketed alongside them.
tuition: EUR 6,100 headline for the whole 30-ECTS programme (2026/2027 edition), with UFV's own internal breakdown reconciling to EUR 6,500. No separate non-EU rate is published.
otherFees: Reservation/place fee EUR 960 and enrolment EUR 5,540, per the official breakdown — presented as components of the price rather than additions, though they do not reconcile to the stated total. No separate application, materials or exam fee published — UNVERIFIED.
totalCost: EUR 6,100–6,500 institutional cost for a three-month, 30-ECTS evening certificate — plus Madrid living costs, which are among the highest in Spain. On a per-credit basis this is the most expensive Spanish option in the slice at roughly EUR 203–217 per ECTS, against UCAM's EUR 65 and La Salle's EUR 199 for an OFFICIAL degree. The included perpetual Ableton Live 12 Suite licence (around EUR 599 retail) and the Avid certification offset perhaps EUR 800–1,000 of that.
scholarshipDetail: None published for this programme — UNVERIFIED, and unlikely for a short título propio.
entry: VERIFIED wording: aimed at people with 'formación o experiencia previa en música o sonido que deseen profesionalizarse' — prior training or experience in music or sound who wish to turn professional. Target profile: musicians, composers, producers, sound technicians and audiovisual professionals wanting to add music production to their projects. Rolling enrolment, limited places. Notably there is no stated requirement to hold a university degree at all, which underlines that this is a professional short course rather than a postgraduate qualification.
acceptsNonMusic: PROBLEMATIC. The published target profile requires prior TRAINING OR EXPERIENCE in music or sound. He has neither a music qualification nor professional audio experience. Whether self-taught production work would satisfy 'experiencia previa' is UNVERIFIED — he would have to ask, and a strong portfolio would be his only lever. Note the contrast with UCAM, which names computer engineering graduates as a welcome profile, and with La Salle, which requires no music background at all.
portfolio: Not published — UNVERIFIED.
audition: None published. Admission is by direct contact with the programme office (postgrado@ufv.es / +34 91 709 14 24).
deadline: No fixed deadline — rolling until places fill. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: the published cycle is the September 2026 edition; 2027 dates are not yet available.
duration: 30 ECTS over 3 months. Advertised edition runs September 2026 to January 2027, face-to-face on the Madrid campus and at The Music Station, Monday to Friday 18:00–20:00.
englishTest: Not applicable — the programme is taught in Spanish. No IELTS required.
study: Module 1 — audio fundamentals, music theory, songwriting, Pro Tools training (41 hours). Module 2 — pre-production techniques and workflow (22 hours). Module 3 — production processes and creative direction (32 hours). Module 4 — post-production, mixing, mastering and industry contracts (57 hours). Roughly 152 contact hours in total. Taught inside a working production facility.
recommendation: AVOID for his purposes, and the reason is now legal rather than a judgement call. This is not a master — it is a 30-ECTS certificate delivered over three months of two-hour evening classes, and at 10 contact hours per week it falls below BOTH thresholds in Spain's student-authorisation criteria (20 hours per week generally, or at minimum 12 in-person hours for concentrated programmes). It therefore cannot support a student residence permit, which makes it useless as a September 2027 relocation plan regardless of its merits. Compounding that: its published entry profile expects prior music or sound training that he does not have; it is taught entirely in Spanish; it costs more per credit than La Salle's official Máster Universitario; and UFV's own page contradicts itself on the price by EUR 400. On the positive side it is a genuinely good short skills course — real facilities, Warner Music Spain professionals, and two portable certifications (Avid PT101/PT110 and a perpetual Ableton Live 12 Suite licence) that he would otherwise pay for separately. The only scenario where it makes sense is as a paid upskilling course taken once he is already legally resident in Madrid on some other basis. Do not build a relocation plan around it, and if he does ever enrol, get the correct total price in writing first.

institution: Universidad Francisco de Vitoria (UFV) in collaboration with Warner Music Spain
programme: Postgrado en Producción Musical y Artística (with Warner Music Spain) — NOT A MASTER
whyChance: Names engineering or computing as a welcome background, but taught in Spanish — language is the real gate

tuition: €6,100 as headlined by UFV. ARITHMETIC DISCREPANCY CONFIRMED, not a transcription error on our side: the two components UFV publishes sum to €6,500, which is €400 MORE than the €6,100 total UFV advertises. otherFees: The €960 reserva de plaza is included in the headline total. No application, materials or exam fees are published. Genuinely and unusually included: Avid Pro Tools PT101 + PT110 official certification, a PERPETUAL Ableton Live 12 Suite licence, and 6 hours of Ableton training — collectively worth several hundred euros and unusually transparent.
totalCost: €6,100 (or possibly €6,500 — see the discrepancy) in fees for three months, plus roughly €3,000–€4,500 in Madrid living costs for that period, plus a laptop. Around €10,000–€12,500 all in — for no visa, no master, and 30 ECTS.
scholarshipDetail: UNVERIFIED — none published for this postgrado, and nothing specific to non-EU applicants. UFV's page contains no becas section at all for this programme.
entry: 'Formación o experiencia previa en música o sonido' — prior TRAINING OR EXPERIENCE in music or sound, stated as preferred rather than absolute. Targeted at musicians, composers, producers and audio technicians, plus audiovisual and media professionals moving into music production. Places are deliberately limited because of the practical, personalised format. Admission runs through the postgraduate team: +34 91 709 14 24 or +34 649 24 00 74, postgrado@ufv.es, named contact Patricia Pérez Merino.
acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY. The bar is 'training OR experience in music or sound', not a music degree — so a self-taught producer with a credible body of work can qualify, and the requirement is framed as preferred rather than mandatory. But a candidate with neither training nor experience would not clear it. His software-engineering degree is irrelevant either way; what would carry him is a genuinely developed portfolio, which he does not yet have. He would need roughly a year of serious output first.
portfolio: None formally published, but with limited places and a prior-experience expectation, work will be assessed informally at admission.
audition: None published. Admission is handled by the postgraduate admissions team with a named advisor rather than by audition.
deadline: No published deadline; limited places for the September 2026 start. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for a September 2027 edition, which has not been announced.
opens: Rolling until the limited places fill.
duration: 3 months; 30 ECTS. Monday to Friday, 18:00–20:00 — 10 contact hours a week.
englishTest: No IELTS and no English requirement. Taught in Spanish.
study: Practical training in composition, editing, mixing and artistic direction, with direct collaboration opportunities with Warner Music Spain professionals. VERIFIED inclusions: official Avid Pro Tools certification at PT101 and PT110 levels, a PERPETUAL Ableton Live 12 Suite licence for every student, and 6 hours of dedicated Ableton training.
recommendation: The best industry connection in this batch and refreshingly honest about what it is — but it cannot be his plan. It is THREE MONTHS, 30 ECTS and 10 evening hours a week: it will not carry a Spanish student visa, it is not a master, and at €6,100 it costs almost as much as a full 9-month master elsewhere, at roughly double the cost per credit. He also does not currently meet the stated 'training or experience in music or sound' entry expectation. I have listed it precisely so the Warner Music branding does not tempt him into treating a certificate as a degree. Where it genuinely shines is as a LATER add-on: if he is already legally resident in Spain — say, after a full-time programme that does carry a visa — this is an excellent three-month investment for the Warner-adjacent network, the Pro Tools certification and a perpetual Ableton Live 12 Suite licence he keeps forever. One thing to do before paying anything: ask UFV to reconcile €960 + €5,540 = €6,500 against the €6,100 they advertise, and get the answer in writing.

institution: Universidad Nebrija
programme: Máster de Formación Permanente en Radio, Podcast y Audio Digital
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's, but taught in Spanish — language is the real gate
qualification: TÍTULO PROPIO — 'Máster de Formación Permanente en Radio, Podcast y Audio Digital', 60 ECTS. CONFIRMED on Nebrija's own programme page. NOT a Máster Universitario Oficial.
accreditation: NOT OFFICIAL — CONFIRMED. This is Nebrija's own 'formación permanente' diploma (título propio). Under Spanish law (RD 822/2021) a Máster de Formación Permanente is NOT ANECA-verified, is NOT an official degree, does NOT give automatic access to a Spanish doctorate, and is not automatically recognised across the EHEA. Universidad Nebrija itself is a legitimate, ministry-recognised private university, so the paper carries a real university's name — but the award is a school diploma, not a degree.
tuition: EUR 11,500 for the whole 60-ECTS programme, 2026/27 edition (official page). His 2027/28 figure is not yet published and is likely higher.
otherFees: NOT ITEMISED anywhere on the official pages — application fee, reservation/matrícula fee and insurance are UNVERIFIED. Nebrija's fees page is behind a 'consulta el precio de matrícula' funnel. Assume a reservation payment exists (standard Spanish practice) and request the full breakdown in writing.
totalCost: EUR 11,500 published tuition + unquantified reservation/enrolment fees + Madrid living costs. Spanish student-visa proof of funds is 100% of IPREM (approx. EUR 600/month, approx. EUR 7,200/year) which he must evidence on top. Realistic first-year outlay approximately EUR 21,000–25,000 all-in, and higher if the 2027 fee rises again.
scholarshipDetail: Nebrija states it offers 'becas, descuentos y opciones de pago flexibles' and points to the fees page for detail, but publishes NO amounts, criteria or deadlines on the programme page — UNVERIFIED. Nothing identified as specifically open to non-EU or Tunisian applicants. Note: Spanish government (MEFP) general scholarships are restricted to official degrees, so a título propio is ineligible for them — any discount must come from Nebrija itself.
entry: VERIFIED wording: 'Es requisito indispensable para el acceso a los programas de Máster estar en posesión del título de Licenciado o equivalente' — i.e. any completed bachelor's degree or equivalent. A 'Licenciatura en Ciencias de la Comunicación (Periodismo, Comunicación Audiovisual, Publicidad y RR. PP.)' is 'especially valued'. Non-EU degrees will need legalisation/apostille; homologación is not normally required for a título propio.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — his BSc Software Engineering meets the formal bar. The published requirement is simply 'estar en posesión del título de Licenciado o equivalente', with communication degrees merely 'especially valued', and the programme explicitly welcomes candidates from scientific and technical backgrounds who show strong interest in the humanities. No music degree, portfolio or audio experience is demanded. He would be admissible — the problem is the subject, not the door.
portfolio: None published — UNVERIFIED. No portfolio requirement appears anywhere on the official page.
audition: None. No audition or practical test published.
deadline: No published deadline — rolling until places fill. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for October 2027.
opens: Rolling. 'Inscripciones abiertas' shown on the official page; admissions +34 917 800 040. No published opening date for the 2027 cycle.
duration: 60 ECTS, one academic year, October to June. CONFIRMED on the official page.
englishTest: Not applicable — the programme is taught entirely in Spanish. IELTS is irrelevant here; what he would need instead is demonstrable Spanish (realistically B2+). No Spanish-test threshold is published — UNVERIFIED.
study: Radio and new digital audio formats, podcast production and digital audio workflows, with guaranteed internships at leading audio companies. Nebrija states it has taught audio for twelve years. Full module list is not published on the programme page — UNVERIFIED.
recommendation: Verified as real, priced and open to him — and still the wrong programme. He would be admitted (any bachelor's degree qualifies, no portfolio, no audition), and the Cadena SER link is a genuine asset. But radio and podcast production shares only the toolchain with what he wants: there is no electronic music, no DJing, no music mixing, no sound design for music, no production of tracks. He would pay EUR 11,500+ — the highest confirmed price in this batch — to train for a career he has not asked for, in Spanish, for a non-official diploma. Concrete action if he ever reconsiders: ask for the full fee breakdown and the 2027/28 price before anything else. Otherwise, rule it out.

institution: Universitat de Barcelona - IL3 Institute of Lifelong Learning

scholarshipDetail: THIS ENTRY EARNS ITS PLACE BECAUSE IED'S DSU BANDO IS THE CLEAREST PUBLISHED PROOF THAT A NON-EU STUDENT AT AN ITALIAN PRIVATE ACADEMY CAN WIN REGIONAL STATE AID. All of the following are VERIFIED verbatim from Bando DSU 25/26, BAN 8203 rev 06 of 04/09/2025, total fund €354,392.15 under D.G.R. XII/4704 of 14.07.2025. ELIGIBILITY expressly includes 'i cittadini di Stati non appartenenti all'Unione Europea' alongside Italians and EU citizens, for students admitted or enrolled on a Diploma Accademico di Primo or Secondo Livello at Milan, Rome, Turin, Cagliari or Florence. INCOME TEST: ISEE Universitario must not exceed €26,516.70 AND ISPE must not exceed €57,645.03 — 'I due limiti indicati devono essere rispettati entrambi congiuntamente', breaching either one disqualifies. MERIT for a first-year II livello student: simply be regularly enrolled by 31 October and hold the first-level title by 31 January; full confirmation then requires 40 credits by 10 August. AMOUNTS, inclusive of the €140 regional-tax reimbursement and an €818 meal allowance: in sede €3,383 / €2,950 / €2,114 by income band; pendolari €4,754 / €4,134 / €3,254; FUORI SEDE €8,134 / €7,073 / €5,776. Awards can rise by up to 40% for students with disability. THE DECISIVE PROVISION, quoted from footnote 7: 'L'Art. 13 comma 3 del D.P.C.M. 9/04/2001 stabilisce che gli studenti stranieri non appartenenti all'Unione Europea sono considerati comunque studenti fuori sede indipendentemente dalla sede della loro residenza in Italia ad eccezione del caso in cui il nucleo familiare dello studente risieda in Italia' — a Tunisian student is AUTOMATICALLY placed in the highest bracket, €5,776 to €8,134 a year, provided the accommodation is paid for and a registered rental contract is filed by the deadline (failure to file downgrades him to 'pendolare'). NON-EU DOCUMENTATION: an ISEEU-ISPEU parificato is required, built from foreign family-composition and income declarations issued by the official tax agency of the country of residence — 'L'autocertificazione relativa a redditi e/o patrimoni esteri non può essere presentata', self-certification is refused outright — all translated into Italian and legalised. Tunisia appears on neither the London-Convention exemption list (Moldova, Sweden) nor the Apostille shortcut list (Albania), so full consular legalisation applies. A floor applies: 'il reddito degli studenti stranieri appartenenti a paesi Extra-EU non potrà essere inferiore a € 7.002,97 annuali', the visa subsistence minimum. Free ISEEU assistance is available via CAAF CGIL Lombardia (Corso di Porta Vittoria 43, Milan) under an IED agreement. EXCLUSIONS THAT MATTER: anyone already holding an equal or higher qualification is excluded (his BSc does NOT block a II livello application); anyone benefiting from another income- or merit-based grant for the same year is excluded; Foundation-course students are excluded; and the bando covers ONLY Diploma Accademico di I/II livello, so IED's one-year 'Master' courses get nothing. IED separately runs a commercial scholarship competition covering 50% of tuition on Master of Arts and Master programmes, open to international students — details UNVERIFIED on the pages read, request the current bando.
entry: A first-level degree (laurea triennale or Diploma Accademico di Primo Livello) or a foreign qualification 'deemed suitable'. Foreign qualification holders must supply a Dichiarazione di Valore in loco from the Italian Embassy in the country of award. Proof of knowledge of the language in which the course is taught is required. For DSU purposes the first-level title must be held no later than 31 January of the academic year.
acceptsNonMusic: Yes at the level test — a BSc Software Engineering satisfies 'a Degree (1st cycle) or a qualification obtained abroad deemed suitable'. Programme-specific admission criteria UNVERIFIED. But note the language gate: the Rome Interactive Environments course is taught in Italian and 'students must also present proof of knowledge of the language in which the chosen IED course is taught'.
portfolio: UNVERIFIED on the pages read. Assume a portfolio and motivational interview, as is standard for IED admissions.
audition: None — design-school admission, not audition-based.

Verified 2025/26 DSU calendar: applications 9 September to 7 November 2025; provisional rankings from 28 November 2025, and from 6 February 2026 for first-year II livello students; rental contract and proof of rent payment for fuori sede status by 10 December 2025. Enrolment regularisation by 31 October. Expect the 2027/28 window to run early September to early November 2027.

Keep IED in the file for one reason only: its DSU bando is the clearest published proof that a non-EU student at an Italian PRIVATE academy is automatically classified 'fuori sede' under Art. 13(3) d.p.c.m. 9/04/2001 and can therefore win €5,776-€8,134 a year in regional state aid. Two practical warnings that transfer to any Italian application: start collecting the Tunisian tax-agency income certificates, property statements, family-composition certificate, sworn Italian translations and consular legalisations at least four to five months before the September-November window — self-certification is refused outright and employer letters are not accepted; and file a registered rental contract before the December deadline or he is downgraded from fuori sede (€8,134) to pendolare (€4,754), losing over €3,000.

programme: Produzione Musicale e Sound Design — Bachelor of Arts (3 years) / Corso Annuale (1 year). NOT A MASTER
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's, but taught in Italian — language is the real gate
qualification: NOT A MASTER, AND NOT AN ITALIAN RECOGNISED DEGREE. The awarding/accrediting body is now IDENTIFIED (it was not in the prior entry): EABHES — the European Accreditation Board of Higher Education Schools. Mohole advertises a "Laurea Europea Bachelor of Arts — riconosciuto in UE, UK e USA", EQF Level 6, 180 ECTS. It also issues an Attestato di competenza professionale from Regione Lombardia and RSL (Rockschool London) certifications. It is NOT a MUR/AFAM Diploma Accademico and Mohole is NOT in the AFAM system. The one-year option (60 ECTS) is simply year one of the same undergraduate course — not a postgraduate qualification of any kind.
accreditation: NOT OFFICIAL in the Italian system — and the accreditation claim is now RESOLVED rather than merely doubted. Accrediting body: EABHES, verified on eabhes.eu as "one of the largest PRIVATE networks of internationally recognised professional and academic institutions", ~60 member schools, ~300 accredited programmes, self-described as aligned to ECTS and the Bologna Process. EABHES is a PRIVATE ASSOCIATION, not a state or national accreditation agency, and its own site does not claim its awards are state-recognised degrees. What this means in practice: the "Bachelor of Arts / Laurea Europea" carries NO valore legale in Italy — it is not a titolo di studio recognised by MUR, cannot be used for Italian public competitions, and is not automatically recognised by any EU, UK or US authority despite the marketing wording "riconosciuto in UE, UK e USA". Recognition would fall to each receiving institution or employer case by case. The only credentials here with a defined Italian legal identity are the regional Attestato (Regione Lombardia) and the RSL music certifications. So: the prior entry's red flag was correct on substance — the marketing overstates what a private-network accreditation delivers — but the awarding body IS named, just not the kind of body the wording implies.
tuition: Approx. €25,500 for the three-year Bachelor of Arts at €8,500/year, BEFORE the undisclosed multi-year discount. €8,500 for the one-year annual course alone.
otherFees: UNVERIFIED — Mohole's dedicated costs page (/iscrizioni/costi-agevolazioni/) publishes NO figures at all: no enrolment fee, no materials fee, no exam or certification fee, no RSL certification cost. It lists only the existence of discounts and financing and directs enquirers to phone or email the segreteria (+39 02 3651 3670 / segreteria@mohole.it). Assume undisclosed extras and demand an itemised written quote.
totalCost: €8,500/year verified tuition; approx. €25,500 over three years before discounts; plus €1,500–3,000 of Mac/DAW equipment, plus undisclosed enrolment and certification fees, plus Milan living costs of roughly €12,000–15,000 per year. Realistic three-year all-in exposure: €65,000–80,000 — for a qualification with no Italian legal value and no clear visa route.
scholarshipDetail: UNVERIFIED and now looking weaker than the prior entry suggested. The costs page does NOT publish any scholarship amounts, criteria or eligibility, and says nothing about non-EU applicants. 'Borse di studio' are discussed only at the orientation interview. For a non-EU applicant who must budget before applying for a visa, an undisclosed discretionary discount decided in a sales conversation is not a financial plan.
entry: Orientation interview (colloquio conoscitivo). No prior experience required — the school's own wording is "si parte da zero" ("you start from zero"). A secondary-school diploma is required for conferral of the Bachelor of Arts; minimum age 18 for the professional competency certificates. No degree required — this is undergraduate-entry, meaning he would be starting a bachelor's again despite already holding one.
acceptsNonMusic: Yes — no prerequisites at all. The school's own wording is "si parte da zero"; entry is by orientation interview and a secondary-school diploma is the only formal document needed for the BA. But this cuts against him, not for him: it is undergraduate-entry, so a graduate with a BSc would be starting a first degree over again, alongside school-leavers.
portfolio: None required. Nothing to prepare — which also means nothing filters the cohort.
audition: None. Orientation interview only, in Italian.
deadline: No fixed deadline published — rolling until places fill, with an early-enrolment promotion that locks a reduced rate. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for any 2027 entry.
opens: Rolling. Entry is by booking a 'colloquio conoscitivo' (orientation interview) online at any time; a 'Super Early Bird' promotion rewards enrolling well ahead.
duration: 3 years / 180 ECTS (EQF 6 claimed), or a 1-year / 60 ECTS single annuality which is year one of the same course. Monday–Friday full-time attendance. October 2026 start.
englishTest: Not applicable, and IELTS is of no use here. The course is delivered in Italian; English appears only as a taught subject. Italian proficiency is the real language requirement and no level is published — ask.
study: Year 1 (= the one-year annual course): Music Production 1, Sound Design 1, Linguaggio Musicale 1, Musica d'insieme, Logic Pro, Ableton Live, piano/keys, complementary instrument, Tecniche del suono 1, Scenari musicali, English, plus workshops. Year 2: Music Production 2, Sound Design 2, Music Industry, Tecniche del suono 2, DJ | Tecniche di mix. Year 3: Music Production 3, Sound Design 3, Music Management, AI e Musica, Sound Design per Videogiochi, DJ | Live Performance, Social e Brand Identity, showreel/portfolio and thesis project. Software taught, verified: Logic Pro, Ableton Live, MuseScore and Unreal Engine (the latter for game audio).
recommendation: RIGHT SUBJECT, WRONG EVERYTHING ELSE — and verification has now hardened this from suspicion to fact. Three things changed since the prior entry: the €8,500/year fee is CONFIRMED on Mohole's own page; the awarding body is CONFIRMED as EABHES; and EABHES is CONFIRMED, from its own website, to be a private association rather than a state accreditation agency. So the 'Laurea Europea recognised in EU, UK and USA' is a private-network award marketed in the vocabulary of official recognition. Add the rest: it is an undergraduate course for a man who already has a degree, taught entirely in Italian, with no published visa pathway and no AFAM status to fall back on. If he ever contacts them, three questions in writing, and do not enrol without all three answered on paper: (1) is the Bachelor of Arts recognised by MUR and does it carry valore legale in Italy — yes or no; (2) can you issue the documentation for Universitaly pre-enrolment and a type-D study visa for a Tunisian national — yes or no; (3) send the full itemised cost sheet including enrolment fee, RSL certification fees and the actual value of the early-bird and three-year discounts. Expect the answer to (1) to be no and to (2) to be evasive. Until then, unusable.

otherFees: CORRECTION AND ADDITION to the prior record, which said only 'UNVERIFIED, see the Programme Specification'. Two concrete cash items are now confirmed. First, the course page states 'Read more about additional fees in the Programme Specification' — those itemised extras remain unenumerated, so download the 2026 curriculum programme specification PDF linked from the course page. Second and far more important: Hertfordshire's international scholarship terms require a MINIMUM £5,000 TUITION FEE DEPOSIT, cleared into the University's bank account by a stated date, to qualify for the early postgraduate scholarships. scholarshipDetail: CORRECTED — the prior record said 'Not stated on the course page' and 'UNVERIFIED'. Hertfordshire's official international scholarships pages confirm several automatic awards, all published for the September 2026 intake and expected to run analogously for 2027. (1) Chancellor's International Scholarship: a variable award of £500 to £4,000 for new international undergraduate or postgraduate taught students joining the UK campus; NO application required — the University automatically assesses the course application form and supporting documents and emails the awarded amount. (2) Early-deposit postgraduate taught scholarships: a £3,500 one-off scholarship for international PGT applicants who pay a minimum £5,000 tuition deposit by 30 April; a £3,000 one-off for a £5,000 deposit by 17 July; a £3,000 one-off for a £5,000 deposit by 14 August. All applied to tuition fees, one-off, automatic, no application required. (3) A £1,000 full-payment discount for full-time students paying fees in full at registration. (4) A 20 per cent Herts alumni graduate discount — NOT applicable to him. IMPORTANT LIMIT: the terms state awards generally cannot be combined with other University scholarships or discounts unless exceptionally approved, so assume roughly £3,000–£4,000 total, not the sum of all of them. Realistic net tuition: about £14,000–£15,000. Chevening and GREAT remain the routes to full funding.

study: CONFIRMED module list, all compulsory, Level 7: Research and enterprise in the music and sound industries (30 credits — research methods plus business, legislation and professional practices in the music and sound industries); Studio technologies, processes and practices (30 credits — recording studio and performance technology, physical infrastructure, systems integration, software control, mastering, restoration and re-mastering, contemporary audio plugin technologies); Audio engineering (30 credits — complex multichannel systems, sophisticated audio network protocols, design of purpose-built recording studio environments, capture and measurement of acoustic spaces); Audio production and design (30 credits — current music production techniques and aesthetics, synthesis and music-oriented sound design); Major project in audio engineering (60 credits). Key staff CONFIRMED: Bruce Aisher (Programme Leader for PG Music; work on over 100 tracks including a US Billboard Club Chart No.1, a Platinum album; products by Apple, Clavia, Native Instruments), John Brough (formerly chief engineer at Metropolis Studios, worked with Queen), Dr Kyriacos Michael, Rob Wright (Head of Music).
recommendation: CORRECTIONS MADE. Two things in the prior record were wrong or incomplete and both matter. FIRST, fundingLevel was 'Check' and scholarships were recorded as 'Not stated / UNVERIFIED'. That is now corrected: Hertfordshire runs automatic, no-application international scholarships — a Chancellor's International Scholarship of £500–£4,000 assessed automatically from the course application, plus one-off postgraduate awards of £3,500 (deposit by 30 April), £3,000 (by 17 July) or £3,000 (by 14 August), plus a £1,000 full-payment discount. Awards generally do not stack, so assume about £3,000–£4,000, bringing net tuition to roughly £14,000–£15,000 — materially cheaper than the prior record suggested and cheaper than USW's headline. SECOND, a real cost was missing: those early scholarships require a minimum £5,000 TUITION DEPOSIT cleared by the stated date. That is a big early cash call he must plan for. CONFIRMED UNCHANGED: £17,950 international 2026/27, IELTS 6.5 with no band below 5.5, the 26/09/2027 start with apply links already live, the entry wording, and the Neve studio estate. The MSc-versus-MA discrepancy is CONFIRMED and is sharper than the prior record stated — it is specifically the FULL-TIME 2026 specification that reads 'MA Audio Engineering' while the part-time one reads 'MSc'. Since he would study full-time, get the parchment title in writing before paying a deposit. Net judgement: strong programme, best facilities, viable net cost, but of the two Herts music options this one has the narrower subject wording ('related subjects' rather than 'related discipline'), no stated classification floor to lean on, and content aimed at studio engineering rather than at becoming an artist. Prefer the MA Music Production and Artist Development unless he specifically wants to be an engineer rather than a producer.

scholarshipDetail: University of Hertfordshire international scholarships and discounts, described on the official international pages as "up to GBP 4,000 towards study fees". Open to overseas applicants, so a Tunisian national is eligible in principle. No named Tunisia-specific award and no fully funded route found. An international applicant requiring a CAS must also pay a tuition deposit as a condition of the offer.
entry: Quoted verbatim from the official page: "A good honours degree (1st, 2:1 or 2:2) in Music, Music Technology, Music Performance, or a related discipline (or an equivalent international qualification)" OR "A minimum of five years' professional industry experience, assessed at the discretion of the Admissions Team or Programme Tutor." Then, and this is the line that matters most for him: "All applicants are expected to demonstrate a solid prior knowledge of standard music studio equipment and its functions, along with practical experience using a range of common audio software platforms." The page confirms "Applications open to international and EU students: Yes". No IELTS/TOEFL score is quoted on the course page itself — he must confirm the English requirement with the international admissions team (he has not sat a test yet).
acceptsNonMusic: Check — genuinely ambiguous, and he must ask before investing. The named degrees are Music, Music Technology and Music Performance "or a related discipline"; BSc Software Engineering is not obviously within that family. There is no explicit statement that non-music bachelors are accepted, and there is no explicit exclusion either. The harder gate is the separate sentence requiring demonstrated prior knowledge of studio equipment and common audio software — that applies to ALL applicants regardless of degree, so he cannot route around it. Practical advice: email the Programme Leader, Bruce Aisher (b.aisher@herts.ac.uk, named on the official page), with his situation and a link to his work, before applying.
portfolio: NOT published. The official course page specifies no portfolio, showreel or work-sample requirement — the entry-requirements block lists only the degree/experience condition and the studio-knowledge expectation. Do not assume there is none: for a composition-titled MA, admissions will very likely ask for evidence of creative work, and the studio-knowledge clause effectively demands it. He must obtain the exact brief from the programme team. Application is direct to the university, not via UCAS: international applicants use the herts.ac.uk international application portal; the portal asks for the standard transcript/qualification documents.
audition: None published. No audition, no on-site test and no interview is mentioned anywhere on the official course page. Assessment on the course itself is 100% coursework ("All assessment is coursework-based").
deadline: No fixed closing date is published. UK postgraduate taught admission here is rolling — applications are considered until the cohort fills. For a September 2027 start he should apply in autumn 2026 to early 2027, well ahead of the UK student-visa (CAS) and deposit timeline. Because no deadline is published at all, nothing here is a lapsed prior-cycle date.
opens: ALREADY OPEN for the 2027 intake — this is the standout practical fact. The official page's 'How to apply' table lists a 2027 instance: start 22/09/2027, end 30/09/2028, UH Hatfield Campus, with live 'Apply online' links for both full time and part time. The 2026 instance (22/09/2026) is also still listed.
duration: 1 year full time (or 2 years part time). 180 UK credits total = approx. 90 ECTS: two taught semesters of 120 credits plus a third semester for the 60-credit major project. Institution code H36.
study: Five compulsory Level 7 modules, all named on the official page: 'Soundtrack in Interactive Games' (30 credits — composition and production of music and sound in non-linear environments, plus integration and automation of audio layers using industry-standard game audio tools and middleware); 'Soundtrack in Narrative Film' (30 credits — film and narrative theory, then composition and production across music, sound design and foley, diegetic and non-diegetic); 'Sound Design for Visual Media' (30 credits — sound-design principles plus the studio techniques and technologies of current sound production); 'Industry, Innovation and Enterprise' (30 credits — research methods, business, legislation and professional practice in the music and sound industries); and the 'Major Project in Music and Sound for Film and Games' (60 credits — a substantial self-directed creative or technical work suitable for showing to employers). The stated deliverable is a professional showreel. Teaching is interactive lectures, workshops, one-to-one tutorials and practical work, with cross-course collaboration alongside the animation, games and film students.
recommendation: Content-wise this is by far the best match in this batch: real studios, Ableton and Logic, a producer as programme leader, game-audio middleware, and a showreel as the output — it teaches the craft he actually wants. Two caveats keep it out of A. First, money: GBP 17,950 tuition against a maximum GBP 4,000 discount, plus a CAS deposit and Hatfield living costs, so realistically GBP 30,000+ out of pocket with no fully funded route — that is the opposite of his stated preference. Second, the entry wording asks for a music-family degree or five years of industry experience, and expects everyone to already know their way around a studio and a DAW; he has neither a music degree nor pro experience, so his admission depends on convincing the programme tutor with self-taught production work. Concrete plan if he wants it: spend the next twelve months building a real body of Ableton production and sound-design work, then email Bruce Aisher directly for a read on his eligibility before spending anything.

Award is fully funded (tuition, living costs, travel). BUT three hard bars apply: it funds ONLY full-time TAUGHT master's courses that are UK-based, start in the autumn term and last 9–12 months ('Chevening will not support a course that is longer than 12 months in any form'; part-time, distance learning, PhD and research master's are excluded); the applicant must have at least TWO YEARS of work experience acquired AFTER the undergraduate degree, equivalent to 2,800 hours; and applicants must apply to three different eligible UK courses. Tunisia is NOT on the list. (3) COMMONWEALTH SCHOLARSHIPS — not available; Tunisia is not a Commonwealth country. Net effect: for this candidate the only realistic full-cost UK route is Chevening, and only if he has two years of post-graduation work experience by 6 October 2026 and picks a 12-month taught master's. acceptsNonMusic: VERDICT: CASE-BY-CASE, leaning NO without strong artistic evidence. There is NO sentence naming computer science or engineering as an accepted background. The rule is a bachelor in Computer Music / Sound Art / Composition and Music Theory 'oder eines gleichwertigen Studiums' (or an equivalent course of study), and equivalency is decided by the Dean of Studies before you are even invited to the exam. Mitigating quote: 'Im Rahmen des Zulassungskolloquiums wird gegebenenfalls festgelegt, in welchem Umfang die Zulassungsbewerber*innen Lehrveranstaltungen aus dem Bachelorstudium „Computermusik und Klangkunst" als Wahlfächer im Umfang bis zu 20 ECTS-AP zusätzlich zu den Lehrveranstaltungen des Masterstudiums zu absolvieren haben, um fehlende oder unzureichende Fähigkeiten gezielt auszugleichen.' — i.e. up to 20 ECTS of bachelor bridging courses can be prescribed to fill gaps. A BSc Software Engineering plus a genuinely strong artistic portfolio is the only realistic route here.
portfolio: Exact: 'two examples or your artistic work, each with a duration of approximately 5 minutes'. Upload at https://go.iem.at/cmkk as a single document or zip file labelled 'surname_firstname'. Either (1) a text file listing online links, or (2) compressed audio/video (mp3, h264 or similar), total size no more than approx. 150 MB, as a single zip. 'There is currently no way to adequately listen to multichannel files in the selection process, so all multichannel work must be reduced to stereo.' Hard warning, verbatim: 'If you do not submit examples of your artistic work, you will not be invited to the examination interview.'
audition: YES but REMOTE — a major advantage for a visa-needing applicant. Verbatim: 'The entrance exam takes place online.' and 'The oral examination interview takes place via Zoom.' The basis for the interview is formed by two artistic works (for example, sound installations, documentation about the performance or interpretation of music compositions for computer, the development of instruments used in computer music or other usages in the area of music informatics) that the applicant must have handed in as an audio-document or video-document before the application deadline.'

entry: A completed bachelor degree; Czech at B1 (CEFR) for international applicants; full round-1 portfolio (below) uploaded by the works deadline; and 40/60 points minimum across both rounds, with a minimum score in each sub-exam. Non-FAMU bachelor graduates must additionally attach a CV with address/email/phone, proof of the passed state bachelor examination, and a school-certified transcript of all courses with grades. Maximum admitted: 6 students.
acceptsNonMusic: FORMALLY YES, PRACTICALLY NO — this corrects the previous 'No'. The official document states the master is "přístupné absolventům a absolventkám bakalářského studia studijního programu Zvuková tvorba FAMU, případně též absolventům a absolventkám jiného vysokoškolského studijního programu" (open to graduates of FAMU's own BA in Sound Design, or possibly also to graduates of ANOTHER university study programme). So a software-engineering BSc is not barred by rule. But the round-2 oral exam requires theoretical knowledge "na úrovni absolventa bakalářského studia Zvukové tvorby FAMU" (at the level of a FAMU Sound Design BA graduate) plus musical erudition, and round 1 demands sound works produced during his bachelor. Only 6 places. Effectively closed to him.
portfolio: EXACT, from the official 2026/27 specific conditions (uploaded via https://prihlaska.amu.cz after the application closes and the fee is paid): (1) A list of ALL your own sound works created during bachelor studies — audiovisual or multimedia works, music recordings, radio and theatre sound work — each with title, genre, director's first and last name, plus production, running time and year of production, ordered by date of creation, INCLUDING works still in progress. (2) TWO audiovisual works on whose sound component you contributed significantly, with detailed written explications for both, PLUS your own theoretical work in the field. (3) A written project for master's study at FAMU: your intended specialisation, expected study outputs, which elective courses at FAMU or other universities you would take, and any interest in a study-abroad placement. FORMATS: files named "TASK NUMBER - TASK NAME - SURNAME FIRSTNAME" without diacritics; audio as WAV; video preferably MP4/MOV, H.264, max 10 Mbit/s; all written documents as PDF with a header giving programme, name and address. A SIGNED SWORN DECLARATION OF AUTHORSHIP is mandatory, and it explicitly requires you to declare whether generative AI was used (permitted only for research, language/grammar checking, or consulting narrative quality of finished text) — failing to respect this means the admission condition is not met.
audition: TWO ROUNDS, and round 2 is IN PERSON IN PRAGUE. Round 1 (2026/27 date: 14 Sept 2026) assesses talent from the submitted works only, with no applicant present; the commission decides who advances. Round 2 (2026/27 date: 17 Sept 2026, prezenčně) is an oral examination before the departmental board: the master's project and the list of your own sound works form the basis of the interview; you must demonstrate theoretical knowledge of the artistic and technical problems of the field at the level of a FAMU Sound Design BA graduate, AND musical erudition by one of — playing a musical instrument (melodic, rhythmic OR ELECTRONIC), singing, or another suitable form of live performance. You then also sit a PITCH-MEMORY TEST and a RHYTHMIC DICTATION. Pass mark 40 of 60 points overall plus a minimum in every sub-exam.

Two specialisations confirmed: 'Zvuková produkce a nahrávání' (Sound Production and Recording, 72 compulsory credits) and 'Akustika a audiovizuální technika' (Acoustics and Audiovisual Technology, 65 compulsory credits). The remaining elective-compulsory and free-elective credit split was not restated on the programme record and is UNVERIFIED at that level of detail.
study: The Sound Production and Recording specialisation covers recording technique for different instruments and building the mix, studio practice, audio effects design, compression algorithms, hardware and software implementation of audio processing, sound analysis, multimedia/interactive/VR audio, and room acoustics. The JAMU cooperation gives access to filmmaking and multimedia-composition subjects. Note for calibration: the linked BACHELOR programme is described by the faculty as 67% electrical engineering and 33% arts content — this is an engineering degree with an arts component, not the reverse.
recommendation: Still the best 'leverage your CS degree' option in the region — DSP, audio software, effects and plugin design and studio recording in one degree, with JAMU artistic subjects alongside. It would make him an audio engineer or audio developer rather than a DJ, but it is the one route where his existing background is an asset. Verification sharpened two blockers: there is a real written entrance exam in acoustics, analogue low-frequency technology, electroacoustics and digital audio signal processing that a software-only curriculum does not prepare him for, and the whole programme is taught in Czech. A third, smaller flag: accreditation runs out 1 May 2028, mid-way through a 2027 intake, so confirm re-accreditation. On the plus side, the June–July application window is late enough to give him another year of Czech and DSP preparation, and there is no portfolio to build.

scholarshipDetail: GENERAL EMJM RULES RELEVANT TO A TUNISIAN APPLICANT: Tunisia is an Erasmus+ PARTNER COUNTRY (not a Programme Country), so a Tunisian applicant competes in the non-EU pool. Under the EMJM 2021-2027 rules the scholarship is a single all-inclusive unit contribution of 1,400 EUR per month for up to 24 months, PLUS a full waiver of the programme's participation costs. The older EMJMD (2014-2020) model of a separate travel allowance (1,000-3,000 EUR/year) and a 1,000 EUR installation allowance NO LONGER APPLIES to newly funded programmes, although several third-party scholarship websites still quote those figures — these are misleading. EMJM rules also cap the number of scholarships that may be awarded to students of any single nationality, which is why the Partner Country pool is the relevant competition. A candidate may apply to a MAXIMUM OF THREE different EMJM programmes per intake and can hold only one scholarship — UNVERIFIED against the current official rules for the 2027 call and MUST be confirmed before submitting.
deadline: Applications for the 37 new programmes open in AUTUMN 2026 for a September 2027 start. Individual deadlines are set per consortium and are not centrally published. NO CENTRAL EMJM DEADLINE EXISTS — each consortium runs its own.
study: The European Commission announced that 37 Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters projects were selected under the latest Erasmus+ call. QUOTE from the official Erasmus+ page: these programmes 'will be opening for student applications in the autumn of 2026 to start programmes in September 2027.' THIS IS EXACTLY THE CANDIDATE'S INTAKE. The official page names only a sample of the 37 and does NOT publish the full list; among the named examples only 'European Master in Animation' is creative-sector. A third-party list (erasmuscatalogue.com, NOT OFFICIAL) enumerates all 37 and contains NO dedicated music, sound design or audio programme in the new cohort — the closest are ReAnima (animation) and WAVES Plus (acoustics and vibration ENGINEERING, a technical not artistic programme). CONCLUSION: the September 2027 opportunity in sound/music rests on the EXISTING catalogue programmes (ReSound, DIGICREA, RESONO), not on the new cohort. The third-party enumeration is UNVERIFIED and the official EACEA catalogue should be re-checked once the 37 are added to it during autumn 2026.

recommendation: AVOID FOR HIM — not because there is anything wrong with the programme, but because it fails him on four independent counts simultaneously, and the previous record's 'long-shot' framing was too generous. To be clear about what it IS: a genuinely free, genuinely public, genuinely accredited 120-ECTS in-person master's at Greece's national art school, confirmed in the Ministry of Education register at zero tuition for everyone including non-EU nationals. That is a rare and real thing and worth keeping in the database. But for him: (1) IT IS NOT HIS SUBJECT. The Ministry's own description makes the frame explicitly CONTEMPORARY VISUAL ARTS — time-based, interactive and computational media, with theoretical study of photography, cinematography, videography and digital computer systems. Sound art is at most tolerated; music production, audio engineering and electronic music are absent. (2) IT IS TAUGHT IN GREEK, which he does not speak, in a programme assessed largely through critique and oral defence. (3) HE WOULD ENTER ONLY THROUGH THE EXCEPTION CLAUSE, admitted purely on submitted artistic work, judged by a fine-arts jury against fine-arts graduates — and he has no portfolio and no fine-arts background whatever. (4) THE TIMING IS PROBABLY WRONG: the 19th cycle (2026-2028) was called on 16 June 2026 and has closed, and on a biennial reading the next intake is 2028-2030, a full year past his September 2027 target. If he wants to keep it alive at all, one email to artdm@asfa.gr settles it: is admission annual or biennial and when is the next call; has the exception clause ever admitted an engineering graduate; is any teaching possible in English; and send the current portfolio guidelines. Realistically, close the file.

study: VERIFIED module-by-module from the official DCSL34 accreditation PDF. YEAR 1 (60 CFA): Storia della musica elettroacustica 6; Ritmica della musica contemporanea 6; Esecuzione e interpretazione della musica elettroacustica — Ambienti esecutivi e di controllo per il live electronics 6; Composizione musicale elettroacustica 18 (INDIVIDUAL lesson); Informatica musicale 6; Tecnologie e tecniche della ripresa e della registrazione audio 2; Analisi compositiva 6; Acustica degli spazi musicali 4; Lingua straniera comunitaria 6. YEAR 2 (60 CFA): Storia della musica elettroacustica 6; Esecuzione e interpretazione — Ambienti esecutivi multimodali e interattivi 6; Composizione musicale informatica 18 (INDIVIDUAL); Informatica musicale 6; Tecnologie e tecniche della ripresa e della registrazione audio 2; Acustica degli strumenti musicali 4; a scelta dello studente 6; Prova finale (COME/02, composizione musicale elettroacustica) 12. THE DECISIVE DETAIL, newly verified from the published syllabus of Prof. Mario Salvucci (Informatica musicale COME/05): BIENNIO YEAR 1 = programming in Max MSP + java/javascript/nodejs; gen~/genexpr/C++ implementation of synthesis algorithms; adaptive filters; deterministic chaos, self-similar structures, strange attractors, flocking; MACHINE LEARNING — Markov chains, generative grammars, genetic algorithms, neural networks, GAN/StyleGAN/VAE, Stable Diffusion and GPT; ML libraries in Max (ml5js, MediaPipe, Magenta, Essentia); TensorFlow. BIENNIO YEAR 2 = introduction to C++ (control structures, functions, classes, pointers, dynamic memory) and to JUCE, culminating in implementing a full subtractive synthesizer AS A PLUGIN (MIDI in/sound out, oscillators, envelopes, polyphony and voice handling, modulation, filtering, GUI, host parameter communication); sound design of dynamic systems (artificial, natural, idiophone, mechanical, organic sources); Jitter, matrix/tensor operations, real-time video-audio interaction, OpenGL pipeline and SHADER PROGRAMMING, glitch/pixel-sort/databending algorithms, raytracing/raymarching; physical modelling (mass-spring, string, bowed instrument, waveguides). The composition syllabus (Prof. Silvia Lanzalone, COME/02) biennio year 1 covers composing the soundscape and acoustic ecology, intermedia Sound Art, SOUND INSTALLATION projects, multimedia/intermedia interaction with image and dance, electronic lutherie and sound design for augmented instruments (sensors, feedback systems, embedded systems); year 2 covers generative music, open forms, ecosystems and non-deterministic processes. Each year you deliver an original composition project supervised by the teacher.
recommendation: The strongest single find in this batch. Two things now verified change the picture completely: (1) the admission bar for a non-music graduate is just TWO original works plus an interview — the lowest documented bar of the six; (2) the biennio informatics syllabus is, in substance, an audio-software-engineering degree — he would spend year 2 writing C++ and building a polyphonic synthesizer plugin in JUCE, and year 1 doing ML for music in Max/TensorFlow. His BSc is a direct, compounding asset, not a handicap. The composition side is also more craft-oriented than assumed: sound design, DAW editing and montage, installations, augmented instruments, generative music. THE OBSTACLE IS ITALIAN — instruction is in Italian, the exam is on-site in Rome, and non-EU entry runs through Universitaly. Also note the aesthetic: this is art electronic music and sound art, not club or dancefloor production; it will make him a formidable sound designer and audio programmer, not a house producer. Realistic path: start Italian now (roughly 12 months to a usable level before the spring 2027 exam), and build two strong original audiovisual/electronic works.

I predetti titoli debbono essere coerenti con il corso prescelto.' Admission test: 'accertamento delle competenze musicali (storia della Musica Elettroacustica, Analisi d'ascolto, Teoria musicale), accertamento delle competenze in acustica e psicoacustica, informatica e tecnologie elettroacustiche, esame del curriculum di studi e/o artistico-professionale, e colloquio per verifica delle motivazioni e attività svolte.'
acceptsNonMusic: QUOTE: '...è riservata agli studenti in possesso di diploma accademico di primo livello, o di diploma di laurea, o di diploma di Conservatorio... Possono essere altresì ammessi studenti in possesso di altro titolo di studio equivalente conseguito all'estero e riconosciuto idoneo. I predetti titoli debbono essere coerenti con il corso prescelto.' Verdict: CASE-BY-CASE — 'diploma di laurea' (any bachelor's degree) is explicitly listed, and a foreign equivalent is explicitly admissible, but the final clause requires the title to be 'coerenti con il corso prescelto' (coherent with the chosen course). A software-engineering BSc is a plausible coherence argument for 'musica elettronica e tecnologie del suono' but is not guaranteed, and the musical-competence part of the entrance exam is a hard filter.

entry: CONFIRMED AND VERBATIM: 'L'accesso ai corsi di II livello è riservato a chi in possesso di Diploma Accademico di I livello, di Laurea di I livello o di Diploma di Conservatorio vecchio ordinamento.' A Laurea di I livello — any three-year university degree — is accepted as a plain qualifying title. His BSc qualifies. CORRECTION: the previous report framed this as conditional, claiming university graduates may apply only with 'adeguata e documentata preparazione' and with debiti formativi assigned. That conditional wording does NOT appear on the admission page as fetched; the published rule is unconditional. Bridging coursework may still be assigned in practice, but do not report it as a published entry condition.
acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY — the formal door is open, the examination door is not. Entry qualification: a Laurea di I livello is explicitly and unconditionally accepted, so his BSc qualifies him to APPLY. But he is exempt from neither exam: he must sit the written electroacoustic analysis (exemption limited to Musica Elettronica/Musica Applicata first-level diploma holders) AND the second exam covering lettura cantata, intonation, rhythm, ear training and music history (exemption limited to conservatoire first-level diploma holders). That is a full musicianship examination for a man with no conservatoire training, no music degree and no formal theory. Eligible to apply is not the same as able to pass.
portfolio: CONFIRMED. Before the exam date, candidates email 'alcuni propri lavori (audio, multimediali, etc…) ed un curriculum vitae' to mets@conservatoriocuneo.it using PERMANENT sharing links (Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive) — explicitly not time-limited links. The oral then requires him to present and defend his own electronic compositions. NOTE ON A PREVIOUS OVERSTATEMENT: the previous report claimed the oral demands 'documentation of live-set executions', and treated that as a unique reward for a DJ practice. That specific requirement was not visible on the admission page in this pass. Live-set documentation is very likely welcome as supporting evidence, but do not treat it as a published requirement or as a structural advantage he can bank on.
audition: CONFIRMED, TWO-PART, and the second part is the problem. FIRST EXAM (early September): a WRITTEN component, 'Analisi di un brano elettroacustico' — analysis of an electroacoustic piece supplied by the commission. Exemption applies only to holders of a first-level diploma in Musica Elettronica or Musica Applicata, so HE IS NOT EXEMPT and must sit it. Plus an ORAL component: presentation of his own composed works, demonstrated knowledge of audio editing software, twentieth-century music history, history of electroacoustic music, acoustics and psychoacoustics, and a motivational interview. SECOND EXAM: verbatim, 'I candidati in possesso di diploma accademico di I livello di conservatorio sono esonerati dalla prova' — exemption is limited strictly to holders of a first-level CONSERVATOIRE academic diploma. A foreign university BSc does NOT exempt him. He must therefore sit a conventional musicianship examination covering ear training, lettura cantata (sight-singing), intonation and rhythm, and music history to triennio standard. For someone with no conservatory training and no music degree this is a real, substantial obstacle requiring roughly a year of dedicated preparation. CORRECTION: the previous report claimed the METS FAQ describes biennio admission more lightly, as merely a motivational interview, and flagged a 'tension' to resolve. The FAQ as fetched says no such thing — it simply links to the two admission-exam pages. There is no conflicting lighter description and no ambiguity to exploit. The exam pages are authoritative and they are strict.

The conservatoire publishes an annual 'AMMISSIONI A.A. 20XX/20XX' notice; the 2026/2027 notice appeared around July 2026, which is a PRIOR CYCLE — confirm the 2027/2028 dates directly. Admission exams sit in early September, teaching starts November. Non-EU applicants must complete Universitaly pre-enrolment on the Ministry's separate and earlier calendar. Note the July-notice/September-exam rhythm is TIGHT for a candidate who must also obtain a visa.

languageReq: UNVERIFIED — CONFIRMED AS A GENUINE GAP. No Italian level is published anywhere on the METS admission pages, which is unusual and materially unhelpful. Italian state conservatoires generally require or test B2. Given that the admission process here is heavily oral — a motivational interview, a discussion of his works, and an examination in music history — functional Italian is a practical necessity regardless of what is formally demanded. Ask mets@conservatoriocuneo.it directly.

study: Composition and sound design at second level. Detailed module list UNVERIFIED — the METS study-plan page lists course titles but not inline syllabi. Request the piano di studi from METS.
recommendation: VALUE VERDICT: CONDITIONAL. RATING: B. — A genuine, cheap, well-accredited degree at a serious electronic music school, blocked by one real obstacle that he can only remove with a year of deliberate work. Downgraded from the previous report's enthusiasm on two counts: the supposed FAQ 'tension' suggesting a lighter interview-based admission does not exist, and the 'documented live-set executions' requirement that was said to reward his DJ practice was not found on the page. Neither of the softening factors the previous agent relied on survives verification. What survives is solid: METS is a dedicated electronic music school inside a state conservatoire, a Laurea di I livello is unconditionally accepted as an entry title, the ISEE parificato should drive his fees to near-nothing, and Cuneo has the lowest living costs of any option here. Against that: he must pass an ear-training, sight-singing and music-history examination to triennio standard, plus a written analysis of an electroacoustic piece, in Italian, with no published language level to prepare against. Actions for autumn 2026, in writing to mets@conservatoriocuneo.it: (1) confirm that a foreign three-year Software Engineering degree does not exempt him from either prova, and ask what standard the second prova expects; (2) ask what Italian level is required or tested; (3) request the Regolamento contributi for the lowest ISEE parificato band. Practical judgement: he should apply here as a SECOND choice behind Rovigo, and treat the musicianship gap as work to do rather than a reason to walk away — basic ear training and solfège are the recurring obstacle across the whole Italian conservatoire sector and closing that gap raises his ceiling everywhere, not just at Cuneo. Do not make this his only application.

entry: NOW CONFIRMED — this was UNVERIFIED in the previous report and is no longer. The dedicated Biennio TS admission page states verbatim: 'L'accesso ai corsi di II livello è riservato a chi in possesso di Diploma Accademico di I livello, di Laurea di I livello o di Diploma di Conservatorio vecchio ordinamento.'
