acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY — CORRECTED DOWNWARD. The previous report called this 'LIKELY THE MOST OPEN OF ANY ITALIAN OPTION FOUND' and speculated that a sound-engineering degree would have no reason to demand solfège. That is now disproven from source: the second prova covering lettura cantata, intonation, rhythm, ear training and music history applies to this track identically, with exemption limited to conservatoire first-level diploma holders. He would sit it. The entry TITLE is open (Laurea di I livello explicitly accepted) and the FIRST exam is genuinely well-matched to him — a practical mix, a foley reel, an engineering portfolio and a motivational interview are all things a software engineer can build toward. But the musicianship examination stands, exactly as at DCSL34. Open on paper, gated in practice.
portfolio: CONFIRMED and now specific, where the previous report could only guess. Submit 'alcuni propri lavori (audio, multimediali, etc…) ed un curriculum vitae' to mets@conservatoriocuneo.it via permanent sharing links before the September exam. Critically, the oral requires an ORIGINAL FOLEY / VIDEO SOUND WORK plus prior sound engineering projects — so the portfolio year should produce, specifically: a foley-and-sound-design reel cut to picture, multitrack recordings he has engineered, mixes and masters, and any DSP or audio-software work salvageable from his engineering degree. He must also be able to mix a supplied multitrack under exam conditions, which is a trainable, concrete skill — genuinely the most learnable examination in this whole set, and one where his engineering brain is an asset rather than a handicap.
audition: MAJOR CORRECTION — THE PREVIOUS REPORT'S CENTRAL HOPE IS FALSE. The previous agent recorded this as 'UNVERIFIED for this track', stated that METS 'did not publish separate requirements' for Tecnico del Suono, cited the wrong page (/piani-di-studio/) as its source, and hypothesised that admission rests on 'an aptitude and motivational interview rather than a musicianship examination', calling this the 'single highest-value unanswered question'. METS DOES publish a dedicated admission page for this track — /info-per-iscrizioni/esami-di-ammissione-biennio-ts/ — and it disproves the hypothesis. The structure is: FIRST EXAM, practical component — 'Mixaggio e finalizzazione della registrazione su tracce indipendenti di un brano fornito dalla commissione', i.e. mix and finalise a multitrack supplied by the commission; exemption applies ONLY to holders of a first-level diploma in Tecnico del suono or Musica Elettronica (technical track), so he must sit it. Oral component — presentation of an original foley/video sound work, presentation of prior sound engineering projects, and a motivational interview. SECOND EXAM — verbatim, 'I candidati in possesso di diploma accademico di I livello di conservatorio sono esonerati dalla prova'. Exemption is again limited to conservatoire first-level diploma holders, so HE MUST SIT IT: lettura cantata, intonazione e ritmica, ear training, and storia e storiografia della musica to triennio standard. The musicianship hurdle applies here EXACTLY as it does at DCSL34. This track is not the open back door the previous report hoped it was.

recommendation: VALUE VERDICT: CONDITIONAL. RATING: B. — CORRECTED SIGNIFICANTLY. The previous report flagged this as 'INVESTIGATE AS A PRIORITY — potentially the best fit of all' on the hypothesis that admission rested on an aptitude interview rather than a musicianship exam. That question is now answered, and the answer is no: METS publishes a dedicated Biennio TS admission page the previous agent never found, and it imposes the same second prova (lettura cantata, ear training, storia della musica) on anyone without a conservatoire first-level diploma. The previous record also cited the wrong source URL. This is not the open door it was billed as. What remains genuinely attractive, and it is not nothing: DCSL61 is a real state second-cycle degree in SOUND ENGINEERING, the subject closest to his actual background and stated career interest; the entry title requirement explicitly accepts his Laurea di I livello; and the first exam — mixing a supplied multitrack, presenting an original foley/video sound work, presenting prior engineering projects, and a motivational interview — is the most learnable and most engineer-friendly assessment of any programme here. Verdict for him: apply, but as a co-equal second choice with DCSL34 and behind Rovigo, and only if he commits to closing the ear-training and solfège gap during the portfolio year. Between the two Cuneo tracks he should prefer THIS one over DCSL34 — same musicianship hurdle, but a first exam that plays to his strengths instead of testing compositional skills he does not have. entry: A completed first-cycle degree. CONFIRMED verbatim that a foreign graduate must submit, with the application or at latest at enrolment, a decision recognising equivalence of the first-cycle qualification from a competent Slovak institution, OR may ask UNIZA itself to recognise the document — UNIZA doing it in-house is a real convenience versus separate ministry nostrification. Slovak/Czech graduates in the SAME field with a weighted average up to 2.00 are admitted to Multimedia Engineering without an entrance exam; everyone else — including every foreign applicant and every applicant from a different field — goes through the selection procedure with an interview.
acceptsNonMusic: YES. No music degree, conservatory training or performance ability is required or assessed. The interview tests IT knowledge plus creative output and motivation. CONFIRMED. Note the 0.75 coefficient penalty applies only to non-informatics bachelors, which should not affect him.
portfolio: YES, AND THE SCORING IS NOW EXACT. CORRECTED AND SHARPENED from the previous record's vague 'up to 70 points combined'. The official rule sets a 100-point maximum built from: (a) weighted GPA from the first-cycle degree, scored 0-30 points scaled linearly from 30 points for a GPA of 1.50 or better down to 0 points at 3.00, then MULTIPLIED BY A COEFFICIENT OF 1.0 if the bachelor's was in the study field 'informatika' and 0.75 if in any other field; (b) at interview, demonstration of general knowledge of informatics and multimedia technologies, 0-40 points; (c) at interview, PRESENTATION OF THE APPLICANT'S CREATIVE ACTIVITY AND OUTPUTS in informatics and multimedia plus overall motivation to study, 0-30 points. Admitted candidates are ranked down to a 61-point floor. So a creative portfolio is worth up to 30 of 100 points and is scored ALONGSIDE, not instead of, IT knowledge — precisely the blend he will have. His Software Engineering degree should attract the 1.0 coefficient as an informatics-field award, but confirm that classification with the study office. Exact portfolio format still UNVERIFIED — request the current 'Zásady a pravidlá prijímacieho konania' and see https://kmikt.uniza.sk/index.php/uchadzaci/moznosti-studia/inzinierske-studium
audition: No audition. An in-person selection interview only ('prijímacie konanie vrátane prijímacieho pohovoru sa realizuje prezenčne formou výberového konania'). Note 'prezenčne' — in person, so he must plan to travel or request an accommodation. CONFIRMED.
deadline: CONFIRMED verbatim for the prior cycle: 'Termín podania prihlášky do 30. 4. 2026' for entry in 2026/2027. For SEPTEMBER 2027 entry expect ~30 April 2027 — later than his assumed Oct 2026 - Feb 2027 window. But the Slovak Government Scholarship application, if he pursues it, closes much earlier and is the real timeline driver. Decisions are posted within 30 days of the admission procedure.
opens: Winter/spring preceding the academic year via the UNIZA e-application portal.
duration: 2 years, full-time (denná forma), 120 ECTS. Still UNVERIFIED on the faculty's own programme sheet — confirm with the FEIT study office.
languageReq: SLOVAK AT B1 — CONFIRMED verbatim: an applicant who obtained his bachelor's abroad and applies for study in Slovak must submit, with the application or at latest at enrolment, a 'certifikát/doklad o úrovni znalostí zo slovenského jazyka minimálne na úrovni B1'. The rule explicitly adds that the language preparation and its certificate can be completed AT UNIZA before the admission procedure — a concrete, university-run route. This remains materially milder than PWr's C1 Polish fee-waiver threshold or a Czech-language talent examination.

study: Theoretical foundations of informatics; digital and analogue processing of IMAGE AND SOUND SIGNALS; processing and transmission of multimedia streams over communication technologies, networks and services; interface and application development. Through compulsory-elective subjects a student can specialise narrowly in AUDIO INFORMATION PROCESSING rather than image or graphics. Creatively oriented subjects are built in so graduates can create and process multimedia works at an appropriate technical, aesthetic and artistic level; the faculty names 'audio technician and designer' as a target job.
recommendation: CONFIRMED AS THE BEST BALANCED OPTION, AND THE RE-CHECK MADE THE CASE STRONGER, NOT WEAKER. Every load-bearing claim held up against the official admission-conditions page, and the scoring is now exact rather than approximate: a 100-point scale in which his first-cycle GPA is worth up to 30 points at a full 1.0 coefficient (because Software Engineering sits in the informatics field), general IT and multimedia knowledge up to 40, and PRESENTATION OF HIS CREATIVE WORK AND MOTIVATION up to 30. That is the only admission process among the six where a portfolio-building year and an engineering degree are additive rather than in tension. Free tuition for a Tunisian, an explicit audio-processing elective track, no audition, no aural test, no music degree needed, and the lowest living costs of any option. The only real gate is Slovak at B1 with a certificate — and the faculty explicitly says the preparation and certificate can be obtained at UNIZA before the admission procedure, which is the mildest language pathway in the slice and genuinely reachable in the twelve-plus months before an April 2027 deadline. One practical caveat to plan for: the interview is held in person in Žilina. Actions: (1) enrol in Slovak now and target a B1 certificate by early 2027, ideally via UNIZA's own preparation so the certificate is unimpeachable; (2) e-mail the FEIT study office for the current 'Zásady a pravidlá prijímacieho konania' and ask what the creative portfolio must contain and whether his degree counts as the informatika field for the 1.0 coefficient; (3) run the Slovak Government Scholarship application in parallel. READ WHAT THAT MEANS FOR HIM: only about 9 ECTS of the mandatory load is hands-on craft (The Art of Sound Engineering plus the Creative Workshop), against 8 ECTS of pedagogy and teaching methodology, 8 ECTS of research methodology, 6 ECTS of PEDAGOGICAL practice, and a 13 ECTS thesis-and-exam block. The degree trains sound-engineering LECTURERS AND RESEARCHERS. The general profile text does genuinely include the strands the previous record quoted — computer musicology, digital and multimedia technologies in audio production, electrical engineering, musical acoustics, and 'технології штучного інтелекту для аналізу, синтезу та обробки аудіо контенту' (AI technologies for the analysis, synthesis and processing of audio content) — but those are described as the programme's subject area, not as a set of production modules. Attestation is by public defence of a qualifying work plus an attestation exam; the OPP requires the thesis to present 'науково обґрунтоване розв'язання складної наукової задачі або мистецької проблеми' — a scientifically grounded solution to a complex research or artistic problem. For a man who wants to be an international DJ and producer, this is an academic degree with a studio attached, not a producer's education.
recommendation: DO NOT APPLY — AND THE ACADEMIC CASE FOR IT IS WEAKER THAN THE PREVIOUS RECORD CLAIMED. That record called this 'academically the best-matched programme in this slice' with a syllabus 'close to ideal' for a software engineer who wants to produce. Having extracted the actual master's component table from the official OPP, I am correcting that outright. The 90 ECTS break down as roughly 9 ECTS of hands-on craft (The Art of Sound Engineering, Creative-Performance Workshop) against 8 ECTS of pedagogy and teaching methodology, 8 ECTS of research methodology, 6 ECTS of pedagogical practice and a 13 ECTS thesis-and-attestation block. Ukrainian arts master's degrees of this shape train lecturers and researchers; the qualifying work must present a scientifically grounded solution to a research or artistic problem. That is not what turns a software engineer into a producer. Three further blockers, one of them newly verified. FIRST AND DECISIVE: Ukraine is at war. Kyiv is under regular missile and drone attack and martial law is in force. No responsible adviser sends a 22-year-old there for a discretionary arts master's starting September 2027, and an application he must commit to in late 2026 offers no way to hedge. SECOND, NEWLY VERIFIED: the OPP itself states that foreign students may obtain education only after completing a course in the Ukrainian language. The previous record treated this as an assumption; it is now confirmed from the Academy's own document. That is a year of his life on a language with no bearing on a career as an international DJ and producer. THIRD: the programme is only CONDITIONALLY accredited (deferred accreditation, NAZYAVO 13.01.2026, protocol No 1 (92), case No 1769/АС-25) — friction on top of the friction a Ukrainian wartime degree already carries. FOURTH: nobody will tell him the price; the official foreign-citizen tuition PDF exists but pages 2-3 contain no extractable digits, which I verified myself. VERDICT: record it, do not apply. Rating C. His September 2027 effort belongs in the EU, with Tbilisi as the paid fallback.

No DJing, no club-music production, no mixing/mastering curriculum.
recommendation: Free and prestigious, and the A2 German bar is remarkably low — but the entry gate is the wrong shape for him. The binding regulations require a bachelor in Electronic or Instrumental Composition; a software-engineering BSc lands him in the 'außerordentliche Begabung' exception, which he has no evidence to satisfy. And even if admitted, the content is contemporary art-music composition assessed on knowledge of new-music repertoire and compositional technique — the colloquium would expose the gap immediately. Nothing here builds DJ or dance-music production craft.

entry: CRITICAL CORRECTION — the official Eignungsprüfungsanforderungen page states: 'Voraussetzung ist der Nachweis eines abgeschlossenen künstlerischen Bachelor- oder Diplomstudiums oder eines gleichwertig anerkannten künstlerischen Studiengangs mit Schwerpunktsetzung im Bereich Musikproduktion (z.B. Tonmeister, Soundengineering, Musikregie etc.). Im Sinne eines künstlerischen Abschlusses gilt auch ein Bachelorstudium im Studiengang Ton und Bild.' A completed ARTISTIC bachelor or diploma (or equivalent recognised artistic degree) WITH AN EMPHASIS IN MUSIC PRODUCTION is mandatory. Plus German B2 (Goethe), plus passing the concentration-specific Eignungsprüfung. Aptitude-test fee €50 for the first application, €10 for each additional application (confirmed).
acceptsNonMusic: No — this is a hard correction to the earlier 'Check'. The requirement is not merely 'a bachelor's degree': it must be an artistic bachelor/diploma with a music-production emphasis, and the examples given are Tonmeister, sound engineering, Musikregie, or RSH's own Ton und Bild bachelor. A BSc in Software Engineering is neither artistic nor production-focused in the sense meant, so he is formally ineligible, before the audition is even considered.
portfolio: NOW EXACT (from the official Eignungsprüfungsanforderungen page). Jazz/Pop major pre-selection: a portfolio of FOUR TO SIX already-realised works (or excerpts) in different styles from the jazz/popular-music production field; one audio file/track package per work sample; TOTAL DURATION 15–20 MINUTES; accepted formats stereo, 5.1/7.1 or Atmos; stereo mixes as stereo .wav, multichannel as clearly labelled mono .wav files (5.1/7.1) or as an ADM file (Atmos); each work sample accompanied by a short description of how it was made. PLUS unedited videos of the applicant's own artistic performance on instrument/voice (jazz/pop) with improvisation or ad-libs, tempi and styles varying, own composition allowed, max 20 minutes total — with an important alternative for keyboard/jazz piano: 'die Einreichung von bis zu drei Stücken mit Improvisation mit Hilfe von elektronischen Instrumenten wie Keyboards, Synthesizern, DAWs (z.B. Ableton live) mit deutlich erkennbarem spielerisch-handwerklichem Anteil sowie erkennbar eigener Soundgestaltung' (up to three pieces with improvisation using keyboards, synths or DAWs such as Ableton Live, with clearly recognisable playing craft and own sound design). PLUS a motivation letter referencing the chosen major and a CV with certificates. (Classical major differs: 5–6 works, 30–45 minutes, plus three works from different stylistic periods on video.)
audition: Yes — a substantial ON-SITE examination (Präsenzprüfung) in Düsseldorf, in four parts: (1) artistic presentation on instrument or voice with the same repertoire as the pre-selection, plus a prepared solo transcription (or a short a cappella piece for jazz/pop voice) AND sight-reading / sight-singing; six copies of the scores or lead sheets must be brought. (2) An UNPREPARED practical task in the chosen major, e.g. a mix or an edit, typically one to two hours. (3) Written examinations of both musical and technical hearing: musical ear (~40 min: dictations from piano and from recordings, intonation hearing, error detection, short aural analysis, instrumentation hearing) and technical ear (~40 min: listening examples including technical artefacts, level judgement, formant hearing). (4) A Fachgespräch with the selection panel, max 30 minutes. Fee €50.
deadline: 1 March, published as a standing annual deadline: 'Der Bewerbungsschluss zum Wintersemester ist der 1. März.' Aptitude tests for Künstlerische Musikproduktion are held for the WINTER SEMESTER ONLY ('Für die Masterstudiengänge Künstlerische Musikproduktion und Musikfilmregie ... gibt es Eignungsprüfungen ausschließlich zum Wintersemester'). So a September/October 2027 start means applying by 1 March 2027. The date is a standing rule rather than a prior-cycle artefact, but confirm it is unchanged when the 2027 links open. (The earlier note that entry is possible in winter OR summer was wrong for this programme.)
opens: Not published; the muvac application links are opened roughly one month before each deadline (as stated for the sister programme).
duration: 4 semesters (2 years). ECTS total not stated on the programme page or the Modulplan page — UNVERIFIED.
study: Two majors: Classical Acoustic Music Production, and Jazz and Pop Music Production. Three interwoven strands over four semesters: practical production work across genres and formats using the most recent production methods; instrumental/vocal tuition with ensemble performance; and technical methodology plus musical analysis including acoustics and ear training. Goal is artistically independent, methodically grounded professional production work. CONFIRMED on the official page — genuinely the most production-focused public master in this batch.
recommendation: Content-wise this is the best genuine music-production master in the batch — a real Jazz/Pop production track, Atmos-aware, with mixing and editing as examined craft. It is also the most firmly closed to him. The prerequisite is an artistic bachelor with a music-production emphasis (Tonmeister, sound engineering, Musikregie, or RSH's Ton und Bild), which a software-engineering BSc is not; and even if that were waived, the on-site exam demands an instrumental/vocal performance with sight-reading, a live mixing task, and 80 minutes of written musical and technical ear tests, all in German at B2. Realistic only after a production-focused artistic bachelor plus years of instrument and ear training. Worth noting as a long-term aspiration and as a source of a training checklist — the Ableton/synth alternative for the keyboard performance shows what standard would eventually be expected — but not a 2027 target.

It does not advance the DJ/producer craft by a single hour of studio time, and it demands DSH/TestDaF-level German, which is the same 12-18 month investment TH Köln demands but for a much smaller payoff in his chosen direction. Two specific risks the previous record understated: the committee may simply rule a software-engineering BSc not fachverwandt to musicology and reject him on subject grounds regardless of how open the admission is, and the published 23 October deadline is a domestic date that is visa-impossible for a Tunisian national. institution: SAE Institute Milano (SAE Italia S.R.L. International Technology College — SAE / Navitas global chain)
programme: Produzione Audio / Audio Production and Music Technologies — Diploma Accademico di Primo Livello
whyChance: States it does not accept a non-music background
qualification: Diploma Accademico di PRIMO livello — a first-level, bachelor-equivalent AFAM academic diploma, legally recognised by the Italian Ministry of University and Research. A genuine, official Italian qualification — but BACHELOR level, not a master. CONFIRMED: SAE Milano is authorised for first-level diplomas only and has NO 'Diploma Accademico di secondo livello' anywhere in its catalogue.
accreditation: OFFICIAL — CONFIRMED, and the only officially accredited programme in this batch. SAE Institute Milano appears BY NAME on MUR's official register of legally recognised AFAM institutes, listed under Lombardia as 'SAE Institute. Creative media education – Milano'. It is a non-state institution operating inside the national AFAM framework, ministerially authorised under Ministerial Decree 280 of 16 May 2017 pursuant to Art. 11 of DPR 212/2005. An AFAM first-level diploma is equated to a three-year laurea within the Italian higher-education qualifications framework. CRUCIAL CAVEAT, now firmly established: this official status covers the FIRST-LEVEL diploma only. Any SAE Italy course not on that ministerial list — including the Electronic Music Production and Urban Music Production short courses — is a purely private certificate with no legal academic value.
tuition: UNVERIFIED — no published figure for the three-year diploma anywhere on the official site. This is the single biggest information gap in this batch and stands in sharp contrast to SAE Amsterdam and Abbey Road, which publish every instalment total.
otherFees: UNVERIFIED — no enrolment, exam or materials fees published.
totalCost: UNVERIFIED — no tuition figure is published for any SAE Milano programme. Three years of unpublished fees plus Milan living costs, which are among the highest in Italy. He cannot budget for this without phoning the school directly.
scholarshipDetail: Genuinely valuable and unique in this batch, though amounts UNVERIFIED. Because SAE Milano is a recognised AFAM institution, its students can apply for Italian regional right-to-study grants (borse di studio per il diritto allo studio universitario); in Lombardy these are administered regionally and are generally open to non-EU students meeting income and merit criteria. No other private provider in this batch gives access to state right-to-study funding. Amounts and deadlines UNVERIFIED — confirm with the Lombardy regional authority, not the school. SAE Italy also runs occasional sponsored scholarships, e.g. the Billboard Italia 'Women in Music' bando covering 100% of tuition (not applicable to him).
entry: CONFIRMED. Domestic: minimum age 18; high school diploma or equivalent validated by the relevant authorities for Italy; aptitude interview, with possible additional skill assessments. International (his category): minimum age 18; certified translation of a qualification equivalent to the Italian high school diploma; certified Italian at minimum B2 CEFR; aptitude interview and possible additional assessments.
acceptsNonMusic: Not applicable in the way he needs. Entry is UNDERGRADUATE: the requirement is a high school diploma or foreign equivalent 'validated by the relevant authorities for Italy' — not a bachelor's. No music background is required, and no portfolio. His BSc would over-qualify him for a programme that sits BELOW his current level.
portfolio: No portfolio required — CONFIRMED. Admission is by aptitude interview and possible skills assessment only. Notable as the only programme in this batch with no portfolio gate.
audition: Aptitude interview ('colloquio attitudinale'), with the Academic Board reserving discretion to request additional assessments evaluating suitability.
deadline: UNVERIFIED — no application deadline published on the course page. Non-EU visa pre-enrolment deadlines are set nationally and are typically EARLIER than the school's own; both must be confirmed.
opens: UNVERIFIED — not published on the course page. Non-EU applicants must in practice work backwards from Italian national pre-enrolment (Universitaly) timelines, which typically run in spring/early summer preceding an October start.
duration: 3 years, 180 CFA (the AFAM credit unit, equivalent in weight to ECTS). CONFIRMED on the official course page.
englishTest: IELTS is NOT the relevant test and is not an entry route. The published language requirement for international students is certified ITALIAN at B2 CEFR. Even though teaching is bilingual English/Italian, no English test substitutes for the Italian certification.
study: Three years, 180 CFA. Foundational technical training in acoustics, recording, mixing and mastering, combined with contemporary applications: immersive systems, game audio, sound design and AI in music production. Delivery is explicitly project-based, 'replicating industry dynamics'. Internships and placements are organised during the programme. Career outcomes: recording engineer, music producer, sound designer, live sound engineer, audio programmer for games.
recommendation: Officially accredited, visa-viable, and still the wrong programme — the mismatch is level and language, not quality. This is the only programme in this batch verified at the ministry itself: SAE Institute Milano is named on MUR's official AFAM register, which means a real Italian qualification and, uniquely here, a plausible route to a study visa. But it is a three-year bachelor-equivalent he does not need, and international entry demands certified Italian at B2 — a requirement that bilingual English/Italian teaching does not waive, and which he cannot realistically reach and certify before an October 2027 start. Three things are worth carrying forward. First, it proves SAE can hold genuine accreditation where it seeks it, which throws its unaccredited Amsterdam certificates and any Spanish 'máster' claims into unflattering relief — always check the national register, never the school's own wording. Second, its AFAM status opens Italian REGIONAL right-to-study grants (borse di studio) to non-EU students, the only state funding identified anywhere in this batch; if Italy interests him at all, that mechanism is worth understanding, though he must confirm amounts and deadlines with the Lombardy regional authority rather than the school. Third, and decisively for planning: SAE Milano has NO second-level authorisation at all, so there is no Italian SAE master coming — do not wait for one. One practical warning if he ever reconsiders Italy: SAE publishes no fees anywhere, so he cannot budget without phoning 02 8912 0540, and non-EU Universitaly pre-enrolment deadlines typically fall well before the school's own.

institution: Εθνικό και Καποδιστριακό Πανεπιστήμιο Αθηνών / National and Kapodistrian University of Athens (NKUA)
programme: ΠΜΣ «Βυζαντινή Μουσικολογία και Ψαλτική Τέχνη» / MA in Byzantine Musicology & Psaltic Art — Department of Music Studies…
whyChance: Wants professional audio experience he does not have
qualification: Δίπλωμα Μεταπτυχιακών Σπουδών (ΔΜΣ) in Byzantine Musicology & Psaltic Art, with two specialisations: (1) Βυζαντινή Μουσικολογία / Byzantine Musicology, (2) Ψαλτική Τέχνη / Psaltic Art. 90 ECTS over 3 academic semesters — CONFIRMED, Άρθρο 3-4 of ΦΕΚ 2643/2018. A genuine state-recognised second-cycle degree that supports a Greek student residence permit. This part of the prior record was correct.
accreditation: State-recognised, established by published Government Gazette decree under ν. 4485/2017. NOTE — Άρθρο 6 of the founding decree authorises the programme to operate only ΜΕΧΡΙ ΤΟ ΑΚΑΔΗΜΑΪΚΟ ΕΤΟΣ 2027-28 ('until academic year 2027-28'), subject to meeting evaluation criteria. A September 2027 intake would therefore begin in the final authorised year and would finish (3 semesters) beyond it, requiring a renewal decree. Additionally, Greek law 5094/2024 re-regulated all ΠΜΣ and forced many to be re-founded with fresh decrees and possibly revised fees — the 2018 instruments cited here may have been superseded. Both points need confirmation with the department before relying on any figure.
tuition: €2,100 total (€700 x 3 semesters) — the SAME rate he would pay as a Tunisian national. Greek public ΠΜΣ fees are set by decree as a single figure with no EU/non-EU differential, so the prior record was right that there is no separate non-EU rate but wrong on the amount. Caveat: these are the 2018 decreed figures and law 5094/2024 may have prompted a re-founding with revised fees — confirm with the Secretariat.
otherFees: ΔΟΑΤΑΠ recognition of his Tunisian BSc (a mandatory, slow and separately-charged process), certified translations of degree and transcripts, Greek student visa (type D) and residence-permit fees, mandatory health insurance, and proof of sufficient means for the visa. None of these are quantified in the official instruments — obtain current figures from the Greek consulate and ΔΟΑΤΑΠ if this were ever pursued.
totalCost: Tuition is genuinely cheap at €2,100 for the whole degree. Athens living costs over 18 months dominate — budget roughly €700-900 per month, i.e. approximately €12,500-16,000, plus ΔΟΑΤΑΠ, translation, visa, permit and insurance costs. Order of magnitude €15,000-19,000 all-in. Living-cost figures are my estimate, not an official publication.
scholarshipDetail: No dedicated scholarship. The only relief published in the regulation is the standard statutory fee EXEMPTION under ν. 4485/2017: full waiver of tuition for students whose individual income does not exceed 100%, and family income 70%, of the Greek national median equivalised disposable income per ELSTAT, capped at 30% of admitted students and usable for one ΠΜΣ only. This is means-tested against Greek statistical thresholds and in practice requires Greek tax documentation, making it awkward-to-impossible for a first-year non-EU arrival. Crucially it is a fee waiver worth at most €2,100 — it is NOT a stipend and would not cover a single month of living costs. There is no funded route here.
entry: CORRECTED against ΦΕΚ 4568/2018, Άρθρα 3-4. Άρθρο 3: holders of a first-cycle degree from ANY department of a Greek ΑΕΙ, or from an equivalent foreign institution RECOGNISED BY ΔΟΑΤΑΠ (the Greek foreign-qualification recognition body). The prior record's paraphrase about the Coordinating Committee being satisfied of 'specialised knowledge or experience in the cognitive subjects' does not appear in the founding text — the real gate is not a discretionary clause but a hard competitive examination. Mandatory documents: application form; CV; certified copy of degree; peer-reviewed publications if any; evidence of professional/research/artistic activity if any; ID; TWO letters of recommendation from university professors; C1 English certificate; Greek proficiency certificate for foreign applicants; ΔΟΑΤΑΠ certificate of equivalence for foreign degrees. Selection criteria: (a) degree grade of AT LEAST 7.5/10 — the Committee may waive this by specially reasoned decision only if the candidate holds a second university degree, a master's, notable published/research/artistic work, or significant professional experience in cognate fields; (b) WRITTEN ENTRANCE EXAMINATIONS for BOTH specialisations on the programme's subject matter, with syllabus and prescribed bibliography announced in advance; (c) a PRACTICAL EXAMINATION before a panel of professors for the Psaltic Art specialisation; (d) a PERSONAL INTERVIEW before the Coordinating Committee. Final ranking: Byzantine Musicology = 50% written exam + 50% interview; Psaltic Art = 30% written + 50% practical + 20% interview. Intake is 20 students per academic year, selected separately per specialisation.
acceptsNonMusic: Formally yes — Άρθρο 3 admits graduates of any department, and a Software Engineering BSc is not excluded on paper. In substance no. He must pass a written entrance examination in Byzantine musicology, sat in Greek against a prescribed Greek bibliography, and then a Greek-language interview assessing his command of the field's scholarly literature. The departmental page further records that for the Psaltic Art specialisation candidates must hold a Diploma of Byzantine Music with grade 'Excellent' from a recognised Greek music school or equivalent studies. Formal eligibility here is meaningless without the chant training and the Greek he does not have.
portfolio: No portfolio in the creative-industry sense. What is required instead is documentary: CV, certified degree, ΔΟΑΤΑΠ equivalence certificate, two academic reference letters, and optional evidence of research/artistic activity. His planned production portfolio would carry no weight — it is not a scored criterion.
audition: SPECIFIED, contrary to the prior record's 'UNVERIFIED'. Written entrance examination for both specialisations. For the Psaltic Art specialisation there is a compulsory PRACTICAL EXAMINATION in Byzantine chant before a faculty panel, worth 50% of the final ranking, with specifications set out in each year's call. Plus a personal interview for all candidates who pass the written stage. This is a competitive entrance-exam admission, not a portfolio review.
deadline: Set in each year's call, typically September, and extendable by decision of the Department Assembly. The most recent documented cycle (2022-23) had a deadline of 16 September 2022 with submission through the university's electronic protocol system. Successful candidates must enrol within 15 days of the Assembly's decision. Exact 2027 dates will only be known when the June 2027 call is published.

Άρθρο 4 of ΦΕΚ 4568/2018: the call (προκήρυξη) is published EACH JUNE by decision of the Department Assembly, on the department and university websites, announcing the specialisations offered, places per specialisation, entrance-examination dates, examinable subjects, syllabus and bibliography per specialisation, and required documents. This directly contradicts his planning assumption that calls open October 2026 - February 2027: for a September 2027 start the call would not appear until around June 2027.
duration: 90 ECTS over three (3) academic semesters, full-time — CONFIRMED verbatim, Άρθρο 4 of ΦΕΚ 2643/2018.
languageReq: FULLY SPECIFIED in ΦΕΚ 4568/τ.Β΄/18-10-2018, Άρθρο 4 — the prior record's 'UNVERIFIED' was wrong, the requirements are published and they are brutal for him. TWO separate certificates are demanded: (1) «Πιστοποιητικό γλωσσομάθειας αγγλικής γλώσσας, επιπέδου C1» — an English proficiency certificate at CEFR level C1, mandatory document no. 8; knowledge of a further European language is a positive factor. Level is proven either by holding the diploma or by sitting a departmental examination. (2) «Οι αλλοδαποί υποψήφιοι φοιτητές θα πρέπει να προσκομίζουν πιστοποιητικό επάρκειας στην ελληνική γλώσσα» — FOREIGN candidates must additionally produce a certificate of PROFICIENCY IN GREEK. As a Tunisian national he falls squarely in this category. He has no Greek whatsoever, so this is an absolute, non-negotiable blocker independent of everything else.
englishTest: CEFR C1 English certificate REQUIRED as a mandatory application document (ΦΕΚ 4568/2018, Άρθρο 4, item 8). C1 corresponds to roughly IELTS 7.0-8.0 or TOEFL iBT ~95-110. His English is described as 'working' and he has taken no test; C1 is a demanding bar he would have to clear on top of, not instead of, the Greek proficiency certificate. The prior record's 'no IELTS/TOEFL band is published' was incorrect — a CEFR level is published, which is stricter and more specific than a band.
study: Byzantine musicology, Byzantine notation, theory, manuscript sources, and performance practice of Orthodox ecclesiastical psalmody, taught and examined in Greek. Contains ZERO sound design, ZERO music production, ZERO audio engineering, ZERO electronic music and ZERO music technology. There is no overlap of any kind with his stated field or with a DJ/producer career.
recommendation: The programme is REAL, is a genuine master's, and is accredited — but almost every substantive claim in the prior record was wrong, and the record's central 'finding' collapses. CORRECTIONS: (1) LANGUAGE — it is taught in GREEK, not English. The founding decree ΦΕΚ 2643/τ.Β΄/6-7-2018 Άρθρο 4 says «Τα μαθήματα διεξάγονται στην ελληνική γλώσσα». Only the thesis may optionally be written in English. The prior agent appears to have mistaken the FEK's bilingual programme TITLE for the language of instruction. The claim that this is 'the only English-taught music master's in Greece' is therefore false. (2) FEES — €700 per semester, €2,100 total, not €3,000. (3) LANGUAGE CERTIFICATES — not 'unverified' but precisely specified: a C1 English certificate AND, for foreign applicants specifically, a certificate of proficiency in GREEK. (4) ADMISSION — not 'unverified' but a competitive written entrance examination in Greek on a prescribed Byzantine-musicology bibliography, plus interview, plus a 50%-weighted practical chant audition for the performance track, plus a minimum degree grade of 7.5/10, plus two academic reference letters, plus ΔΟΑΤΑΠ recognition of his foreign degree. (5) TIMING — calls are published each JUNE with a September deadline, not October-February as his planning assumed. scholarshipDetail: CONFIRMED that AFAM students (conservatoires included) are eligible for the regional DSU borsa di studio — the Lazio DISCO and DSU Toscana 2026/27 bandi both cover AFAM institutions. The 2026/27 national minimum amounts are approximately €2,850 (in sede) rising to about €7,072–€7,171 for a 'fuori sede' student — the figure quoted in the brief (€7,171.11) is consistent with the 2026/27 MUR minimum, but I could NOT locate the exact decree line confirming that precise number; treat the exact cent value as UNVERIFIED. Two hard practical constraints found: (1) 'fuori sede' status is only recognised if the student registers a genuine, Agenzia delle Entrate-registered tenancy contract by the bando deadline (Lazio DISCO 2026/27 sets that at 27 December 2026 for that cycle) — so a late-arriving student can lose the highest band; (2) a student resident abroad CANNOT file an ordinary ISEE and must instead obtain an 'ISEE parificato', which requires income and property documentation from the home country, translated and legalised by the Italian diplomatic authorities there. THIS CONFIRMS THE WRINKLE IN THE BRIEF: without an ISEE/ISEE parificato in hand at enrolment the student is placed in the TOP fee band for year one, dropping only once the parificato is filed. The ISEE parificato can in fact be obtained from abroad through a CAF before arrival, which is the practical workaround — but it needs consular legalisation and should be started months ahead.

Verified directly: Conservatorium van Amsterdam (AHK) Master in Immersive Audio awards a 'Master of Music (MMus)', 2 years, 120 ECTS, taught entirely in English, and the page confirms positive NVAO accreditation — an officially recognised Dutch qualification. Both institutions are government-funded (bekostigd) and therefore outside a 'private-sector' brief — but they are the ONLY Dutch route that produces a real master's degree in this field. (2) PRIVATE = NOT ACCREDITED AS DUTCH HIGHER EDUCATION. Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam publishes no accreditation claim anywhere on its FAQ or course pages; its own FAQ states 'Since Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam is a private Institute, students are not eligible for a visa or a student loan', and 'As the Advanced Diploma is not a 3 year degree programme, the course is not eligible for any kind of student loan.' SAE Netherlands explicitly routes its degree-awarding through a UK university rather than NVAO. CRKBO (VAT-exemption register for short vocational training) and NRTO (private-training trade association mark) are NOT accreditations and confer no degree status — no evidence was found contradicting this. This candidate — BSc Software Engineering, no music degree, no professional audio experience — does NOT currently meet those requirements. The prior entry recommended CvA without flagging this. HKU is materially more open: its page states the programme can make exceptions for candidates without a formal music bachelor's degree if they demonstrate 'exceptional talent and a steady track record'.

PUBLIC FALLBACKS: CvA Immersive Audio effectively NO for this candidate as things stand — it requires 'a bachelor's degree in music or related field' plus 'professional-level audio engineering experience'. HKU Master Music Design is the realistic accredited Dutch target: applicants need 'a bachelor's degree in a relevant field or equivalent professional experience', and the programme 'can make exceptions for candidates without a formal music bachelor's degree if they demonstrate exceptional talent and a steady track record' — a software-engineering BSc plus a strong portfolio is a plausible fit for that wording, though talent must carry the application.

Treat it as unverified and confirm with admissions before relying on it. WHAT IS VERIFIED AND MORE USEFUL: the CvA Master in Immersive Audio runs a three-stage selection — portfolio submission (motivation letter plus audio recordings), an interview, and a practical test in which applicants complete 'a 10-minute stereo mix of a pre-recorded 24-track session in Pro Tools'. That is a concrete, published, industry-credible standard and a far better target to build against than an unverified spec: it tells him exactly what a Dutch accredited programme expects — recorded work he can present, and demonstrable Pro Tools mixing competence under time pressure.

VERIFIED AND MORE IMPORTANT FOR HIM: HKU Master of Music Music Design publishes upload deadlines of 24 November, 12 January, 16 February and 13 April, and explicitly advises non-EU/EEA candidates to apply before 1 April to allow time for immigration procedures — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for September 2027 entry, but the shape of the calendar means his real decision point is roughly November 2026 to February 2027.

Verified comparators (public, outside brief): CvA Master in Immersive Audio = 2 years, 120 ECTS; HKU Master of Music Music Design = 2 years, 120 ECTS. Abbey Road Amsterdam full-time Advanced Diploma = 1 year, 48 weeks of tuition, classes Monday–Thursday 10:00–14:00 plus Friday workshops, ~40 hours/week total commitment (verified on its course page); no ECTS assigned. Alternatives listed: TOEFL 72 (UG) / 79 (PG); Duolingo 120 (UG) / 105 (PG); PTE 59; Cambridge B2 First 169, C1 Advanced 176, C2 Proficiency 180; GCSE/IGCSE English grade C or above. Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam publishes NO English-language requirement on its FAQ — UNVERIFIED, ask them directly. Practical takeaway: an IELTS 6.5 with no band under 6.0 clears the published private-sector bar and is a sensible target for the accredited Spanish/Portuguese/Italian applications too. He has not yet sat the test; book it well before any 2027 deadline.
study: Private sector, verified: Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam's Advanced Diploma in Music Production & Sound Engineering, one year, 48 weeks of tuition, Monday–Thursday 10:00–14:00 with Friday workshops. SAE Institute Amsterdam offers BA/BSc (Hons) Audio Production, Film Production, and Game Art & 3D Animation, plus short certificates in DJing, Electronic Music Production, Advanced Mixing & Mastering, Music Business, Video Production and Content Creation, and an MA/MSc Professional Practice — all awarded by the University of Hertfordshire. SAE describes its degrees as 'project-based learning including industry placement' with accelerated 2-year options. The content is hands-on and relevant to his goals; the problem is the paper it comes on and the visa it cannot obtain.
recommendation: BOTTOM LINE: DO NOT BUILD THE SEPTEMBER 2027 PLAN AROUND A DUTCH PRIVATE SCHOOL. The verification confirms the two things he needs — an accredited master and a student residence permit — cannot both be bought from the Dutch private sector at any price. The visa finding is not an inference: SAE and Abbey Road each state in writing that their students are not eligible for a visa. Concentrate the accredited-master applications on the Spain, Portugal and Italy slices. IF HE WANTS THE NETHERLANDS SPECIFICALLY, there is exactly one workable route and it is public, not private: HKU's Master of Music — Music Design (Utrecht, MMus, 2 years, 120 ECTS, primarily English) is the realistic target, because it is the only accredited Dutch programme found whose published entry rules bend for someone like him — exceptions are possible without a music bachelor's for candidates showing 'exceptional talent and a steady track record' — and because HKU sponsors non-EU students, advising them to apply before 1 April for immigration processing. Treat November 2026 – February 2027 as his live application window and confirm the 2027 dates when published. DEPRIORITISE the Conservatorium van Amsterdam Master in Immersive Audio despite its NVAO accreditation: it demands a bachelor's in music or a related field AND professional-level audio engineering experience, and screens with a live Pro Tools mixing test on a 24-track session. He has neither the degree nor the experience today; applying for September 2027 would be a wasted application unless he spends the next year acquiring demonstrable professional mixing work. WHAT HE SHOULD ACTUALLY DO WITH THE NETHERLANDS IN THE MEANTIME: build the portfolio he does not have, to a published standard rather than a vague one. The CvA practical test tells him the benchmark precisely — a body of presentable recorded work plus the ability to deliver a clean 10-minute stereo mix from a 24-track Pro Tools session. Short courses in Amsterdam can be attended on an ordinary Schengen tourist visa and require no accreditation, and timing a visit around Amsterdam Dance Event in October adds scene contacts — but get every price in writing by email first, because none of the circulating figures survived verification. Also book IELTS early; 6.5 with no band under 6.0 clears every published bar found.

entry: HARD MUSIC-BACHELOR GATE. Verbatim from HEMU's 'Masters: prerequisites and repertoires' section: 'Candidates must hold a Bachelor's degree in Music from a Swiss university or an equivalent qualification to be eligible. There is no age limit.' (Compare the bachelor rule on the same page, which is far looser: 'Candidates must hold a certificate granting access to higher education or an equivalent qualification'.) Additional programme documents, verbatim: 'Une biographie, 1'000 signes espaces compris maximum, à intégrer à la suite du Curriculum Vitae; Une présentation écrite de l'esquisse d'un projet artistique d'envergure que le·la candidat·e envisage de réaliser (trois pages maximum) ou un lien vers une vidéo d'explication de 3 à 5 minutes; Un dossier artistique ...; Fiche technique de la prestation de la seconde épreuve.'
acceptsNonMusic: NO. Quoted verbatim: 'Candidates must hold a Bachelor's degree in Music from a Swiss university or an equivalent qualification to be eligible.' A BSc Software Engineering is not an equivalent of a music bachelor. THIS RULE IS HES-SO-WIDE and therefore also closes every master at HEM Genève and at the HEMU sites in Fribourg and Sion. It is the single reason French-speaking Switzerland is effectively shut to this candidate.
portfolio: Verbatim: 'Dossier artistique comprenant trois œuvres représentatives, consistant en des interprétations, improvisations, ou compositions originales. Tous les styles de musique – classique, contemporaine, musiques actuelles, jazz, etc. – peuvent être représentés. Pour les interprétations ou improvisations, un lien vers une vidéo de la performance est obligatoire. Pour tout exemple de plus de 10 minutes, veuillez indiquer les passages les plus représentatifs en fournissant les repères temporels.' So: EXACTLY 3 representative works, any genre including musiques actuelles, delivered as a PDF with links; anything over 10 minutes needs timecodes; interpretations/improvisations must include a performance VIDEO link.
audition: AN AUDITION, NOT A PRODUCTION TEST. Verbatim under 'Compétences à l'admission': 'Démontrer un haut niveau de maîtrise musicale (et plus généralement artistique selon le projet) PAR LE BIAIS D'UNE AUDITION.' The second stage, verbatim: 'Seconde épreuve — En présentiel: lundi 27 avril 2026. Épreuve de 40 minutes: Prestation ou présentation artistique d'une durée de 10 minutes. Possibilité de bénéficier de 10 minutes de préparation en cas de besoin de mise en place technique. Dispositif de base sur place: piano, percussions (limitées), diffusion stéréo, dispositif audiovisuel. Entretien de 20 minutes, avec présentation d'un projet artistique d'envergure (5 minutes) et réponse aux questions du jury.' The 10-minute slot allows a 'présentation artistique' rather than a strict performance, and the on-site rig includes stereo playback — so a producer could in principle present rather than play. But the competency wording explicitly calls it an audition demanding 'un haut niveau de maîtrise musicale', and it is IN PERSON in Lausanne ('En présentiel'), with no published online option. No ear-training exam is published. No practical production test.

And: 'Cette filière, conçue comme un laboratoire d'expérimentation, place le travail par projet, l'interdisciplinarité et l'autonomie au cœur de la formation.' acceptsNonMusic: NO, not realistically. HSLU charges 'CHF 200 per entrance examination (will be credited upon enrolment)', and the admission fee schedule refers to CHF 390 for two practical examinations, which implies the practical exam is a real, separately-priced component.
deadline: 28 FEBRUARY ANNUALLY (29 February in leap years) for all degree programmes — stated as a standing annual rule, not a one-off cycle date, so this one does not need the prior-cycle caveat. Entrance examination fees are due at online registration. THIS IS THE ONE PROGRAMME IN THIS SWEEP WHOSE DEADLINE ACTUALLY FALLS INSIDE HIS OCTOBER 2026 – FEBRUARY 2027 WINDOW: for a September 2027 start he applies by 28 February 2027.
opens: Not published as a fixed opening date — UNVERIFIED; online registration runs up to the 28 February deadline. Ask musik@hslu.ch.
duration: Master's programmes build on the bachelor; the standard Swiss MA in Music is 4 semesters / 120 ECTS but the exact ECTS is not stated on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED, ask musik@hslu.ch. IMPORTANT ADDITIONAL RULE, published officially: applicants WITHOUT a bachelor's degree from a Swiss music university may be required to sit a 'Standortbestimmung Theorie' (theory placement assessment), and depending on the outcome must pass an Auflagenmodul (bridging module) in the first master semester covering the target competences of the HSLU bachelor. Continuation beyond the first semester depends on passing it. For a candidate with no music degree at all, this bridging module is not a formality — it is a second exam.
languageReq: Published officially and specific: B1 German for most master's programmes (including MA Music); B2 for Major Instrumental/Vocal Pedagogy and Church Music; C1 for Major Musiktheorie and School Music II. Crucially, HSLU states 'Knowledge of German is not required for the entrance examination, but knowledge of the German language must be proven in a language test' before studies begin. So he could sit the audition without German, but must certify B1 German before starting. No English certificate is required for the MA (C1 English is required only for the doctorate).
study: Major Komposition is deliberately open: the curriculum is explicitly 'not profile-specific' and is set by individual target agreements, with Classical and Jazz orientations that 'can be individually modified and mixed'. On top of the major, the student stacks minors — Electronic Music Composition, Groove und Electronics, and Media Composer being the three that map onto electronic music production and scoring.
recommendation: IMPORTANT AS A DATABASE GAP, NOT AS A 2027 APPLICATION. Hochschule Luzern – Musik was absent from the database entirely, and its Minor Electronic Music Composition / Minor Groove und Electronics / Minor Media Composer are the closest thing to electronic-music-production training in central Switzerland — that is worth recording. But for THIS candidate the verdict is negative and should be stated plainly: a composition entrance examination, a theory placement test with a first-semester bridging module he must pass to continue, B1 German certified before he starts, roughly CHF 7,500 in institutional fees plus Swiss living costs, and no funding he is known to be eligible for. The single thing worth doing now, cheaply: the deadline is a standing 28 February, which does fit his planning window, so if in eighteen months his portfolio and German have both moved further than expected, this becomes reachable for a 2028 or 2029 start. File it, do not chase it.

qualification: CORRECTED — THIS WAS THE BIGGEST UNKNOWN IN THE PREVIOUS RECORD AND IT IS NOW RESOLVED. InMICS is a genuine JOINT MASTER'S DEGREE PROGRAMME, and the consortium states plainly: 'At the end of the two years, and upon validation of the study programme, students receive TWO MASTER'S DEGREES.' So it is a real double-degree award from the two hosting institutions the student attends, not a HOGENT master with a decorative consortium certificate. 2 years, 120 ECTS (60 + 60). On the Belgian side it sits inside HOGENT's accredited Flemish master in music. The previous record's warning that he might 'end up with one recognised diploma or several' is resolved: he would get two recognised European second-cycle degrees.
accreditation: The Belgian component is delivered within HOGENT's accredited master in music (Flemish Higher Education Register); the Lyon and Bologna components sit inside those states' own accredited second-cycle music degrees (French CNSMD master, Italian AFAM biennio). Two national accreditations are therefore engaged rather than a single consortium accreditation. Specific decision references UNVERIFIED.
tuition: €2,000 PER YEAR — MAJOR CORRECTION. The previous record left this UNVERIFIED and warned it might be the Flemish non-EEA rate of €8,800.20. Both the caution and the guess are now superseded by the consortium's own published figure: 'The amount of tuition fees for 2026-2028 will be: First year: €2000 ... Second year: €2000. The two thousand Euros fee is payable to the institution at which the student will be studying. No fees are due to the institution where the student is not currently studying.' So the total tuition for the whole 120 ECTS double-degree is €4,000 — roughly one fifth of what the previous record feared, and about one sixth of the Maastricht bill. This is an Erasmus+/Creative Europe co-funded consortium fee, and it is outstanding value. Still worth getting in writing from info@inmics.org before relying on it for a future cycle, since the figure is quoted for the 2026-2028 cohort specifically.
otherFees: €92 NON-REFUNDABLE APPLICATION FEE, payable on the Cadence platform at the time of application — newly identified, absent from the previous record. Beyond that: the mobility now involves TWO European countries rather than four countries including Canada, so he would need one Schengen student residence permit procedure per host country (Belgium, France or Italy), each with its own cost and lead time — but NO Canadian study permit is required under the current curriculum. Certified diploma copies and certified translations are additional. Whether HOGENT levies its separate 'contribution towards study costs' on InMICS students UNVERIFIED — ask.
totalCost: Tuition: €2,000 × 2 = €4,000 total for 120 ECTS and two master's degrees, plus a €92 application fee. Living costs across two of Ghent/Lyon/Bologna, plus two residence-permit procedures and two relocations, dominate the real budget — call it €12,000–€18,000 per year in living costs and administration depending on city. The tuition itself is close to negligible. This is dramatically cheaper than the previous record's €17,600 tuition estimate.
scholarshipDetail: No InMICS-specific scholarship is published. entry: CONFIRMED AND HARDENED. The institutional page states: 'We welcome applications from anyone already composing music for the screen. However, an undergraduate degree in music or equivalent is required.' The consortium's own application checklist turns this into a documentary gate that cannot be argued around: the administrative registration on the Cadence platform requires a 'CERTIFIED COPY OF THE FIRST CYCLE (BACHELOR) DIPLOMA OR DEGREE IN MUSIC, with transcripts in the original language' (or a signed, stamped statement of expected award date), plus a certified English translation if not in English, French, Italian or Dutch. He cannot produce a certified music bachelor. Applications are handled entirely through the CNSMD de Lyon platforms, not through HOGENT's webreg.
acceptsNonMusic: NO — CONFIRMED and now airtight. The stated requirement is an undergraduate degree in music or equivalent PLUS being 'already composing music for the screen', and the Cadence administrative checklist demands a CERTIFIED COPY OF A BACHELOR DIPLOMA IN MUSIC as a mandatory upload. The 'or equivalent' wording in the prose does not survive contact with a documentary requirement for a certified music diploma. A BSc in Software Engineering cannot satisfy it, and the portfolio gate is separately out of reach: three to five works including at least one score synchronised to picture, plus a 2,000-word academic research proposal, judged against trained composers.
portfolio: NOW FULLY PUBLISHED. Submitted on muvac: (1) a RESEARCH PAPER PROPOSAL for the two-year programme — provisional research question, provisional title, brief description, max 2,000 words, optionally with bibliography/filmography/music references, on a topic related to composition for screen; (2) A MINIMUM OF THREE AND MAXIMUM OF FIVE pieces of music, total duration across all works max 20 minutes, as mp3/wav or movie files, of which AT LEAST ONE must be a score for screen uploaded as a movie file with the music synchronised to the picture (recording, VST simulation or electronic piece all acceptable), with the written score if available; (3) a DECLARATION OF HONOUR on the authenticity and artistic authorship of all scores and recordings; (4) a COVER LETTER, max 1,000 words, stating motivation and a preference among the partner institutions; (5) a complete CV of experience and education in music and/or music for screen. All documents must use his legal name, not an artist or DJ name.
audition: NOW FULLY PUBLISHED — the previous record had this as UNVERIFIED. TWO PHASES. Phase 1, online application by the deadline, submitted on BOTH platforms (both mandatory): muvac (artistic portfolio and questionnaire) and Cadence at concours.cnsmd-lyon.fr (administrative data and the €92 application fee). Results of round 1 announced by end of April, with an invitation to interview and a COMPULSORY PRELIMINARY ASSIGNMENT — composing music for a short film of 5 to 10 minutes, due at a set deadline in early May. Phase 2: a 30-MINUTE ONLINE INTERVIEW with the recruitment committee/jury (mid-May). Results end of May; the jury also reveals which TWO of the partner institutions each admitted student will attend, and that decision is FINAL. Admission must be confirmed by mid-June, after which the student registers separately according to the procedures of both hosting institutions.

recommendation: EXISTS, IS REAL, IS A GENUINE DOUBLE MASTER'S DEGREE, AND IS EXCELLENT VALUE — BUT IS UNAVAILABLE TO HIM, AND UNAVAILABLE TO ANYONE FOR SEPTEMBER 2027. Three corrections matter. (1) INTAKE: this master recruits BIENNIALLY, not annually. The 2026-2028 cohort applied 2 March – 12 April 2026 and started in September 2026; the next cohort is 2028-2030, applying around March 2028. There is no September 2027 entry, so it cannot be on his 2027 list at all. (2) COST: tuition is €2,000 per year flat for EU and non-EU alike, total €4,000 for the whole programme plus a €92 application fee — not the €8,800.20/yr the previous record feared. (3) AWARD AND STRUCTURE: students receive TWO master's degrees, and study at TWO of the three European institutions (Ghent, Lyon, Bologna); Montréal is no longer a study location under the curriculum in force since 2024, so the Canadian study-permit worry is obsolete. What blocks him is not money and not accreditation — it is that the application requires a certified copy of a bachelor's diploma IN MUSIC, and a portfolio of three to five screen-scoring works plus a 2,000-word research proposal. Keep this on file as a strong LONG-TERM target: if he completes the Maastricht Master of Music (or any recognised music master) by summer 2029, he would hold the diploma the Cadence platform demands and could apply in March 2030 for the 2030-2032 cohort — cheaply, in English, with his French an asset for the Lyon track. If he contacts them now, the only useful question is whether the consortium would ever accept a non-music bachelor as 'equivalent'; ask info@inmics.org in writing, and expect no.

(2) "Proof of at least 12 months of professional experience relevant to the course of study, completed AFTER earning the first university degree... should be accumulated by the start of the program. It can, however, be acquired cumulatively... gained within the last five years prior to the application." (3) A portfolio documenting creative and scholarly achievements, plus English at minimum B2. International applicants must ALSO have their degree validated by uni-assist in parallel, by the same deadline, with certified copies and certified translations if the documents are not in English or German. acceptsNonMusic: Yes, without qualification — "a university degree... in any field", and the FAQ adds "The MA Game Development and Research program welcomes applicants from all professional backgrounds." The real gate is not the degree but the 12 months of post-bachelor professional experience in a games/media-relevant field: he graduates in 2026 with none, so for a September 2027 start he would need roughly a year of relevant work between graduation and enrolment (employment, self-employment, project work, internships and research-assistant posts all count, and can be accumulated in pieces).
portfolio: Now fully documented. The portfolio is free-form work samples, explicitly NOT required to be game work: "These do not need to be works in game design, since we do not require that applicants have previous experience in that field." Submit as a PDF, a Dropbox/Google Drive link or an online portfolio; analogue work must be scanned or photographed. CGL's own list of acceptable content includes, under 'Samples of other Audiovisual Artwork': "Audio Work: If you have sound design or music composition skills, present examples" — so his production work would count. Alongside the portfolio, every MA GDR applicant must complete the annual application TASK, which consists of a project idea, an application video of maximum 10 minutes, and three short written assignments; the exact brief is published only when the portal opens on 1 March. Other uploads: CV, portrait photo, scanned certificates and degree, proof of the 12 months' experience (contracts or dated project documents), and optionally an English certificate.

An interview is only sometimes used: "In some cases, the committee may invite applicants to an individual online-interview (approximately 10 minutes)... The interview is an additional method to evaluate an applicant's language skills." It is ONLINE, short, and about English proficiency, not performance. CORRECTION to the prior entry: the '11 and 13 June' interview dates came from a one-off news post about an extended cycle, not from the standing admission process.
deadline: 31 March at 23:59 CEST — published as a standing annual rule: "The application deadline is always March 31, at 23:59 CEST", with the uni-assist submission deadline also 31 March, and successful applicants notified in June to start in September. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date only for the extension: the news page that was originally cited as the source announced a one-off extension to 24 April with interviews on 11 and 13 June; that is not the standing rule and must not be planned around. Practical timing for September 2027: begin uni-assist paperwork by roughly January 2027 (evaluation takes up to four weeks or longer at peak), watch for the tasks on 1 March 2027, submit by 31 March 2027.
opens: 1 March each year — "The application tasks are always published on March 1st", which is also when the application portal opens. For a September 2027 start, expect 1 March 2027.
duration: 4 semesters (2 years) / 120 ECTS. Official wording: "Graduates complete the MA 'Game Development and Research' with 120 ECTS." Timetabled to be combinable with a part-time job — required attendance is Mondays all day plus Wednesday evenings.
study: Confirmed module structure, four semesters. Semester 1 'Equalization & Exchange' — levelling projects 'Playing with Theater', 'Playing with Cinema', 'Playing with Video Games', plus Media and Game Studies 101, Visual Design 101, Game Design Theory 101. Semester 2 'Critical Play & Adaptation' — projects on Board Games, Serious Games and Non-Linear Adaptation, plus the 102-level theory courses. Semester 3 'Professionalization & Experimentation' — the commercial games market, financing, self-publishing versus publishers, pitch and marketing strategy, plus a larger experimental third-semester project and the 103-level theory courses. Semester 4 — Master's Project: thesis with a theoretical and a practical part, plus a colloquium. Only 20 students per year. THE DECISIVE FINDING: there is no audio, sound-design, music, Wwise/FMOD or middleware module anywhere in the published structure. The programme describes itself as research into "non-linear audio-visuality", which reads as audio-related but in practice means audiovisual media as a whole; the taught strands are game design, visual design, media and game studies, programming and professionalization. Graduate profiles listed by CGL: Game Designer, Game Artist, Game Programmer, Interactive Designer, Concept Author, Stage Director, Project Manager — no audio role.
recommendation: Verified as existing, well-run and genuinely open to a software engineer — and verified as the wrong programme for him. It is English-taught, accepts any bachelor, accepts an audio portfolio, needs no audition, needs no IELTS, and costs a manageable EUR 10,000 plus fees. But it does not teach sound. If his goal shifts to games programming or games research it is a strong option; for becoming a producer, DJ or sound designer it teaches him nothing he needs. Secondary blocker even then: 12 months of post-degree professional experience in a media-relevant field, which he will not have until roughly late 2027 at the earliest. Recommend excluding from the audio shortlist.
