scholarshipDetail: None. Romanian Government/MFA and ARICE scholarships fund licență, masterat and doctorat cycles at accredited institutions. A 15-ECTS postgraduate certificate is not a study cycle and would not be covered. Do not expect funding.
entry: A bachelor's degree or equivalent — CONFIRMED. No music degree is formally named, but the entrance exam assumes conservatoire-level aural training, which functions as a de facto music-degree requirement.
acceptsNonMusic: NO in practice — CONFIRMED. The formal condition is only a bachelor's degree in any field, but the entrance examination requires 16-bar melodic dictation, notation of transposing instruments, and aural timbre and instrument recognition. These are conservatoire skills. Without a music background he would fail the exam, and no amount of DAW proficiency substitutes.
portfolio: None specified — CONFIRMED. The gate is the aural-skills examination, not a portfolio. Which is worse for him, not better: a portfolio he could build in a year, an ear he cannot.
audition: DISQUALIFYING FOR THIS CANDIDATE — CONFIRMED IN SHARPER DETAIL THAN PREVIOUSLY RECORDED. Two components. (1) WRITTEN test: melodic dictation of up to 16 measures with a key signature of up to two sharps or flats, plus identification and notation of transposing instruments. (2) ORAL exam: identifying instrument timbres by ear and answering related questions. Taking a 16-bar melodic dictation in up to two accidentals is a skill built over years of formal solfège; identifying transposing instruments and their written-versus-sounding pitches is standard conservatoire theory. Someone with no music degree, no conservatoire training and one year of self-study will not pass this.
deadline: Not published — UNVERIFIED. Ask UNMB's Studii Postuniversitare office. Moot in practice, given everything below.
duration: CONFIRMED VERBATIM: 146 contact hours, 15 ECTS, in-person attendance. For scale, a genuine Romanian master's is 120 ECTS over two years — at 15 ECTS this is one-eighth of a master's. It is a short professional course.
languageReq: Not separately published — UNVERIFIED — but since teaching is in Romanian and the entrance exam is oral and written in Romanian, Romanian competence is required in practice. IELTS/TOEFL are irrelevant. UNMB does publish a non-EU admission methodology; ask its postgraduate office whether that route even applies to postuniversitare courses.
study: Music direction (regie muzicală), the classical Romanian tonmeister discipline. Detailed syllabus not published on the official page — UNVERIFIED. The entrance exam content is itself the clearest evidence of the discipline's nature: melodic dictation, notation of transposing instruments, timbral hearing and instrument recognition. This is built entirely on classical-music aural skill. There is nothing here about electronic production, DJing, DAWs or club music.
recommendation: CONFIRMED IN FULL, NO CORRECTIONS NEEDED — DO NOT PURSUE. I re-checked every figure against the official UNMB page and all of them are exact: 146 hours, 15 ECTS, Romanian instruction, 8,000 lei domestic and €1,600 international in three instalments, 100 RON registration plus 150 RON enrolment, certificate of professional competency C.O.R. 265228 registered in the National Registry of Postgraduate Programmes. This entry was accurate. AVOID stands. Searching 'music direction Romania master' or 'regie muzicală' leads straight here, at Romania's national music university, at an apparently affordable €1,600 for international students. It is not a master's degree. It is a 146-hour, 15-ECTS professional certificate — one-eighth the volume of a real second-cycle degree — it will not support a student residence permit, it is taught in Romanian, and its entrance exam is a conservatoire aural test (16-bar melodic dictation in up to two accidentals, transposing-instrument notation, timbral recognition) that he cannot pass without years of solfège. The low price signals what it is; it is not a bargain. Note also that UNMB's genuine master's portfolio contains NO sound-technology programme: the Faculty of Composition, Musicology and Music Pedagogy offers only Stil și limbaj compozițional, Sinteză muzicologică, Stilistică dirijorală, Jazz și culturi muzicale pop, Educație muzicală contemporană and Culturi muzicale religioase, and the Faculty of Musical Interpretation offers only performance-stylistics masters. UNMB is a dead end for him and should be closed off entirely — the Romanian opening is at UNATC, whose English-taught MAs need no Romanian and no conservatoire ear.
url: https://www.unmb.ro/oferta-educationala/studii-postuniversitare/regie-muzicala/ (official UNMB postgraduate programme page, re-verified: postgraduate status and National Registry inscription, 146 hours, 15 ECTS, Romanian instruction, written melodic dictation up to 16 measures and max 2 accidentals plus transposing instruments, oral timbre identification, 8,000 lei Romanian / 1,600 EUR international in 3 instalments, 100 RON registration and 150 RON enrolment, certificate C.O.R. 265228) and https://www.unmb.ro/admitere/ (official admissions page listing the actual master's programmes, none sound-related) and https://www.unmb.ro/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Metodologia_admitere-cetateni-straini-NON-UE_2026-2027.pdf (UNMB non-EU admission methodology, covering degree cycles)

institution: Akademija umetnosti (Academy of Arts), Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
programme: Master akademske studije MUZIČKA PRODUKCIJA (MAS Music Production) — Interdisciplinary Studies
whyChance: States it does not accept a non-music background
verdictWhy: A one-year Master Music Producer degree for EUR 1,800, gated by an entrance exam whose scored centre is producing on supplied raw material — the ideal shape for him — and closed anyway by two conditions: documented proof of Serbian, and a 240-ECTS four-year bachelor that a three-year licence would not meet.
correction: DUPLICATE of index 60; merge. The cost band 'EUR 1.5k-5k/yr' is correct but imprecise — the exact figure is EUR 1,800 for the entire degree, since it is one year, not per-year-times-two. Corrects the gate 'Portfolio + exam/interview' by naming the PRACTICAL PRODUCTION TEST at its centre and confirming there is no audition and no ear-training exam. Adds the decisive missing condition: documented proof of Serbian language for foreign nationals.
qualification: Master akademske studije (MAS) — a real, state-recognised second-cycle degree, 60 ECTS, 1 year, 2 semesters. Professional title per the accredited curriculum sheet: 'Мастер музички продуцент' (Master Music Producer). CONFIRMED verbatim from the official accredited curriculum PDF. Supports a Serbian study residence permit.
accreditation: ACCREDITED — now verified at national level, correcting the previous 'decision could not be machine-read'. The National Body for Accreditation and Quality Assurance in Higher Education (NAT) register 'Vodič kroz akreditovane visokoškolske ustanove i studijske programe u Republici Srbiji', edition of 21 July 2026, lists under Akademija umetnosti, Novi Sad, entry 90: 'ИМТ МАС - МУЗИЧКА ПРОДУКЦИЈА, 03.10.2023, БС 10'. So: accredited 3 October 2023, field IMT (interdisciplinary/multidisciplinary), approved annual intake 10. Serbian accreditation runs 7 years, so this decision is valid through October 2030 and covers his September/October 2027 entry.
tuition: EUR 1,800 for the whole degree — THE RATE HE WOULD PAY. CONFIRMED verbatim: the konkurs quota table has a dedicated column 'Школарина за странце (евра)' showing 1800 against Muzička produkcija (and against every master programme at the Academy; doctoral studies are 2,400). Since the master is one year, EUR 1,800 is the total tuition, not an annual instalment of a longer degree.
otherFees: MATERIALLY CORRECTED — the previous record's '4,000 RSD to the University plus 4,000 RSD to the Academy' figure does not appear in any official document and is withdrawn. Actual published figures: (1) ENTRANCE-EXAM FEE 12,000 RSD — konkurs §6: 'Кандидати који приступају пријемном испиту уплаћују 12.000,00 дин' (previously UNVERIFIED); (2) ENROLMENT COST ON ADMISSION 5,500 RSD — konkurs §6 'Трошкови уписа за кандидате који положе пријемни испит износи 5.500,00 дин', corroborated by the official 'ZA UPIS 2026-2027 JE POTREBNO' sheet which also requires the original diploma for inspection, two 3.5x4.5 cm photos, an index book and two ŠV-20 forms; (3) both paid to account 840-32790845-46, poziv na broj 300 for the Drama Department and interdisciplinary studies; (4) DIPLOMA RECOGNITION at the University of Novi Sad — 30,000 RSD, or EUR 260 if paid from abroad, PLUS a 14,900 RSD administrative tax, applicant bears all bank charges (previously UNVERIFIED; source uns.ac.rs recognition page, applied for online at priznavanje.uns.ac.rs, contact priznavanje@uns.ac.rs / 021 485-2021). Compulsory health insurance for foreign students — cost still UNVERIFIED.
totalCost: Now largely computable. Tuition EUR 1,800 for the entire 60-ECTS degree. Plus institutional/administrative costs: 12,000 RSD exam fee + 5,500 RSD enrolment + 30,000 RSD (or EUR 260) recognition fee + 14,900 RSD administrative tax, i.e. roughly EUR 480–560 at ~117 RSD/EUR. So about EUR 2,300–2,400 in institution-side costs for the whole master, before living costs, visa fees, health insurance and Serbian-language tuition. Living costs in Novi Sad are not published by the Academy — UNVERIFIED. This remains among the cheapest genuinely accredited music-production masters in Europe.
scholarshipDetail: No programme-level or Academy-level scholarship for non-EU applicants is published on any official page — UNVERIFIED, unchanged after re-checking. Do not assume one exists. Realistic avenues to ask: (1) the Serbian Ministry of Education's bilateral scholarship offers, which are distributed through the applicant's home ministry — he should ask the Tunisian Ministère de l'Enseignement Supérieur whether Serbia offers Tunisia places in a given year; (2) the University of Novi Sad international office. Erasmus+ credit mobility is inbound-only for already-enrolled students and is not an admission route.
entry: THE DOCUMENTED CONTRADICTION IS REAL — I re-read both source documents and confirm it, but I now judge which one governs. (a) The 2026/27 konkurs, §2, programme-specific clause: 'Студијски програм – Музичка продукција: завршене основне академске студије у четворогодишњем трајању из уметничке области Музичка продукција, или сродан студијски програм (240 ЕСПБ)' — a four-year BA IN THE ARTISTIC FIELD of music production, or a cognate programme. (b) The informator, Opšti uslovi: 'Пријемни испит могу полагати лица која су завршила основне академске студије у четворогодишњем трајању (240 ЕСПБ)' — any four-year 240-ECTS bachelor. CORRECTION OF EMPHASIS: the konkurs is the legally binding enrolment act adopted on the University's template and issued on the basis of a Government decision; the informator is a summary of exam content. Where they differ the konkurs governs. Read that way, a BSc Software Engineering is NOT in the artistic field of music production and is unlikely to be accepted as 'srodan'. Second, the konkurs §2.2 general rule requires 'najmanje 240 ESPB' and lists the ONLY four exceptions permitted at 180 ECTS — Konzervacija i restauracija, the Guitar/Performing Arts joint programme, Kreiranje serija, and Pozorišni oblici modul Lutkarstvo. Muzička produkcija is NOT among them. A Tunisian three-year 180-ECTS licence is therefore ineligible, full stop. Foreign nationals additionally file the diploma-recognition decision, health-insurance proof and Serbian-language proof.
acceptsNonMusic: NO on the governing document — this is a correction of emphasis from the previous record, which left it 'ambiguous'. The konkurs restricts entry to a four-year bachelor in the artistic field of Music Production or a cognate programme. Software engineering is not cognate to music production in any ordinary reading. Even on the permissive informator reading he would still face a Serbian-language written subject test in music production, a written musical analysis, a commission interview and a portfolio. Unlike a conservatory master there is no instrumental audition, which is the one thing in his favour.
portfolio: CONFIRMED and EXPANDED — the previous record omitted two konkurs-level documents. Informator required documents: diploma or certificate of a completed four-year 240-ECTS bachelor; CV (biografija); motivation letter; MEDICAL CERTIFICATE WITH AN AUDIOGRAM (ophthalmologist, ENT specialist, psychologist); scanned/read ID; photo min. 1200x800 px JPG under 1 MB; proof of payment of the application fee. Separately, 'uz prijavu kandidati prilažu': (1) the medical certificate with audiogram, (2) a PORTFOLIO of works created in the 3 years preceding the date of the entrance exam. ADDITIONALLY required by konkurs §5 and omitted from the previous record: the completed PRIJAVNI LIST (application form, downloadable as Prijavni-list-za-master-studije-2026-2027.pdf) and the UVERENJE O POLOŽENIM ISPITIMA (official transcript of passed exams). Submission is 100% electronic, one e-mail per candidate to aunsprijemni.dramski@uns.ac.rs, all files under 12 MB total, every file named with the candidate's full name, study programme named in the subject line. His one-year portfolio plan does map onto the 'previous 3 years' rule.
audition: CONFIRMED verbatim. Two stages. PART ONE (pass/fail): written test in the professional-artistic field of Music Production; written analysis/evaluation of a musical work against subjective and objective criteria set by the commission; interview with the commission. Those who pass proceed to multi-day exercises and PART TWO: assessment of submitted works up to 30 points; practical work on the Academy's own material/equipment up to 20 points; oral examination of knowledge in the professional-artistic field of AUDIOVISUAL MEDIA (interview with the commission) up to 30 points. BA grade average scores separately, up to 20 points (10.00 = 20 pts; 6.49–6.00 = 4 pts; below 6.00 scores nothing). A candidate not exceeding 50 total points fails and is not ranked. Mobile phones and auxiliary devices are strictly banned from the exam rooms. Conducted in Serbian.
deadline: CORRECTED — the previous record missed the SECOND application round entirely, which materially improves his odds. 2026/27 cycle, Drama Department / Interdisciplinary studies (PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates for 2027/28). FIRST ROUND: electronic application 05.10.2026; entrance exam 07–13.10.2026; preliminary ranking 15.10.2026; final ranking 20.10.2026; enrolment 20.10.2026. SECOND ROUND (DRUGI KONKURSNI ROK): electronic application 21.10.2026; entrance exam 23–28.10.2026; preliminary ranking 30.10.2026; final ranking and enrolment 03.11.2026. Appeals to the Dean within 24 hours of the preliminary list. The timing trap stands: applications close in EARLY OCTOBER of the year of entry, not the preceding winter — but the diploma-recognition process, the audiogram/medical certificate and Serbian-language study must start many months earlier.
opens: 2026/27 cycle: konkurs text published 29 May 2026 (per the Drama Department admissions page), informators posted July 2026 (the Kreiranje serija informator appeared as late as August 2026). For a September/October 2027 entry, expect the 2027/28 konkurs around May–June 2027 and informators in July 2027 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Note the informator itself states that the Drama Department's application and exam dates 'will be published on the Academy website', so the konkurs is the document to watch.
duration: 1 year / 2 semesters, 60 ECTS. CONFIRMED from both the informator and the accredited curriculum sheet.
languageReq: Konkurs §9 (Upis stranih državljana): a foreign national enrols 'pod istim uslovima kao i domaći državljanin' and additionally files (a) rešenje o priznavanju strane diplome, (b) dokaz o zdravstvenom osiguranju, (c) 'dokaz o poznavanju srpskog jezika'. The required LEVEL and the accepted certificate are still NOT published — UNVERIFIED, confirmed by re-checking the University of Novi Sad's general rule, which only refers back to 'the University Statute and the Faculty Statute'. Ask: Služba za studije i studentska pitanja, 021/422-177 lok. 2 or 021/422-176 lok. 2, aofarts@uns.ac.rs.
englishTest: None. No IELTS/TOEFL appears anywhere in the konkurs or informator. Confirmed. His untaken IELTS is genuinely irrelevant here — the language barrier is Serbian, and it is a much harder one for him than IELTS would be.
study: CONFIRMED verbatim from the official accredited curriculum sheet (mas-muzicka-produkcija-2024.pdf). Compulsory: Muzička produkcija (2+2, both semesters); Zvuk i muzika na filmu (2+1); Savremene tendencije u muzičkoj produkciji 1 (1+2) and 2 (2+2); Muzika-događaj-publika (1+1, both semesters); Master rad – istraživanje (0+0+6); Master rad (0+0+5). Electives, 12 ECTS per semester block chosen from: Dramaturgija savremenog filma (2+1); Metode u muzičkom obrazovanju u digitalnom okruženju (2+0); Istorija elektroakustičke muzike (2+0); Istorija popularne muzike (2+0); Produkcija muzike za nove medije (1+2); Muzika u medijima (1+1). Hours are weekly, as (lectures)+(exercises)+(DON).
recommendation: Content-wise this is still the best-matched accredited music-production master in the Serbian state sector, and at roughly EUR 2,300 all-in it is extraordinarily cheap. But after re-reading the governing documents I am less optimistic than the previous assessment, which called it 'the single best find'. Three gates, and he currently fails all three. (1) THE 240-ECTS RULE IS ABSOLUTE. Konkurs §2.2 lists the only four programmes at the Academy that accept 180 ECTS, and Muzička produkcija is not one of them. If his SMU MedTech BSc is a three-year 180-ECTS licence he is ineligible regardless of talent, portfolio or motivation. Verify this FIRST. (2) THE FIELD RESTRICTION IS REAL. The binding konkurs requires a four-year bachelor 'iz umetničke oblasti Muzička produkcija, ili srodan studijski program'. The permissive informator wording is a summary, not the rule. A software-engineering degree is very unlikely to qualify as cognate. (3) SERBIAN. The entrance exam is a written subject test plus a written musical analysis plus two commission interviews, all in Serbian. Going from zero Slavic to exam-level Serbian in twelve months while also building a first audio portfolio and arranging an ENT audiogram in Tunisia is not a realistic 2027 plan. Everything is verified and correct in the record; what has changed is the honest read of his odds. Concrete next step, one e-mail to aofarts@uns.ac.rs copying aunsprijemni.dramski@uns.ac.rs, asking: (a) can a 180-ECTS three-year foreign bachelor ever be accepted for MAS Muzička produkcija; (b) is a BSc in Software Engineering treated as a 'srodan studijski program' under the konkurs; (c) which Serbian-language certificate and level satisfies the requirement; (d) may foreign nationals compete for the 2 budget places.
url: https://akademija.uns.ac.rs/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Tekst-Konkursa-Master-Doktorske-2026.pdf (official 2026/27 master konkurs — quotas, foreigner tuition EUR 1,800, 12,000 RSD exam fee, 5,500 RSD enrolment, both application rounds, foreign-national rules); https://akademija.uns.ac.rs/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Informator-MAS-Muzicka-produkcija-2026-27.pdf (official entrance-exam informator — documents, audiogram, portfolio, exam structure); https://akademija.uns.ac.rs/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/mas-muzicka-produkcija-2024.pdf (official accredited curriculum, title 'Мастер музички продуцент'); https://akademija.uns.ac.rs/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/ZA-UPIS-2026-2027-JE-POTREBNO.pdf (enrolment checklist); https://akademija.uns.ac.rs/prijemni-dramski-mas/ (Drama Department master admissions hub); https://www.nat.rs/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Vodič-za-studente-21.07.2026.pdf (Serbian National Accreditation Body register, 21.07.2026 — entry 90, MAS Muzička produkcija accredited 03.10.2023); https://www.uns.ac.rs/index.php/studije/priznavanje-diploma/priznavanje-strane (diploma recognition procedure and 30,000 RSD / EUR 260 + 14,900 RSD fees)

institution: Real Conservatorio Superior de Música de Madrid (RCSMM)
programme: Máster en Enseñanzas Artísticas en Nuevas Tecnologías de la Música Actual: Creación e Interpretación
whyChance: States it does not accept a non-music background
scholarship: Becas del Ministerio de Educación (MECD) general grant; Comunidad de Madrid bonificaciones
qualification: Título Oficial de Máster en Enseñanzas Artísticas. CONFIRMED on the official page as MECES Nivel 3 (Real Decreto 1614/2009) / EQF Level 7, and the page explicitly states it 'habilita acceso al Doctorado'. This is a real state-recognised second-cycle degree, legally equivalent in rank to a Máster Universitario. Not a título propio.
accreditation: Official. Título Oficial de Máster en Enseñanzas Artísticas, MECES 3 / EQF 7 with doctoral access, stated on the conservatoire's own programme page. Ministry-register listing and Fundación Madri+D verification are consistent with this but were not re-read in this pass.
tuition: THE RATE HE WOULD PAY: between €2,593.20 and €12,966.00 for the single year, plus €19 admin and €1.12 insurance. There is no separate nationality rate — the scale is income-based, not nationality-based, so in principle a Tunisian applicant with a low family income falls in the 80% band at €2,593.20. The open question is EVIDENCE: RCSMM does not publish how a family with no Spanish tax declaration proves 'renta familiar', and if it cannot be evidenced the default is the undiscounted €12,966.00. Ask the Secretaría in writing: 'Un estudiante extracomunitario sin declaración de renta en España, ¿con qué documentación acredita el tramo de renta familiar, y en qué tramo se le sitúa por defecto?'
otherFees: Administrative fee €19 (CONFIRMED on the official masters page — previously logged as an unverified secondary-source figure). Seguro escolar €1.12/year, compulsory for students under 28. Separate Ministry fee for homologación/equivalencia of the foreign degree — amount UNVERIFIED.
totalCost: Tuition €2,593–€12,966 for the one year depending on how the income band is evidenced, plus roughly €20 in fees. Madrid living costs approximately €1,000–1,400/month, so €9,000–12,600 for the academic year. Realistic all-in for a best-case discount: roughly €12,000–15,000; worst case roughly €22,000–25,000.
scholarshipDetail: No programme-specific scholarship is advertised. Spanish MEFP general becas normally require prior legal residence and are not available to a first-time arrival on a study visa. Comunidad de Madrid becas coverage of enseñanzas artísticas superiores másteres for non-EU students is UNVERIFIED.
entry: CORRECTED AND MADE PRECISE. The official page states the programme is for 'Titulados en Enseñanzas Artísticas Superiores, de Composición o Interpretación' OR 'titulados superiores de Grado o equivalente' from Spanish or foreign universities 'en centros de educación superior musical'. The second route is a degree route, but the qualifying clause is that it must be from a HIGHER MUSIC EDUCATION institution. SMU MedTech is not one. Separately the general RCSMM masters page states the baseline as 'Título Superior de Música, Grado Universitario o equivalente' (MECES 2 / EQF 6) plus programme-specific requirements — marginally looser wording, but the programme-specific music clause governs. HARD BLOCKER stands.
acceptsNonMusic: NO — CONFIRMED as the decisive blocker. Both published entry routes require a music qualification: higher artistic education in Composition or Performance, or a Grado from a higher MUSIC education institution. A BSc in Software Engineering from a technology university satisfies neither. On top of that, 40% of the admission score is a conservatoire-level performance or a set of three original compositions.
portfolio: For the composition track: three original works, worth 40% of the admission score, plus CV (max two sides) and motivation letter. For the performance track: a contemporary work of up to 20 minutes. Submission format and file specifications are not published — ask the master coordinator.
audition: CORRECTED — the 40% component has TWO alternative forms, which the previous record collapsed into one. Official weighting: personal interview 10% + motivation letter 10% (20% combined); adecuación del programa al perfil 15%; CV, maximum two sides, 15%; related experience 10%; and then EITHER 'Interpretación de obra de música actual (máx. 20 min.)' 40% for the performance track OR 'Composición: presentación de tres obras originales' 40% for the composition track. The composition route is therefore a submitted portfolio of three original works, not a live audition — meaningfully different from what was previously recorded, though still assuming conservatoire-level compositional output.
deadline: Approximately 23 June 2027, extrapolated from the confirmed 8–23 June 2026 window for 2026-27 (PRIOR CYCLE — confirm when the 2027-28 calendar is published, from about April 2027).
opens: CORRECTED — this was previously logged as UNVERIFIED and guessed as 'spring'. The official masters page publishes the 2026-27 calendar: registration 8–23 June 2026, entrance exams 30 June – 4 July 2026 (PRIOR CYCLE). For a September 2027 start expect an early-to-mid June 2027 registration window with exams end of June / early July 2027 — a summer cycle, not a spring one. This matters: it collides with the Italian conservatoire timetable and leaves very little margin before a September start.
duration: 60 ECTS, one academic year in two semesters. CONFIRMED breakdown: Formación General 16 ECTS; Formación Creativa 20 ECTS; Formación Complementaria 12 ECTS; Trabajo Fin de Máster 12 ECTS. NEW FACTS from the official masters page: attendance is mandatory ('asistencia obligatoria'); timetable is Thursday afternoon, Friday morning/afternoon and Saturday morning/afternoon; maximum permitted duration is 2 years, extendable to 3 with justification; a student must pass a minimum of 12 ECTS in the first year to continue.
languageReq: No certificate level is published. The admission process includes a personal interview (10%) plus motivation letter (10%) conducted in Spanish, and the TFM and its defence must be in Spanish. Whether a DELE/SIELE certificate is formally demanded remains UNVERIFIED — ask the Secretaría. Practically he would need solid B2+ Spanish.
englishTest: None. English is not the medium of instruction and no IELTS/TOEFL appears anywhere on the official pages. This removes one obstacle but replaces it with a harder one.
study: Electroacoustic and multimedia creation and performance, contemporary repertoire, technology applied to current art music. It is an academic contemporary-music programme. There is no commercial production, DJ practice, mixing/mastering or music-business content, so even if he got in it would not directly serve the producer/DJ goal.
recommendation: DO NOT APPLY for September 2027. Two errors in the previous record are now corrected and both make it worse for him, not better: the cheapest possible fee is €2,593.20 and not €648, and the application window is June–July, not spring. The entry gate is unchanged and closed — both routes demand a music qualification and 40% of the score is a performance or three original compositions. One genuinely useful nuance did emerge: the composition route is a submitted portfolio rather than a live audition, so if he ever does obtain a qualifying music degree this is reachable without performance chops. Keep it as a five-year aspiration, not a 2027 application. Do still send the Secretaría the income-band evidence question, because the same Madrid public-price mechanism governs every Madrid enseñanzas artísticas option he might consider later.

institution: Trazos — Escuela Superior de Artes Digitales
programme: COVERAGE CHECK — 'Máster en Imagen y Sonido' NO LONGER EXISTS in the current catalogue; postproduction masters contain …
whyChance: No explicit statement — ask admissions, but taught in Spanish — language is the real gate
qualification: A Trazos school 'Máster' — a private certificate with no university validation, no ECTS and no official status. Its own postproduction page describes the outcome as a professional demo reel and portfolio rather than a formal degree. Separately, Trazos' university division offers Pearson BTEC HND qualifications (British, regulated by Ofqual) — but NOT in the postproduction masters, and not in anything audio.
accreditation: NOT OFFICIAL. A private school certificate — not a Máster Universitario Oficial, not ANECA-verified, no ECTS, no EHEA standing. The only formal recognitions published are Adobe Authorised Training Centre status (a software-vendor accreditation, not an academic one) and, in a separate division, Pearson BTEC HND awards that do not apply to these masters.
tuition: €2,560–€4,868 depending on which postproduction master, both discount-inclusive headline prices. No audio content is included at any price point.
otherFees: None published. Financing is offered via Aplazame from about €100 per month. No application or enrolment fee is stated separately.
totalCost: €2,560–€4,868 in tuition plus Madrid living costs — but irrelevant, because the audio content he is paying for does not exist.
entry: Open access, quoted verbatim from the school's own page: "No necesitas titulación previa ni experiencia" — no prior qualification and no experience needed. Admission is a consultation with an adviser to confirm the programme suits you, not an academic assessment.
portfolio: None required on entry. A demo reel is the OUTPUT of the course, not an entry condition.

whyChance: States it does not accept a non-music background

tuition: CHF 1,500 tuition + CHF 250 administrative fee = CHF 1,750 PER SEMESTER — CONFIRMED as the rate for 'all other students', which is what he would be. CHF 3,500 per year; CHF 7,000 over the 4-semester master.
otherFees: CONFIRMED AND EXPANDED — the previous record missed the application fee. Matriculation CHF 250 one-off; ADMISSIONS/APPLICATION FEE CHF 100 (payable with the application, confirmation of payment is a required document); student union CHF 5 per semester; Bachelor's/Master's final exam CHF 250; reassessment of a non-main subject CHF 100; reassessment of main subject CHF 200; reassessment of final exams CHF 350; extraordinary intermediate exam CHF 250; DEFERRED FINAL EXAM CHF 500; RETAKEN ECTS CHF 500 PER CREDIT; appeals CHF 100; leave of absence CHF 250 per semester. The CHF 500-per-retaken-ECTS charge is brutal and worth knowing about — Swiss music schools price failure aggressively.
totalCost: Institutional fees over 4 semesters: 4 × CHF 1,750 = CHF 7,000, plus matriculation CHF 250, application CHF 100, student union CHF 20, final exam CHF 250 — roughly CHF 7,620 before any re-sits. The Swiss student permit requires proof of means — figure UNVERIFIED; confirm with the Swiss representation in Tunis and the Ticino migration authority.
scholarshipDetail: MAJOR CORRECTION — the previous record said 'nothing published at programme level'. That is wrong. The Conservatorio publishes a SUM SCHOLARSHIP FUND on its Study Grants page. For academic year 2026-27 it offers 6 scholarships covering TUITION FEES, ADMINISTRATIVE FEES AND EXAMINATION FEES for the entire duration of studies — 3 for Bachelor's (3 years) and 3 for MASTER'S (2 years). Awarded to candidates who apply and obtain the best marks in the entrance examination, giving priority to those with the greatest financial difficulty. First-time applicants are explicitly eligible and NO NATIONALITY RESTRICTION is published. Application requires an online form plus CV in tabular form, motivation letter, letter of recommendation, family tax return and annual budget. DEADLINE 31 MARCH (incomplete or late applications are not evaluated). Anyone not awarded one is automatically placed on the list for Study Aid funded by the CSI's philanthropic partner network. This is effectively a full institutional-fee waiver — it would zero out the whole ~CHF 7,600 — though not living costs. It is gated entirely behind entrance-exam performance, which is precisely where he fails. Separately, the Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships Art Scholarships stream remains the external route; confirm Tunisia's presence on the art-stream country list for the 2027 call.
entry: CORRECTED AND HARDENED. The official admission page for this master states the requirement verbatim as 'successful completion of a BACHELOR OF ARTS IN MUSIC OR EQUIVALENT MUSICAL EDUCATION' plus passing an admission exam. The previous record hedged this as 'specific academic prerequisites are not itemised — UNVERIFIED'. They are itemised, and they close the door: a music bachelor, or demonstrably equivalent musical education, is required in substance. Required documents: payment confirmation for the CHF 100 application fee, valid ID or passport copy, BA diploma (or self-certification if the exam is pending), CV in tabular form, and a motivation letter.
acceptsNonMusic: NO — CONFIRMED AND HARDENED. The official requirement is 'successful completion of a Bachelor of Arts in Music or equivalent musical education'. The assessment is a composition dossier plus a written analysis-and-ear-training paper plus an oral solfège examination. A candidate with no music degree, no conservatory training and no existing portfolio cannot clear this, in one year or three.
portfolio: NOW VERIFIED — the previous record marked this UNVERIFIED. Candidates must submit 'own compositions, any orchestration work, any analytical work' for committee review and discussion. That is a composer's dossier, not a producer's showreel.
audition: NOW VERIFIED IN FULL, and it is decisive. Entrance examinations are held by invitation only after application review, in the window 30 MARCH – 29 APRIL. Three parts: (1) portfolio presentation and discussion with the admissions committee; (2) a WRITTEN TEST of maximum 60 minutes assessing 'competences in ANALYSIS AND EAR-TRAINING'; (3) an oral exam and interview covering SOLFÈGE, the portfolio, the candidate's musical education background, career goals, performance techniques and knowledge of technology. A written analysis-and-ear-training paper plus an oral solfège examination cannot be passed in a year by someone with no conservatory training. This is a conservatory gate, unambiguously.
deadline: 20 FEBRUARY — CONFIRMED on the official programme page ('Application deadline: February 20') and on the application page ('Deadline application 20th February 2026'). Presented as the standing master's deadline. Entrance exams 30 March – 29 April (the institution reserves the right to change the schedule). ADDITIONAL AND SEPARATE: the scholarship deadline is 31 MARCH — later than the application deadline, so an applicant applies first and bids for money afterwards. For a September 2027 start, expect 20 February 2027 — INSIDE his October 2026 – February 2027 planning window.
opens: Not published — UNVERIFIED. Applications close 20 February, so the window opens some months earlier; ask servizi.accademici@conservatorio.ch.
duration: 4 semesters, 120 ECTS, full time — CONFIRMED on the official programme page. Officially described as requiring total dedication in terms of time and emotional involvement.
languageReq: Italian at CEFR B2 or CELI 3. Notably generous in timing: applicants who do not have that level at the start of studies must still demonstrate a sufficient level and reach B2/CELI 3 BY THE END OF THE FIRST YEAR of study. No English certificate is mentioned. For a French-fluent Arabic native, Italian to B2 in a year is more achievable than German to B2 — the single most forgiving language regime in this set, and worth remembering if he ever looks at Italian-language options, even though the rest of this record is negative.
study: Composition, with an electronic music section delivered in partnership with IRMus (Accademia Internazionale della Musica, Milan). Composition, orchestration and analysis are the spine of the assessment, which tells you what the teaching is.
recommendation: RECORD IT, DO NOT APPLY — verdict unchanged, and now better evidenced. Two of the previous record's gaps are closed and one of its claims was wrong. CLOSED: the entry requirement is explicitly 'a Bachelor of Arts in Music or equivalent musical education', and the entrance exam is a portfolio of own compositions plus a 60-minute written analysis and ear-training paper plus an oral solfège examination. That is a conservatory gate and it definitively excludes him. WRONG: the previous record said there were no programme-level scholarships. There are — the SUM Scholarship Fund awards 3 Master scholarships for 2026-27 covering tuition, administrative and examination fees for the whole degree, open to first-time applicants with no published nationality bar, deadline 31 March. Worth correcting for the database even though he cannot reach it, because it means the real cost of this institution for a strong musician is near zero rather than CHF 7,600. FOUR THINGS FROM THIS RECORD REMAIN USEFUL TO HIM PERSONALLY EVEN THOUGH THE PROGRAMME IS NOT. (1) The visa-to-attend-the-audition problem, which applies to every Swiss music-school entrance exam he might ever consider, including HSLU Lucerne — plan it months ahead, and always ask whether a remote option exists. (2) The MA-versus-MAS trap at this institution: the 'MAS in Music Composition' is continuing education, not a degree, and applying for it would be a serious mistake. (3) The Italian B2-by-end-of-first-year rule — the most forgiving language regime found anywhere in this sweep. (4) The CHF 500-per-retaken-ECTS charge, a reminder that Swiss institutions price failure. As a September 2027 target it fails on the entrance examination, on composition not being music production, and on the fact that the one funding route is gated behind the exam he cannot pass.

The two things he must resolve before spending anything: whether the programme is actually deliverable in English (the school's own pages contradict each other, and the programme page says Dutch-spoken), and whether he can find EUR 8,800.20 a year, because there is no funding attached and that is well past 'a little'.
correction: Input gate 'Exam/interview only' is imprecise — it is a set composition assignment (two scored video clips) plus an intake interview, and the interview can be done online. Input cost band 'EUR 5k-15k/yr' is confirmed precisely: EUR 8,800.20 per 60-credit year for non-EEA, versus EUR 1,181.40 for EEA. The unflagged risk is the language: the programme page states 'This is a Dutch spoken programme'.
qualification: Master of Music / Master in de muziek, 120 ECTS (60 + 60). CONFIRMED on the official programme page, which lists the degree as 'master music' and shows a 1e Master of 60 credits and a 2e Master of 60 credits. A real, state-recognised Flemish second-cycle degree registered in the Higher Education Register of the Flemish Community; supports a Belgian type-D student visa and student residence permit for a non-EU national.
accreditation: Accredited Flemish master (NVAO / Flemish Higher Education Register), delivered inside HOGENT's recognised master in music. The school describes it as 'the first school of arts in Flanders' to offer a comprehensive master's programme for composing music for moving images. Specific NVAO decision reference UNVERIFIED — check hogeronderwijsregister.be or ask the admissions officer, Paul Lamont (paul.lamont@hogent.be).
tuition: €8,800.20 PER YEAR — CONFIRMED CORRECT, this is the rate he would pay. The school's official financial page publishes for 2026-2027 an increased tuition fee ('verhoogd studiegeld') for non-EEA students in drama, visual arts, audiovisual arts and MUSIC programmes of a fixed €916.20 plus €131.40 per credit, i.e. €8,800.20 for a full 60-credit year. The site notes some non-EEA students belong to a category exempted from the increased fee; whether a Tunisian national qualifies remains UNVERIFIED — ask HOGENT student administration. Do not assume he does.
otherFees: CONFIRMED to exist, amount still not published. On top of tuition, students pay a 'contribution towards study costs' (studio/atelier fee), which the school states is 'calculated individually based on the programme, the number of credits taken, and the ratio of practice-based credits to the total', with specifics set out in the Education and Examination Regulations. For a practice-heavy music master this is likely to be a meaningful three-figure sum. Amount UNVERIFIED — ask the KASK study administration. On top of that: Belgian type-D visa fee, residence-permit/city-registration costs, health insurance, and diploma apostille/legalisation and sworn-translation costs.
totalCost: Tuition alone: €8,800.20 × 2 = €17,600.40 for 120 ECTS, plus an unpublished study-cost contribution. Ghent living costs and the Belgian proof-of-sufficient-means figure for a student visa are not published on these pages — UNVERIFIED; get the current annual sufficient-means amount from the Belgian Immigration Office (Dienst Vreemdelingenzaken).
scholarshipDetail: UPGRADED FROM THE PREVIOUS RECORD, which called this 'Partial'. The realistic route is the FLEMISH GOVERNMENT MASTER MIND SCHOLARSHIP, and it is far stronger than previously described: verified on studyinflanders.be, a Master Mind Scholarship is a grant of €10,225 PLUS A TUITION FEE WAIVER per academic year — the host institution may charge the awardee no more than the lowest Flemish rate, €136.50 for 2026-2027. That is effectively FULL funding, not a partial offset. It is open to outstanding students from around the world with no exclusion of Tunisia; only a handful of places are RESERVED for priority countries (Japan 3, Mexico 3, Palestine 2, USA 5), and unfilled reserved places revert to the general ranked list. The 2026-2027 call is closed; the 2027-2028 call would open in the usual autumn/winter window. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: Master Mind is nominated through the institution, so HOGENT must put the programme and the candidate forward, and whether THIS Dutch-taught master is on HOGENT's Master Mind list is UNVERIFIED — ask the HOGENT International Office. No programme-specific scholarship is published on the course page. NOTE THAT NONE OF THIS HELPS HIM, because he cannot clear the entry gates below.
entry: SHARPENED AND CORRECTED — the previous record understated how closed this is. The programme's OWN admission-requirements page states the hard rule verbatim: 'To start in the master in music, you need either a bachelor in performing music (for the master in classical music or jazz/pop), OR A BACHELOR IN COMPOSING MUSIC (for the master in music production, composition or music theory).' This master sits in the composition family, so the named requirement is a bachelor in COMPOSING music — not merely 'a music degree'. On top of that sits the diploma-rating cascade: an academic bachelor gains direct admission on passing the orientation interview; a professional bachelor must first complete a TRANSITION programme (schakelprogramma) built from third-bachelor-year courses; an academic bachelor in ANOTHER ARTISTIC discipline may have to take a PREPARATORY programme; and a bridging programme exists 'if you wish to begin a master's program, but do not have the appropriate underlying bachelor's degree'. Route: register at webreg.hogent.be, submit documents, sit the orientation test. NEW FINDING ON DOCUMENTS: KASK requires a physical copy bearing an original certification/apostille/legalisation stamp before it will issue an invitation to enrol (not needed to apply or audition, but needed before enrolment). Tunisia is listed by KASK in BOTH the apostille list AND the legalisation list — the page contradicts itself, so he must email and get it in writing which applies (Tunisia has been a party to the Hague Apostille Convention since 2018, so apostille should be correct). Named contact CORRECTED/ADDED: the admissions officer is Paul Lamont, paul.lamont@hogent.be (the previous record only had the generic toelatingsproeven@hogent.be).
acceptsNonMusic: NO — CONFIRMED, and the case against is now stronger than the previous record stated. The programme's own admission page names the required prior degree as 'a bachelor in composing music'. A BSc in Software Engineering is not a music bachelor, not a composition bachelor, and not even 'an academic bachelor in another ARTISTIC discipline' — it falls outside all three named categories, leaving only the discretionary 'bridging programme' for applicants without the appropriate underlying bachelor's degree. That would mean a bridging or preparatory year BEFORE the two master years, in Dutch. And the whole programme is Dutch-spoken. He is blocked on two independent gates, either of which alone would be disqualifying for a September-2027 start. The orientation-test assignment (scoring two 2-3 minute clips) is the one part he could plausibly do.
portfolio: A dossier is assessed alongside the assignment — official wording: 'Based on your dossier and the assignment, you will be invited for an interview.' The dossier contents are still not published anywhere on the site. UNVERIFIED — ask paul.lamont@hogent.be.
audition: CONFIRMED EXACTLY. Orientation test in two parts. ASSIGNMENT: 'You provide soundtracks for 2 video clips (2-3 minutes). The soundtrack is your own choice consisting of several possibilities and genres.' The selection of video clips is emailed to the candidate three weeks before the deadline. INTERVIEW: an intake with the orientation committee — 'several teachers and experts in the field' — covering motivation, artistic discipline, communication skills and knowledge of the specific domain; the committee makes the final decision on enrolment. Location: 'All intakes take place at one of our campuses in Ghent and a personal presence is our preference. If you have to travel far, you can also participate in the interview or audition online' — the online option is confirmed and matters for a Tunisian applicant. Results by email within two working weeks of the interview.
deadline: CONFIRMED from the official orientation-test page, published 2026 cycle: registration deadline for the APRIL session 27.03.2026 (23:59); interview April session 27.04.2026; deadline for the ASSIGNMENT for the AUGUST session 25.06.2026; interview August session 24.08.2026, with the agenda entry showing the test window as 24.08.26 – 26.08.26. (Minor correction to the previous record, which gave the August interviews as 24-26.08.2026 without distinguishing the single published interview date from the test window.) PRIOR CYCLE — for a September-2027 start expect an equivalent late-March/April 2027 session and a late-June/August 2027 session. A non-EEA applicant must aim at the SPRING session because of visa lead time. Confirm from autumn 2026 with paul.lamont@hogent.be or toelatingsproeven@hogent.be.
opens: Registration via webreg.hogent.be, with orientation-test sessions announced per season. For the 2026-27 cycle the April-session registration closed 27.03.2026. PRIOR CYCLE — confirm the new dates for a September-2027 start.
duration: 2 years, 120 ECTS (60 + 60) — CONFIRMED from the official curriculum table. Year 1 (1e Master): Compositie voor media, video, games & artistiek onderzoek Master I; Electroakoestische compositie & producing Master I; Masterseminaries; plus film history and supporting subjects. Year 2 (2e Master): Masterproef Compositie voor media, video & games, audiovisual composition, film analysis, professional practice.
languageReq: CORRECTED. The previous record asserted that 'a Dutch-language proof is required' and left the accepted certificate UNVERIFIED. That is wrong in form, though not in practical effect. The official master-level admission-requirements page — both the general one and the one specific to THIS programme — publishes NO formal language certificate requirement at master level at all. Verbatim: 'You can study all our master's programs in Dutch or English. There are no formal level requirements for English in the master programs, but the Vantage B2 level is strongly recommended.' The detailed Dutch certificate list the previous agent was reaching for (ITNA B2, CNaVT STRT/PROF, NT2 Programma II, NVA5, any University Language Centre or CVO B2) is published on the PROFESSIONAL BACHELOR section of that page and applies to professional bachelors, not to masters. PRACTICAL EFFECT FOR HIM IS UNCHANGED AND STILL FATAL: no certificate is demanded on paper, but the teaching, the orientation interview and the entire curriculum are in Dutch, which he does not speak. Do not read 'no formal requirement' as 'accessible in English'.
study: Composition for documentary, animation, games, video and installation contexts; electroacoustic composition and producing; virtual orchestration; film history and film analysis; master seminars; and a substantial master's project (masterproef). Formal collaboration with HOWEST for game development ('offers the opportunity to become acquainted with the medium of games and develop the necessary technical competencies') and with Film Fest Gent for annual masterclasses, lectures and film-music concerts. The wider music department also runs four project weeks per academic year with guest speakers and interdisciplinary co-creation. Named staff CONFIRMED: Ruben De Gheselle and Dominique Pauwels.
recommendation: A genuine, well-designed, fairly-priced accredited Flemish master — and a bad fit for HIM, confirmed on re-check and now with harder evidence than before. Two independent blockers: (1) the programme is DUTCH-SPOKEN end to end, verified in three separate places on the official site; (2) the named prior-degree requirement is 'a bachelor in composing music', which routes a software-engineering graduate at best into a discretionary bridging programme, and HOGENT warns that a student visa for a language-preparation year is only issued once enrolled in a full course at a university language centre. Do not spend effort here for September 2027. TWO THINGS WORTH SALVAGING FROM THIS CHECK, HOWEVER. First, the same admission page reveals that KASK runs a separate MASTER IN MUSIC PRODUCTION inside the same master-in-music family — much closer to his actual goal than composition for screen, and worth investigating as its own record (it carries the same 'bachelor in composing music' gate and probably the same Dutch-language problem, but that should be verified rather than assumed). Second, the Master Mind Scholarship is a true full ride at Flemish institutions (€10,225 plus a fee waiver down to €136.50, open worldwide) — that is a strong reason to keep Flanders on his map generally, provided he can find an English-taught Flemish master whose entry rules do not demand a music bachelor. If he ever does contact Ghent, write to Paul Lamont (paul.lamont@hogent.be), not the generic address.

institution: Koninklijk Conservatorium Antwerpen (AP School of Arts, AP Hogeschool)

tuition: €25,065 per year for a 60-credit year — NEWLY VERIFIED and the single biggest correction here. AP publishes for 2026-2027: non-EEA "tuition fee fixed part: 2.500,00 euro + 375,00 euro / ECTS + 65 euro course related fee" (confirmed independently in AP's official Reglement Studiegelden 2026-27: "Studiegeld buitenlandse studenten — Diploma- en creditcontracten 2500 375"). At 60 credits that is 2,500 + 22,500 + 65 = €25,065; across a two-year 120-credit master, roughly €50,130 total. For comparison, an EEA student pays €305.40 + €14.60/ECTS + €65, i.e. about €1,246 a year. Non-EEA students lost Flemish basic financing from 2026-2027, which is what produced this.
scholarshipDetail: Government of Flanders Master Mind. AP University of Applied Sciences and Arts IS a confirmed participating host institution, with a deadline of 1 March 2026 for the 2026-2027 call — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date; expect roughly 1 March 2027 for a September 2027 start, which fits his timeline if he starts early. Three hard obstacles: (a) GPA of 3.5/4.0 on his BSc; (b) IELTS overall band minimum 6.5 for schools of arts, certificate no older than 3 years — he has not sat it; (c) the master must be ENGLISH-TAUGHT, and AP's music master has no official language requirements at all rather than being an English-taught programme, so eligibility must be confirmed with AP's international office before counting on it. No Tunisia-specific allocation exists; reserved places go to Japan (3), Mexico (3), Palestine (2), USA (5).
entry: Verified verbatim from the official registration page: "een diploma academische bachelor Muziek, afstudeerrichting Jazz of Jazz/lichte muziek geeft toegang tot de masteropleiding Muziek, afstudeerrichting Jazz" — Live Electronics sits inside the Jazz afstudeerrichting. A professional (non-academic) bachelor requires a bridging programme. A foreign diploma goes to the admissions committee: "De toelatingscommissie kan een kandidaat-student toelaten die een buitenlands diploma of getuigschrift heeft behaald ... voor zover de toelatingscommissie het behaalde diploma en het specifieke opleidingsprofiel van de student van voldoende niveau acht" — request to toelating@ap.be, uiterlijk 1 oktober. An artistic entrance exam (toelatingsproef) is required on top of the diploma condition; a voorbereidingsprogramma may be imposed.
acceptsNonMusic: NO in practice — corrected from the earlier draft's 'Check'. The registration page is much stricter than the marketing page's "open to all music students with an undergraduate degree": direct access requires an academic bachelor in MUSIC with a Jazz or Jazz/lichte muziek specialisation. The foreign-diploma clause is not a general-purpose escape hatch — the committee must judge "het behaalde diploma EN het specifieke opleidingsprofiel van de student" to be of sufficient level for this programme, which a Software Engineering BSc with no music training will not satisfy. The realistic published path for him is a voorbereidingsprogramma (preparatory year) before the master, and he should ask toelating@ap.be directly about it, well before the 1 October deadline.
portfolio: UNVERIFIED for Live Electronics specifically. AP publishes no portfolio specification (number of works, durations, formats) for this specialisation. Related data point: for Jazz, AP allows audition via media uploaded to an "online platform (YouTube, Vimeo, soundcloud, etc.)", and for Composition it requires recordings plus scores. Ask the jazz department.
audition: An artistieke toelatingsproef is compulsory for all master applicants: "All master applicants must pass an orientation-based artistic test", with content varying by specialisation. The content for Live Electronics is NOT published. Given the live-performance and improvisation orientation (algoraves, jam sessions) expect a practical performance component. Administrative fee €30 per separate School-of-Arts enrolment, never refunded.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Two dates are published and they are different things: the foreign-diploma admission request to toelating@ap.be is due "uiterlijk 1 oktober"; and 1 May is cited as the application deadline covering the full academic year / both semesters. Neither is given as a 2027-specific date. Confirm both directly with the jazz department and toelating@ap.be before relying on them.
opens: UNVERIFIED — AP does not publish an opening date for the artistic entrance-exam registration.
duration: 2 years — CONFIRMED ("Na je bacheloropleiding van drie jaar zet je jouw opleiding verder in de tweejarige master"). ECTS total NOT published; a two-year Flemish master is conventionally 120 ECTS but AP does not state it, so treat 120 as inference, not fact. This matters for the fee calculation below.
study: CONFIRMED on the official page. Live electronic performance and improvisation using live-coding environments (Sonic Pi, TidalCycles, Strudel, Vortex); modular synthesis on a vintage Roland System 100M plus modern eurorack; custom instrument building with Axoloti, Raspberry Pi, Arduino and Max; artificial intelligence for generating music in both audio and MIDI; performance at algoraves and jam sessions through an immersive eight-speaker system for spatial composition; both open-source and commercial DAWs. "Everything revolves around your artistic ambitions" — a personalised trajectory rather than a fixed syllabus. Teaching staff: Dago Sondervan, Lennart Heyndels, Inne Eysermans.
recommendation: Still the most code-native music master in the slice, and the language position is genuinely favourable — no official language requirement, no IELTS needed to enrol. But two facts that were UNVERIFIED in the earlier draft have now resolved badly. First, admission: direct access needs an academic bachelor in Music (Jazz or Jazz/lichte muziek), not merely 'a bachelor'; his route would be the foreign-diploma committee plus almost certainly a voorbereidingsprogramma, adding a year. Second, cost: €25,065 a year, about €50,130 for the two-year master, with no automatic funding. Practical next steps if he wants to keep it alive: email toelating@ap.be now about whether a Software Engineering BSc plus a self-built electronic-music portfolio can reach the committee at all and what preparatory year would be required, and separately ask AP's international office whether the music master counts as English-taught for Master Mind. Both answers are needed before this can be ranked above C.

recommendation: DO NOT APPLY — INELIGIBLE, AND ON CURRENT EVIDENCE NO LONGER RUNNING. The previous record was right to flag this as a trap: the title 'Music Production MA, one year, Bulgaria' is exactly what he will search for and exactly what will surface. Two independent reasons to cross it off permanently. First, the published entry rule limits admission to graduates of six named music specialties at NMA Sofia and AMTII Plovdiv — a Tunisian software-engineering graduate cannot qualify now or after any portfolio year. Second, and new: the programme is absent from BOTH academies' official 2026/2027 candidate handbooks, having been listed in NMA's 2025/2026 handbook as a one-year ТКДФ master's. Only AMTII's stale specialty web page still advertises it. If a directory site or aggregator shows it, that listing is out of date. The theoretical path in — complete AMTII's Тонрежисура first, then this — is now doubly closed, because Тонрежисура itself requires a music bachelor's he does not have.

entry: CORRECTED — THE DECISIVE UNKNOWN IS NOW ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS NO. The official 2026/2027 candidate handbook, p. 34, states the conditions verbatim: „Условия към кандидатите: - да са придобили степен „Бакалавър“ в сферата на музикалното изкуство; - не се допускат кандидати с трайни слухови нарушения.“ A bachelor's IN THE FIELD OF MUSICAL ART is required, and candidates with permanent hearing impairments are excluded. A BSc Software Engineering does not qualify. Separately confirmed: holders of foreign higher-education diplomas must have COMPLETED the Bulgarian academic-recognition procedure at the moment of submitting master's documents.
acceptsNonMusic: NO — CORRECTED from UNVERIFIED. The 2026/2027 official handbook requires a bachelor's degree in the field of musical art. This closes the programme to him.
portfolio: No portfolio is required — CONFIRMED. The exam is aural, written and oral. This is not the advantage it looks like: the aural stage is harder for him than a portfolio would be.
audition: CORRECTED — the previously 'UNVERIFIED' exam is published, and it is a three-stage examination including an ear test. Stage I: aural analysis of fragments of musical works — (a) identifying the instruments sounding in a given recording; (b) determining the amplitude-frequency differences between two recordings of the same work. Stage II: a written test on the specialty (sample questions cover tone vs. noise, dynamic and tempo terminology, what determines timbre, WAV and AIFF, mono/stereo/surround, whether MIDI is digital, MIDI technology and what it transmits, master keyboard, balanced vs. unbalanced cable, ADC/DAC converters, the sampling rate and bit depth of standard audio CD) plus an interview. Stage III: interview with the commission on electroacoustic transducers (microphones and loudspeakers), computer systems, hardware, software and peripherals, musical acoustics and sound engineering. Stages I and III are effectively a trained-ear audition — the written test alone is preparable by a software engineer, the aural analysis is not, without ear training.
deadline: Two windows per year: late June and mid-to-late September. Expect the same for 2027. The binding earlier deadline is the Bulgarian academic-recognition procedure, which must be COMPLETE before documents are submitted — start it at least six months, realistically a year, ahead.

recommendation: THE OPEN QUESTION IS ANSWERED AND IT RULES HIM OUT. The previous record correctly identified 'is a music bachelor's required?' as the question on which everything turned, and correctly refused to guess. AMTII's official 2026/2027 candidate handbook answers it on page 34: a bachelor's in the field of musical art is required. Two further published facts, both previously unverified, reinforce the verdict — the entrance examination has three stages including an aural analysis (identify the instruments in a recording; hear amplitude-frequency differences between two masters of the same piece), and candidates with permanent hearing impairments are excluded. Even setting the degree rule aside, an untrained ear would not pass stage I. There is no scholarship route: every channel AMTII operates requires Bulgarian origin, North Macedonian citizenship or temporary-protection status. Substantively this was the best studio-craft curriculum in the Bulgarian set and the cheapest per year in the cheapest city — it is simply not available to him. Drop it; do not spend the year emailing the Учебен отдел about it.

audition: CORRECTED — the exam is published and is doubly disqualifying. Stage I, a test of linguistic and musical culture: (1) correcting spelling errors in given Bulgarian words; (2) explaining the meaning of given musical terms; (3) correcting punctuation and factual errors in a given Bulgarian text; (4) aural recognition of well-known Bulgarian and foreign performers and groups (Elvis Presley, The Beatles, Deep Purple, Queen, Pink Floyd, U2, Madonna, Eminem, Rihanna, Lady Gaga and others). Stage II: an oral test of speech technique in front of a microphone, plus an interview. Ranking is the arithmetic mean of the two stages; a mark below Добър 4.00 fails. A non-native speaker cannot pass a Bulgarian orthography-and-punctuation correction test or a Bulgarian microphone speech-technique assessment.

entry: CORRECTED — AND THIS REVERSES THE PREVIOUS RECORD'S CENTRAL FINDING. The 2026/2027 handbook, section IX, states verbatim: „Специалност „Звукорежисура и звуков дизайн за игри“, срок на обучение две години. Необходимо е кандидатът да притежава музикална образователно-квалификационна степен „Бакалавър“.“ A MUSIC bachelor's degree IS now required for the two-year track. The one-year track is worse: it requires a bachelor's specifically in „Звукорежисура, звуков и медиен дизайн“, and external candidates must have graduated in „Звукорежисура“ at another HEI. The previous agent's finding rested on the 2025/2026 handbook, where the clause was genuinely absent — I checked both PDFs side by side and the clause was ADDED for 2026/2027. Additional hard requirement for foreign-diploma holders: documents for the Bulgarian recognition procedure must be filed with the Учебен отдел during the academic year PRECEDING application and at least two months before the candidate documents themselves.
acceptsNonMusic: NO — CORRECTED. This is the single most important change to the previous record. The 2026/2027 official handbook explicitly requires a MUSIC bachelor's for the two-year track, and a sound-engineering bachelor for the one-year track. A BSc Software Engineering is not an eligible entry qualification for either. The previous record's headline claim ('unlike Musicology/Composition/Conducting, the sound-engineering specialties carry NO such clause') was true of the 2025/2026 handbook and is false for 2026/2027.
portfolio: CONFIRMED — no portfolio is demanded by the published exam programme for external candidates; admission is by interview on the technical syllabus. (NMA's own graduating students are instead admitted on their diploma-project defence: an independent sound-recording product plus a written theoretical exposition.)
audition: Single-stage oral interview (събеседване) on the four technical topics. No instrumental audition, no solfège. Format CONFIRMED unchanged for 2026/2027 — but now academically out of reach for him.
deadline: For a September 2027 start, expect the same shape: ТКДФ documents late May – early June 2027, non-EU direct-admission deadline around 12 June 2027. Exact 2027 dates publish on nma.bg/priem each spring. Because foreign-diploma recognition must start a full academic year earlier, the real deadline for him would have been autumn 2026.
opens: 2026/2027 cycle, ТКДФ: documents 26 May – 4 June 2026; exams 8–20 June 2026; ranking 23 June 2026; enrolment 23–26 June 2026. Non-EU direct admission (without preparatory course): до 12 юни 2026 г. Non-EU with preparatory course: до 25 юни, then 1–3 September. Non-EU nationals who completed a bachelor's at a Bulgarian HEI apply 1–15 June and 1–15 September. Documents are submitted online.
duration: CORRECTED. Not 'two years only'. The 2026/2027 handbook offers this specialty as 'една или две учебни години' — ONE OR TWO academic years. The handbook also resolves the previously unverified credit total: one-year master's = minimum 60 credits (for holders of a bachelor's in the SAME specialty); two-year master's = minimum 120 credits (ECTS).
languageReq: CONFIRMED. Foreigners must demonstrate Bulgarian ('За чужденците се изисква да владеят български език'), by one of three routes: (1) a document issued by a Bulgarian higher-education institution; (2) passing written AND oral Bulgarian examinations before a commission appointed by the NMA Rector; or (3) completing NMA's one-year preparatory course in language and specialised preparation, which ends with examinations in all subjects including written and oral Bulgarian. IELTS/TOEFL are irrelevant and not accepted.
englishTest: None. No IELTS or TOEFL is required or accepted anywhere in this admission. His untaken English test is irrelevant here — which is not an advantage, because the substitute demand is certified Bulgarian.
study: Sound engineering and sound design for video games. Interview syllabus (unchanged 2025/26 → 2026/27): (1) physical acoustics, behaviour of sound in space, sound phenomena; (2) sound-technical devices — electroacoustic transducers, mixing desks, amplifiers, processors; (3) spatial sound formats; (4) computer and electronic music technologies. Reading: Ballou, Huber & Runstein, Huber (MIDI Manual), Eargle (Microphone Book, Loudspeaker Handbook), Blackstock, plus Malyakov, Malinovski and Kusev.
recommendation: PREVIOUS RECORD OVERTURNED — HE IS NOT ELIGIBLE. The 2025/2026 handbook did not require a music bachelor's for this specialty; the 2026/2027 handbook, section IX, does, in the same boilerplate sentence used for Musicology, Composition and Conducting. I verified this by extracting and comparing both official PDFs directly. Unless NMA reverses the clause again for 2027/2028 — worth one email to sbogdanova@nma.bg, but do not plan around it — a BSc Software Engineering graduate cannot apply. Everything that made this look like the best academic match in the sweep (technical interview instead of an audition, no portfolio, game audio and spatial sound content) is now behind a door he cannot open, and even if it reopened, the €8,500/year with no winnable scholarship and the certified-Bulgarian requirement would still stand. Remove it from the shortlist.

A BSc Software Engineering is none of these. The list says these are "pre-approved", implying other degrees may be individually assessed, but the PDF does not state a dispensation route. audition: THIS IS A PRACTICAL PRODUCTION TEST, NOT A PERFORMANCE AUDITION — the single most important distinction for this candidate, and RAMA is the clearest example of it in the region. institution: The Royal Danish Academy of Music (Det Kongelige Danske Musikkonservatorium, DKDM / RDAM)
programme: Master of Music (MMus) in Tonmeister / Sound Engineer (Tonemester)
whyChance: States it does not accept a non-music background
verdictWhy: The assessment is one he could genuinely pass — two submitted productions and a twenty-minute conversation, with no live exam of any kind — but entry is restricted by regulation to holders of a Bachelor of Music as tonemeister, which he does not and cannot have. Add roughly EUR 11,000–14,000 a year and it is closed twice over.
correction: Two significant corrections. (1) The record's gate 'Exam/interview only' misses that DKDM runs NO LIVE ENTRANCE EXAM AT ALL for master's — no ear test, no audition, no set task for tonmeisters. The gate is two submitted productions (one rhythmic, one classical, each at least 7 minutes) plus a production plan for non-EU applicants and a 20-minute discussion. Contrary to the Tonmeister stereotype, the assessment is not what closes this door. (2) The record omits the closed prerequisite that does close it — 'Bachelor of Music as tonemeister' — and omits the live 2027 deadline: 1 December 2026 for the autumn 2027 intake, which is the single most time-critical date found in this slice.

tuition: EUR 11,100 per academic year for the Tonmeister/Sound Engineer MASTER (non-EU/EEA), paid in two instalments: 1 June (new students) and 1 September. Free for EU/EEA. For comparison the master fee table runs EUR 11,000-14,900 across specialisations.

RDAM's general prerequisites page states a "Bachelor's degree in music ... or equivalent from a higher education institution abroad at a level equivalent to RDAM".
acceptsNonMusic: NO. The published requirement is a Tonmeister bachelor or an equivalent conservatory-level music degree. A BSc Software Engineering does not meet this and no discretionary clause is offered on the pages read. This is the best-fitting curriculum in the whole slice and the hardest gate - he would need a music/audio bachelor or a documented equivalent first.
portfolio: Two musical production examples, EACH at least 7 minutes: one from the rhythmic genres (pop/rock/jazz) and one from classical music. Non-EU/EEA applicants must ADDITIONALLY submit a production plan documenting the creative process - timeline, equipment/software used, roles of participants and the recording context. (The certified audiogram, max 1 year old, is a Bachelor-level requirement, not master.)
audition: Principal-study audition of approximately 30 minutes including assessment, built around a roughly 20-minute discussion of the submitted works plus theoretical and practical questions on your "technical and musical standpoint". EU/EEA applicants audition IN PERSON; non-EU/EEA applicants audition ONLINE, with a possible additional interview covering piano, ear training/solfege and theory. Graded on the Danish 7-point scale; decision based on documentation of previous education plus evaluation of the submitted productions.
deadline: 1 December for both EU/EEA and non-EU/EEA applicants at Master level - PRIOR CYCLE date pattern, confirm the 2027-intake date. RDAM aims to answer non-EU/EEA Bachelor and Master applicants about six weeks after the deadline.

study: Principal study is music production and recording techniques, organised in close collaboration with the Danish Broadcasting Corporation (DR). Alongside: aural studies, basic piano, music theory and music history. Semester projects, set productions, studio recordings, CD recordings, film sound design and PA work for performances. Students can specialise by genre, sector, producer role or sound-technician role. "Well-equipped studios and plenty of mobile equipment." Study trips, masterclasses, company visits and listening tests.
recommendation: Content-wise this is the classic Nordic recording/production master - DR collaboration, real studios, both rhythmic and classical production, and non-EU applicants audition online so no travel cost. The deal-breaker is entry: it presumes a Tonmeister bachelor. Also note the portfolio demands a CLASSICAL production of 7+ minutes, which a DJ/electronic producer will not have. entry: A bachelor's degree or equivalent of at least three years (180 credits) with at least 20 credits at level 2 in the specialisation unit; for the Electronic Music/performance specialisations, at least 80 credits in performing music / electronic music, a music-technology degree, or another approved programme; minimum grade average of C across the bachelor. acceptsNonMusic: NO as published - the entry route requires "at least 80 credits in performing/electronic music, music technology degree, or other approved programs" plus a C average, plus documented music theory/analysis. A pure software-engineering BSc would need an exceptional individual assessment; nothing on the pages read promises one.

deadline: Non-EU/EEA international applicants: 1 November - 15 December, with an extended deadline of 15 April 2026 noted for the 2026 intake - PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date; expect 1 Nov - 15 Dec 2026 for a Sept 2027 start

study: The programme emphasises balancing "practice, composition, programming and production" with theoretical grounding in popular musicology. The Electronic Music specialisation focuses on "music technology and sound design in the studio, or use of Live Electronics in a concert context" and on "performance and its relationship to music technology and sound design". Course structure (2023 plan, indicative): MF-404 Aesthetics (5 ECTS), MF-405 Audience Development and Marketing (5 ECTS), MF-406 Arts Entrepreneurship (5 ECTS), MUR402-405 Individual Performance and Interpretation I-IV (15 ECTS each), music-business courses, musicological theory, and a 30-ECTS master's thesis. Sibling specialisations: Performing Music, World Music, Songwriting, and Music Business and Management. UiA also runs a Bachelor in Electronic Music, so the department has an established electronic-music teaching base.
recommendation: Of all the Nordic craft-focused options this is the closest fit to "I want to make electronic music and perform it": English-taught, an explicit Electronic Music specialisation covering studio sound design and live electronics, entrepreneurship and audience-development modules that map onto a DJ career, and at NOK 135,000/yr it is roughly a third the cost of NTNU or NMH. The obstacles are the 80-credits-in-music prerequisite, an audition worth 50% of the score whose remote-submission status is unpublished, and a flat no-scholarship policy. Highest-value action in this slice: email Per Elias Drablos in autumn 2026 with a portfolio and ask directly whether an engineering BSc plus documented electronic-music practice can satisfy the 80-credit rule.

audition: NOT AN AUDITION — but a PARTIAL AURAL GATE plus a MEDICAL HEARING TEST. Three components: (1) the three-recording portfolio above; (2) an ORAL EXAM on 'wybrane zagadnienia z przedmiotów kierunkowych (elektroakustyka, technika studyjna, znajomość metod mikrofonowania, SOLFEŻ BARWY, język angielski specjalistyczny)' — selected topics from the core subjects: electroacoustics, studio technique, knowledge of microphone methods, TIMBRE SOLFÈGE, and specialist English; (3) a qualification interview on motivation, specialist interests, expectations and career plans. SEPARATELY: 'Od kandydata wymagany jest pozytywny wynik badania audiometrycznego' — a POSITIVE AUDIOMETRIC (hearing) TEST RESULT IS REQUIRED. recommendation: AVOID THIS SPECIFIC PROGRAMME, BUT NOT THIS INSTITUTION. Two hard corrections. First, the fee is now known and it is 6 700 EUR per semester — 26,800 EUR for the degree — for a Polish-language music-criticism, journalism and cultural-PR qualification that contains no audio engineering, no music technology and no production content. Paying master-level money in a language he does not speak for a journalism degree is indefensible for a man whose goal is producing and DJing. Second, and more usefully, the previous record's headline 'negative finding' — that Gdańsk has no sound-engineering master's — is simply wrong. The academy runs a second-cycle 'produkcja muzyczna i realizacja dźwięku' specialization under kierunek Jazz i muzyka estradowa on Wydział IV, and a second-cycle 'Kompozycja muzyki do filmu, gier i mediów' on Wydział I. Those two should be opened as separate records and assessed properly: they are Polish-taught and audition-gated and cost 8 403 and 9 296 EUR per semester respectively, so they are almost certainly out of reach financially, but the database should not carry a false negative about this institution.

But that is a VOCATIONAL, SUB-DEGREE award, and its officialness does not transfer to this master. The school's homepage claim that its qualifications are 'homologados por el Ministerio' refers to the FP catalogue, not to this programme.

But Module 3 is compulsory practical instrumental training on piano, electric guitar, bass or drums WITH ENSEMBLE PLAYING, and Module 5 is harmony, arrangement and notation. A candidate with no instrumental training and no conservatory background starts those two modules from zero alongside classmates who do not. Of the five programmes in this batch, this is the most conventionally musician-oriented and the worst match for his profile. recommendation: A credible, well-established school and a fair 1,200 hours for the money — but the wrong programme for THIS candidate, and I would not put it ahead of the alternatives. The decisive issue is fit, not price: two of the five modules are compulsory instrumental performance with ensemble playing and classical harmony/notation, and he has no instrumental training whatsoever. This is a musician's production master, and he would spend a third of the year fighting a deficit rather than building the electronic-production and DJ craft he actually wants. Layered on top: CEV itself concedes the award has no equivalence in Spanish university education, publishes no ECTS, no entry requirements, no fees and no scholarship figures on its own site, and says nothing about visas. Its structural advantage — 1,200 in-person hours, which is the only programme here that plainly clears the 20-hours-a-week visa threshold — is real and worth noting, but it does not outweigh a fundamental content mismatch. Consider only if he decides he wants formal musical grounding alongside production, which is not what he has asked for.
