For 2026/27 it offered 140 scholarships worth up to €6,000 across undergraduate and foundation courses, with IED Milano allocated 33 — the largest single allocation, ahead of Barcelona (29), Roma (20), Madrid (14), Torino (13), Firenze (10), Accademia di Como (8), Bilbao (7) and Cagliari (6). Reported award structure: SEE students resident in Italy receive €2,600 to €6,000 depending on ISE band; students from EU candidate countries receive a flat €4,400; extra-SEE/non-European students are reported to receive a single flat award of €6,000. Tunisia falls in the extra-European category. The 2026/27 deadline was 5 May 2026 at 23:59 (GMT+1) — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date; IED's scholarship page currently states "Al momento non ci sono concorsi attivi" (no competitions currently active). Even at the maximum €6,000, his net cost would remain around €15,000/year. As an accredited Italian institution IED students may in principle access regional Diritto allo Studio grants, but these are means-tested on Italian ISE and are effectively closed to a new non-resident non-EU arrival — UNVERIFIED.

Confirm directly.
study: Milan: "the languages and technologies of sound", covering recording techniques, sound synthesis, sound design for audiovisuals, video games, apps, interactive installations and multimedia performances, plus transversal skills across creative sectors and new technologies. Rome: broader sound production with particular focus on sound applied to images — "music production and soundtracks, sound engineering, live recording, post-production, performance and DJing". Worth noting that the Rome variant is the only IED sound programme whose published description explicitly names DJing and music production, i.e. it is closer to his interest than Milan — but it is Italian-only and still undergraduate. Detailed module lists remain UNVERIFIED.
recommendation: Rule out, and treat this as a negative finding rather than an option — but the reason is now far more damning than previously understood. The headline correction is the money: IED's official 2026/27 tariff puts a NON-EUROPEAN student on the top band with no income assessment available, at €2,500 enrolment plus €18,300 tuition = €20,800 per year, plus a €190 regional tax, so €20,990 a year and roughly €63,000 across three years before living costs. The previously cited €8,000-€15,000 range was IED's general marketing band and is simply not the price he would pay; the real figure is more than double the bottom of it. And he would be paying that for a Diploma Accademico di PRIMO livello — a bachelor-equivalent, 180 CFA, undergraduate qualification at exactly the level of the BSc he already holds. Two genuine corrections in IED's favour, neither of which rescues it: an English-taught stream DOES exist in Milan (IED's own page records the language as "Italian | English"), so the language barrier assumed earlier is not real there; and the credit total is confirmed at 180 CFA/ECTS with a proper ministerial accreditation behind it. It is a legitimate institution selling a legitimate degree — just the wrong degree, at the wrong level, at a price that would consume his entire budget. Also note that the ROME variant is the only IED sound page that explicitly mentions "performance and DJing" and music production, so it is nearer his interest than Milan's installation-and-events emphasis — but Rome is Italian-only and equally undergraduate, so it changes nothing. The useful conclusion for him is the one this batch keeps confirming from three directions: the international-chain landscape at genuine master's level in these four countries is far thinner than the marketing suggests. IED has no sound master anywhere despite campuses in both Spain and Italy; SAE's electronic music offering is an unpriced private certificate outside its own AFAM authorisation; and Portugal's best chain-adjacent option is a sub-bachelor BTEC. At master's level in this field it is essentially Berklee Valencia and little else — everything else is diplomas, certificates and título propio.

scholarshipDetail: STRONG ON PAPER, BUT ONE CORRECTION MATTERS ENORMOUSLY. (1) INTERNATIONAL POSTGRADUATE SCHOLARSHIP (portfolio-based): partial first-year tuition coverage; NON-EU students are placed at 'up to €6,000' on the postgraduate scholarship page, while the February 2027 competition page quotes 'up to €7,000 depending on income bracket' for Master of Arts. EU-resident MA candidates get €2,200-€3,000 in brackets 1-5 and up to €6,000 in bracket 6; Academic Master EU-passport candidates get €3,000. RENEWABLE for the second year if the call's conditions are met. Assessed by faculty and admissions jury with decisive weight on the portfolio. Winners must ENROL WITHIN 7 DAYS of notification or forfeit. (2) *** NOT COMBINABLE *** — NABA states these scholarships 'cannot be combined with other NABA scholarships, DSU scholarships or additional financial grants'. THIS KILLS THE STACKING ASSUMPTION: he CANNOT take the international scholarship AND the early-enrolment discount, and he CANNOT take it AND a DSU regional grant. He must pick one. (3) EARLY ENROLMENT SCHOLARSHIP: 10% off tuition for October 2026 starts, international students and new registrations only, applied automatically on enrolling by 29 January 2026 — no separate application; those who previously registered and postponed are excluded. For October 2027 NABA has announced 15% for Bachelor of Arts — the MA equivalent for 2027 is UNVERIFIED, ask. (4) EUROPEAN INTERNATIONAL SCHOLARSHIP COMPETITION for postgraduates: deadline 24 July 2026 (October 2026 entry). (5) FORMER NABA STUDENTS: 20% off total tuition excluding regional tax — not applicable. (6) AUSONIO ZAPPA SCHOLARSHIP: total tuition exemption, currently expired, registration open for future announcements — worth registering interest. (7) DSU / regional right-to-study: NABA administers it and non-EU students are eligible, but it is not combinable with the NABA international scholarship, and second-level places put to competition are extremely few.

His portfolio is the single highest-leverage item for both admission and money here.

deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates. Verified 2026 cycle: 27 May 2026 — international postgraduate portfolio scholarship, October 2026 entry. 24 July 2026 — European international scholarship competition, postgraduate. 25 September 2026 — international scholarship for MA/Academic Master starting FEBRUARY 2027 (this one is still live as of now). 11 September 2026 — the parallel BA competition for February 2027. 29 January 2026 — early-enrolment 10% discount for October 2026. Sound work exists only as a component inside these broader media/performance degrees, never as the subject of the degree. Detailed module lists UNVERIFIED at this depth.
recommendation: On process and money transparency NABA is the best-run non-EU institution in this batch, and the portfolio-judged scholarship genuinely names non-EU students at up to €6,000-€7,000, renewable. But two hard facts must land. FIRST, the stacking he might have been counting on does not exist: NABA states the scholarship 'cannot be combined with other NABA scholarships, DSU scholarships or additional financial grants', so the realistic best case for year one is €22,250 minus about €6,000-€7,000, i.e. roughly €15,000-€16,000 — not the €14,000 that a stacked 10% discount would have implied. SECOND, and more important, THERE IS NO MUSIC PROGRAMME HERE. I checked the entire MA and Academic Master catalogue: nothing in music, sound design, audio production or electronic music. Digital and Live Performance and Creative Media Production are performance-technology and media-production degrees where a software engineer would do well and where sound is one element among many. Pursue NABA only if he consciously reframes his ambition towards live/performance technology and media production and accepts that he will build his DJ/producer craft outside the curriculum. If he does apply: apply in the EARLIEST session, choose ONE relief (the scholarship, since it is worth more than 10%), and put everything into the portfolio because the portfolio is what the jury weighs.

recommendation: ALL FIGURES IN THE PRIOR RECORD CONFIRMED — no corrections needed. £23,000 international fee, IELTS 6.5/5.5, 2.2 in a listed relevant subject, three £3,000 Harrison bursaries, 14 August 2026 advisory deadline, 30 full-time places, MUS7109 at 60 CATS, and the 10-minute RPEL video cap are all verbatim correct. study: KCB describes Music and Technology as 'essentially an instrumental course' with a technical side (sound physics, digital studio work, programming, synthesis, sound design) and an artistic foundation resting on 'the triangle performance – composition (creation) – digital lutherie'. Underlying subject areas: Computer Music (using the computer as an instrument, performatively and compositionally); Creative Programming (Max and Ableton Live, progressively complex assignments); Sound Theory & Digital Education (frequency, amplitude, oscillators, microphone handling, recording, live mixing); Modular Synthesis & Sound Design; Sound Installation (mechanical, acoustic and electronic techniques); Electro Acoustic Multimedia Ensemble. Master specialisations: Live Electronics (electronics as primary instrument, performance emphasis), Computer Music Composition (music creation and sound installation), Hybrid Performance (acoustic instrument plus electronics — requires a prior BA3 instrument diploma). Programme founded 2018. Staff named: Benjamin Van Esser (coordinator) and Roel Das.
recommendation: Content-wise this is a near-perfect match for a programmer-turned-electronic-musician — Max patches and Ableton sessions are literally accepted as portfolio items, and 'digital lutherie' is exactly where a software engineer has an edge. But it is the clearest NO in the slice for a September 2027 master start: KCB states plainly that it does not admit anyone directly to the master, not even holders of other music degrees. The honest recommendation is to email Benjamin Van Esser about the accelerated bachelor route and treat KCB as a 3–4 year plan rather than a 2027 master.

study: 'La pratique de l'électroacoustique est envisagée comme discipline principale.' The name is deliberately open 'afin de pouvoir accueillir toutes les formes de projets, d'usages et de visées dans le domaine des musiques électroniques, qu'elles soient accompagnées ou non d'images, de vidéo, de mise en scène ou de lumières.' Studies are defined 'en termes de pratique quotidienne (aux contacts du studio et de ses machines)'; there is 'pas de parcours étudiant·e « type » ou prédéfini ; les projets compositionnels individuels sont le support même des études'. Structure: UE1 discipline principale; UE2 associated knowledge + one complementary discipline linked to the master research project; UE3 transversal (language, professional-insertion placements, research methodology, master's mémoire); UE4 disciplines d'ouverture from over a hundred options. Annual participation in the Empreintes creation festival; collaborations with ENSBAL and ENSATT, Mannheim and symphonic orchestra formats, an improvisation collective; principal teacher François Roux, plus Michele Tadini in the electroacoustic class.
recommendation: Artistically this is one of the most attractive electronic-music masters in France — individual composition projects, daily studio practice, an explicitly open definition of 'musiques électroniques', and cheap public tuition. The blocking clause is the admission rule requiring a licence-grade degree 'dans la discipline concernée' plus the age cap of 30. For a CS graduate with no conservatoire background this is realistically closed for 2027; a plausible two-step plan would be a French university master in electroacoustic/musical computing first (e.g. Saint-Étienne or Gustave Eiffel), then this.

institution: Liszt Ferenc Zeneművészeti Egyetem (Liszt Academy of Music), Composition Department
programme: Zeneszerző MA (Music Composition MA) — Elektronikus zenei médiaművészet (Electronic Music Media Art / EZMM) specialisat…
whyChance: States it does not accept a non-music background
qualification: MA
tuition: UNVERIFIED for self-funded non-EU applicants — the Liszt Academy publishes fees per programme; not confirmed on pages read. Fully covered if admitted through Stipendium Hungaricum.
scholarshipDetail: STIPENDIUM HUNGARICUM — Tunisia is an eligible partner country (one of fifteen eligible Arab states). The Liszt Academy is a Stipendium Hungaricum host institution and 'MA Music Composition' appears in the Stipendium Hungaricum course catalogue as an English-taught option. Also relevant: Hungarian Diaspora Scholarship (not applicable here).
entry: BA diploma. All applicants must submit a PRELIMINARY CREDIT RECOGNITION REQUEST to establish whether their BA diploma can be accepted for the MA, unless the BA was taken at the Liszt Academy — the request form plus the BA transcript/diploma supplement and English course descriptions go in with the application. Certificates need an official certified attested Hungarian translation. Applications route through felvi.hu (Hungarian central admissions) or through the Stipendium Hungaricum portal.
acceptsNonMusic: No, in practice. Nothing formally bars a non-music BA, but the mandatory preliminary credit-recognition check on the BA diploma, plus a Bach fugue, a classical sonata/rondo movement, score sight-reading and an orchestration task, make a software-engineering BSc holder without conservatory theory effectively unadmittable. Quote from the Academy: applicants 'must submit a preliminary credit recognition request to determine whether the applicant's BA diploma can be accepted to apply for the MA programme'.
portfolio: Uploaded portfolio evaluated first: sheet music of THREE of the applicant's own compositions, with recordings if possible. For the EZMM specialisation the presented works must total NO MORE THAN 25–30 MINUTES and comprise (a) one recorded tape/fixed-media piece and (b) one work for instrument + electronics, OR an interactive live performance, OR an audiovisual work. Style exercises additionally required: one fugue in the style of J. S. Bach (EZMM candidates may realise the Bach-style task electroacoustically), one classical sonata or rondo movement, and one 20th-century etude in the style of a named composer. EZMM candidates also sit an electronic-music fundamentals test.
audition: YES — mandatory in-person. 'All applicants are required to appear before the Entrance Examination Committee in person.' Components: a practical examination (live audition) in the chosen specialisation; a written theoretical examination; written and oral form analysis based on Schoenberg's 'Fundamentals of Musical Composition' including analysis of classical/romantic and 20th–21st century works; an on-site orchestration/scoring task; score reading (sight-reading classical/romantic and contemporary scores); and a career-orientation interview.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Two routes: (a) Stipendium Hungaricum — the 2027/28 call is reported to open November 2026 with a 15 January 2027 deadline (confirm on stipendiumhungaricum.hu when the call is published); (b) self-funded/Hungarian route via felvi.hu, mid-February deadline in the ordinary Hungarian cycle — exact 2027 date UNVERIFIED.
opens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Stipendium Hungaricum 2027/28 reported to open November 2026.
duration: 2 years (4 semesters); ECTS UNVERIFIED (Hungarian MA standard 120)
study: Composition at master level with the option to deepen electronic-music work; the EZMM strand continues the Academy's electronic music media art line (launched 2011) covering the history and compositional technique of electroacoustic and computer music, sound analysis, synthesis and transformation, MIDI/OSC, interactive and algorithmic music. Composition-related special courses are chosen freely according to the student's interests. Applicants who did NOT take electronic-music courses in their prior studies must complete a 2-semester 'Foundations of Electronic Music Composition' course during the first MA year.
recommendation: This is the only fully-funded English-possible master in the whole slice that touches electronic music — Stipendium Hungaricum would pay tuition, stipend and housing, and Tunisia is eligible. But the admission is a classical composition examination: Bach fugue, sonata form, orchestration, score reading, in person in Budapest, on top of a diploma credit-recognition check. Without conservatory theory this is not a realistic September 2027 target. Keep it on the list only if he is willing to spend 2026–27 on harmony, counterpoint and score reading.

entry: HARD BLOCKER — CONFIRMED, but the previous report's description needs CORRECTING as too narrow. The previous report stated entry is restricted to holders of a Composition diploma. In fact the official page accepts a wider set: Diploma in Composizione (previgente ordinamento), diploma accademico di primo livello in Composizione, diploma accademico di primo livello in MUSICA ELETTRONICA, and correlated first-level or previgente-ordinamento courses of the Conservatorio di Como. So Electronic Music graduates are admitted too — the previous report was wrong to exclude them. HOWEVER, the correction does not help HIM: unlike Rovigo and both Cuneo tracks, this course does NOT list a generic 'laurea triennale' or 'Laurea di I livello' among qualifying titles. Every accepted route requires a prior MUSIC qualification. His Software Engineering BSc is not a qualifying title. All candidates must additionally pass a selection examination.
acceptsNonMusic: NO — CONFIRMED AND FINAL. Every qualifying entry title requires a prior music qualification (Composition or Electronic Music at first level, or the previgente-ordinamento equivalents); no generic three-year university degree route is published. And even for those who qualify, the entrance examination requires writing a four-voice fugue, composing a piano piece to a given outline, orchestrating to commission, analysing a twentieth-century score, and presenting three notated compositions for small orchestra, chamber ensemble and voice-plus-instrument. This is categorically closed to a candidate with no formal composition training. There is no angle, no exception route, and no amount of portfolio work in the next year that changes it.
portfolio: Not a portfolio in the sense he means it. The three required works are notated scores for small orchestra, chamber ensemble, and voice and instrument — orchestral and chamber writing, not audio productions. A DAW-based electronic portfolio, however good, does not satisfy this requirement. This is the sharpest demonstration in this whole set of how differently Italian conservatoires interpret the phrase 'sound design'.
audition: The hardest examination of the four, and HARDER than the previous report recorded. Verbatim framing: 'Per essere ammessi al biennio è necessario superare un esame di ammissione consistente in una Prova specifica di selezione relativa alla disciplina principale.' WRITTEN tests: 'Realizzazione di una esposizione, di un divertimento e di uno stretto di fuga a 4 voci' on a given subject — i.e. writing the exposition, divertimento and stretto of a FOUR-VOICE FUGUE; composition of a piano piece on a provided outline; orchestration of a piano piece chosen by the commission; and analysis of a significant twentieth-century score. ORAL: CORRECTION — the previous report said 'three original compositions' generically. The page is more specific and more demanding: 'almeno tre composizioni libere: una per piccola orchestra, una per gruppo da camera, una per voce e strumento' — at least three free compositions, one for small orchestra, one for chamber ensemble, one for voice and instrument — plus a discussion of musical competencies. Additionally, candidates arriving from 'un percorso non accademico (c.d. del Previgente ordinamento)' must pass a 'Verifica delle competenze musicali in ambito storico, musicologico e analitico'. Writing a four-voice fugue and orchestrating to commission are skills requiring years of formal harmony, counterpoint and orchestration training. This is categorically out of reach within any realistic timeframe.

study: Year one: audiovisual communication theory, orchestration, audiovisual composition, music informatics, electives. Year two: advanced audiovisual composition, music applied to images, audio post-production technologies, integrated audiovisual composition. The presence of orchestration and the weight of composition modules confirm this is a composer's degree, taught to people who can already write music on paper.
recommendation: VALUE VERDICT: AVOID. RATING: C. — DO NOT APPLY. To be clear about why: this is not a scam and not a fake degree — it is a legitimate, accredited, state second-cycle qualification, and the AVOID verdict is about fit, not integrity. It is simply and completely closed to him. Two corrections to the previous record. First, its entry list was too narrow: the official page also admits holders of a first-level diploma in MUSICA ELETTRONICA, not only Composition graduates — so the course is somewhat more open than reported, just not open in any direction that includes him, because no generic laurea triennale route exists. Second, the audition is HARDER than reported: the three required compositions are specified as one for small orchestra, one for chamber ensemble and one for voice and instrument, i.e. notated ensemble scores, on top of the four-voice fugue, the piano composition, the orchestration and the twentieth-century score analysis. The value of keeping this record is that it marks the boundary of what is reachable. Italian state conservatoire second-level courses vary enormously in openness under similar-sounding titles: Rovigo's DCSL60 admits any three-year degree and assesses by portfolio and conversation; Como's course, in nearly the same subject area, demands a composition diploma and a fugue. Knowing Como sits at the closed end saves him an application, a fee and several weeks. If the audiovisual composition subject matter is what attracts him, Rovigo's DCSL60 Musica Applicata covers substantially the same ground — composition for music applied to images is its largest credit block — and is open to him on the published rules. Choose Rovigo over Como on every dimension that matters: entry, examination, cost of living, and probability of admission.

scholarshipDetail: ALL PRINCIPAL FIGURES VERIFIED AGAINST THE IED BANDO DSU 2025/26 PDF AND THE NABA DSU 2025/26 GUIDE. (1) NON-EU ELIGIBILITY — CONFIRMED VERBATIM. The IED bando lists as eligible applicants 'i cittadini italiani', 'i cittadini degli Stati membri dell'Unione Europea', and 'i cittadini di Stati non appartenenti all'Unione Europea (d.p.r. 31.8.1999, N.394 inter alia art. 44 bis, attuativo del d.lgs 25.7.1998, n.286 nonché d.p.r. 31.8.1999, n. 394, art. 46 comma 5)'. Non-EU students at a PRIVATE academy are explicitly in scope. (2) THE 'FUORI SEDE' RULE — CONFIRMED VERBATIM, footnote 7 of the bando: 'L'Art. 13 comma 3 del D.P.C.M. 9/04/2001 stabilisce che gli studenti stranieri non appartenenti all'Unione Europea sono considerati comunque studenti fuori sede indipendentemente dalla sede della loro residenza in Italia ad eccezione del caso in cui il nucleo familiare dello studente risieda in Italia. Al fine dell'ammontare della borsa di studio l'alloggio deve essere a titolo oneroso.' Fuori sede is the top payment band, and he lands in it automatically provided he pays for accommodation. (3) AMOUNTS (IED, 2025/26, inclusive of the €140 regional-tax reimbursement and the €818 meal allowance) — EXACT MATCH TO THE DRAFT: FUORI SEDE €8,134.00 / €7,073.00 / €5,776.00 for income bands 1/2/3; PENDOLARI €4,754.00 / €4,134.00 / €3,254.00; IN SEDE €3,383.00 / €2,950.00 / €2,114.00. Award can be increased up to +40% for students with disability over 66%. NABA quotes 'da un minimo di circa € 2.000 fino ad un massimo di circa € 8.000, comprensivo di un pasto giornaliero gratuito' — confirmed. (4) INCOME TEST — CONFIRMED: ISEE Universitario not above €26,516.70 AND ISPE not above €57,645.03; both must be satisfied. Bands: 1ª €0.00–€13,258.35; 2ª €13,258.36–€17,677.80; 3ª €17,677.81–€26,516.70. Reference year for a first-time first-year student in 2025/26 is 31/12/2023 (i.e. income two calendar years back — plan documents accordingly). (5) MERIT FOR A FIRST-YEAR SECOND-LEVEL STUDENT — CORRECTED. The draft said '38–40 credits'. The bando says 40: full confirmation of the benefit is conditional on obtaining a minimum of 40 CFA by 10.08.2026; the scholarship is REVOKED, with repayment of the first instalment, for first-year students who have still not reached 40 credits by 30.11.2026. (6) NON-EU PAPERWORK — CONFIRMED AND IF ANYTHING HARDER THAN THE DRAFT SAID. Documents from employers are expressly NOT accepted; the income declaration must be issued by 'l'agenzia delle entrate ufficiale del governo del paese di residenza dello studente'; 'L'autocertificazione relativa a redditi e/o patrimoni esteri non può essere presentata' — self-certification of foreign income or assets is inadmissible, full stop. Everything must be 'tradotti in italiano da un traduttore riconosciuto e legalizzato dall'autorità locale competente nel Paese di residenza' (alternatively legalised by the Italian Prefettura). scholarshipDetail: THE DECISIVE MECHANISM: NON-EU STUDENTS ARE ELIGIBLE, AND THEY LAND IN THE HIGHEST-VALUE BRACKET. (1) ELIGIBILITY: the IED bando states plainly that applications may be made by Italian citizens, EU citizens, AND 'i cittadini di Stati non appartenenti all'Unione Europea' (under DPR 394/1999 arts. 44-bis and 46(5), and D.lgs 286/1998). Non-EU students at a PRIVATE academy are explicitly in scope. (2) THE 'FUORI SEDE' RULE: under Art. 13(3) DPCM 9/4/2001, non-EU foreign students are AUTOMATICALLY treated as 'fuori sede' regardless of where they live in Italy (unless their family lives in Italy), provided they pay for accommodation. Fuori sede is the top payment band. (3) AMOUNTS (IED, Lombardy, 2025/26, including €140 regional-tax reimbursement and €818 meal allowance): fuori sede €8,134 / €7,073 / €5,776 by income band 1/2/3; pendolari €4,754 / €4,134 / €3,254; in sede €3,383 / €2,950 / €2,114. NABA quotes a range of roughly €2,000 to €8,000 including a free daily meal. So a Tunisian student renting a room in Milan is looking at €5,776–€8,134 per year. (4) INCOME TEST: ISEE Universitario ≤ €26,516.70 AND ISPE ≤ €57,645.03 — both must be satisfied. Income bands: 1st €0–13,258.35; 2nd €13,258.36–17,677.80; 3rd €17,677.81–26,516.70. (5) MERIT FOR A FIRST-YEAR SECOND-LEVEL STUDENT: essentially just enrolment plus holding the first-level title; full confirmation then requires 38–40 credits by the following 10 August. (6) THE NON-EU PAPERWORK — THIS IS THE HARD PART: he needs an 'ISEEU-ISPEU parificato' built from (a) a certificate of current foreign household composition, (b) income declarations for each household member for the reference calendar year issued by the OFFICIAL GOVERNMENT TAX AGENCY of the country of residence — employer documents are expressly NOT accepted and self-certification is expressly NOT valid, (c) property holdings with square metres or a certificate of no property for every member aged 18+, (d) movable assets (securities, dividends, shareholdings, company net-worth fractions, accounts). Everything must be translated into Italian by a recognised translator and LEGALISED. TUNISIA IS NOT on the bando's legalisation-exemption list and NOT on the Apostille list — so full consular legalisation applies. A floor also applies: non-EU declared income cannot be treated as below €7,002.97/year, the visa subsistence minimum. IED has a convention with CAAF CGIL Lombardia to help foreign students obtain the parificato. (7) COMPETITION IS THE RISK: for 2025/26 NABA Milano put just ONE scholarship to competition for first-year second-level students (and one at NABA Roma); IED pooled €354,392.15 across four ranking lists proportional to applicant numbers. Ranking for first-year students is purely a function of ISEE — a lower ISEE ranks higher. (8) INCOMPATIBILITY: receiving any other income- or merit-based grant for the same year is an automatic exclusion, so DSU cannot be stacked with the institution's own scholarship. (9) PAYMENT: two instalments (roughly February and July/September); second-assignment winners get one payment around December. Paid ONLY by bank transfer to an Italian or SEPA account in the student's name — he will need a European bank account.

Private, niet-bekostigd providers sit outside both. A non-accredited programme generally cannot support a student residence permit. THE PARTICIPATING LIST — CONFIRMED, WITH ONE NUMBER CORRECTED. For 2026-2027 the participating institutions are 11 research universities and 23 universities of applied sciences (the draft said 24 — the live page says 23; the list changes every year, so re-check for 2027-2028). Every participating institution is a PUBLICLY FUNDED (bekostigd) Dutch institution. No private, niet-bekostigd provider appears. THE EXCLUSION — CONFIRMED BY ABSENCE AND BY THE PROVIDERS' OWN WORDS. A non-EEA student enrolling at SAE Institute Amsterdam, Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam, Dutch Dance Music Academy, Sound Education Nederland, Music Production Academy, Pro Audio Education NL or any comparable private audio provider CANNOT access the NL Scholarship, because none of them is a participating institution. Deadlines are set individually by each participating institution — irrelevant to him, since none of the relevant audio providers participates. DUTCH STUDENT FINANCE IS ALSO CLOSED. Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam states on its own FAQ/fees pages that it cannot assist non-EU residents with visa applications, that because it is a PRIVATE institute its students are not eligible for a visa or a student loan, that the Advanced Diploma is not a 3-year degree programme and so is not eligible for any kind of student loan, and that it is classified as 'short vocational education' which does not entitle study finance (tuition is merely tax-deductible). SAE's own 'Current Student FAQs' page was fetched and says NOTHING about visas, residence permits, DUO/study finance or scholarships — so the negative position is corroborated at search level but NOT confirmed in SAE's own words. scholarshipDetail: THE NATIONALITY RULE — VERIFIED on the DGES 'Condições de atribuição' FAQ. Eligible applicants are: Portuguese citizens; 'cidadãos nacionais de Estados membros da União Europeia com direito de residência permanente em Portugal'; third-country nationals who are holders of a PERMANENT residence authorisation, or beneficiaries of long-term-resident status, or nationals of States with cooperation agreements conferring the benefit, or nationals of States whose law grants Portuguese students equal treatment in equal circumstances; stateless persons and political refugees; and 'beneficiários de estatuto de refugiado em situação de emergência humanitária ou proteção temporária'. THE INTERNATIONAL-STUDENT EXCLUSION — VERIFIED VERBATIM on the DGES 'Atribuição de bolsas de estudo' FAQ: 'De acordo com o estabelecido no diploma que regula o estatuto do estudante internacional (Decreto-Lei n.º 36/2014, de 10 de março, alterado pelo Decreto-Lei n.º 62/2018, de 6 de agosto), os estudantes internacionais beneficiam exclusivamente da ação social indireta.' Indirect social action means canteens, facilities and services — NOT the monetary grant. The same FAQ confirms that students admitted through the special international-student admissions process are ineligible, except those granted emergency-humanitarian status. A Tunisian arriving on a study visa is therefore excluded from DGES cash support at BOTH public and private institutions. THE ONE EXCEPTION — confirmed and not applicable to him: 'estudante em situação de emergência por razões humanitárias' status carries the full range of direct and indirect support. THE SILVER LINING — CONFIRMED IN SUBSTANCE, THOUGH THE EXACT DGES WORDING WAS NOT LOCATED ON THE TWO FAQ PAGES FETCHED. Portuguese PRIVATE higher-education institutions run their own bolsas for economically disadvantaged students including foreign students without a permanent residence title in Portugal, typically taking the form of a variable REDUCTION IN THE ANNUAL PROPINA rather than a cash grant, awarded after assessment of the student's situation. This is precisely the door he should push on, and it is the highest-value action available to him in Portugal. Named leads carried over from the sibling slice and NOT re-verified in this batch — treat each as UNVERIFIED until he has the regulation in hand: UCP Porto reportedly grants scholarships annually to candidates of non-Portuguese nationality NOT resident in Portugal, giving partial exemption from master's tuition, awarded on application average plus interview (contact ee.bolsas@ucp.pt); UCP's Escola das Artes reportedly runs Bolsas de Mérito e Incentivo à Investigação for master's students giving total or partial tuition exemption; The Social Hub Changemaker Housing Scholarship targets refugee and international students; Lusófona publishes no equivalent on the pages previously read (UNVERIFIED — ask directly).

scholarshipDetail: TWO ABSOLUTE EXCLUSIONS HE MUST UNDERSTAND BEFORE CHOOSING SPAIN. (1) TITLE-TYPE EXCLUSION: Becas MEC can be requested only for official undergraduate (grado) and OFFICIAL master's studies. They CANNOT be requested for a 'título propio' or a permanent-education programme. Third-cycle studies, specialisation studies and títulos propios are all outside the scheme. Fees must be paid to a Spanish centre. This alone kills MEC funding for Universidad Europea's Máster en Producción Creativa de la Música, TAI's Máster en Producción Musical, SAE Spain's UDIMA Máster de Formación Permanente, and every microFusa diploma. (2) NATIONALITY/RESIDENCE EXCLUSION: non-EU foreigners must hold LEGAL RESIDENCE ('residencia legal') in Spain to qualify. The situation of 'estancia' — which is exactly what a study authorisation confers — does NOT give any right to a university grant. Holding an authorisation of stay is expressly not sufficient. EU citizens must be permanent residents or prove employment. A Tunisian arriving on a study visa is therefore excluded even if he chose an OFFICIAL master's. (3) COMUNIDAD DE MADRID: its student grants target students enrolled at MADRID PUBLIC universities on official grado or master's studies in disadvantaged socio-economic situations; and its Becas de Excelencia expressly EXCLUDE 'estudios de máster, especialización o títulos propios'. No Comunidad de Madrid route exists for a private-university título propio. (4) GENERALITAT DE CATALUNYA non-university grants (€300–350 basic, €50–125 performance, €1,700 income-based, €2,700 relocation, 2026-2027) are tied to Catalan income/academic and residence conditions and are not reachable by a newly arrived non-EU student. (5) WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN TO HIM IN SPAIN: only institution-level commercial discounts (early place-reservation, alumni, referral) and one genuinely nationality-blind private award found in this research — the YAMAHA MUSIC EUROPE FOUNDATION grant of €1,000–2,000 per year for students under 25 enrolled at a recognised European music institution, distributing roughly €66,000 a year.

scholarshipDetail: VERIFIED — EXCLUSION 1, TITLE TYPE. becaseducacion.gob.es (Ministry, university section, 2026/2027 content) states that the following are NOT included in this convocatoria: 'estudios de tercer ciclo o doctorado, estudios de especialización, títulos propios de las universidades'. Covered studies are grado, máster universitario oficial, enseñanzas artísticas superiores (grado and máster), access courses for over-25s at public universities, and complementos de formación. CONSEQUENCE (confirmed): every 'Título Propio' / 'Máster de Formación Permanente' sold by a Spanish private school — Universidad Europea's Máster en Producción Creativa de la Música, TAI's Máster en Producción Musical, the SAE Spain/UDIMA Máster de Formación Permanente, every microFusa diploma — is outside the beca general regardless of who applies. VERIFIED — EXCLUSION 2, NATIONALITY/RESIDENCE. The Ministry's 'Qué necesitas' page states for non-EU nationals that entitlement requires being under 18 OR having obtained a RESIDENCE PERMIT ('permiso de residencia') as at 31 December of the relevant year, and states explicitly that holding an authorisation of STAY is 'no es suficiente'. A Tunisian arriving on 'estancia por estudios' therefore has no entitlement EVEN IF he chose a fully official ANECA-accredited máster universitario. This is the harder of the two exclusions because he cannot design around it. VERIFIED — COMUNIDAD DE MADRID BECAS DE EXCELENCIA. The convocatoria expressly excludes from its scope 'las ayudas para la realización de estudios correspondientes al tercer ciclo, postgrado o doctorado, estudios de máster, especialización o títulos propios de las universidades o de centros superiores de enseñanzas artísticas', and additionally excludes applicants who already hold (or are in a position to obtain) an official university qualification. As a BSc holder applying to a master's-level título propio he is doubly out. Latest traced convocatoria: Orden nº 6113/2025, curso 2025-2026 (PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date). CORRECTED — YAMAHA MUSIC EUROPE FOUNDATION. The draft described this as 'the only genuinely nationality-blind private award found' and as a plausible fallback. THAT CHARACTERISATION IS WRONG AND MUST NOT BE RELIED ON. Verified from europe.yamaha.com/en/education/ymfe/: it is an AUDITION-BASED CLASSICAL PERFORMANCE award. For the 2026/2027 round the discipline is EXCLUSIVELY CLASSICAL PIANO (the eligible instrument changes every year — past rounds include flute). Amount for the current round is stated as €1,300–€2,000 (not €1,000–€2,000), a one-time payment; the foundation distributes roughly €66,000 a year across 33 European countries; age limit 25 or under at the time of award (usually February/March); selection is by video pre-screening then a NATIONAL AUDITION before a panel of musicians. Registration opens October 2026, applications close 30 November 2026. A self-taught electronic music producer with no conservatory instrumental training has effectively zero chance, and music production / electronic music are not eligible disciplines. UNVERIFIED: whether a non-European national studying in Europe may enter at all — the public page does not say, and it must be checked on the country-specific entry form before any effort is spent. WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN TO HIM IN SPAIN: institution-level COMMERCIAL discounts only — early place-reservation discounts, alumni discounts, referral discounts, and whatever a school will negotiate. No public money, national or regional.

Applicants must hold ONE of: 'Grado en Música'; 'Grado en Musicología'; 'Grado en Historia y Ciencias de la Música'; or 'Título Superior de Música de Conservatorio en cualquier especialidad'. All four credential routes require a music degree or a superior conservatory diploma; the fifth route requires two years' professional experience as a conservatory/institutional music teacher or as a director or instrumentalist in a national or regional orchestra. A BSc in Software Engineering with no music degree, no conservatory training and no professional music experience satisfies NONE of them. He is ineligible as things stand, and no portfolio or self-taught evidence can substitute — admission here is by credential, not by demonstrated ability.

Delivered through live online classes; no studio attendance.
recommendation: On paper the most legally valuable music qualification in this batch — a genuine ANECA-verified official Spanish master — and in reality completely closed to him and useless for his goals. He fails all published entry routes: no Grado en Música, Musicología or Historia y Ciencias de la Música, no Título Superior de Conservatorio, and no two years teaching music in a conservatory or playing/directing in a national or regional orchestra. There is no portfolio route to argue around it. Even if he somehow qualified, it is 100% online so it cannot support a Spanish student visa, it teaches instrumental/electroacoustic composition rather than DJ and electronic production, there is zero studio time, and UNIR will not tell him the price until he hands over his contact details. Rule it out completely. It is documented here for one reason: this is the 'official Spanish music master' he will see advertised everywhere while researching, and he should know before he spends time on it exactly why it is not an option — the entry bar, not the money, is what excludes him.

institution: Universidad Europea de Madrid (private university, Permira-owned international private-education group)
programme: Máster en Producción Creativa de la Música
whyChance: States it does not accept a non-music background
qualification: TÍTULO PROPIO — the university's OWN diploma, not a 'Máster Universitario Oficial'. No ANECA verification and no RUCT registry entry could be found. Note the classic Spanish trap: the word 'Máster' in the title does not make it an official degree. One aggregator describes the award as 'Máster en Artes', which is not an official Spanish qualification category.
accreditation: NOT OFFICIAL — and, more seriously, NOT CURRENTLY CONFIRMABLE AT ALL. It is a título propio: no ANECA verification, no RUCT entry, not a Máster Universitario Oficial. It carries no automatic EHEA recognition, gives no right of entry to a Spanish doctorate, and is not valid for Spanish public competitive examinations. Universidad Europea is itself a legitimate RUCT-registered private university — which is precisely why the distinction matters: the institution is real, this particular title is not an official degree. For contrast, UEM's genuinely official music master is the online 'Máster Universitario en Investigación Musical' (60 ECTS) — a research degree, not a production degree, and not a fit for him.
tuition: UNVERIFIED — must be requested from admissions in writing.
otherFees: UNVERIFIED. Universidad Europea operates a 'reserva de plaza' (place-reservation) payment to hold a place, typically payable before scholarship decisions are issued, but no figure is published for this programme.
totalCost: UNVERIFIED — no tuition figure exists in the public domain, so no honest total can be given. This is the single biggest problem with this entry for a budget-sensitive applicant.
scholarshipDetail: CRITICAL EXCLUSIONS. As a TÍTULO PROPIO the programme is shut out of Spanish state aid: Becas MEC (Ministry general scholarships) cannot be requested for a título propio or a permanent-education programme — they are restricted to official grados and official másteres — and non-EU nationals additionally require legal RESIDENCE in Spain, which a study stay does not confer. Comunidad de Madrid excellence grants expressly exclude 'estudios de máster, especialización o títulos propios'. What remains is the university's own commercial discounting: an early place-reservation discount (15% for reserving before 31 October in the published cycle); a 15% alumni discount on postgraduate programmes; a stated continuity plan of up to 40% for continuing students; and 50–60% discounts on VIRTUAL/online master's under country-specific agreements (SENESCYT–Ecuador 50%, ICETEX–Colombia, OIJ 50%, OEA/OAS 50%). EVERY ONE of those named international schemes is Latin-America-specific — there is NO Tunisian, Maghreb or African scheme published. Realistic prospect for him: the generic early place-reservation discount only. Ayudas a la Excelencia at the Real Madrid School (40%) do not apply to this programme.
entry: Per press coverage only: aimed at graduates in Audiovisual Communication, music creators, sound engineers, music graduates and academically trained musicians interested in producing sound and audiovisual content. No official admission criteria published. UNVERIFIED.
acceptsNonMusic: NOT EXPLICITLY, AND PROBABLY NOT AS ADVERTISED. The only published target audience is 'graduados en Comunicación Audiovisual, creadores musicales, ingenieros de sonido, titulados en música y músicos con formación académica'. A BSc Software Engineering appears on none of those lists. Because it is a título propio the university has full discretion to admit him anyway, but this is unconfirmed and must be obtained in writing.
portfolio: UNVERIFIED — no admission or portfolio specification is published anywhere.
audition: UNVERIFIED — none published.
deadline: UNVERIFIED — rolling admission is typical for títulos propios. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm dates for an October 2027 start, assuming the programme still runs.
opens: UNVERIFIED. The only published date is a place-reservation discount deadline of 31 October — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
duration: 60 ECTS, October to June (nine months) per the 2024 launch coverage; one aggregator lists '8 MESES' and 13 subjects. Figures are inconsistent across secondary sources and NOT confirmed on any official university page.
englishTest: NOT APPLICABLE — the programme is taught in Spanish. IELTS is irrelevant here; the binding barrier is SPANISH proficiency, which he does not have and for which no required level is even published. UNVERIFIED.
study: Creative and artistic production processes with the producer as the central axis, covering all phases of a musical recording: from the original idea to its possible extensions, applying appropriate tools and methods and preparing the product for its final finish. Faculty named in press coverage includes Carlos Jean, Miguel Álvarez and Sergio Jiménez Lacina; directed by Abel Hernández and José Sánchez Sanz. No official module list exists on any university page. UNVERIFIED.
recommendation: AVOID on present evidence, and treat any enthusiasm from an admissions agent with scepticism. This is a Spanish-language, título-propio, unpriced programme with no published curriculum, no published facilities, no scholarship route open to a Tunisian, zero eligibility for Spanish state aid, and — decisively — no live official webpage anywhere on the university's own site in August 2026. He should not spend time on it unless UEM confirms IN WRITING all four of: (1) that the programme will actually run in October 2027; (2) the full price including reserva de plaza; (3) that a software-engineering graduate with no Spanish is admissible, and what Spanish level is required; (4) that they will issue the documentation for a 'visado de estudios' for a título propio. Absent all four, this is a dead end, and his money is far better placed against a fully-priced programme such as Berklee MPTI or an A3ES/ANECA-accredited public-sector option.

duration: 2 years / 120 ECTS / 4 semesters — CONFIRMED (previously UNVERIFIED). Catalogue: '2 years (120 ECTS), 4 Semesters, 16-18 weeks per semester'. Structure: at least 7 courses, 1 seminar, 1 specialisation course and thesis, minimum 21 local credits.
study: CONFIRMED from the official DEU course catalogue. Required: Methods of Scientific Research and Publication Ethics (GSE 5011, 5 ECTS); Guided Writing in Music Technology I (MZT 5011, 6 ECTS) and II (MZT 5028, 4 ECTS); Seminar (MZT 5096, 3 ECTS); Field of Study (MZT 5800, 6 ECTS); Thesis (MZT 5900, 54 ECTS). Electives, all in two-semester pairs: Media Analysis I/II, Studio Recording Techniques I/II, Acoustic Design I/II, CAD and Electro-acoustic Applications I/II. Note the shape: the thesis alone is 54 of 120 ECTS (45%), and there is no course in composition, arrangement, electronic-music production, DAW work, DJing or live electronics. Graduate profile is stated as 'sound recording, audio post production, arrangement, broadcast sound... and also work in the academic fields'.
recommendation: Keep on the list only as a documented NEGATIVE. Four independent blockers, each sufficient on its own: (1) the music-technology bachelor is enforced verbatim against the diploma, and non-matching candidates are refused entry to the exam; (2) 100% of the entrance mark is an on-site technical interview in İzmir, conducted in Turkish; (3) the entire curriculum is Turkish and all registration documents must be Turkish; (4) probable ALES requirement, a Turkish-language national exam. Separately, even if he were eligible the content is wrong for him: 54 of 120 ECTS is a research thesis, with acoustics and studio-engineering theory and zero production, electronic-music or DJ craft. Do not apply. Do not spend enquiry effort here either.

whyChance: Requires a music degree

verdictWhy: This is the strongest combination in the batch: an English-taught master's whose Sonic Arts portfolio brief explicitly accepts creative audio coding and programming, with no audition, no score requirement and no stated music-degree bar — paired with a Türkiye Bursları Art Scholarship that names İTÜ as a host, pays 6,500 TL a month plus tuition, accommodation and flights, and whose under-30 age cap he clears. Two things must be resolved. First, the three-hour written General Music Knowledge and Music Theory examination, which every MIAM master's candidate sits and which he is currently unprepared for — ask MIAM whether it can be taken remotely and what it covers. Second, confirm Tunisia's eligibility in the TBBS system. Both are answerable by email now.
correction: The input row records the gate as 'Portfolio only'. That is wrong and it matters: every MIAM master's applicant sits a written General Music Knowledge and Music Theory examination plus a field exam and an interview, on top of the portfolio. Conversely the row understates how open the portfolio itself is — Sonic Arts explicitly accepts 'examples of creative audio coding / programming' and non-sonic material, requires no scores and sets no minimum number of works, which makes it far more accessible to a software engineer than the sibling Composition concentration at index 56 that demands at least three scores. Also record that Türkiye Bursları names İTÜ as a host institution for its Art Scholarship, pays 6,500 TL/month at master's level, and caps master's applicants at under 30.
